### What

Complements #2282 with direct and mixed storage-image heap regression tests and a concise entry in `docs/dev/TechnicalDebt.md`. Depends on #2282; merge that implementation first. Its original commit is included with MathiasDevelopes's authorship retained, followed by the additional tests/documentation commit.

The existing tests in #2282 cover several dynamic-mip images. These additions use the real binding allocator to check:

- Eight and five direct 2D float storage images, matching heap demands observed during a private Silent Hill 2 startup investigation.
- Sixteen direct images accepted and seventeen rejected.
- One dynamic-mip image reserving four slots alongside one or twelve direct images, requiring five or sixteen total elements.
- A thirteenth direct image alongside the dynamic image rejected at seventeen elements.
- Direct resource indices retained, with exactly four references to the dynamic image.

No title-specific behavior, captured shader, game asset, or new production implementation is introduced by the additional commit. The documentation records that the new direct/mixed cases have allocation coverage only.

Related #2347 separately raises sampled-image capacity while preserving bindless table size. It is needed in the local title integration stack but is not a dependency of these storage allocation tests.

Overlap audit, 9 October 2026, at main `f8c2f072`: #2141 raises sampler-pair capacity and changes the physical shader-data layout; #2347 raises sampled-image capacity and preserves the bindless table length. This branch includes #2282's storage-image capacity change. These are different heaps, not duplicate implementations. Combining them must retain `StorageHeapCapacity = 16`, `StorageMipSlots = 4`, `SampledHeapCapacity = 32`, `BindlessTableSlots = 16`, and #2141's sampler capacity, ABI version and matching layout assertions. #2226 changes conservative-rasterization documentation beside the new storage-heap entry; retain both entries. Virtual merges confirm text conflicts in `RuntimeAbi.hpp` and `TechnicalDebt.md`; they do not validate a combined runtime. Rebase and retest when one lands first. The implementation dependency remains **Depends on: #2282**.

### Tested

Windows, MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2, NVIDIA RTX 4070 Laptop GPU.

- Test first on the local integration stack: the new eight-direct-image case failed with `shader image heap capacity exceeded` in 0.07 seconds before #2282 was applied.
- Combined local #2282/#2347 stack: 12/12 focused checks passed in 3.99 seconds with Vulkan required, including GPU bindless-image execution, shader device profile, shader memory/cache, prepared graphics/shaders, and zero-stride vertex fetch. This stack includes earlier startup fixes and is not the isolated PR branch.
- The local title retry cleared both image-heap errors and stopped at a later unsupported depth/stencil storage access. It exited naturally after 146 seconds with 319 intro flips, approximately 30 FPS and at least 7,658,053,632 bytes of system commit headroom. Gameplay was not verified.
- Isolated PR branch based on main `0fdda7be9495e2f799306f31198857d037b31194`: `agc_shader_device_profile` passed, with a final restored run taking 0.08 seconds. Temporarily restoring the old four-element storage admission limit reproduced `shader image heap capacity exceeded` in 0.07 seconds; that negative control was removed and the test passed again.
- Full Linux/Windows builds require a maintainer's manual CI run and have not been claimed here.
- No native PS5 hardware validation was performed; this change adds allocator tests and documentation.

body:
### What

Textures in `5_6_5_UNORM` (133), `1_5_5_5_UNORM` (134) and `4_4_4_4_UNORM` (136) are sampled with their channels in the wrong order.

On AMD hardware the first component of a packed format sits in the least significant bits. Mesa's `gfx10_format_table.py` reverses the size list of each name ("Keep the bit sizes in little-endian order"). So:

| format | X | Y | Z | W |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5_6_5 | 4:0 | 10:5 | 15:11 | — |
| 1_5_5_5 | 4:0 | 9:5 | 14:10 | 15 |
| 4_4_4_4 | 3:0 | 7:4 | 11:8 | 15:12 |

`TextureFormat.cpp` maps them to `VK_FORMAT_R5G6B5_UNORM_PACK16`, `VK_FORMAT_A1R5G5B5_UNORM_PACK16` and `VK_FORMAT_R4G4B4A4_UNORM_PACK16`. Those Vulkan formats name the most significant field first: R5G6B5 has R in bits 11..15, A1R5G5B5 has R in bits 10..14, and R4G4B4A4 has R in bits 12..15 and A in bits 0..3 (*Formats*).

`ViewComponents` sends DST_SEL X straight to `VK_COMPONENT_SWIZZLE_R`. So a 5_6_5 texel `0x001f` (X = 1) samples as (0, 0, 1, 1), and 1_5_5_5 swaps red and blue the same way. In 4_4_4_4 the order is fully reversed, so X comes back from the alpha nibble.

radv uses the same three Vulkan formats and compensates in the view swizzle: `vk_format.c` maps them to `PIPE_FORMAT_B5G6R5_UNORM`, `B5G5R5A1_UNORM` and `A4B4G4R4_UNORM`.

This adds `TextureComponentChannel`, which gives the Vulkan channel that holds a guest component: X, Y, Z, W read B, G, R, A for 133 and 134, and A, B, G, R for 136. `ViewComponents` composes it after DST_SEL, so every sampled view of these formats reads the bits the guest meant, with any swizzle. The VkFormats are unchanged, and no other format is affected.

Tests:
- `RunTextureFormatTests` checks, for each component of the three formats, that the chosen Vulkan channel starts at the guest bit (low-bit table taken from the Vulkan format definitions).
- `agc_driver_image_packed16_load` (new) fills a 256×1 texture of each format, with every component either all zeros or all ones. It then checks `image_load` of every texel and `image_sample_lz` of texel 0 on the GPU, with DST_SEL X Y Z W and Z Y X W.

Found by comparing AnyPS5's GFX10 format tables with Mesa's and the Vulkan format definitions. Two independent passes flagged the same three entries.

### Tested

Windows 11 (26200), WinLibs GCC 15.2.0 r7, CI configure flags, main at d70b8998:

- `agc_driver_graphics` and `agc_driver_image_packed16_load` pass with `--repeat until-fail:3` on an RTX 4070 Laptop GPU and an Intel Raptor Lake-S iGPU.
- With `TextureComponentChannel` returning the component unchanged, as on main, both fail:
  - `format 133 component 0 is not read from bit 0`
  - `5_6_5_UNORM image_load X Y Z W: texel 0 component 0 is 0x00000000, expected 0x3f800000` on the RTX 4070.
- Full suite on the RTX 4070: 508/508 passed.

### What

Two TechnicalDebt entries said what the recompiler assumes without a hardware measurement. Measured on RDNA2 (gfx1036, Ryzen 7950X3D iGPU) with `tools/hw-oracle` (Linux, CachyOS kernel 7.2.9, hsa-rocr 7.2.4, clang 23.1.1 as the assembler, tools at `main` d70b8998, mode IEEE 0, f32 denormals flushed, f16/f64 kept, DX10_CLAMP 1, RNE), in wave32 and wave64, and recorded in the entries:

- `s_call_b64` (SIMM16 = 3): the link pair receives `PC + 4` and the branch goes to `PC + 4 + signext(SIMM16) * 4`; `s_setpc_b64` of the link returns to the instruction after the call (a counter shows the callee, +1, and the return path, +2, each ran once). The entry's "native RDNA2 ... execution" becomes measured; execution on the PS5 (gfx1013) and title compatibility stay unverified.
- `s_swappc_b64` with SDST 125 (the null register): the hardware branches to the source pair (the instruction at the skipped address is not executed) and leaves a marker SGPR pair untouched; with an SGPR destination the link is `PC + 4`. So the existing decode as `s_setpc_b64` matches the hardware.
The `s_memtime` measurements from the same run are posted on #1632, which rewrites that entry.

No code changes. Bodies, rows, outputs and the script: https://github.com/SleglJan/AnyPS5/tree/audit/oracle-2026-10-08/oracle-audit/scalar-misc.

### Tested

`tools/check_conventions.py --base upstream/main` passes; the entries are documentation only.

Overlap: #2302 (open) edits the same `s_swappc_b64` entry, and #2161 and #2178 add entries next to the `s_call_b64` one; none of them shares code with this PR or is built on by it, so whichever merges second needs a one-line rebase.

body:
### What

Follow-up to #1979, which makes the cycle exact. Two errors remain after it, both in the step from the cycle to the driver's sine and cosine of the radians:
- A tiny cycle is multiplied by 2π and handed to the driver's `sin`, whose absolute error (about 2^-22 on NVIDIA) swallows the result: through the sweep below on an RTX 3080 (615.71.09), 12,930 of 32,832 `v_sin_f32` inputs come back as zero for a finite hardware result (6,465 of each sign), and `v_sin_f32` of −2^-126 is −0 where the hardware returns 0x81c90fd5 (−7.4e-38).
- Near the zeros of sine at k + 0.5 and of cosine at k ± 0.25 the f32 radians drop the low bits of the cycle: `v_cos_f32` of 0x3e7fffff (0.24999999) is 0 on the RTX 3080 where the hardware returns 0x33c90fd9 (9.4e-8), and with correctly rounded radians the result is still up to 51% off, as #1979's description says.

Measured on RDNA2 (gfx1036, Ryzen 7950X3D iGPU) with `tools/hw-oracle` (Linux, CachyOS kernel 7.2.9, hsa-rocr 7.2.4, clang 23.1.1 as the assembler; IEEE 0, f32 denormals flushed and also kept, f16 kept, DX10_CLAMP 1, RNE) over every f16 input, 32,832 f32 rows (every exponent with 64 mantissas of both signs, 13 specials, 26 cycle counts around 256 and beyond, 25 zero rows of padding), a dense sample of 20,480 inputs in [0, 0.25], and 1,920 inputs at 2^-k (1 + m/16) off the half and quarter turns:
- below 2^-12 of a turn the hardware returns the input times 6.2831826 (0x40c90fd5, six ULP below the f32 2π): 16 of 16 mantissas at every exponent from 2^-13 down to 2^-22, 8 of 16 at 2^-12, never the f32 2π;
- at a distance q below 2^-12 from the half and quarter turns its result is 4 to 14 ULP above q × 0x40c90fd5, so within 7 ULP of q × 2π, and no single constant reproduces it;
- it gives sin 0 and cos 1 for |x| ≥ 2^23, differs from the exact fraction by up to 10 ULP just below integers and up to 15 ULP beyond ±256 cycles, and no odd polynomial of degree 9 to 13 fitted to the dense sample by least squares reproduces its sine (9 ULP off).

Within 2^-12 of a turn from a zero of the function the lowering now returns the linear term of the exact distance to that zero (`0.5 − |r|` for the sine and `0.25 − |r|` for the cosine, both exact by Sterbenz's lemma, |r| itself at the integers), with the hardware's constant at the integers and the f32 2π at the half and quarter turns; the sine's sign is applied on the bits. Everywhere else the driver's sine or cosine of the radians stays as it is, so RADV keeps selecting its native `v_sin_f32` and `v_cos_f32` on the cycle (`RADV_DEBUG=shaders` on the new test shows `v_rndne_f32`, `v_sin_f32` and `v_cos_f32`, no `v_fract_f32`). The translation's zero, infinite and NaN picks are unchanged. A fold of the whole quarter turn was measured too and rejected: with the same 2^-12 band it moves 848 of the 20,480 dense cosines on RADV by up to 15 ULP (the hardware's cosine is not its sine of the complement) and gains the RTX 3080 nothing outside the band (1,166 against 1,149 ULP).

The sweep through the recompiler (f32 with denormals flushed), results equal to the hardware bits and the largest ULP distance, #1979 → this PR:

| | RADV (Mesa 26.2.4, the iGPU) | RTX 3080 (615.71.09) |
|---|---|---|
| `v_sin_f16` | 65,536 of 65,536 → 65,536 | 63,086 of 65,536, max 4 → 65,230, max 1 |
| `v_cos_f16` | 65,536 → 65,536 | 65,512, max 1 → 65,514, max 1 |
| `v_sin_f32` | 32,424 of 32,832, max 15 → 32,422, max 15 | 14,864, max 8,388,062, 12,930 zero for a finite value → 29,456, max 1,166, none |
| `v_cos_f32` | 32,488, max 15 → 32,486, max 15 | 29,092, max 163, 2 zero for a finite value → 29,092, max 163, none |

Input by input: on RADV the change touches 4 of the 32,832 f32 inputs (the two sines within 2^-14 of ±0.5 by 1 ULP, the two cosines at ±0.24999999 by 2 ULP) and 10 of the 20,480 dense cosines by up to 5 ULP, all inside the bands; on the RTX 3080 14,618 sine and 2 cosine results move closer to the hardware and none away (14,592 sines become the hardware's bits), and 2,144 f16 sines become exact. What remains on the RTX 3080 is the driver's: its sine at the edge of the band (1,166 ULP at 0xc57fffff, whose cycle is exactly 2^-12, the first value outside it) and its cosine inside the quarter turn (1,149 ULP on the dense sample at 0x3e7fbc00). For reference, at `main` before #1979: RADV `v_sin_f32` 24,529 exact with a maximum of 855,638,025 ULP and `v_cos_f32` 32,285 with 202; RTX 3080 `v_sin_f32` 14,752 exact, 6,466 zero for a finite value, maximum 847,249,963, and `v_cos_f32` 28,864 with 1,746,018,777.

The other transcendental ops are unchanged and recorded in the same TechnicalDebt entry: RADV returns the hardware's bits for every f16 and f32 input of rcp, rsq, sqrt and log and all but one of exp (f16 0x11c5, 1 ULP); NVIDIA stays within 2 ULP except its log2 between 0.52 and 1.32 (40 inputs over 2 ULP, up to 24 million at 0x3f7fffff).

Data (the sweeps, the hosts' summary at `main` and their results at #1979 and with this PR input by input, the dense sample and the fold measurements, scripts): https://github.com/SleglJan/AnyPS5/tree/audit/oracle-2026-10-08/oracle-audit/transcendentals.

### Tested

Linux (CachyOS, kernel 7.2.9, GCC 16.2.1), Release, `ANYPS5_ENABLE_SPIRV_TOOLS=ON`, RTX 3080 and RADV, on this branch (#1979 at e6eb64aa plus one commit).

- New `agc_driver_sin_cos_near_zero`: 32 inputs per type in each lane (f32 and f16: tiny and small negatives, ±6.1e-5, the neighbours of ±0.5 and ±0.25, the cardinal points, 255.5, 256.25, −1000.5, 3.4e38, ±0, inf, NaN, eight ordinary values), pinned on the oracle in the titles' mode and run in FLOAT_MODE 0xc0; zero, infinite and NaN results must match the bits, the others are compared in ULPs with a per-lane tolerance: 0 for 18 lanes (7 of which take ±1 from the driver's sine or cosine of the f32 π/2 and π, exact on RADV, the RTX 3080 and lavapipe), 2 for the ±6.1e-5 lanes (the cosine's maximum, where RADV returns the hardware's 0x3f7ffffe, NVIDIA 0x3f7ffffd and Intel ANV 0x3f800000), 1 for the ±0.49999997 lanes, 2 for the ±0.24999999 lanes, 12 for the eight ordinary lanes (measured maxima there: RADV 0, NVIDIA 9). Written first: on #1979 alone it passes on RADV, whose native instruction already covers the bands, and fails on the RTX 3080 at lane 0 (`v_sin_f32` of −2^-126 is 0x80000000, expected 0x81c90fd5); with the change it passes, three repeats on each GPU.
- `agc_driver_sin_cos_reduction` (#1979's test), `agc_driver_vop1_float_unary`, `agc_driver_float16_misc`, `agc_driver_float16_result_modifiers`, `agc_driver_formatted_store`, `agc_driver_image_sample_unnormalized` and `agc_driver_typed_heaps` pass on both GPUs, three repeats; full `ctest` 499/499 on each GPU. (Unrelated to this branch: on `main` d70b8998 `agc_driver_dcc_keys_first_write` fails on the RTX 3080 and `agc_driver_storage_cache_budget` on the iGPU without any change.)
- `tools/check_conventions.py` (against #1979's head) and `tools/check_test_registration.py` pass.
- Fork CI on this branch: https://github.com/SleglJan/AnyPS5/actions/runs/37960569207 at e58e1a6e (this code; the later commits only reword the TechnicalDebt entry and widen the ±6.1e-5 lanes to 2 ULP, 036e825a): Linux with lavapipe 518/518 including `agc_driver_sin_cos_near_zero`, Windows 509/509 with the AGC GPU tests skipped (no Vulkan device), relinker matrix green.

### What

`SegmentFilter::ShouldSkip` (`core/relinker/elfpatcher/src/general/SegmentFilter.cpp`) decides which guest program headers the relinker drops when it lays out the native image (`ProgramHeaderLayoutBuilder`). It had no direct unit test — it was only constructed as a dependency in `Amd64OnlyConverterTests`, which asserts nothing about its filtering.

Add `segment_filter_tests` covering every branch:
- `PT_LOAD` kept, `PT_DYNAMIC` skipped;
- the SCE OS range skipped — `PT_SCE_DYNLIBDATA`, `PT_OS_RELRO`, the `PT_LOOS`/`PT_HIOS` bounds and an interior value — and the types just outside the range kept;
- the `PT_OS_PROCPARAM` and `PT_GNU_EH_FRAME` exceptions, which are kept even though both fall inside the SCE OS range (so the test pins the fact that they are matched before the range check, not after);
- `PT_NOTE` skipped only when unmapped and non-empty, and kept when mapped or empty.

No production code is changed; this documents and pins the current behaviour. A small indirect bit of the SCE-range branch is already exercised by `test_string_table_bounds.py`; everything else here was unasserted.

### Tested
Built relinker-only on macOS (Apple Silicon, AppleClang) with `-DANYPS5_RELINKER_ONLY=ON -DBUILD_TESTING=ON`; all CTest tests pass, including the new `segment_filter`. Also sanity-checked that the test fails if the `PT_OS_PROCPARAM` exception is flipped, to confirm it actually guards the behaviour. No title or homebrew involved — it is a host-side unit test.

body:
### What

`VertexInputNumericClass` (`RdnaDescriptorFormat.cpp`) lists the UINT and SINT buffer formats so that their vertex inputs get an integer SPIR-V type. It is missing `10_10_10_2_UINT` (54) and `10_10_10_2_SINT` (55), which fall through to `Float`.

`DecodeVertexFormat` (`VertexInput.hpp`, since #119) already decodes those two as `VK_FORMAT_A2B10G10R10_UINT_PACK32` / `_SINT_PACK32`, with scalar `u32` / `i32`. So a vertex shader that reads one of these attributes declares an `f32` input for an integer attribute format:

| V# format | attribute (`VertexAttributeSignature`) | shader input (main) |
|---|---|---|
| 54 | `u32x4` | `f32x4` |
| 55 | `i32x4` | `f32x4` |

Vulkan requires the two to match ("The numeric type of the attribute's format must match the numeric type of the input variable in the shader", *Vertex Input Description*). AnyPS5's own shader validation compares them and fails with `vertex attribute metadata disagrees with shader input` (`ShaderValidation.cpp:506`).

The two formats are added to the Uint and Sint groups. `VertexInputNumericClass` is already part of the shader cache key (`CacheKey.hpp`), so no stale entry can be reused.

`agc_driver_graphics` now checks every format 1–127 that `DecodeVertexFormat` accepts: a `u32` or `i32` attribute must get a Uint or Sint shader input, and nothing else may. The existing assertion next to it only checks `DecodeVertexFormat(55).scalar`, which is why the mismatch went unnoticed.

Found by comparing AnyPS5's GFX10 format tables with Mesa's `gfx10_format_table.py` and the Vulkan format definitions.

### Tested

Windows 11 (26200), WinLibs GCC 15.2.0 r7, CI configure flags, main at d70b8998:

- `agc_driver_graphics` passes on an RTX 4070 Laptop GPU and an Intel Raptor Lake-S iGPU. With the two `case` lines removed it fails with `vertex format 54 declares a shader input of another numeric type than its attribute`.
- Full suite on the RTX 4070: 507/507 passed.

body:
### What

The VOP2 table still decodes six GCN gfx6/7 opcodes that RDNA doesn't have:

| VOP2 | decoded as | on RDNA |
|---|---|---|
| 0x15, 0x17, 0x19 | `v_lshr_b32`, `v_ashr_i32`, `v_lshl_b32` | not an instruction; only the `*rev` forms (0x16, 0x18, 0x1a) exist |
| 0x22, 0x23, 0x24 | `v_bcnt_u32_b32`, `v_mbcnt_lo/hi_u32_b32` | not an instruction; these are VOP3-only at 0x364–0x366, which already decode |

Because VOP3 0x100–0x13f reuses the VOP2 table, the same six also decode as VOP3 0x115, 0x117, 0x119 and 0x122–0x124.

Three more VOP2 opcodes have no VOP3 form, but the VOP3 alias path accepts them:

- 0x37 and 0x38 are `v_fmamk_f16` and `v_fmaak_f16`. VOP3 0x137 and 0x138 still decode to `VFmamkF16` and `VFmaakF16`, although a VOP3 encoding has no literal K.
- 0x3c is `v_pk_fmac_f16`, which is VOP2 only.

`isUnsupportedVop3EncodedVop2Alias` already refuses the F32 counterparts (0x20, 0x21, 0x2c, 0x2d) and the VOP2-only dot ops (0x02, 0x0d). This adds 0x37, 0x38 and 0x3c to the same list.

References:
- AMD's machine-readable ISA for RDNA1 and RDNA2 (`amdgpu_isa_rdna1.xml`, `amdgpu_isa_rdna2.xml`) has no VOP2, VOP2-literal or DPP encoding at 0x15, 0x17, 0x19 or 0x22–0x24. It has no VOP3 encoding at 0x115, 0x117, 0x119, 0x122–0x124, 0x137, 0x138 or 0x13c.
- LLVM [`VOP2Instructions.td`](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/f5d74f58b7b2/llvm/lib/Target/AMDGPU/VOP2Instructions.td) defines `V_LSHR_B32`, `V_ASHR_I32`, `V_LSHL_B32` and VOP2 `V_BCNT`/`V_MBCNT` only through `VOP2_Real_gfx6_gfx7` (L2515-2521). gfx10 gets `V_BCNT_U32_B32` and `V_MBCNT_*` as `VOP3Only_Real_gfx10<0x364..0x366>` (L2408-2410). `V_FMAMK_F16` and `V_FMAAK_F16` are `VOP2Only_Real_MADK_gfx10` (L2380-2381), and `V_PK_FMAC_F16` is `VOP2_Real_e32_dpp_dpp8_gfx10` (L2385), with no e64 form.

Changes:
- The six table rows are removed. `VLshlB32`, `VLshrB32` and `VAshrI32` become unreachable, so the enum values, their classification and their translation cases go too.
- The shader disk cache is keyed on the recompiler sources, so renumbering the enum doesn't affect stale cache entries.
- The hand-assembled shaders in `agc_driver_buffer_atomic_csub` and `agc_driver_global_load_addtid` used the gfx6/7 VOP2 encodings of `v_mbcnt_lo/hi_u32_b32 vN, -1, vN` (`0x46......`, `0x48......`). They now use the gfx10 VOP3 encodings (`0xd765000N`/`0xd766000N`, `0x0002..c1`), with no other change to the programs. Both are straight-line, so the two extra words move nothing else.

`agc_vop2_encoding_decode` decodes the valid neighbours: VOP2 `v_lshrrev_b32`, `v_fmamk_f16` with its literal, `v_pk_fmac_f16`, VOP3 `v_lshrrev_b32`, and VOP3 `v_bcnt`/`v_mbcnt` at 0x364–0x366. It also checks that all 15 encodings above are refused.

### Tested

Windows 11 (26200), WinLibs GCC 15.2.0 r7, CI configure flags, main at d70b8998:

- `agc_vop2_encoding_decode` passes. With the 0x22–0x24 rows and the old alias list put back, it fails, reporting VOP2 0x22–0x24 and VOP3 0x122–0x124, 0x137, 0x138 and 0x13c as not refused.
- Full suite on an RTX 4070 Laptop GPU: everything passes. That includes `agc_driver_buffer_atomic_csub` and `agc_driver_global_load_addtid` after the re-encoding; they fail with `VOP2 opcode is not implemented` without it. Both also pass with `--repeat until-fail:3` on an Intel Raptor Lake-S iGPU.
- Intel full suite: `buffer_unaligned_base`, `flat_store`, `sdwa_float_selectors`, `vop1_float_unary`, `vop3_mad_i64` and `vopc_compare` fail on Intel exactly as they do on `main` d70b8998.

Stride-0 `R32_UINT` instance attributes with `NUM_RECORDS=1` and `OOB_SELECT=2` stopped Silent Hill 2 startup with `vertex fetch exceeds descriptor byte range`. This complements #1769 with two Vulkan regressions for that descriptor shape: first instance 0 and 17. They check the nonzero fetched word and the missing components `(0, 0, 1)` for every vertex.

Depends on #1769. Its implementation and original five-case test are included as a prerequisite commit, retaining TideOPL's authorship (original `c17c5ebd4dca4129550076eb4356e81f7df0a1e7`). My contribution is the two additional cases and their TechnicalDebt coverage limits. The branch starts at current main `d70b89989473ba1f6ae13e44e079e67f1f8a44b0`.

Overlap audit, 9 October 2026, at main `f8c2f072`: #2253 changes draw vertex/index ranges to use host imports where safe. It does not implement #1769's zero-stride range and zero-buffer rules or these two scalar regressions. Its conflict with this branch is in `prepareDrawInputs`: a combined implementation must retain the zeroed-attribute branch and `fetchOf` mapping, while using #2253's range handles and import offsets for the remaining attributes. The embedded vertex fetch scanner folded `S_BFE_U32` on constant SGPRs as a plain right shift and ignored the width field. It now calls `scalarBfeU32`, which matches the translator's `sBfeU32`: offset `S1 & 31`, width `(S1 >> 16) & 0x7f` clamped to 32, and 0 when the width is 0.

body:
### What

A program with a single GLC or DLC buffer load or store (28b09d4d) decorates the whole guest `buffers` descriptor array `Coherent`. Every other buffer access in the program is then coherent as well, including the loads the guest made without GLC or DLC. On NVIDIA the SM's L1 cache is not coherent between SMs, and the coherent loads lose it: in a compute program that re-reads a 4 KiB window, one GLC store at the end makes it about 2.7 times slower (Tested). GLC/DLC buffer accesses come from `globallycoherent` buffers and volatile accesses, e.g. decoupled look-back scans (the radix sort behind 28b09d4d) and GPU-driven work queues, and these programs usually read a lot of other buffer data with plain loads.

#### Why the loads without GLC or DLC don't need to be coherent

RDNA does not keep them coherent either. A vector load without GLC or DLC can hit the per-CU L0 and the per-shader-array L1 caches, and neither is coherent between work-groups. The LLVM AMDGPU memory model for GFX10 (https://llvm.org/docs/AMDGPUUsage.html, "Memory Model GFX10-GFX11") describes it:

- "a buffer_gl1_inv is required for coherence between wavefronts executing in different work-groups as they may be executing on different SAs that access different L1s", and a `buffer_gl0_inv` "is also required for coherence between wavefronts executing in different work-groups", and in WGP mode for wavefronts of the same work-group.
- An agent-scope acquiring load is `buffer/global_load glc=1 dlc=1`, `s_waitcnt vmcnt(0)`, then `buffer_gl1_inv; buffer_gl0_inv`, which "Ensures that following loads will not see stale global data".
- On GFX10, GLC and DLC are set on volatile and atomic accesses; a nontemporal load uses `slc=1` only.

So guest code that needs another work-group's data either reads it with GLC/DLC, or invalidates the caches and then reads it with plain loads. Only the second case needs the plain loads to be coherent on the host, and it is visible in the program as a cache invalidation.

#### Change

- The program metadata records whether the program invalidates a cache: `buffer_gl0_inv`, `buffer_gl1_inv`, `s_gl1_inv` and `s_dcache_inv`. They still emit nothing.
- A program with GLC or DLC buffer accesses and no invalidation gets a second descriptor array, `buffers_coherent`, on the same binding as `buffers`, decorated `Coherent`. All buffer arrays of the program are decorated `Aliased`, as `buffers` and `buffers_u64` already are for 64-bit atomics.
- Loads without GLC or DLC read through `buffers`. GLC/DLC loads, every store and the 32-bit atomics go through `buffers_coherent`, so the program's writes stay coherent as before. `buffers_u64` is unchanged and stays `Coherent`.
- A program that invalidates a cache keeps the previous lowering: the whole `buffers` array is `Coherent`.

| Program | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| No GLC/DLC buffer access | `buffers`, not coherent | unchanged |
| GLC/DLC accesses, no cache invalidation | `buffers` `Coherent` for every access | plain loads: `buffers`; GLC/DLC loads, stores, atomics: `buffers_coherent` (`Coherent`, `Aliased`) |
| GLC/DLC accesses and a cache invalidation | `buffers` `Coherent` | unchanged |

Plain loads in programs without GLC or DLC accesses were already incoherent; this treats plain loads in programs with GLC/DLC accesses the same way. The `Volatile` memory operand on GLC/DLC accesses and the BDA path (GPU-selected V#s, `SpirvBdaRead.cpp`) are unchanged.

#### Which GPUs gain

The gain comes from plain loads staying in L1. It was measured on Ada (RTX 4060) only. The CUDA C++ Programming Guide says that on compute capability 5.x and 6.x (Maxwell, Pascal) global loads of data that is not read-only are not cached in L1 by default, so those GPUs may gain less. Other vendors were not measured.

### Tested

Windows 11, MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0 (WinLibs r7), Release, `ANYPS5_ENABLE_SPIRV_TOOLS=ON`, `main` at d70b8998. GPU tests on an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Laptop GPU (591.86, subgroup 32) and on lavapipe (Mesa 26.2.4 for Windows, `GALLIUM_OVERRIDE_CPU_CAPS=avx`).

- New check in `agc_shader_memory` (no GPU needed): four wave32 compute programs that load from one guest buffer and store to another, inspected in the emitted SPIR-V:
  - no GLC: one `buffers` array, not `Coherent`, used by the load and the store;
  - GLC store: `buffers` without `Coherent` and `buffers_coherent` with it, both `Aliased`; the load goes through `buffers` and the store through `buffers_coherent`;
  - GLC load: the load and the store go through `buffers_coherent`;
  - GLC store after `buffer_gl0_inv`: one `buffers` array, `Coherent`, as on `main`.
- Negative checks, each fails the new check:
  - plain loads through the coherent array: `coherent buffers: the two buffer arrays are not decorated Aliased` (`buffers` is then unused and no longer in the module);
  - cache invalidations not recorded: `coherent buffers: a program that invalidates the vector caches does not keep every buffer access coherent`;
  - the previous lowering (no alias): `coherent buffers: a GLC store has no coherent buffer array`.
- Every shader test (`agc_driver_*`, `agc_shader_*`, `agc_spirv_*`, `vector_*`, `agc_masked_select`, `agc_validate_program`, 234 tests):
  - RTX 4060: all pass, 1 skipped (`agc_driver_storage_cache_budget`). This includes `agc_driver_look_back_scan`, a decoupled look-back scan across 4096 work-groups with GLC pair loads, atomics and plain loads and no cache invalidation, which now takes the new lowering (checked in its SPIR-V: plain loads on `buffers`, the GLC loads and stores on `buffers_coherent`).
  - lavapipe: 208 pass, 26 skipped for missing device features (subgroup operations, mesh, DPP, `look_back_scan` among them); all 26 pass on the RTX 4060.
- Full ctest after `cmake --build build` and `--target libs`, serial, `--timeout 120`, RTX 4060: 505 of 511 pass, 2 skipped (`agc_driver_storage_cache_budget`, `guest_video_out_wqhd_detection_no_vulkan`), 4 fail. All four are relinker tests, whose build contains no recompiler sources: `windows_import_modules` (Windows Error Reporting keeps its GUI fixture open, #2227), and `tls_function_coverage`, `windows_gui` and `windows_icon`, which fail to open an executable they just wrote to the temporary directory because Windows Defender removes it (Defender logged the detections during the run).
- Throughput on the RTX 4060, not committed: a wave32 compute program whose 32 lanes read 512 dwords each from a 4 KiB window of one buffer (64 batches of 8 `buffer_load_dword`, L1-resident after the first pass), sum them and write the result with one `buffer_store_dwordx4`; 8192 work-groups, timed per dispatch including submit and wait, best of 8 dispatches. All variants run in one process, in a rotated order each round, because the laptop's clocks change by up to 4x over a few seconds and separate runs could not be compared. A `buffer_gl0_inv` at the start selects the previous lowering for the same program (the instruction itself emits nothing), so the last column is what `main` does for this program:

  | Round | No GLC | No GLC, `buffer_gl0_inv` | GLC store (this PR) | GLC store, `buffer_gl0_inv` (`main`) |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 1 | 1.11 ms | 1.13 ms | 1.26 ms | 3.09 ms |
  | 2 | 2.78 ms | 1.26 ms | 1.14 ms | 3.13 ms |
  | 3 | 6.01 ms | 6.87 ms | 4.85 ms | 17.44 ms |
  | 4 | 4.80 ms | 6.92 ms | 7.58 ms | 12.59 ms |
  | 5 | 6.88 ms | 7.03 ms | 7.36 ms | 20.98 ms |
  | 6 | 3.48 ms | 1.33 ms | 3.64 ms | 17.36 ms |

  The previous lowering is the slowest variant in every round, 1.7 to 4.8 times the GLC store with this change (2.7 times in the best rounds: 3.09 ms against 1.14 ms); with the change, the GLC program runs about as fast as the program without GLC. All variants produce the same output (same checksum). An earlier in-process run with a temporary switch that dropped the `Volatile` memory operand from the GLC store showed no measurable difference, with either lowering; the difference is the `Coherent` decoration on the loads.

body:
### What

Fresh shader registrations hold the process-wide preparation writer lock throughout decoding, front-end work, cache lookup and SPIR-V preparation. Independent registration threads therefore wait for one another before they can publish anything, contributing to the startup contention reported in #2292.

Prepare each private shader snapshot before acquiring the writer lock. The transaction still exists from function entry, so a caught preparation failure aborts an enclosing transaction. Default transactions and every shared-state operation still acquire the writer lock. Publication acquires it before the driver mutex and retains the existing identity recheck, preserving already prepared ABIs when identical registrations race.

This addresses the registration lock scope in #2292. It complements #2327's removal of a redundant Structurize precheck. Linked ABI resolution and null-pixel preparation retain their existing locking behavior. No instruction semantics or cache format changes.

### Tested

- Native Ubuntu 24.04, x86-64, GCC 13.3, CMake 3.28.3, Mesa 25.2.8 lavapipe, on locally managed self-hosted runners.
- Seven focused preparation/publication tests passed. The new concurrency test takes approximately 0.44 seconds with the disk shader cache disabled. It checks deferred shared-state locking, translation reaching its expected rejection while another writer is held, nested rollback, and eight simultaneous registrations of four cold compute configurations followed by dispatch.
- Negative control: restoring the old eager registration lock makes the new progress assertion fail; restoring the patch passes.
- Full Release build and patched libraries succeeded at final head `26a670a7`: 517 tests, 490 passed, 26 capability skips, one failure. `agc_driver_flat_store` timed out at 30.05 seconds with the same fence-wait output already reproduced on unmodified `d70b8998`; it remains enabled and its timeout is unchanged. The new concurrency test passed in 0.44 seconds.
- `python3 tools/check_conventions.py --base origin/main` passed.

No affected retail title, physical GPU or Windows runtime was tested. This does not establish a title-level startup speedup or resolve all of #2292's remaining front-end costs.

body:
### What

Fixes #2296.

On Windows, `_wstat64`/`_fstat64` report `st_ino` 0, and `st_dev` is the drive number from `stat` but 0 from `fstat`. So the guest `st_dev`/`st_ino` identity check matched every pair of files from `stat` and never matched across `stat` and `fstat`.

`NativeStat.cpp` now takes the identity from the file's handle with `GetFileInformationByHandle`, the same way for path and descriptor `stat`:

- `st_dev` = `dwVolumeSerialNumber`
- `st_ino` = the 64-bit file index folded into the guest's 32-bit `ino_t` (low ^ high)
- `st_nlink` = `nNumberOfLinks`

Path `stat` opens the file with `FILE_READ_ATTRIBUTES` and `FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS` (so directories work too) and full sharing. Descriptor `stat` uses `_get_osfhandle`. body:
### What

`sceKernelAprSubmitCommandBuffer` returned `EINVAL` for any buffer object that `sceAmprAprCommandBufferConstructor` had not tagged with `BufferType::Apr`. That tag is AnyPS5's own. In the retail object, as [ampr_emu](https://github.com/drakmor/ampr_emu) lays it out, the type word only holds state bits (gather/scatter valid, map active). The `CommandBuffer` constructor writes 0 there and the `AprCommandBuffer` constructor only zeroes the map and gather/scatter state. So a zero-filled object that was bound with `SetBuffer` is a valid APR buffer, and ampr_emu's submit does not check the type.

CRI's file system, as linked into Sonic Origins (PPSA05324), relies on this. It lays out its 0x28-byte `AprCommandBuffer` objects in its own zeroed work memory and never calls either constructor: it only calls `SetBuffer`, `Reset` and the record functions. Its first read is a `ReadFile`, a `WriteAddress` and a `WriteKernelEventQueue`, submitted with priority 1. That submit returned `0x80020016`, CRI logged `FS:Failed in submitCommandBuffer` and stopped. No movie was ever opened, and the title stayed on a white screen after the SEGA logo (#2021).

The submit now only rejects a null buffer. `sceAmprAprCommandBufferConstructor` still sets the tag, and `sceAmprCommandBufferGetType` still returns it. ampr_emu returns 0 there, but that is a separate change.

### Tested

Ubuntu 26.04, GCC 15.2, Release build, AMD Radeon R9 380 (RADV, Mesa 26.0.8).

- `guest_ampr_markers` passes. The new check builds a buffer object as CRI does: zero-filled, no constructor, `SetBuffer` and `Reset`. It then records a `ReadFile`, a completion write and an AMPR event, and submits with priority 1. It checks the read data, the written value and the event on the queue. Without the change it fails at the submit (`GuestAmpr.cpp:542`).
- `guest_equeue_events` passes.
- Sonic Origins (PPSA05324), on the testing branch from #2021 with this change, at 960x540 (`--res_x=960 --res_y=540`):
  - CRI reads `raw/movie/sonicteam_logo_4k.usm` and the H.264 decoder is created (`[videodec2] decoder 1: codec=1 max 3840x2160`).
  - The Sonic Team logo movie plays, followed by the Retro Engine, Headcannon and CRIWARE logos and the auto-save notice.
  - Without the change, the same build stays white after the SEGA logo.
- `tools/check_conventions.py --base origin/main` and `git diff --check` pass.

Guest programs import `rewind` from `libSceLibcInternal` (#1578). libc now implements it the way FreeBSD does: seek to the start of the stream, drop a pushed-back character, and clear the end-of-file and error indicators. `fseek` to the start leaves a guest encoding error set, so `rewind` clears that afterwards. body:
### What

Fixes #1635.

In `SCE_AVPLAYER_AV_SYNC_MODE_NONE`, `takeVideo` hands out every decoded frame in order. A title that requests video slower than the film's frame rate (PPSA12544 requests 7-19 frames per second for a 30 fps cinematic) therefore falls further behind its audio on every call.

While the title pulls audio (`audioDriving`), no-sync mode now skips queued frames of the current epoch that the audio clock has already passed. This reuses the loop that sync mode already runs. Frames that are not late are handed out as before; no-sync mode still never refuses a frame for being early, and nothing changes when no audio is pulled or at a trick speed. Whether the console hands out every frame in this mode is unknown, so the behaviour is recorded under Functional in `TechnicalDebt.md`.

`TestUnsyncedVideoKeepsUpWithAudio` reproduces the issue in miniature: no-sync mode, audio pulled in real time, about 15 video requests per second for the 30 fps test movie, and it checks that video stays within 150 ms of the audio.

@awake-devel the issue's open question (whether the title requests several frames per game frame when behind) is not settled by this change. If you can, a run of PPSA12544 on this branch would confirm it on the title.

### Tested

Fedora 44 host, build and run inside an Ubuntu 24.04 container (GCC 13, as CI), `guest_avplayer_tests` only:

| | worst video lag behind audio | test |
|---|---|---|
| `main` | 442-475 ms (3 runs) | fails |
| this branch | 30 ms (4 parallel runs) | passes 5/5 |

`python3 tools/check_conventions.py --base upstream/main` passes. Not tested on a title or on Windows.

body:
### What

`template.s` allocated a fixed 4 KiB group segment, so a body with LDS immediates past it could not be measured. `--lds BYTES` (Python `lds=`) now sets the group segment size, 0 to 64 KiB, with 4096 as the default; `oracle.c` already reads the size from the kernel descriptor. `HW_ORACLE.md` documents the option and, next to `extra`, the way to feed a kernel more than 4 input dwords per lane: the rest go in `extra` and the body loads them from `s[4:5] + 16 * rows`.

With that, the five execution-test kernels the float-mode audit in #981 could not run (four needing more than 4 KiB of LDS, two needing 6 or 8 inputs per lane) run on the oracle. Measured on RDNA2 (gfx1036, a Ryzen 7 7700X iGPU, not the PS5's gfx1013), `--ieee 0 --dx10-clamp 1 --denorm32 0 --denorm16 3 --round32 0 --round16 0 --fp16-overflow 0`:

| Kernel | Oracle run | Cells | Result |
|---|---|---:|---|
| `LdsReadWrite.cpp` `Wave64Code` | words 5-317 on the 64 `Rows`, `--wave64 --lds 8192`, 4 parts of 16 columns | 3712 | equals `Expected64` |
| `LdsAddtid.cpp` `Wave64Code` | words 5-246, same, 3 parts | 2304 | equals `Expected64` |
| `LdsIntegerAtomics.cpp` `Wave64Code` | words 5-215, same, 3 parts | 2816 | equals `Expected64` |
| `DsWrxchg2B64.cpp` `Code` | words 12-23 with the 8 `Fill()` dwords per lane from `extra`, `--lds 12288` | 512 | satisfies `Check()` |
| `LdsAtomics64.cpp` `Code` | words 19-245 with `a`, `b` in the rows and `c` from `extra`, `--lds 8976`, 8 parts | 1696 + contention | satisfies `CheckLanes()` and `CheckContention()`; identical at `--ieee 1` |

The three wave64 kernels run with `--lds 4096` differ from `Expected64` in 1198, 1042 and 1219 cells, and a second `--lds 8192` run reproduced every value. So the five kernels' pinned or computed expectations hold on a second RDNA2 part, and the audit's per-mode coverage now reaches every ALU and LDS kernel but the two whose opcodes have no gfx103x encoding.

Raw data (bodies, rows, extra inputs and the output registers): https://gist.github.com/snoozedDev/51eb44c9c3f2ea1e0a41d34913a4f4fe

body:
### What

#1959 moves the switch over every buffer format into one function per resource when the descriptor is prepared. It keeps the inline switch for GPU-selected descriptors (`memory.gpuDescriptor`). For those, every `buffer_load_format_*` / `buffer_store_format_*` still emits all 77 cases inline, and each case inlines the address computation, bounds checks and BDA reads of `formatted()`.

A title with about 300 such accesses in one compute program (Ghost of Yōtei, PPSA26344, 0x8000289300, 102 guest blocks) compiles to 37.1M SPIR-V words: 292 `OpSwitch`es, about 700k blocks, 287 distinct block shapes. Each pipeline takes 40 s or more to create on NVIDIA, and each shader disk-cache entry is up to ~300 MB. This is probably also the 13.4M-word module reported on #1183.

- `formattedGpuCall` emits one `DontInline` SPIR-V function per component count, direction, d16, coherence, kind and stop mode, and runs `formatSwitch` inside it.
  - It takes the descriptor fields (base, records, stride, word 3, swizzle, valid), the index, offset, soffset and the access's PC. Each access is one call.
- When BDA faults stop invocations, the function returns `{value, stopped}` (just `stopped` for a store). Inside it, a stop returns that through `bdaStopValue`, as `read_bda_span` does. The caller calls `StopBdaInvocationIf` on the flag, so the pixel-shader interlock and `OpKill` handling stay in the entry function.
- `BdaInstructionPc` returns the instruction's PC, or the PC parameter inside the shared function (`SpirvEmitterState::bdaPcOverride`). The BDA read, write, store, atomic and overflow paths use it, so a fault records the PC of the access that faulted.

### Tested

Windows 11, MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0, RTX 4090 (driver 617.42).

- `agc_formatted_buffer_once` gains a GPU-selected case: dword 3 of the V# comes from `v_readfirstlane_b32 s11, v0`.
  - It checks that two more loads add calls but no function, no switch and less than 10% words.
  - It fails on #1959 alone ("2 more format switches") and passes with this change.
- Full ctest: 506/506 passed.
- Ghost of Yōtei, same tree before and after:
  - 0x8000289300 goes from 37,110,613 to 1,447,831 words, and its recompile from 7.2 s to 0.25 s.
  - 0x800036e100 goes from 818,855 to 260,672 words; its pipeline now takes 2.4 s.
  - The average disk-cache entry drops below 1 MB.
  - The title reaches its first presented frames (the SIE intro card). Before, a 25-minute run was still creating the second and third 37M-word pipelines.

body:
### What

A compute program of PPSA26344 (Ghost of Yōtei) writes a 1D storage image (T# type 8, `80000fac`) with `image_store` DIM 2D. No runtime image mode matched the descriptor:

```
image descriptor is incompatible with the static runtime image interface
```

`RuntimeImageModes` offers a 3D mode for a 2D access and plain modes for array accesses. For a 2D access on a 1D T# it offered nothing.

- `RuntimeImageModes`: a 2D storage image that is only written (not read, not atomic, not `image_store_mip`, not packed, BY or depth) gets a 1D mode for each of its numeric modes. The emitter already builds the coordinate from the components the mode's dimension uses, so the store addresses texel x.
- `EmitWriteOp`: a DIM 2D store through the 1D mode is dropped when y is not 0, as a one-texel-high image bounds it. This mirrors what was measured for 3D loads through 2D T#s in #2023: a load at z ≠ 0 returns zeros. The 1D case is not measured, so it is listed in TechnicalDebt.
- Loads, atomics and `image_store_mip` through a 1D T# with DIM 2D still throw, as before. Mip stores are left out because their LOD is taken from the address component after the coordinates, which would move.

Related: #2133 and #2140 add 2D modes for 3D accesses (a 2D T# under DIM 3D). This is the same situation one dimension down, for stores, and doesn't overlap their changes.

### Tested

Windows 11, MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0, RTX 4090 (driver 617.42).

- New execution test `agc_driver_image_store_line_through_plane`:
  - 32 lanes run two DIM 2D `image_store`s into a 32-texel 1D T#: x = tid with y = 0 and dmask 0xF, then y = 1 with dmask 0x5. This is done for 32_SINT and 32_32_32_32_SINT.
  - Every texel must hold the y = 0 values, and the bytes past the texture must be untouched.
  - A read-only DIM 2D `image_load` through the 1D T# is still refused.
  - Without the y ≠ 0 check the test fails: the y = 1 store rewrites texel x, and component 1 reads 0. Without the 1D mode it fails with "image descriptor is incompatible with the static runtime image interface".
- Full ctest: 508/508 passed.

body:
### What

A typed sampled-image heap holds `SampledHeapCapacity` = 16 images. A compute program of PPSA26344 (Ghost of Yōtei) binds 29 sampled 3D images of one class, and the shader fails with:

```
ShaderRecompiler::Recompile: shader image heap capacity exceeded
```

`SampledHeapCapacity` goes to 32. Heap arrays are declared with their compact length (`binding.count`), and the capacity enters neither `ShaderData` nor the runtime ABI structs, so every shader that fitted before gets the same layout and SPIR-V. `Version` is unchanged.

`ResourceMaterializer::BindlessSlots()` returned the same constant. It sizes the bindless image tables, and each table takes `slots - 1` extra image entries against `ShaderInfo::MaxImages`, so tying it to the heap would double their cost. It now returns `BindlessTableSlots` = 16, the previous value.

Related open PRs: #2141 raises the sampler heap to 32, and #2282 raises the storage heap to 16 (splitting out `StorageMipSlots`). Neither touches the sampled heap, and none of the three conflict beyond adjacent lines in `RuntimeAbi.hpp`.

### Tested

Windows 11, MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0, RTX 4090 (driver 617.42).

- `agc_shader_device_profile`:
  - A sampled heap now holds 32 images of one class, and bindless tables keep 16 slots.
  - With `SampledHeapCapacity` = 16 the new check fails with "shader image heap capacity exceeded".
- Full ctest: 507/507 passed (one test skipped without Vulkan).
- PPSA26344 on an integration branch: the program above dispatches, and the title reaches its first presented frames. That also needed other changes, listed in discussion #675.

body:
### What

On FreeBSD, `unlink` (and so `remove`) ignores the file's own permission bits: what matters is write access to the directory. A guest that does `chmod(path, 0400)` and later `remove(path)` therefore succeeds on the console.

On Windows, the guest `chmod` (`_wchmod`) sets `FILE_ATTRIBUTE_READONLY` when the write bit is cleared. `DeleteFileW` then fails with `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED`, so `remove` returned -1 with `EACCES`, and the file stayed.

When deletion fails with `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED` and the entry carries `FILE_ATTRIBUTE_READONLY`, `remove` now clears the attribute and retries. If the retry fails too (e.g. the file is open without delete sharing), it restores the original attributes and reports the retry's error, so a failed `remove` leaves the file as it was. Linux is unchanged.

### Tested

Windows 11, WinLibs GCC 15.2.0 r7, Release, `-DBUILD_TESTING=ON`:

- `guest_filesystem`: a file made read-only with `sceKernelChmod(0400)` is removed by `remove`, and no longer exists.
  - On `main` it fails at that line with guest errno 13.
  - With the fix it passes. On Linux the case already held, and it still does.
- Probed separately on the fixed build:
  - a read-only file held open by another handle: `remove` fails (`EBUSY`), the file stays, and `FILE_ATTRIBUTE_READONLY` is restored;
  - guest `chmod` never sets the attribute on directories, so directory removal is unaffected.
- `ctest -E "^agc_|video_out"`: 249/249.
- `tools/check_conventions.py` passes, and `tools/pr_overlap.py --branch` reports no overlap. It also merges cleanly with the open PRs that touch `GuestFilesystem.cpp` and `Filesystem.cpp`: #1192, #1620, #1624, #1628, #1755, #1764, #1777, #2086, #2115, #2129, #2170, #2260, #2289 and #2300.

`sceKernelUnlink`/`unlink` in libkernel likely behave the same way on Windows. They are left for a separate PR, because #2289 changes that function.

A Linux and Windows full build will be posted here once it has run.

body:
### What

The entry stubs call the title's entry with `rbp` = 0: on Linux as the process starts, on Windows as the argument loop (`dec ebp`) leaves it. The title's start code pushes `rbp`, so the frame-pointer chain of its main thread ends in a null frame pointer.

Unreal Engine walks that chain to capture a call stack (for a fatal error or an ensure). It stops at a return address of 0, but it reads `[rbp + 8]` of each saved frame pointer first, so a null link makes it read address 8 and crash. On the console the chain ends in a frame record whose return address is 0.

- Linux: the stub pushes a zero frame record (saved `rbp` 0, return address 0) and points `rbp` at it before `call`. Two 8-byte pushes keep the 16-byte alignment at the call.
- Windows: the stub writes the record into unused slots of its own frame (`rsp+0x40`, `rsp+0x48`; it uses `0x20`-`0x3c` and `0x58`-`0x5c`) and points `rbp` at it before calling the entry.

### Tested

Linux (Ubuntu 24.04, GCC 13.3), RX 7600.

- New `entry_stub` test: the Linux stub passes the initial stack pointer, aligns, pushes the zero record, points `rbp` at it, clears `rsi`, calls the entry and ends with `ud2`.
- Full `ctest` 517/517. `tools/check_conventions.py` and `tools/check_test_registration.py` pass.
- Disney Epic Mickey: Rebrushed (PPSA15657, UE4), on its testing stack (#2255):
  - Before: in about half of its runs the title screen ends in a SIGSEGV with no message. gdb stops in Unreal's stack walk at eboot `0x186cfbf`, `mov 0x8(%rdx),%rax` with `rdx` = 0, after following the chain to the stub's `rbp`.
  - After: the same walk ends at the stub's record (a gdb walk of the chain shows 24 frames, then `saved=0 ret=0`), so Unreal reports its own error instead of crashing in the walk. Here that is `LowLevelFatalError ... RemoveFromOuterMap NumRemoved = 0`, a separate problem.
- The Windows stub change is covered by the build and the existing Windows stub tests only; it was not run on Windows.

Guest threads started by `RunThread` call their entry from host frames too. That needs a trampoline with unwind information and is left for a separate change.

Overlaps #2097, which changes the same function's call encoding: its new test helper reads the call at `entry + 10`, and with this change the call is at `entry + 17`. Whichever lands second needs that offset updated.

body:
### What

#1362 reads `INT_SEL` from `packet[2]` before it checks that the packet is a `RELEASE_MEM` (opcode `0x49`). `preparePacketMemory` runs for every PM4 packet, so packets shorter than three dwords are read past their end. Release builds don't show it, but it is undefined behaviour, and builds with `_GLIBCXX_ASSERTIONS` abort on the `std::span` bounds check. GCC 15 turns those assertions on in every unoptimized build, so a Debug build also aborts.

This PR reads `packet[2]` only for `RELEASE_MEM`. For `RELEASE_MEM` packets the result is the same as before.

### Tested

Windows 11, AMD Radeon 860M, MinGW GCC 15.2. Clean build with `-DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS=-D_GLIBCXX_ASSERTIONS`:

| | `agc_driver` | `agc_driver_pm4` |
|---|---|---|
| `main` d70b8998 | aborts: `std::span::operator[]` assertion in `Driver::preparePacketMemory` | aborts, same place |
| this PR | passes | passes |

Bisecting with that build points to b25c6cce, the merge commit of #1362: its parent d026063a passes.

A normal Release build passes both tests before and after the change. Fork CI (Release, Linux and Windows): green ([run](https://github.com/LeandroLP23/AnyPS5/actions/runs/37950873010)).

body:
### What

`SCE_NGS2_VOICE_PARAM_MATRIX_LEVELS` and the matrix levels command of `sceNgs2VoiceRunCommands` stored levels as given. Now:

- levels are clamped to -4..4, so a level of 8 no longer plays twice as loud as on the console; NaN is kept, as the library keeps it;
- a level count of 0 throws instead of emptying the matrix. The library rejects that count and keeps the matrix, but its PS5 error code is unknown.

TechnicalDebt records that this comes from the PS4 library.

### Reference

- **PS4 firmware 11.00 `libSceNgs2.sprx`**, dumped and decrypted from a console. It was loaded on Windows with a small test loader and driven through `sceNgs2VoiceControl`; neither the loader nor the library is part of this PR. In-range, out-of-range, infinite and NaN levels were set and read back from its rendered output, and a count of 0 was rejected with the matrix unchanged.
- `sceNgs2VoiceRunCommands` is not in the PS4 library, so its matrix levels command is assumed to clamp the same way.
- **PS5 firmware 10.06 `libSceNgs2.sprx`**: its readable ELF headers match the PS4 library (3,460-byte `.eh_frame_hdr`, 431 functions). A decrypted PS5 SELF was not used; anyone with a decrypted PS5 `libSceNgs2.sprx` can help confirm this.

### Tested

- Windows 11, WinLibs GCC 15.2.0 r7, Release.
- `ngs2_render` `TestMatrixLevelClamp` renders a mono sampler through matrix 0, set both by voice param and by command: ±4, 4.0001, -4.5, ±100 and ±infinity render as ±4 would, 3.5 and -0.25 pass unchanged, NaN stays NaN, and a count of 0 throws.
- With `main`'s `Voice.cpp` the test fails. Four mutations each make it fail: no clamp, no upper bound, a bound of 8, and accepting a count of 0.
- Full ctest merged with `main` d70b8998, together with #959, #964 and #2336: 507/507.
- #964 treats an empty matrix as unset. With this PR a count of 0 can no longer empty a matrix.
- Linux not tested.

body:
> Replaces #960, which was closed pending a reference. The reverb now follows the PS4 firmware 11.00 `libSceNgs2.sprx`, read from its code and checked against its output (see the reference section). #1384 is a draft with an approximate reverb that is waiting for the same kind of reference.

### What

`sceNgs2RackCreate` throws for rack id `0x2001` (reverb). This adds the rack, with the reverb the console library renders.

- **Options:** `SceNgs2ReverbRackOption` (rack option, `max_channels`, `reverb_size`). The defaults come from KytyPS5: 8 channels and `reverb_size` 1.
- **Voice params:**
  - `0x20010000` setup takes input and output channel counts and flags. It accepts 1, 2, 6 or 8 channels; other counts are invalid arguments. Non-zero flags and differing input and output counts throw.
  - `0x20010001` takes `SceNgs2ReverbI3DL2Param` (88 bytes). The layout of both params, and of the voice state, matches shadPS4's `ngs2_reverb.h`. Values are clamped to the library's ranges, as it does; NaN throws.
  - `sceNgs2VoiceGetState` returns the common voice state.
- **Rendering**, as in the library:
  - The input is mixed to mono with the library's fixed gains (0.707 for stereo, 0.316 for 5.1, 0.267 for 7.1), without the LFE channel.
  - A 14400-sample buffer feeds four reflection taps placed by the reflection pattern tables (16 patterns), plus a late feed.
  - Sixteen damped comb filters with a pre-emphasis stage; their lengths follow `density`.
  - Each output channel takes a signed selection of the combs, then runs four allpasses driven by `diffusion`.
  - A two-pole room HF filter at `hf_reference`, then the wet and dry levels. The LFE channel passes dry.
  - New params crossfade over one grain, and wet and dry levels ramp. Until the title sends I3DL2 params, the setup defaults leave the wet output almost silent.
- **The points the PR was closed for:**
  - The Freeverb-style approximation is gone.
  - `density` and `reflection_pattern` are used.
  - Before any I3DL2 param, the voice renders the library's setup defaults; it no longer passes its input through.
  - Only the default `reverb_size` of 1 is handled, with its 14400-sample buffer; other sizes throw.
- **Not implemented:** the library's half-rate mode, channel conversion, and system sample rates below about 7.5 kHz, where an allpass would have no samples. All three throw, and TechnicalDebt records them.

### Reference

- **PS4 firmware 11.00 `libSceNgs2.sprx`**, dumped and decrypted from a console. It was loaded on Windows with a small test loader and called directly; neither the loader nor the library is part of this PR. The reverb was read from its disassembly, and the test values are its output.
- Against that library, the output matches to float rounding (110 to 180 dB SNR). That covers presets, every reflection pattern, short and long delays, 1, 2, 6 and 8 channels, noise input, 11.025 to 48 kHz and parameter changes during playback.
- **PS5 firmware 10.06 `libSceNgs2.sprx`** (the module titles import as `libSceNgs2`): its readable ELF headers match the PS4 library: the same `.eh_frame_hdr` size (3,460 bytes, 431 functions) and code plus read-only data within 1% (321,328 bytes against 323,432). A decrypted PS5 SELF was not used; anyone with a decrypted PS5 `libSceNgs2.sprx` can help confirm this.
- **A PS5 recording of Animal Well** (a public walkthrough): the decay of its jump sound, averaged over 382 jumps there and 72 here, matches within about 0.5 dB for the first 120 ms. Later the background music covers the tail, so that part couldn't be compared.

### Tested

- Windows 11, WinLibs GCC 15.2.0 r7, Release.
- `ngs2_render` `TestReverb` uses 8 cases with the PS4 library's output, to 2e-7 + 1e-5 of each value:
  - the "cave" preset Animal Well uses;
  - a damped room;
  - 5.1;
  - a parameter change mid-stream;
  - clamped values;
  - short delays with pattern 15;
  - noise input with a change;
  - a density change.

  Channel 3 is skipped: the PS4 mastering voice low-passes the LFE channel, and AnyPS5's doesn't yet.
- `TestReverbSetup`: 3, 4, 5 and 7 channels are rejected; channel conversion, flags and NaN throw; the setup defaults render a non-zero level below 1e-8; rendering at 7000 Hz throws, and rack options with `reverb_size` 0 or 2 throw.
- On `main` the tests fail, because rack 0x2001 throws. 25 mutations of `Reverb.cpp`, and removing either new throw, each make them fail.
- Full ctest merged with `main` d70b8998, together with #959, #964 and #2337: 507/507.
- Seen in PPSA22520 (Animal Well): it creates the rack with default options, sets up a 2-in, 2-out voice, loads I3DL2 preset 9 ("cave" in the standard preset order) and patches it to its mastering voice. Played with #959 and #964 on `main`: the jump reverb is the one compared with the PS5 recording above, the game runs at 59 FPS, and there are no NGS2 errors.
- Linux not tested.

body:
### What

The guest passes and expects UTF-8 path names. On Windows, though, `opendir`/`readdir` in `Directory.cpp` used MinGW's narrow dirent API (`opendir`, `readdir`), which works in the ANSI code page. The result:

- `opendir` failed for a directory whose UTF-8 name contains characters outside the code page (e.g. `セーブ` on a Western code page).
- `readdir` returned entry names as ANSI bytes rather than UTF-8. A character the code page lacks came back as `?`, so the guest could not open the entry it had just listed.

On Windows the directory is now opened with `_wopendir` and read with `_wreaddir` (`_wclosedir`/`_wrewinddir` for the rest), and each name is converted to UTF-8 with `std::filesystem::path::u8string()`. Linux keeps `DIR`/`readdir`, since its names are already bytes.

This is the directory half of #2329. The `fopen`/`freopen` half is left out on purpose, because #1549, #2033 and #2170 already touch that line.

### Tested

Windows 11, WinLibs GCC 15.2.0 r7, Release, `-DBUILD_TESTING=ON`:

- `GuestDirectory.cpp` has a new case. It creates `セーブ/été.txt`, opens the directory with `opendir` using its UTF-8 path, and requires that `readdir` return `été.txt` in UTF-8 with type `DT_REG`, plus `.` and `..`.
  - On `main` it fails: `opendir` returns null.
  - With the fix it passes.
- `ctest -E "^agc_|video_out"`: 249/249.

### What
Implements `collate<wchar_t>::_Getcat`
(`_ZNSt7collateIwE7_GetcatEPPKNSt6locale5facetEPKS1__nid_postfix`) in `libc`:
- Implements the wide-character collation facet `collate<wchar_t>` for the classic C locale.

body:
### What
At `unused-filter=1` the CFG followed only direct branches and `call/jmp [rip+slot]` through RELATIVE-relocated slots. Code reached through a register (`lea reg, [rip+f]; call reg`, vtables and callback tables, switch jump tables) was unreachable, and imports used only there were removed. GOT accesses were counted only for `mov` loads and `call/jmp [rip+slot]`.

The CFG now also walks RELATIVE relocation targets in text, RIP-relative `lea` targets, and int32 jump tables at a `lea`'d data address, using the strict filter's walk moved to `ReadRelativeTableTargets`. Any RIP-relative operand that names a GOT slot counts as an access. Address-taken targets are walked after the direct control flow. A target that does not decode is not code and ends that path, so a stray table entry cannot abort the conversion. Strict filter behaviour is unchanged.

Absolute immediates (`mov r, imm`, `push imm`) and raw data words pointing into text are still not roots at level 1.

Changes the same files as #2238 (LEA roots for the Windows TLS collector) and #2304 (CFG decoding performance), with a different scope.

### Tested
macOS arm64, relinker-only Release build: ctest 39/39, `strict_nid_filter` unchanged. `test_unused_filter_indirect.py` covers lea + call reg, a RELATIVE pointer called through a register, a jump-table case block, GOT access by lea/push/cmp, two unreachable controls, and two address-taken targets on undecodable bytes. On main the six indirect cases report `CFG/GOT filtering: 1 -> 0`. No title was converted from a retail dump.

Linux (Ubuntu 24.04, GCC 13.3), relinker-only Release build: ctest 44/44.

Also converted 43 open-source titles from the [PS5 homebrew catalog](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-homebrew-catalog) (eboot.bin and bundled libc.prx, unwrapped from fSELF) with main and with this branch, for Linux and Windows at unused-filter 0, 1 and 2. No conversion changed outcome. At unused-filter=1, all 38 titles that convert keep more imports, 1 to 283 each (5,812 in total), on both outputs; none keeps fewer.

Runtime check on Linux (Ryzen 9 9950X, RTX 3090, NVIDIA 595.99.02) with DOOM PPSA99666 v1.1.1 from the catalog. Both trees relink it with `--registry unused-filter=1` and run the title's own `test/console-play.cfg` without its `serve` line: it starts `doom1.wad`, plays and exits at frame 900. Both trees carry #1529, without which the bundled `libc.prx` shim takes DOOM's libc imports on Linux (#1497); this PR does not depend on it.

| Relinker | Imports kept | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `main` d70b8998 + #1529 | 110 of 171 | SIGSEGV after `HU_Init`, before the first frame (2 of 2 runs) |
| this branch + #1529 | 171 of 171 | Plays to frame 900 and exits 0 (2 of 2 runs) |

On `main` the crash is a call to address 0 in the audio thread. Its start routine is referenced only by the `lea` that passes it to `pthread_create`, so level 1 drops `sceAudioOutOutput`, which the thread loads with `mov <GOT>, %r14` and calls through `%r14`. The other 59 dropped imports include ones used by the download worker and upload server threads (`sceHttp*`, `accept`), the on-screen keyboard (`sceImeDialog*`) and music (`log10`). At levels 0 and 2 both trees produce the same executable. #2238 and #2304, built the same way, produce a level-1 executable byte-identical to `main`'s.

### What
`extractRela` turned every non-RELATIVE relocation into a NID import named after its symbol without reading `st_shndx`. A GLOB_DAT or R_X86_64_64 relocation against a symbol the image defines became an undefined import that no system library provides.

These relocations are now emitted as RELATIVE relocations to `st_value + addend`, the image's own definition, for Linux and Windows output. JUMP_SLOT, TLS, IFUNC, SHN_ABS/SHN_COMMON and other relocation types against defined symbols throw. JUMP_SLOT is rejected because the PLT slot indexing has no clean rewrite. The symbol read is bounds-checked against the whole 24-byte entry.

The unused NID filters take pointers only from RELATIVE relocations in the input. When relocations against defined symbols are present, `unused-filter=1` skips CFG/GOT filtering, as it does for multiple executable segments, and `unused-filter=2` fails.

No PS5 sample with such relocations was available. Changes the symbol bounds check line that #1272 also changes.

body:
### What
`WindowsMappings::Collect` (behind `GuestArenaCollectWrites_nid_postfix`) resets each part of a range as it walks it when `clear` is set. It marks a shared view's page seen and re-arms its aliases, and it calls `GetWriteWatch` with `WRITE_WATCH_FLAG_RESET` on private memory. When it then reaches a `PAGE_NOACCESS` view, or memory that isn't committed private memory, it returns `false`. By then the parts before that point are already reset.

The callers treat `false` as "this range can't be tracked" and fall back, for example to collecting the pieces separately. But the writes to the reset parts are gone, so the fallback no longer sees them. `walkWrites` documents the failure ("Uncommitted pages inside the range make the call fail; such ranges are compared instead") but not the lost writes. Today's callers mostly collect exactly one allocation, which avoids it. I hit it while trying to collect several nearby heap mirrors in one walk: a span with an uncommitted page in the middle lost the writes before the hole.

With `clear`, `Collect` now checks the whole range first, with the same tests the walk uses (no `PAGE_NOACCESS` view, private memory committed), and returns `false` before resetting anything. A collect without `clear` resets nothing and is unchanged. The walk itself is unchanged.

Test (`guest_memory`, Windows), `CheckFailedCollectKeepsWrites`:
- Private arena memory, committed / uncommitted / committed. After a write to the first page, a resetting collect over all three returns `false`, and a collect of the first page alone still reports the written page.
- A two-page shared direct-memory mapping whose second page is mprotected to no access: same check, with the shared view's four 4 KiB pages reported afterwards.
- Both fail without the change (the later collect reports nothing).

### Tested
Windows 11 Pro (26200), MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0 (WinLibs r7), Release, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti (driver 610.88).

- Full local suite: 507 tests, 504 passed, 1 skipped. `guest_sce_net` timed out (it times out locally on unrelated branches too, likely my network filtering), and `audio_out2_timing` failed once in the parallel run but passed 3 of 3 runs alone. It was run from the generated `CTestTestfile.cmake` commands because antivirus blocks `ctest.exe` on this machine.
- `tools/check_conventions.py --base origin/main` passes.

The Linux path (`GuestWriteWatch::Collect`) isn't touched. Not tested on Linux or macOS.

#2054 also changes `Collect`'s private-memory branch. `WindowsMappings.hpp` merges cleanly with it; the conflicts are adjacent additions in `tests/GuestMemory.cpp` and `TechnicalDebt.md`. I'll rebase onto whichever lands first.

body:
### What

`PrepareRegistered` decodes the shader, builds its control-flow graph and structurizes it, then throws the graph away. Next, `ShaderRecompiler::PrepareShader` → `PrepareResourceProgram` decodes, builds and structurizes the same code again with the same `SwappcInfo`. Every registered shader therefore goes through `GraphBuilder::Build` + `Structurizer::Structurize` once more than needed. mrk1987 counted three `Structurize` passes per shader on #2105; this removes one of them.

The removed pass only did one thing: throw early. Any exception it raised is raised again from `PrepareShader` for the same code, so a shader that failed registration before still fails it, with the same message.

No title stops on this; it is a load-time cost. On `main` the registration path runs for every shader a title registers, so I measured it on a title that registers many.

### Tested

Linux (CachyOS, GCC, Release), Ryzen 7 7800X3D, RX 9070 XT, RADV / Mesa 26.2.4.

- `ctest` on this branch (rebased on `main` d70b8998): 512 of 513 pass. The failure is `import_audit` (`source_commit` is `None` because my build tree is a git worktree), unrelated to this change.
- **Rise of the Ronin (PPSA04540)**, cold shader cache (`shader_cache` deleted before each run), headless gamescope at 1920×1080. Ronin does not get far on `main` alone, so these runs use a local stack of open PRs on `main` 43972e69 (#1836's first version, #1837, #1902, #1928, #2105 and others). The only difference between A and B is this commit. Both runs stop at the same later point, `prepared shader artifact is missing for the requested static ABI … stage=1`, which is unrelated to this PR. I time from launch to that stop:

| Run | Before (A) | After (B) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 146 s | 105 s |
| 2 | 144 s | 105 s |

The shaders compiled are the same in both: 804–809 cache misses in the first 10 s, about 850 in total.

### Overlap

#1836 adds its deferral check in `PrepareRegistered` right before the removed `GraphBuilder::Build` line. Whichever merges second needs a small rebase. Nothing else changes.

body:
### What

`getcwd(NULL, size)` returned a buffer from `GuestHeap::GuestHeapAllocate`. The caller releases it with `free()`, which goes through the application heap (`ApplicationHeapFree`). With the default heap, the two are the same allocator, so this worked. When a title registers its own allocator through the malloc-replacement handshake, though, `free()` hands the replacement a pointer it never returned. Every other libc function that returns memory for the caller to free (`strdup`, `strndup`, `asprintf`, `vasprintf`, `malloc` itself) already allocates through `ApplicationHeapAllocate`; `getcwd` was the only one that didn't.

`getcwd` now allocates with `ApplicationHeapAllocate_nid_no_patch`, and, like `strndup`, reports `ENOMEM` and returns null when the allocator returns null. Before, a null buffer would have been written to.

### Tested

Windows 11, WinLibs GCC 15.2.0 r7, Release, `-DBUILD_TESTING=ON`:

- `application_heap_replacement` (the registered replacement allocator in `ApplicationHeap.cpp`):
  - `getcwd(NULL, 0)` returns the replacement's storage, sized `strlen + 1`;
  - `getcwd(NULL, 200)` requests 200 bytes;
  - both are released through `ApplicationHeapFree`, which asserts that the pointer is its own;
  - with the replacement failing, `getcwd(NULL, 0)` returns null with errno 12.

  On `main` the replacement case fails.
- `guest_working_directory` freed the buffer with `GuestHeapFree` and ran without an application heap, which no title does. It now registers an allocator that forwards to the guest heap, as the default heap does. It checks that `getcwd(NULL, 0)` allocates through it and frees with `ApplicationHeapFree`.
- `ctest -E "^agc_|video_out"`: 249/249 with the test update.
- `tools/check_conventions.py` passes, and `tools/pr_overlap.py --branch` reports no overlap. It also merges cleanly with #1369, #1900, #1656 and #1611, which touch the same test files.

body:
### What
Depends on #846. This branch contains its two commits. Only the last commit, `feat(libkernel): start runtime-loaded modules with their arguments on Linux`, belongs to this PR.

#846 starts `--module-dir` modules from `sceKernelLoadStartModule` with the call's `args`/`argp` on Windows. On Linux, the host loader runs their `DT_INIT` at `dlopen` with zeroed arguments, so #846 throws there when start arguments are given. This PR does on Linux what #846 does on Windows, with the same table:

- **Relinker, Linux writer.** A module from `--module-dir` gets no `DT_INIT`, `DT_INIT_ARRAY`, `DT_FINI` or `DT_FINI_ARRAY`. Like the Windows `.ginit` section, it exports `__aps5_guest_initialize`: the initializer's address, the number of `INIT_ARRAY` slots, and each slot's address. The symbol is added to the module's dynamic symbol table and hash. Modules from `sce_module`/`prx` are written as before.
- **libkernel.** After `dlopen`, `OpenModule` looks up `__aps5_guest_initialize`. It takes the module's load bias from `dl_iterate_phdr` and calls the initializer once with `(args, argp, nullptr)`. It stores the return value in `*res`, then runs the `INIT_ARRAY` slots. The table walk and the "only once per module" set are now shared with the Windows path, which keeps its behavior. The `NotImplemented` for start arguments on Linux is removed.
- **TechnicalDebt.** The #846 line now says both platforms start these modules once, from the first call that loads them, and never run their finalizers. Windows already skipped the finalizers.

### Evidence: Hollow Knight: Silksong (PPSA12544) on Linux
Unity loads its plugins from `/app0/Media/Plugins` with `sceKernelLoadStartModule`, and `PSN.prx` is started with start arguments. All runs below are relinked with `--module-dir Media/Plugins`, on `main` `d70b89989` + #1836 + #1431 (the title stops before the plugins without them) + #846:

- **Without this PR:** `terminate ... what(): sceKernelLoadStartModule with start arguments not implemented`.
- **With this PR:** `PSN.prx` starts. The next stop is in the title's bundled `libSceNpCppWebApi`: `CppWebApi::Common::initialize() failed. ret = 0x80553504`, then an uncaught `Unity.PSN.PS5.PSNException` with that code. `Common::initialize` maps flexible memory and passes it to the bundled libc's `sceLibcMspaceCreate`, which refuses the address on Linux. That is the address-window problem of #861, not this change.
- **With this PR and #861:** the title reaches its title menu (START GAME / OPTIONS / EXTRAS) and keeps running at about 60 fps with no error until I stopped it (100 s).

### Tested
- Linux (Arch, GCC 16.2, Release, RX 9070 XT): `ctest` 464/464 on this branch.
  - `guest_module_dir` gains a Linux case. A `--module-dir` module with `DT_INIT`, `DT_FINI` and one `INIT_ARRAY` slot is written without those tags. It exports `__aps5_guest_initialize` as a 12-byte object holding `(0x1000, 1, 0x2380)`. The same module under `sce_module` keeps its tags and has no such symbol. The test fails on #846 without this commit.
  - `guest_dynamic_loader` gains a Linux case with a host fixture module that exports the table. `GuestLoadStartModule_nid_no_patch` with 16 bytes of arguments must call its start function once with those `args`/`argp`, store its return value (7) in `*res`, and run the `INIT_ARRAY` slot once. Loading the module a second time must not run either again. The test aborts on #846 without this commit, on its `NotImplemented`.
- Windows (Server 2025 VM, WinLibs GCC 15.2, CI flags, no GPU, so Vulkan tests are skipped): 458/458.
- Silksong as above.

body:
### What

`PA_SU_SC_MODE_CNTL.PROVOKING_VTX_LAST` (bit 19) currently rejects a draw. Decode it as first/last provoking vertex and use `VK_EXT_provoking_vertex` for native primitive pipelines, including flat P0 inputs already emitted as SPIR-V `Flat`. Keep first-vertex mode usable without the extension. Include the mode in the pipeline cache key and split render-pass instances when the device cannot mix modes within one pass.

This addresses the later raster-state rejection [reported in #2026](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/issues/2026#issuecomment-6075329161), with `PA_SU_SC_MODE_CNTL = 0x00080244`. That execution was reported by another contributor; I have not run the showcase. Bit 19 follows [opengnm's `flatshade_first` mapping at db752da, ps5_screen.c:2244](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-opengl/blob/db752da4c89380af228497b5b6852163a4e61069/src/gallium/ps5/ps5_screen.c#L2244). Pipeline state and pass separation follow [Khronos's provoking-vertex requirements](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkPipelineRasterizationProvokingVertexStateCreateInfoEXT.html).

Last mode throws when the device feature is unavailable, for generated rectangle/geometry/mesh/tessellation pipelines or unsupported topologies, for explicit per-vertex flat inputs, and for triangle strips with any explicit per-vertex inputs. The latter need a verified mapping for [device-dependent barycentric vertex ordering](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkPhysicalDeviceFragmentShaderBarycentricPropertiesKHR.html).
