body:
### What

The f32 `min`, `max`, `min3`, `max3` and `med3` lowering (`EmitMinMaxF32Value`, `EmitFPMedTri32`) picks results on the bits, with the NaN and ±0 rules measured on RDNA. Three changes make it cheaper without changing any result:

- **`EmitClassifyF32Bits`**: a NaN was found from the exponent and mantissa fields separately (two masks, two compares and an and). The magnitude settles it: a NaN is above `0x7f800000`, a zero is `0`. `v_cvt_*_f32`'s NaN test uses the same helper.
- **`EmitMinMaxF32Value`** ended with two NaN selects, `lhs NaN ? rhs` and then `rhs NaN ? lhs`. The ordered compare (`FOrdLessThan`, `FOrdGreaterThanEqual`) is false when either operand is a NaN, so the ordered pick already returns `rhs` for a NaN `lhs`, and the ±0 rule doesn't apply to a NaN. Only the `rhs NaN ? lhs` select is needed; it also returns `lhs` when both are NaNs, as before.
- **`EmitFPMedTri32`** is the minimum of the three when any operand is a NaN and the median otherwise, and built both from the full NaN-aware min and max (five calls, each classifying its operands, plus three more classifications). The median is used only when no operand is a NaN, so it is now three compare-and-select steps with the ±0 rule and no NaN selects. The minimum reuses the operands' NaN tests: `min(a, b)` is a NaN only when both are, and that case already falls out of the ordered pick as above.

f16 `med3` and the IEEE-mode min/max go through the same lowering. Results are bit-identical.

### Tested

Windows 11, MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0 (WinLibs r7), Release, `ANYPS5_ENABLE_SPIRV_TOOLS=ON`, `main` at d70b8998. GPU tests on an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Laptop GPU (591.86, subgroup 32) and on lavapipe (Mesa 26.2.4 for Windows, `GALLIUM_OVERRIDE_CPU_CAPS=avx`).

- Every shader execution and unit test (`agc_driver_*`, `vector_*`, `agc_shader_*`, `agc_masked_select`, `agc_validate_program`) passes on the RTX 4060, and every float-related one on lavapipe. They include the rows measured on hardware in `agc_driver_f32_min_max_nan`, `agc_driver_f32_denormal_flush`, `agc_driver_dx10_clamp`, `agc_driver_f32_result_clamp`, `agc_driver_float16_ternary_clamp` and `vector_min_max_med16`.
- Negative checks, each fails on both devices:
  - no `rhs NaN ? lhs` select: `f32 min max nan: row 1 v_min3_f32 v12, v4, v5, v6 is 0x7f800001, expected 0x80000000`.
  - the median without the ±0 rule: `f32 min max nan: row 18 v_med3_f32 v14, v4, v5, v6 is 0x00000000, expected 0x80000000`.
  - `med3` always taking the median: `dx10 clamp: lane 1 no float mode v_med3_f32 clamp is 0x3f800000, expected 0x00000000`.
  - infinity classified as a NaN: `f32 denormal flush: lane 13 no float mode v_min_f32 v16, v4, v5 is 0x00000000, expected 0xff800000`.
- Full ctest after `cmake --build build` and `--target libs`, serial, `--timeout 120`, RTX 4060: 506 pass, 2 skip (`agc_driver_storage_cache_budget`, `guest_video_out_wqhd_detection_no_vulkan`), 2 fail: `windows_import_modules` (Windows Error Reporting keeps its GUI fixture open, #2227) and `tls_function_coverage` (Windows Defender removes an executable it writes to the temporary directory; Defender logged the detection during the run). Both run only the relinker, whose build contains no recompiler sources.
- Per op on the RTX 4060, pipeline statistics of a compute program with a dependent chain of 8 ops, not committed (instructions per op in `FLOAT_MODE` 0xc0, and with f32 denormals kept, 0xf0):

  | | main | this PR |

  | `v_max_f32` (registers) | 16 / 10 | 13 / 6 |

body:
### What

Follow-up to #573 (the 64-bit LDS atomics), whose TechnicalDebt entry said the f64 forms were not measured on hardware. `ds_min/max_f32`, `ds_cmpst_f32`, `ds_min/max_f64`, `ds_cmpst_f64` and their `_rtn` forms now follow the rule measured on RDNA2 (gfx1036, Ryzen 7950X3D iGPU) with `tools/hw-oracle`, over 14 × 14 operand sets per type (±0, ±1, ±inf, ±smallest denormal, quiet and signalling NaNs of both signs and with payloads) in IEEE 0 and 1 with the type's denormal field kept and flushed; every memory and returned result of the six f64 and nine f32 results per pair, in each of the four modes, 0 mismatches:

- both operands are flushed to a signed zero when the type's denormal field flushes (`FLOAT_MODE` bits 5:4 for f32, bits 7:6 for f64; a shader without a known mode flushes f32 and keeps f64, as elsewhere);
- a signalling-NaN data operand is stored quieted; else a signalling-NaN old value is stored quieted; else a quiet-NaN old value is replaced by the data; else a quiet-NaN data operand loses; else the ordered compare with −0 below +0 decides; the flushed value is what is written, also when the old value wins;
- `cmpst` compares the flushed bits (both zeros equal, NaN never equal) and leaves memory unchanged when they differ;
- the returned value is always the old value as it was in memory; `IEEE_MODE` has no effect.

This is the rule `AtomicFloatBits::minMax` already implements for the buffer float atomics, plus the flush. The shared f32 path used `OpIsNan`/`OpFOrdLessThan`/`OpFOrdEqual` on the bit-cast values, so its NaN and denormal results were the driver's (both RADV and NVIDIA quiet nothing and flush f32 denormals inside those compares in every mode); the shared f64 path (#573) ordered the bits but had none of the signalling-NaN rules. Both now use `AtomicFloatBits`; the translation marks the shared float atomics with the mode's flush in `MemoryInfo::flushDenormals`. The 29 integer 64-bit forms, EXEC masking, immediate offsets, out-of-range addresses (0, no write) and contention (256 lanes, serial order) were measured as well and match the recompiler already; `ds_add_f32` is not measured and is unchanged.

TechnicalDebt: the 64-bit entry loses its "not measured" sentence and gains the measured facts about mixed-width serialisation (hardware serialises 32-bit and 64-bit atomics on one address, the lock does not: in the measurement RADV lost 64 of 128 increments in wave32 and 32 in wave64, NVIDIA 48 in wave32, timing-dependent) and the misaligned fault; a new LDS float atomics entry records the rule; the f32 denormals entry points to it.

Measurement data, scripts and the host comparison before and after the change: https://github.com/SleglJan/AnyPS5/tree/audit/oracle-2026-10-08/oracle-audit/lds64 (`report.md` there is the summary).

Overlap: #2162 adds a sentence to the same f32 denormals TechnicalDebt entry (its `v_fma_mixlo_f16`/`v_fma_mixhi_f16` flush rule), and #2025 and #1290 add entries next to the edited ones; none of them shares code with this PR or is built on by it, so whichever merges second rebases the one line. No open pull request changes the shared float atomics.

### Tested

Linux (CachyOS, kernel 7.2.9, GCC 16.2.1), Release, `ANYPS5_ENABLE_SPIRV_TOOLS=ON`, RTX 3080 (615.71.09) and RADV (Mesa 26.2.4), on this branch (based on `main` d70b8998).

- New `agc_driver_lds_float_atomic_modes`: 32 operand pairs per type (the classes above, both orders), each lane runs the six f32 and six f64 forms on its LDS slot; 27 result dwords per lane pinned bit for bit against the oracle in the titles' mode (0xc0, also used for "no float mode"), with both fields kept (0xf0) and with both flushed (0x00). Written first: it failed on `main`'s lowering at lane 7 (`ds_min_rtn_f32`, flushed denormal) and passes with the change.
- `agc_driver_lds_atomics64`: its CPU model gets the signalling-NaN rule, and the lanes of kind 2 now take their data from `floats[(tid / 4 + 9) % 12]`, which feeds the table's signalling NaN, −inf and the negative denormal into min/max (the old index never reached entry 9). It failed on `main` at lane 2 (`ds_min_f64`, the signalling-NaN data not stored quieted) and passes with the change.
- Mutation checks, each fails: the 64-bit path without the signalling-NaN rules (both tests), the flush disabled (new test, lane 7), the old signalling NaN preferred over the data (new test, lane 22).
- The measured matrices replayed through the recompiler on both GPUs with the change: 0 of 35,072 result dwords differ from the oracle over the 256 lanes (f64 min/max 3,072 × 4 modes, f64 cmpst 1,536 × 4, f32 min/max/cmpst 2,304 × 4, 29 integer forms 7,424); before the change, per mode, 472 (f64 min/max, kept), 584 (f64 min/max, flushed), 40 (f64 cmpst, flushed), 336 (f32, kept) and 412 (f32, flushed) dwords differed, the same on both GPUs.
- `agc_driver_lds_atomics`, `agc_driver_lds_integer_atomics`, `agc_driver_lds_condxchg`, `agc_driver_lds_read_write`, `agc_driver_lds_src2` pass on both GPUs; LDS tests `--repeat until-fail:3` on both; full `ctest` 516/517 on each GPU; the one failure differs per GPU and runs no LDS instruction: `agc_driver_storage_cache_budget` on the iGPU (its memory budget) and `agc_driver_dcc_keys_first_write` on the RTX 3080 ("an unchanged pending image was uploaded again", also reported in several open pull requests today).

body:
### What

Runtime image operations can emit terminating paths inside a guest loop's continuation. Record emitted `OpLoopMerge` offsets and move the SPIR-V continuation to a separate backedge block only when the emitted instruction range contains `OpUnreachable`, `OpReturn`, `OpReturnValue`, `OpKill`, or `OpTerminateInvocation`. Preserve the semantic guest CFG and patch phi predecessors to the actual block exit labels.

This is a SPIR-V structural correction, not a change to RDNA instruction semantics. The rule comes from the SPIR-V specification's structured-control-flow restrictions on continue constructs: https://registry.khronos.org/SPIR-V/specs/unified1/SPIRV.html#_structured_control_flow. Tests cover patch offsets across vector growth, invalid offsets/IDs, terminating opcodes, unchanged guest instruction ranges, and a runtime image loop's three stores plus untouched exit row in wave32 and wave64.

### Tested

Focused build passed; `agc_spirv_module`, `agc_structurizer`, and `agc_driver_runtime_images` passed 3/3 (0.15 s, 0.14 s, 0.80 s) with `ANYPS5_REQUIRE_VULKAN=1`, no skips. body:
### What

The Windows vectored crash reporter sleeps forever after its first fatal-class exception, preventing subsequent first-chance exceptions from reaching later handlers. Return `EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_SEARCH` for subsequent reports and label the initial report first-chance. A child-process regression deliberately faults twice and verifies both faults reach a recovery handler, the child exits, and exactly one report is emitted.

body:
### What
A multi-dword global or flat store (`global_store_dwordx2/x3/x4`) was translated as one `StoreAddressU32` per dword. Each dword got its own write-pointer lookup and its own 4-byte store. Across a wave those are strided partial writes, every lane writing one dword out of each 16 bytes per instruction, and partial writes to host memory are very slow.

RADV's `clear_htile_mask` kernel (17 instructions: one `global_load_dwordx4`, `v_and_or_b32` ×4, one `global_store_dwordx4` per thread) took ~9 ms for 640 KiB on an RTX 5070 Ti. In vkQuake (PPSA99010) it runs three times per frame, which made it 4.6 s of every 10 s of GPU time. Loads already avoid this: a multi-dword load is one `LoadAddressU32xN` that resolves the span once (`EmitBdaDwordReads`).

- Translation emits `StoreAddressU32x2/x3/x4` (`Void`, address resource, `U32xN` data) for a multi-dword store outside scratch, with the same group memory metadata as the wide loads. `APS5_BDA_DWORD_STORES=1` keeps one `StoreAddressU32` per dword.
- `EmitBdaDwordWrites` probes the whole span once with a new non-faulting `probe_bda_write_pointer` (write permission). When the span is in one writable range and both the guest and device addresses are 4-byte aligned, it stores the dwords from that one pointer: one vector store when the device address is 16-byte (x4) or 8-byte (x2) aligned, otherwise consecutive dword stores. It then notes the written page, and the last dword's page too when that differs.
- Anything else (unmapped, read-only, spanning two ranges, unaligned) takes the existing per-dword `EmitBdaStore` path, so faults and their order, byte stores for unaligned addresses and range-spanning stores behave exactly as before.

Tests:
- `RunBdaDwordWriteTests` (`agc_driver_bda_device`), through the emitter: 16-byte-aligned x4, 4-byte-aligned x4, aligned and unaligned x2, x3, x4 and x2 across a 4 KiB written-page boundary, an unaligned x4, an x4 across two writable ranges (no fault), and an x4 whose last three dwords are read-only (first dword stored, Permission fault as before). Each checks the stored bytes, the neighbouring bytes, the fault state and the noted pages. Dropping the second page note, or storing the separate dwords one slot off, fails it.
- New `tests/execution/MaskedGlobalStore.cpp`: RADV's 17-word `clear_htile_mask` kernel, translated and dispatched (64 groups, wave64 and wave32), checks every dword of the buffer for the depth-clear and the expand masks. It passes with the wide path and with `APS5_BDA_DWORD_STORES=1`.

### Tested
Windows 11 Pro (26200), MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0 (WinLibs r7), Release, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti (driver 610.88).

- Full local suite: 508 tests, 506 passed, 1 skipped; `guest_sce_net` timed out (it times out locally on unrelated branches too, likely my network filtering). It was run from the generated `CTestTestfile.cmake` commands because antivirus blocks `ctest.exe` on this machine.
- `tools/check_conventions.py --base origin/main` passes.
- The `clear_htile_mask` kernel alone (640 groups over 640 KiB, a local timing harness): 9.1 ms per dispatch before, 0.54 ms after.
- vkQuake E1M1 demo with `APS5_PROFILE_GPU=1`, on my local test branch (current `main` plus my open RADV PRs and local stubs): GPU time went from ~5,100 ms to ~290 ms per 10 s, GPU busy from 34 ms to 2.9 ms per frame, and ~19 to ~22 FPS (now CPU-bound). The RADV fill kernel also dropped from ~755 ms to ~40 ms per 10 s.

Not tested on Linux or macOS.

#1265 (loops the BDA byte stores) and my #1280 (stacked on it; changes `note_bda_write`) touch the same store helpers in `SpirvBdaRead.cpp`. I'll rebase onto whichever lands first.

### What
Optimizes the CFG discovery fixed-point loop and PLT compaction in `core/relinker`:

- **Zero-Copy Segment Span:** Replaced `std::vector` deep-copying of the `.text` segment in `CodeInstructionCollector::Collect` with a zero-copy `std::span<const uint8_t>`. Eliminates copying the full code segment into newly allocated vectors on every root-discovery iteration.
- **Single-Pass Instruction Decoding:** Added persistent visited tracking across discovery passes (`decodedInstructions` and `sectionReachable`). Instructions are now decoded exactly once across the entire binary instead of re-disassembling previously visited blocks from scratch on every iteration ($O(N)$ vs O(K . N)).
- **Opcode-First PLT Check & Hash Maps:** In `PltCompactor::CompactPlt`, validates all 4 structural bytes of the canonical 16-byte PLT thunk (`0xFF 0x25 ... 0x68 ... 0xE9`) before querying slots, skipping non-PLT indirect jumps immediately. Switched slot tracking from `std::map` to `std::unordered_map`.

body:
### What

Fix the remaining VBRI limitation in `sceAjmDecMp3ParseFrame`: a mono frame with a VBRI header currently throws instead of returning metadata.

- Detect VBRI at byte 36 for all supported MPEG versions and channel counts. Do not derive its offset from the side information or main-data length.
- Preserve the existing 26-byte header bound, encoder-delay result, and VBRI + FGH handling.
- Replace the mono exception expectation with successful parsing. Add MPEG-1/2/2.5 mono and stereo cases, physically truncated buffers at 39/40/43/61 bytes, the 62-byte boundary, and mono VBRI + FGH coverage.
- Update the existing technical-debt entry. CRC-protected frames and non-layer-III OFL requests still throw. PS5 behavior remains unverified.

This completes a case deliberately excluded by merged PR #768. No open VBRI PR was found before publication. This PR does not claim a real-title compatibility improvement.

### Format evidence

FFmpeg's [`mp3_parse_vbri_tag`](https://github.com/FFmpeg/FFmpeg/blob/b91a82d6dd0e7c32caf34b345130c8fb1309a597/libavformat/mp3dec.c) seeks to `base + 4 + 32` independently of MPEG version and channel count. The existing AJM implementation already records this fixed offset in `TechnicalDebt.md`, but throws when the computed side-information offset differs.

The result fields retain the existing AJM behavior. This change does not introduce FFmpeg's duration or frame-count semantics into AJM.

### Tested

Baseline: upstream `d70b8998`, current `main` when the branch was created.

**Synthetic parser checks, not the full linked AJM suite:**

- Windows x86-64: Zig 0.14.1 C++ compiler, `-std=c++20 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -O1`. A temporary harness compiled the actual parser, public wrapper, result layout, fixtures, and `TestMp3ParseOfl` from this checkout.
- Before the source fix, the new regression terminated with `sceAjmDecMp3ParseFrame (VBRI header outside MPEG-1 stereo)`.
- After the fix, all extracted MP3 OFL regression checks passed. Existing LAME, FGH, stereo VBRI, and unsupported CRC/layer checks also passed.
- Linux x86-64: the same harness was cross-compiled with Zig using `-target x86_64-linux-musl -fsanitize=undefined`, then executed under Ubuntu 24.04 in WSL. All checks passed, with no reported undefined behavior.
- The complete `GuestAjm.cpp` translation unit compiled on Windows with `-std=c++20 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -c`.
- `python tools/check_conventions.py --base origin/main` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.

**Not tested:** full project build, linked `guest_ajm` execution, supported MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0 build, or real-title/PS5 behavior. The local environment lacks the supported build toolchain and initialized decoder dependencies. The temporary compiler and harness are outside the repository.

```sh

cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DBUILD_TESTING=ON
```

body:
### What

Addresses #1817; related reports: #2062 and #2207.

Compute shaders can copy a function pointer out of user-data SGPRs and call it with `s_swappc_b64`. Registration has the shader's code and ABI but no invocation user data, so the existing static call analysis rejects these programs before their target is available. Preparing one program per original caller also cannot represent dispatches that select different callees.

Registration now defers only compute programs whose unresolved targets have a proven user-data origin. The analysis follows `s_mov_b32`/`s_mov_b64` definitions, rejects branches that can bypass a definition, and stops at control transfers and earlier calls. An untouched user-data pair remains valid across loops. A pair written elsewhere in the caller is accepted only before its first write and without a back edge across the call. Every captured callee must preserve the source pairs used by this proof. Arbitrary GPU-data-dependent targets still throw.

At dispatch, the existing `ShaderMemory` capture reader synchronizes and reads each callee from guest memory, bounds its size, and decodes it through its final `s_setpc_b64`. The caller's instructions and PCs stay intact. Each call site gets its own callee clone and explicit target/return binding, so one link pair can serve several calls, the same callee can be invoked at several sites, and every return reaches that site's continuation. Relative branches inside a callee retain their offsets. This avoids a dynamic return selector and changes no instruction translation semantics. The existing `PC + 4` link write and `s_setpc_b64` return follow AMD's [RDNA2 ISA](https://gpuopen.com/download/rdna2-shader-instruction-set-architecture.pdf), sections 3.6.3 and 12.3, opcodes 32/33. Native ISA/PS5 equivalence has not been measured.

The source, prepared-interface and disk keys include all combined caller/callee bytes plus each call's PC mapping, target address and user-data provenance. Source lookup still compares the full code on hash matches; disk entries verify the complete key. Prepared handles and captures reject bindings that no longer match their invocation's function-pointer words. Callee reads participate in dispatch-cache validation and are recorded as code reads, so the flat-resource-data fast path cannot mask a changed instruction. Targets aliasing immutable registration snapshots are rejected. Request serialization version 14 and `agc_shader_replay --dis --cfg` preserve the combined program and call bindings.

Remaining unsupported cases throw: non-compute driver integration, arithmetic-derived targets, copy chains that fail the conservative control-flow proof, nested calls/cycles, PC-relative callees, escaping link values, and callees without one final return to the correct link pair. Limits are 64 captured call sites, 64 KiB per callee and 1 MiB combined code. Existing static/direct and fetch-call validation remains in place.

The overlap check was run against current open PRs, with its local query limit also extended to include all open PRs. No other open PR implements this callee-resolution capability. There are mechanical overlaps with #1836/#2257 (registration deferral), #1902/#1928/#2261 (prepared shader lookup), #1491/#1776 (frontend), #1492 (serialization version), #1547 (cache review list), and #2178 (technical debt). This PR contains no prerequisite commits and does not depend on those changes; their overlapping hunks need reconciliation if merged first.

### Tested

All new fixtures are synthetic; no retail title or commercial shader file was used. No compatibility claim is made for Ghost of Yōtei, Astro Bot, Bloodlines 2, or any other retail title.

`user_data_swappc` exercises move-chain provenance, a direct user-data call sharing its link pair, four call sites/two pointers, separate continuations, repeated callee cloning, serialization and source/disk key sensitivity. `agc_driver_user_data_swappc` registers without function-pointer values, resolves at dispatch, and checks observable callee additions and caller additions after every return. It covers wave32/wave64, four shared-link calls, repeated calls inside a loop, two user-data pairs, target changes, and edits to both callees at unchanged addresses. It also checks deterministic guest-memory failures, stale prepared-source rejection, capture of return bytes, registration-snapshot alias rejection, and exclusion of code reads from flat-data masking.

### What

On FreeBSD, `stat("file/")` fails with `ENOTDIR`: a trailing slash asks for a directory. On `main`:

- **Windows:** `std::filesystem::exists("file/")` is true (Win32 ignores the slash), then `_wstat64("file/")` fails, and `File::FillFileStat` throws `FillFileStat: stat failed for ...`, which **aborts the title**.
- **Linux:** `stat` reports `ENOTDIR`, which `std::filesystem::exists` reads as "not found", so the guest got `ENOENT`.

`sceKernelStat` now takes the `std::filesystem::status` once and returns `ENOTDIR` if the host reports `not_a_directory`, or if the guest path ends in `/` and the target exists but isn't a directory. A missing path is still `ENOENT`, and `stat("dir/")` still succeeds. `stat` (the POSIX wrapper) goes through `sceKernelStat`, so both are covered.

The same trailing slash on other calls returns the wrong error without aborting: `open("file/")` and `unlink("file/")` give `EINVAL` instead of `ENOTDIR` on Windows. `open` is being reworked by several open PRs (#1628, #1777, #2144, #2170), and `unlink` is in my #2289, so I kept this to `stat`.

### Tested

Windows 11, WinLibs GCC 15.2.0 r7, Release, `-DBUILD_TESTING=ON`:

  - `stat("present.txt/")` returns -1 with errno 20;
  - `sceKernelStat("present.txt/")` returns `0x80020014`;
  - `stat("<dir>/")` succeeds and reports a directory.

  On `main` the test process aborts with `FillFileStat: stat failed`.
- `ctest -E "^agc_|video_out"`: 249/249 passed, including `guest_path_case`, which also uses `sceKernelStat`.

body:
### What

Fixes the device loss reported in #2155 (`vkQueueSubmit recorder: Vulkan result -4` at the start of `storageRefreshTests` in `agc_driver_recorder_tests`).

On Windows, host imports are compared, not watched, so `unitShadowTests` returns right after it imports its 17 MiB block. Its cleanup then removes the registration and releases the block. The import itself is only retired at the next lookup, which is the `HostImportFor` in `storageRefreshTests`. Its `vkFreeMemory` frees an import whose pages are already gone. The Vulkan spec requires an imported host range to stay valid for as long as the memory object exists.

`Unregister` now looks the range up once more after removing it, as the cleanups in `keysFillTests` and `storageRefreshTests` already do. The import is retired while the block is still committed.

### Tested

Windows 10 (19045), RTX 3060 Laptop (NVIDIA 616.92), MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0 (WinLibs r7), Release. `agc_driver_recorder_tests` was built with `--target`.

| tree | runs | device loss | other result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `main` d70b8998 | 25 | 6 | 19 refresh store (#2155's other failure, fixed by #2248) |
| `main` + this PR | 30 | 0 | 30 refresh store |
| `main` + #2248 | 30 | 7 | 23 pass |
| `main` + #2248 + this PR | 30 | 0 | 30 pass |

With `vkQueueWaitIdle` probes around each step, 7 of 20 runs lost the device. In all 7, the queue was healthy just before the retire's `vkFreeMemory` of the 17 MiB import and lost right after it.

A local probe mode (not part of this PR) imports a 17 MiB block, releases it, and lets the next lookup retire the import:

| block released | runs | device lost |
|---|---|---|
| about 10 µs after the import | 60 | 12 |
| 0.5 ms after the import | 20 | 4 |
| 1 ms after the import | 20 | 1 |
| 1.5, 2, 5, 20 or 100 ms after the import | 20 each | 0 |
| after the retire (this PR's order) | 60 | 0 |

The window fits the late NVIDIA marks on imported pages, about 1.2 to 2 ms after the import, from #1434.

- Not run on Linux. There the test runs to its end, and the end's shrunk registration already retires the import before the cleanup runs.
- `tools/check_conventions.py` passes.

The runtime unmap path has the same order: `GuestAllocationsUnmap_nid_postfix` releases the pages in `apply` before the registry changes, and `refreshImports` retires the import later. I haven't checked whether a title ever releases memory within that window. This PR only changes the test; the runtime order is filed as #2352.

### What

`StorageTexture::upload` allocates a guest-sized CPU snapshot before choosing an upload path, including watched host imports that never read it. Keep snapshots used by untracked comparisons and fast-clear byte proofs, along with the existing generation, alias, write-back and neighboring-byte guards.

body:
### What

`guest_sce_net` checks that a send fails once the peer has closed its socket. It closes the accepted socket after a clean exchange and gives the client 100 sends, 1 ms apart, to see the failure. That relies on the peer's RST arriving within ~100 ms. On a Windows host with a WFP network filter installed (Cloudflare WARP and ProtonVPN here), the client's sends keep succeeding for ~19 s: 1213 to 1214 tries in 3 of 3 runs, past the 100-try loop, so the test aborts at `Require(send_failed)`. A plain Winsock program with the same sequence and no AnyPS5 code does the same (1205 to 1207 tries, ~19 s, then `WSAECONNABORTED`), so it is the host, not libSceNet.

Before closing the accepted socket, the client now sends one more message, and the test waits on the existing epoll until the accepted socket has it. Closing a TCP socket with unread received data sends a RST at once (RFC 2525 2.17, and what Windows, Linux and FreeBSD do), so the next send fails on the first try whatever filter is installed. The check is unchanged: a send to a reset peer fails.

In the plain Winsock program, closing with unread data made the next send fail on try 1 in 5 of 5 runs (`WSAECONNRESET`).

### Tested

Windows 10 (19045), MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0 (WinLibs r7), Release, `BUILD_TESTING=ON`, RTX 4060, on d70b8998.

Since #639, `sceAgcCreatePrimState` also resolves the graphics ABI ahead of time, and that resolve throws when the primitive type is a patch list without HS_EN, or a hull stage is set with another primitive type. body:
### What

FreeBSD treats both result pointers as optional:
- `gettimeofday(tp, tzp)` stores the time only when `tp` is not null (`sys_gettimeofday`: `if (uap->tp) ...`), so `gettimeofday(NULL, &tz)` or `gettimeofday(NULL, NULL)` succeeds.
- `clock_getres(id, res)` stores the resolution only when `res` is not null, so `clock_getres(id, NULL)` succeeds. POSIX says the same, and it is the usual way to check that a clock exists.

Both functions threw `std::invalid_argument` for a null result, which aborts the title. They now write into a local value instead, and every other path is unchanged.

### What

**Depends on: #423.** This follow-up carries `PA_CL_VS_OUT_CNTL` through registered shader preparation and static graphics ABI resolution. #423 passes the control at draw time; preparing an otherwise complete registered vertex shader without it produces a different artifact key, so the draw throws `prepared shader artifact is missing for the requested static ABI`.

Use complete shader headers in the driver regression and resolve the combined graphics ABI for each clip/cull control change. Both draw-key modes verify the rendered pixels. The fixture shuts the driver down explicitly.

Main already uses request version 13 for float modes. Reserve version 14 for the added vertex control instead of changing version 13's layout. The regression replays a version-13 vertex request with non-default float-mode fields and verifies that those fields survive while clip control defaults to zero.

Based on main `d70b89989473ba1f6ae13e44e079e67f1f8a44b0`. The branch includes #423's five prerequisite commits, retaining Michon's authorship; merge conflicts were reconciled with main's multisampled-image capabilities, null-descriptor feature and test registration. The additional follow-up is commit `c16aaec2e`. This draft should wait for #423, then be rebased to remove the prerequisite commits.

The existing position-export mapping and instruction semantics are reused. TechnicalDebt records the mapping's lack of PS5 hardware verification and the unsupported mesh/tessellation clip/cull paths.

Overlap audit, 9 October 2026, at main `f8c2f072`: #2169 adds MSAA sample-location state alongside #423's clip-control state and tests. It does not carry `PA_CL_VS_OUT_CNTL` through registered preparation. Reconciliation must keep both sets of state fields, decoding and tests. #2327 removes the redundant decode/CFG/structurize pre-check beside this follow-up's vertex-control assignment in `PrepareRegistered`; keep the clip-control assignment while removing that redundant pass, with preparation still validating unsupported code. Virtual merges confirm conflicts in the state/test files and `ShaderRegistry.cpp`; they do not establish combined behavior. Rebase and retest after either lands. body:
### What

FreeBSD's `unlink(2)` fails with `EPERM` when the path is a directory. `sceKernelUnlink` passed the host error through, so the guest got a different code on each host:

| Host | `unlink("dir")` on `main` | FreeBSD |
|---|---|---|
| Windows (`_wunlink`) | `EACCES` (13), measured | `EPERM` (1) |
| Linux (`unlink`) | `EISDIR` (21), per `unlink(2)` | `EPERM` (1) |

`sceKernelUnlink` now checks the path with `symlink_status` before unlinking and returns `EPERM` for a directory. A symbolic link to a directory is still unlinked, as on FreeBSD. If the path can't be inspected, the check doesn't match and the native `unlink` reports its own error as before. `unlink` (the POSIX wrapper) goes through `sceKernelUnlink`, so both are covered.

body:
### What
An embedded vertex fetch adds the base vertex or start instance user SGPR to the index VGPR (`v_add_co_u32 v8, vcc, s19, v8`), and the driver folds that SGPR into the Vulkan draw's first vertex and first instance so the replaced attribute fetch starts there. v5 and v8 were `gl_VertexIndex` and `gl_InstanceIndex`, which already hold that offset, so the translated add counted it twice: index + offset before the add, index + 2 × offset after it. This hits direct draws and indirect records drawn on the CPU path alike; PPSA26344 indexes a per-instance buffer with v8 + s19 at start instances up to 59,455.

- A vertex or local program's entry now writes the index VGPRs as the builtin minus the folded SGPR's user data word. Programs without a folded SGPR are unchanged.
- The fold moves into `Driver::FoldDrawOffsets` with the same rules. `APS5_INDX_OFFSET_SKIP_FOLD` and `APS5_NO_INDEXED_OFFSET_FOLD` go, as skipping the fold would now leave the indices short.
- Hardware: the VertexID/InstanceID VGPRs are zero-based; the offsets reach the shader only through the user SGPRs the draw names, which the CP fills from the record for DRAW_INDIRECT and DRAW_INDEX_INDIRECT (Mesa radeonsi `si_emit_draw_packets`, RADV `radv_cs_emit_indirect_draw_packet`).
- A record drawn in place keeps the CPU's SGPR word, so `EmbeddedVertexFetchAnalyzer` now counts the register as shared unless the fetch add is the only reader of the index VGPR and the SGPR (no earlier read, carry, clamp or second add); such records take the CPU path, where both values are exact.
- No request or cache layout change.
- #1896 calls the same `fold` lambda, which keeps its signature.

### Tested
- Windows 11, MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0, based on `main` d70b8998: configure `-DBUILD_TESTING=ON`, full build, `--target libs`, `ctest`:
- 508/508 tests pass (`ctest --output-on-failure`)
- Linux (WSL Ubuntu 24.04, GCC 13.3, Mesa llvmpipe, upstream's job configuration), merged with `main` d70b8998: 517/517 pass
- New `agc_driver_draw_offset_indices`: a vertex program stores v5/v8 before and after its fetch adds for direct draws, records the now public `ClassifyIndirectDraw` sends to the CPU path, one drawn in place and one whose packet names no register; it also checks which programs may stay in place. With main's translator it fails (at start instance 40, v8 reads 40, not 0, and 80 after the add; the 59,455 record gives 118,910), and without the analyzer change a record whose program copies v5/v8 first stays in place.
- Not tested: console behaviour.

body:
### What

The [[recorder](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/blob/main/core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/Recorder.cpp)](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/blob/main/core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/Recorder.cpp) bounds the bytes a batch keeps alive: `BoundKeptBytes` submits an open batch at `KeptBytesBudget` (512 MiB) and waits for the oldest in-flight batches past twice that. Only bytes passed to `Recorder::Keep(object, bytes)` count, and a recorded dispatch or draw kept its `ShaderResources` (and a draw its `DrawBindings` snapshots) with a size of 0. The host-visible copies of guest buffers that these objects own were never counted.

Planet Coaster (PPSA01736) binds a 124 MiB writable guest buffer in nearly every draw after its intro. The process went from 8.7 GB to 20.7 GB private memory within three seconds. 98 buffers of 124 MiB were created and 12 released, until:

```
[videoout] presentation failed: AGC graphics: vkAllocateMemory buffer: Vulkan result -2
```

`GuestBufferMemory::CopiedBytes()` now reports the bytes of its regions that are served by a copy, `ShaderResources::CopiedBytes()` forwards it, and the dispatch keep, the draw keep and the draw snapshots pass their bytes to `Recorder::Keep`. The existing bound then applies to them; nothing else about the bound changes.

Related open PRs: #1364 (and #1366, which contains it) counts retained draw upload pages in the same budget; it does not touch these keeps. #1997 passes sizes for its own image merge buffers. The call sites above are untouched by both.

This is a bound, not a fix of the copies themselves: the title still re-copies that buffer for each draw (see the related region fix in a separate PR).

### Tested

Windows 11, MinGW-w64 15.2.0, RTX 3060.
- `agc_driver_bda_resources`: `CopiedBytes()` is 0 before an upload and, after it, either 0 (served by an import) or the one copied region's size.

body:
### What

A typed storage-image heap held `StorageHeapCapacity` = 4 elements, and a dynamic-mip storage image reserves that many for its mip slots ([`[BindingAllocator::place](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/blob/main/core/shader/recompiler/Optimization/src/BindingAllocator.cpp)`](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/blob/main/core/shader/recompiler/Optimization/src/BindingAllocator.cpp)). A shader with one dynamic-mip storage image and any other storage image of the same class therefore needed 5 elements and failed:

```
what():  ShaderRecompiler::Recompile: shader image heap capacity exceeded
```

Planet Coaster (PPSA01736) hits this with a mip-chain compute shader: the allocator reported group 30 needing 5 of 4 for 6 images (from a temporary diagnostic in the failure message). The title aborts there.

The constant is split in two: `StorageMipSlots` = 4 stays the number of slots per dynamic-mip image, and `StorageHeapCapacity` becomes 16, the elements one storage heap can hold. Heap arrays are declared with their compact length (`binding.count`), so every shader that fitted before gets the same layout and SPIR-V. The ABI structs and `Version` are unchanged.

Related open PRs: #757 and #758 also use `StorageHeapCapacity` for the dynamic mip count in `ResourceMaterializer.cpp`; whichever lands second needs to pick up the rename to `StorageMipSlots` on that line. #2141 changes the sampler heap size only.

body:
### What

`sceNetResolverAbort` currently throws. Give it the `(resolver ID, flags)` signature and implement abort state for the existing synchronous resolvers. An idle abort can preserve one cancellation independently for the next NTOA or ATON lookup. An active abort records EINTR and prevents that lookup from publishing its output or clearing its interrupted error state.

Resolver destruction also suppresses late output. Host lookups use temporary output storage, and completion checks cancellation under the same lock that protects result delivery. A second simultaneous lookup on the same resolver returns resolver EBUSY, including after abort while the cancelled host call is still running. Reuse becomes available only once that call completes. Unknown abort bits and unsupported nonzero start flags throw.

**Limitation:** this does not interrupt host `getaddrinfo` or `getnameinfo`. The cancelled synchronous caller returns only after the host call finishes. Timeout/retry remain unimplemented; no asynchronous resolver or epoll support is added.

The signature, preservation bits, active-abort status and busy code follow [shadPS4 net.cpp](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4/blob/0c9ca525b8add53e62b3ccd9c9c2f6ef2ebabbfa/src/core/libraries/net/net.cpp), [net_resolver.cpp](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4/blob/0c9ca525b8add53e62b3ccd9c9c2f6ef2ebabbfa/src/core/libraries/net/net_resolver.cpp), and its net types/error definitions. These are PS4 reimplementation references, not PS5 measurements. The in-flight-destroy EBADF return and remaining uncertainties are recorded in TechnicalDebt.

Checked open PRs for resolver work and the exact export before starting. #2195 implements `sceNetResolverStartNtoaMultipleRecords`, which this change leaves unimplemented; both branches touch the existing network test and export file, so they may need textual reconciliation. No dependency on that PR.

### Tested

Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200, Ryzen 7 7700X, RX 7900 XT, AMD driver 32.0.31041.1004. WinLibs GCC 15.2.0 UCRT/POSIX/SEH r7, Release, BUILD_TESTING=ON, SPIRV-Tools OFF. Main `d70b89989473ba1f6ae13e44e079e67f1f8a44b0`; local implementation commit `b762bcb0b2d40577552c14b78f622467682f20ce`.

- Extended `guest_sce_net` checks the actual exports: invalid/destroyed IDs, idle abort, independent one-shot preservation, unchanged output on interruption, forward/reverse resolution, multi-record preservation, errno/error state, and rejected flags.
- The extended export regression fails with unchanged main's Export.cpp (`sceNetResolverAbort not implemented`), then passes with the implementation.
- New `net_resolver_state` uses controlled blocking work to verify active forward/reverse cancellation, resolver busy state, destruction, cancellation taking precedence over a late host error, rejected flags during a lookup, exception cleanup, busy rejection of both lookup kinds until cancelled host work finishes, and successful reuse after completion. These tests exercise the state implementation used by the exports without depending on DNS latency.
- Both focused CTests passed 100/100 consecutive runs. Each finishes well below one second locally.
- Full build and explicit libs target, including NID packaging, passed.
- Full CTest on the final implementation: 505 passed, 2 failed, 1 skipped, 508 total, 27.97 seconds. The failures are the independently reproduced existing GPU clock-wrap (#1615) and comparison (#825) bugs; the skip is `guest_video_out_wqhd_detection_no_vulkan`.

body:
### What

Add 24 missing C99 numeric exports to libc in a separate translation unit:

- `sqrtf`, `fabsf`, `ceilf`, `truncf`, `nearbyint`.
- `remquo`, `remquof`, `copysign`, `copysignf`.
- `nan`, `nanf`, `nanl`.
- `nextafter`, `nexttoward`, `nexttowardf`.
- `fdim`, `fdimf`, `fmax`, `fmaxf`, `fmin`, `fminf`, `fmaf`.
- `scalbln`, `scalblnf`.

Min/max implement FreeBSD's signed-zero ordering and NaN handling directly, including no new exceptions when selecting the numeric operand against a signaling NaN. Bit classification avoids arithmetic on the NaN operand. `nexttoward` retains the extended-precision target rather than narrowing it to the result type. Neighbor operations normalize missing MinGW overflow/underflow flags and `ERANGE` at representation boundaries.

Guest `long` exponents are 64-bit on Windows too. `scalbln` bounds the exponent before calling the native int-exponent operation; the bounds exceed the full float/double exponent range. Compile only the new implementation and fixture with `-frounding-math`.

Contracts and signatures follow FreeBSD [math(3)](https://man.freebsd.org/cgi/man.cgi?query=math&sektion=3&manpath=FreeBSD+15.0-RELEASE), [fmax(3)](https://man.freebsd.org/cgi/man.cgi?query=fmax&sektion=3&manpath=FreeBSD+14.0-RELEASE), and [scalbn(3)](https://man.freebsd.org/cgi/man.cgi?query=scalbn&sektion=3&manpath=FreeBSD+14.0-RELEASE). All 24 names occur in the [shadPS4 aerolib table](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4/blob/0fe263a4760dfbfa973366890061749b4af0de97/src/core/aerolib/aerolib.inl).

Checked current open PR descriptions, existing exports across libraries, and relevant libc patches in #2193, #2192 and #2167. #2192 implements `nextafterf`; this branch adds `nextafter` and `nexttoward*`. This branch is independent of #2235 and #2271 and excludes their exports. Shared CMake insertion points may need both independent registrations preserved when rebasing.

The progress scanner changes from 2578/3044 (84.69%) to 2602/3068 (84.81%). Both counts grow because these are newly declared exports.

body:
### What

Follow-up to #2083. `nanResultF32` chooses the NaN result of `v_add/sub/mul_f32` and of the f32 fma family (`v_fma/fmac/fmamk/fmaak_f32`, `v_fma_mix_f32` with f32 sources) on the bits: the first NaN source, quieted in IEEE mode, and `0xffc00000` when no source is a NaN; for the fma family the addend is skipped when the product is infinity times zero. That selection and the infinity-times-zero test run for every op, but a NaN source always gives a NaN result, so for any result that isn't a NaN they return the result unchanged.

For the fma family:

- New `FPNanResultFma32(result, lhs, rhs, addend)`, with the IEEE mode as its flag. `nanResultF32` emits it for three sources, so `invalidProductF32` moves into the emitter.
- The SPIR-V emitter tests the result's bits and makes the selection, including the infinity-times-zero test, in a selection taken only when the result is a NaN; otherwise the result passes through. Inside it the rule is #2083's, unchanged.
- The SRT evaluator computes the op exactly; `MaskedSelectEliminator` treats it as lane-local like `FPFma32`.

Add, sub and mul keep #2083's inline selects. With two sources the selection is cheap, and the branch costs more than it saves on NVIDIA: with the same branch for all four, a dependent chain of 1024 `v_add_f32` went from 8.87 to 12.09 ms (best of 4 alternated runs) and `v_mul_f32` showed no clear gain, while `v_fma_f32` went from 25.5 to 19.1 ms.

Results are bit-identical.

### Tested

### What

Implement six missing libc exports: `bcopy`, `index`, `rindex`, `memrchr`, `wcscspn`, and `flsl`.

`bcopy` preserves the BSD source-before-destination argument order and supports overlapping buffers. Reverse searches preserve the last matching address, character-to-byte conversion and the requested memory bounds. `wcscspn` operates on 16-bit guest code units instead of host `wchar_t`. `flsl` accepts a 64-bit guest `long`, including on Windows, and returns a one-based highest-set-bit position or zero for zero.

Contracts follow FreeBSD [bcopy(3)](https://man.freebsd.org/cgi/man.cgi?query=bcopy&sektion=3&manpath=FreeBSD+14.0-RELEASE), [string(3)](https://man.freebsd.org/cgi/man.cgi?query=string&sektion=3&manpath=FreeBSD+14.0-RELEASE), [memchr(3)](https://man.freebsd.org/cgi/man.cgi?query=memchr&sektion=3&manpath=FreeBSD+14.0-RELEASE), [wcscspn(3)](https://man.freebsd.org/cgi/man.cgi?query=wcscspn&sektion=3&manpath=FreeBSD+14.0-RELEASE), and [fls(3)](https://man.freebsd.org/cgi/man.cgi?query=fls&sektion=3&manpath=FreeBSD+14.0-RELEASE). Checked current open PR descriptions and the relevant patches in #2193, #1772 and #1423; no duplicate implementations found. The existing `strcasestr` in libScePosixForWebKit is left with its current owner.

### What
Two lookups inside `Structurize` searched vectors linearly:

- `ControlFlowGraph::Dominates` and `PostDominates` used `std::find` on a block's `dominators` / `postDominators`. Those vectors are always sorted: both analyses end every update with `sortUnique` or `intersectSorted`, and `applyBlockOrder` re-sorts them through `remapIds` after renumbering. They now use `std::binary_search`. The file's `contains` helper is no longer used and is removed.
- `dominatedBlocks` checked whether a block was already visited with `contains(blocks, id)` on the growing result vector, so each call was quadratic in the region size. It now keeps a `std::vector<bool>` indexed by block id. The result is still sorted with `sortUnique` before it is returned.

Nothing else changes, and the structured graph is identical (see below).

**This does not get any title further.** It only makes the structurizer faster. I found it while investigating Hades (PPSA03355), which still crashes at the same place with this change. It is a separate problem: the title's own texture upload pool fills up, which I am still investigating.

### Measured
Hades (PPSA03355 v01.003) on Linux, Ryzen 7 7800X3D. On `main` it stops earlier (#1798, then #861), so the runs below are on `main` + #1798 + #861. Most of the time is spent in `Structurize` for one pixel shader (code `0x3d0087300`, 258 blocks, 511 after `splitSharedMergeBlocks`), on the game's render thread at registration. This is the same path that #2105 speeds up from another side.

| base | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `main` + #1798 + #861 | ~14.4 s | ~13.2 s (−8 %) |
| same + #2105 | ~1.67 s | ~1.06 s (−37 %) |

Two runs per row, timed around `Structurize` in `PrepareResourceProgram` (local instrumentation, not part of this PR). Without #2105, the post-dominator iteration that #2105 fixes takes most of the time, so the gain here is small. With #2105, the lookups changed here are the largest remaining cost: before this change, `dominatedBlocks` alone took ~735 ms of 1.6 s, over 32 386 calls.

The text dump of the structured graph (`GraphToString`, 688 843 bytes) has the same FNV-1a hash (`0782e3d419460587`) in all four configurations.

body:
### What

On Windows, guest `pthread_rwlock_*` locks can fail to exclude. Two threads can hold the write lock at the same time, or a reader can run during a write.

A guest rwlock is a `PthreadRwlockPrivate` holding a `std::shared_timed_mutex`, created lazily on the guest's first call. With MinGW-w64 libstdc++ that mutex wraps a winpthreads `pthread_rwlock_t` set to `PTHREAD_RWLOCK_INITIALIZER`, which winpthreads turns into a real lock on first use. That first use is not safe when it is concurrent ([winpthreads `rwlock.c`](https://github.com/mingw-w64/mingw-w64/blob/master/mingw-w64-libraries/winpthreads/src/rwlock.c)):

- `rwlock_static_init` returns `EINVAL` when it finds the lock already initialized. The second of two threads that both saw the initializer gets `EINVAL` from `pthread_rwlock_wrlock`/`rdlock`.
- `pthread_rwlock_init` stores `NULL` before it publishes the new lock. A thread that reads it in that window also gets `EINVAL`.
- libstdc++'s `shared_timed_mutex::lock()`/`lock_shared()` only `__glibcxx_assert` the result, so in release builds the failed lock returns as if it succeeded.

Standalone, on the project toolchain (GCC 15.2.0 `x86_64-ucrt-posix-seh`), with no AnyPS5 code involved:

- Two threads racing their first `pthread_rwlock_rdlock` on a `PTHREAD_RWLOCK_INITIALIZER` lock: 19,991 of 20,000 rounds returned `EINVAL`.
- Two threads racing their first `lock()` on a new `std::shared_timed_mutex`: both were inside the exclusive section in 1,732 of 20,000 rounds.

The guest rwlock is now locked and unlocked once in its constructor, on the creating thread, before any other thread can reach it, so the winpthreads lock exists before it is contended. `docs/dev/TechnicalDebt.md` records the winpthreads behaviour and the host `std::shared_mutex` objects that remain exposed.

`guest_pthread_rwlock` gets a case where two guest threads race their first `pthread_rwlock_wrlock` on a fresh lock, 500 times, and counts overlapping exclusive sections. On current `main` it fails (3/3 runs). With this change it passes (5/5 runs).

### Tested

Windows 11, MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0, Release/Ninja on upstream main `d70b8998`.

- `guest_pthread_rwlock` as above.
- Full `ctest`: 507/507 pass (1 skipped: `guest_video_out_wqhd_detection_no_vulkan`).
- `tools/check_conventions.py` and `git diff --check` pass.
- A retail Unreal Engine title crashed nondeterministically in its worker threads during loading. A 32-way sharded map protected by `pthread_rwlock` was read while another thread inserted into it. CDB showed the lock's winpthreads handle as `NULL` while a thread was inside its write section. With this change that crash no longer occurs (0 of 2 runs; it had occurred in every run that reached that point).

### What

Linux conversion writes five synthetic program headers but budgets for four. With one retained load and five input slots, the relinker reports success while overwriting 56 bytes immediately after the input header table. With enough slots, PT_PHDR and the header load still describe a table one entry too short.

Count all five synthetic headers, retain PT_GNU_EH_FRAME when it fits exactly, and keep capacity arithmetic wide enough to reject an unrepresentable output count. Extend the existing regression for full header coverage, exact-fit retention, frame removal, adjacent-byte preservation, insufficient capacity, and a count above uint16. Adjust synthetic fixtures that depended on the undercount; the registry fixture also starts its executable load at its code instead of scanning ELF metadata as instructions.

### What

`run()` packed rows with `struct.pack("<4I")` only after `assemble()` had run, so a value below 0 or above `0xffffffff`, a non-integer or a row of the wrong length ended in a `struct.error` with no row number. On the command line, a value `int(v, 0)` cannot parse (`x`, `010`) ended in a traceback, and a row with the wrong number of values printed `every row needs 4 values` without saying which one.

- `run()` checks every row before assembling and raises `ValueError: row N must hold 4 integers from 0 to 0xffffffff`. The check follows the existing float-mode check (`isinstance(value, int) and value in range(...)`), so floats and strings are rejected too.
- `main()` reports the file and line: `rows.txt:3: every row needs 4 u32 values, decimal or 0x hex`.

New tests in `test_hw_oracle.py`:
- Invalid rows (negative, `1 << 32`, 3 or 5 values, float, string, a bad second row) fail before `assemble()` is called, naming the right row.
- The CLI reports the right line for each kind of bad row, past a blank line, and doesn't call `run()`.
- `0`, `0xffffffff`, `4294967295` and `0X0` are still accepted.

body:
### What

Add 43 missing libc `long double` math exports in a dedicated translation unit, preserving the guest x87 extended format rather than narrowing inputs, outputs or pointer results to `double`.

- Trigonometric and hyperbolic: `acosl`, `asinl`, `atanl`, `atan2l`, `tanl`, `acoshl`, `asinhl`, `atanhl`, `coshl`, `sinhl`, `tanhl`.
- Exponentials, logarithms and roots: `expl`, `exp2l`, `expm1l`, `log10l`, `log1pl`, `log2l`, `logbl`, `sqrtl`, `cbrtl`, `hypotl`.
- Arithmetic and rounding: `fabsl`, `copysignl`, `fdiml`, `fmaxl`, `fminl`, `fmal`, `ceill`, `floorl`, `roundl`, `lroundl`, `llroundl`, `nearbyintl`.
- Remainders, neighbors and decomposition: `fmodl`, `remainderl`, `remquol`, `nextafterl`, `nexttowardl`, `frexpl`, `ldexpl`, `modfl`, `scalbnl`, `scalblnl`.

Guest `lroundl` returns 64 bits on Windows through the host `llround` overload. `scalblnl` accepts a 64-bit guest exponent and bounds it before using the native int-exponent operation, avoiding Windows `long` truncation. Bounds exceed the entire representable x87 exponent range.

Normalize native runtime differences found by the tests: signed-zero fractional results for infinite `modfl` inputs; domain/pole exception flags and errno for `acoshl`, `atanhl` and `sqrtl`; and missing overflow/zero-underflow flags for finite exponential/hyperbolic inputs. Preserve FreeBSD signed-zero ordering for `fmaxl`/`fminl`, and normalize neighbor-operation underflow/overflow flags and `ERANGE`. Use `-frounding-math` only for the new implementation and test translation units.

Contracts and signatures follow FreeBSD [fmax(3)](https://man.freebsd.org/cgi/man.cgi?query=fmax&sektion=3&manpath=FreeBSD+14.0-RELEASE), [math(3)](https://man.freebsd.org/cgi/man.cgi?query=math&sektion=3&manpath=FreeBSD+15.0-RELEASE), [modf(3)](https://man.freebsd.org/cgi/man.cgi?query=modf&sektion=3&manpath=FreeBSD+14.0-RELEASE), and [ldexp(3)](https://man.freebsd.org/cgi/man.cgi?query=ldexp&sektion=3&manpath=FreeBSD+14.0-RELEASE). All 43 export names are present in the [shadPS4 aerolib table](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4/blob/0fe263a4760dfbfa973366890061749b4af0de97/src/core/aerolib/aerolib.inl). Transcendental results use native extended-precision math; bit-identical results across host runtimes are not claimed.

### What
Declares 18 exports that the PS5 modules have and no library defined, as throwing stubs:

- libSceVideoOut: the PS4-era `sceVideoOutRegisterBuffers`, `SetBufferAttribute`, `GetBufferLabelAddress`, `SubmitChangeBufferAttribute`, `ModeSetAny_` and `ConfigureOutputMode_`
- libSceAudioOut: `sceAudioOutGetSystemState`, `MasteringInit`, `MasteringGetState`
- libSceImeDialog: `sceImeDialogInitInternal`, `SetPanelPosition`
- libScePad: `scePadGetBluetoothAddress`, `ReadStateExt`, `SetLightBarForTracker`
- libSceSysmodule: `sceSysmoduleGetModuleHandleInternal`, `IsLoadedInternal`
- libSceSystemService: `sceSystemServiceLaunchApp`
- libSceHttp2: `sceHttp2SetPreSendCallback`

Signatures follow shadPS4 and the OpenOrbis headers (PS4); TechnicalDebt names the source of each and records that they are not confirmed for the PS5.

How the functions were chosen: each one is in the PS5 module's export list in [ps5-payload-dev/sdk `sce_stubs`](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk/tree/master/sce_stubs) (generated from firmware `.sprx` exports), its name hashes to the NID shadPS4 registers, no library in `main` defines that NID, and none of the open pull requests adds it (checked against the `APS5_VABI` definitions in the head of every open PR). body:
### What
When an allocation was partially unmapped via `munmap`, `GuestAllocations` split the live pieces and updated their active extents (`address` and `bytes`) while preserving `allocationAddress` and `allocationBytes` for the root OS reservation release. `sceKernelVirtualQuery` previously checked `allocationAddress` and `allocationBytes` instead of `address` and `bytes`.

The resulting wrong extent is structural, not title-specific: `sceKernelVirtualQuery` returned the root reservation bounds for any partially unmapped allocation, reporting unmapped holes as mapped and failing to advance to subsequent pieces under `SCE_KERNEL_VQ_FIND_NEXT`.

Commercial title import evidence:
- PPSA26344 imports `sceKernelVirtualQuery` from `libkernel.prx` (NID `rVjRvHJ0X6c`).

Update `sceKernelVirtualQuery` to inspect `address` and `bytes`, returning `SCE_KERNEL_ERROR_EACCES` for unmapped addresses and correctly locating the next live segment when `SCE_KERNEL_VQ_FIND_NEXT` is passed.

Closes #1894

body:
### What

`ElfReader::ReadHeader` checks the magic but reads all remaining fields using the ELF64 layout and host byte order regardless of `EI_CLASS`, `EI_DATA` and `EI_VERSION`. Linux conversion accepts a synthetic image declaring ELF32, big-endian encoding or an invalid identification version, and writes an executable and registry.

Require ELF64, little-endian encoding and identification version 1 before reading the remaining header fields. These identification bytes define how the file is interpreted in the [ELF gABI](https://gabi.xinuos.com/elf/02-eheader.html#elf-identification). The check also runs before `--to-intel` processing. Windows already rejects these inputs later in `WindowsLoadImage`; the shared check now rejects them before registry output.

Extend the registered `elf_header` regression with 36 unsupported-identification cases and eight valid controls. It covers Linux and Windows output, with and without `--to-intel`, using the existing executable fixture. Invalid, unsupported and reserved values for each identification byte must exit 2 with the diagnostic and write neither executable nor registry; input bytes must stay unchanged. ELF64 little-endian inputs with System V and FreeBSD OSABI values still convert to the requested output format.

### Tested

Windows x64, WinLibs MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0 UCRT POSIX SEH r7, Ninja Release, Python 3.12.14. Based on upstream `d70b8998`; contribution `a213a26b`.

```text
cmake -S . -B build-relinker -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DANYPS5_RELINKER_ONLY=ON -DBUILD_TESTING=ON
cmake --build build-relinker --parallel 4
ctest --test-dir build-relinker --output-on-failure --timeout 120 --no-tests=error --parallel 2
python tools/check_test_registration.py build-relinker
python tools/check_conventions.py --base origin/main
git diff origin/main --check
```

With only the regression added to upstream `d70b8998`, the registered test fails: `ident-4-0` returns 0 and writes an executable and registry. The two-line fix passes the focused test in 2.78 seconds, including the existing short-file and magic diagnostics.

### What

Registered type-2 NGG vertex programs that use LDS or `s_barrier` were prepared as ordinary vertex shaders. A wave64 program reading lane 63 therefore failed on a 32-lane host subgroup, although the existing mesh path supports its workgroup storage and cross-lane operations.

Defer these programs' registration preparation until primitive and routing state are available. Share the workgroup decision between static graphics ABI resolution and draw decoding, and extend #1825's mesh routing to registered programs. Legacy vertex, geometry, tessellation and NGG passthrough routing retain their existing paths. Reserved program-address bits and misaligned registered entries throw.

**Depends on #1825** (which includes #1732). The branch is based on main `d70b89989473ba1f6ae13e44e079e67f1f8a44b0` and includes the seven prerequisite commits with their original authors and cherry-pick trailers. The additional registered-program change is commit `029b2e415`; this draft should wait for its dependency before merging.

Workgroup use follows Mesa's [NGG shared-memory and barrier lowering](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Mesa/blob/b3588f78dd7fd46fbadc7ecd487e5f14d4213e4b/src/amd/common/nir/ac_nir_lower_ngg.c#L1135). Their shared `SourceHandleFor`/`InvocationFor` edits must retain #1732's raw-graphics preparation and this branch's registered NGG routing, alongside each new deferral/call-capture/diagnostic behavior and its failure tests. #2325's reported conflict is only an adjacent TechnicalDebt insertion; preserve both entries. body:
### What

`sceKernelRename` returned `ENOENT` for a missing source and `EIO` for every other failure. On Windows the rename itself also went wrong: MinGW's `std::filesystem::rename` reports some missing paths as `EIO` and refuses to replace an existing empty directory, which FreeBSD's `rename(2)` does. Measured on `main` (`d70b8998`) with libstdc++'s `std::filesystem::rename` (generic category):

| Case | Windows `std::filesystem::rename` | `sceKernelRename` on `main` | FreeBSD `rename(2)` |
|---|---|---|---|
| source missing, target missing | `EIO` | `ENOENT` | `ENOENT` |
| target's directory missing | `EIO` | `EIO` | `ENOENT` |
| target's directory is a file | | `EIO` | `ENOTDIR` |
| directory onto a file | | `EIO` | `ENOTDIR` |
| file onto a directory | | `EIO` | `EISDIR` |
| directory onto a non-empty directory | `EACCES` | `EIO` | `ENOTEMPTY` |
| directory into its own subtree | `EIO` | `EIO` | `EINVAL` |
| directory onto an empty directory | `EACCES` | fails with `EIO` | replaces it |

`RenameError_nid_no_patch` checks these `rename(2)` conditions before renaming and returns the guest error, the way `sceKernelRmdir` already checks its own. On Windows it removes the empty target directory first, so the replace succeeds as on the console. A rename onto the same file, including a case-only rename on Windows, still goes straight to `std::filesystem::rename`. Any other host failure is still `EIO`.

libc's `rename` has the same Windows behaviour (it calls `std::filesystem::rename` too). I left it alone because #1192 is moving that function into a new file; I can send the same fix for it afterwards.

### Tested

Windows 11, WinLibs GCC 15.2.0 r7, Release, `-DBUILD_TESTING=ON`:

- New `sceKernelRename` checks in `guest_filesystem_tests`, next to the libc `rename` checks:
  - every row of the table, checked against the exact `0x8002xxxx` codes;
  - a failed rename leaves the source tree in place;
  - file replace keeps the moved contents;
  - renaming a file onto itself still succeeds;
  - directory onto an empty directory replaces it with its contents.

  On `main` the test fails on the first new check (`guest errno 5`).
- Mutation check: dropping the Windows empty-directory removal, or the subtree `EINVAL` check, each make `guest_filesystem` fail.
- `ctest -E "^agc_|video_out"`: 249/249 passed, including `guest_kernel_sync`, which renames through `sceKernelRename`.
- `tools/check_conventions.py` passes, and `tools/pr_overlap.py --branch` reports no overlap. It also merges cleanly with #1192, #2170, #2115, #1620, #2129 and #2086, which touch the same files (`git merge-tree`).

body:
### What
A GLC/DLC global load is translated as a `Volatile` load through a physical-storage pointer. Under the GLSL450 memory model, `Volatile` doesn't make another workgroup's stores visible within the same dispatch. On NVIDIA, a workgroup that spins on a flag written by another workgroup never sees the store.

This is the pattern of decoupled look-back prefix scans. RADV's acceleration-structure build uses it (the radix sort), and vkQuake (PPSA99010) triggers that build with `r_rtshadows`. Under AnyPS5 the scan spins until the GPU is lost (`VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST`), or spins silently.

When the non-faulting BDA probe gives a coherent dword read a non-null, 4-byte-aligned physical address, `SpirvBdaRead.cpp` now emits `OpAtomicLoad` at `ScopeDevice` with relaxed semantics instead of `OpLoad ... Volatile`. That covers the wide path in `EmitBdaDwordReads` and the coherent single-dword helper in `DefineBdaDwordReadFunctions`. Unaligned addresses, unmapped addresses and reads that span two BDA ranges still take the existing byte path, which reports faults exactly as before. With byte reads forced (no probe), nothing changes. Non-coherent loads are unchanged.

Tests:
- New `tests/execution/CrossWorkgroupFlag.cpp`: 25 hand-assembled GFX10 words, two workgroups. Workgroup 0 stores a flag with `global_store_dword glc`. Workgroup 1 spins on `global_load_dword glc dlc` and writes 2 if it sees the flag, or 3 after a 1M-iteration bailout, so a failure can't hang the GPU. It runs as wave64 and wave32. A control run with the flag preset by the CPU checks the harness itself.
  - NVIDIA without this change: result 3 (gave up) for both wave sizes. With it: 2.
  - lavapipe passes with and without the change.

This conflicts textually with #1267, which reworks the same read sites; I'll rebase onto whichever lands first.

### Tested
Windows 11 Pro (26200), MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0 (WinLibs r7), Release, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti (driver 610.88).

- Full local suite: 508 tests, 506 passed, 1 skipped; `guest_sce_net` timed out (it times out locally on unrelated branches too, likely my network filtering). It was run from the generated `CTestTestfile.cmake` commands because antivirus blocks `ctest.exe` on this machine.
- `tools/check_conventions.py --base origin/main` passes.
- `CrossWorkgroupFlag` fails on this NVIDIA GPU without the change and passes with it; lavapipe passes either way.
- vkQuake (PPSA99010) on my local test branch (current `main` plus my open RADV PRs and local stubs): the GPU hang during RADV's BVH build went away. The build's output is still wrong for a separate reason I haven't found yet, so `r_rtshadows` doesn't work yet.

Not tested on Linux or macOS.

body:
### What

A shader whose code does not decode ended the whole title. The decode ran outside the `try`/`catch` that
#1836 added for shaders that cannot be prepared at registration, so one instruction this decoder does not
know reached the top and terminated the process.

Ghost of Yōtei (**PPSA26344**) hits it: `unsupported MIMG opcode 229` (0xE5) — issue **#1941**.

The decode now sits in the same deferral path, but only for the failure class that is a *capability gap*: a
new `ShaderRecompiler::UnsupportedInstructionError`, thrown when a family the decoder understands contains an
opcode it does not. Everything else — an unknown instruction family, a truncated instruction, reserved
control bits — still throws exactly as before, so the existing contract that registering corrupt code fails
loudly is unchanged (and remains covered at `tests/execution/PreparedShaders.cpp:239`).

**What this does not do: it does not implement `0xE5`.** The opcode is still unidentified — it is absent from
LLVM's gfx1013 tables, from LLVM's MC tests for that part, and from sharpemu's decoder, yet it appears 38
times in this title's own shader store (see #1941 for that evidence). The affected shaders are deferred with
the opcode named in the reason, and they still throw when a draw actually needs them.

### Tested

Linux, RTX 3080 Ti.

- `agc_driver_prepared_shaders_tests` — the full run passes, including the corrupt-code registration case that
  must keep failing.
- `agc_driver_prepared_shaders_tests --deferred-undecodable` — new mode, passes. It registers a shader whose
  second word is the image instruction this title carries and checks that the failure surfaces on use rather
  than at registration. **Honest limitation:** it passes with and without the registry change (both paths
  surface the same message; only the log line differs), so it documents the behaviour rather than guarding
  it. The discriminating evidence is the title run below.
- **PPSA26344, before/after on one stack** (`#757` + `#1836` + the aperture decode):
  - before: `terminate … unsupported MIMG opcode 229`, exit 134, during shader preparation;
  - after: `Shader 0x… could not be prepared at registration (unsupported MIMG opcode 229); preparing it
    when it is used` for the affected shaders, and the title carries on instead of aborting.
- The failure is reproducible **offline** from the title's own shader store (`cache_ps5/all_shaders.xpps`,
  code word 260), which is how the test fixture was checked before it was written.

body:
### What

`EhFrameReader::Read` checks the segment boundary inside the FDE table loop. When the decoded count is zero, that loop never runs: a truncated `PT_GNU_EH_FRAME` header can consume bytes beyond its declared size and still be accepted. A synthetic header declaring one byte currently relinks successfully.

Reject a segment shorter than the four encoding bytes, and reject a decoded header whose cursor exceeds the declared segment size before using its count. The [LSB definition of PT_GNU_EH_FRAME](https://refspecs.linuxfoundation.org/LSB_5.0.0/LSB-Core-generic/LSB-Core-generic/progheader.html) specifies the location and size of `.eh_frame_hdr`.

The shared reader is used by strict NID filtering (`unused-filter=2`) and Windows TLS code analysis. Ordinary Linux conversion with filtering disabled does not use this reader and is outside this change.

Extend the registered `linux_eh_frame_header` integration test with fixed-width and ULEB128 headers. Every shorter nonempty segment must exit 2 with the new diagnostic, leave the input unchanged and write no executable. Complete headers must still convert. The matrix covers 44 rejection cases and four valid controls across Linux strict filtering and Windows conversion.

This is independent of #2245's signed LEB128 overflow check and #1944's LSDA handling. `git merge-tree` combines this branch with each of them without conflicts. No dependency.

### Tested

Windows x64, WinLibs MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0 UCRT POSIX SEH r7, Ninja Release, Python 3.12.14. Based on upstream `d70b8998`; contribution `ec5a2019`.

```text
cmake -S . -B build-relinker -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DANYPS5_RELINKER_ONLY=ON -DBUILD_TESTING=ON
cmake --build build-relinker --parallel 4
ctest --test-dir build-relinker --output-on-failure --timeout 120 --no-tests=error --parallel 2
python tools/check_test_registration.py build-relinker
python tools/check_conventions.py --base origin/main
git diff origin/main --check
```

All 40 registered test groups passed in 70.14 seconds. Registration, conventions and whitespace checks passed. The focused regression took 1.57 seconds. The existing `tls_function_coverage` test took 64.66 seconds in the full run; no repository timeout was changed.

With only the regression added to upstream `d70b8998`, the registered test fails because `bounds-linux-strict-fixed-1` returns 0 and writes an executable. With the three-line fix it passes, including all 44 malformed inputs and the four valid controls.

GitHub Actions passed Conventions and the relinker build/test matrix on Windows, Linux and macOS for `ec5a2019`: [Build run](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/actions/runs/37936625723), [Conventions run](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/actions/runs/37936625455). The full Linux and Windows build jobs were skipped under the repository's pull-request policy. System-library builds and game/PS5 tests were not run locally.

body:
### What
On Windows, a host import of shared guest memory goes through a read-write alias from `WindowsMappings::MapAlias`. The alias was a single `MapViewOfFile3` of one section, so `MapAlias` threw when the views of the range were not one contiguous run of that section or spanned several sections:

```
read-write alias of shared guest memory 0x…+0x…: the range is not one contiguous run of views of a section
```

`importAllocation` does not catch it, so the title aborts. Two layouts give such ranges:
- one `sceKernelMapDirectMemory` over two adjacent direct memory allocations: each allocation has its own section (`CreateDirectMemoryBacking`), `AddMapping` maps each one, and the mapping is one registered range;
- pages remapped in place (`MAP_FIXED`) to physical pages in another order. Each remap leaves its own registered range, and `importAllocation` imports one registered range at a time, so no host import on `main` asks for this alias yet.

fpPS4's PS4 kernel reimplementation (branch `kern`) accepts a direct memory mapping whose physical range is allocated without gaps and with one `m_acl` (`_dmem_map_test`, [L930-L984](https://github.com/red-prig/fpPS4/blob/76b1a070030e230f70e6548384e3220e56a1a8f2/sys/vm/dmem_map.pas#L930-L984)), and merges neighbouring allocations with equal attributes (`dmem_map_simplify_entry`, [L1198-L1235](https://github.com/red-prig/fpPS4/blob/76b1a070030e230f70e6548384e3220e56a1a8f2/sys/vm/dmem_map.pas#L1198-L1235)). [shadPS4's `MapMemory`](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4/blob/0fe263a4760dfbfa973366890061749b4af0de97/src/core/memory.cpp#L536-L555) also walks several direct memory areas in one call. Neither is a hardware measurement, and this is not verified on PS5.

Such ranges are now aliased run by run: a placeholder reservation is split at each run of consecutive pages of one section, and each run maps that section at its offset with `MEM_REPLACE_PLACEHOLDER`, the mechanism `Map` uses for guest pages. Two adjacent allocations give two views. `UnmapAlias` unmaps every run and forgets the alias even when one unmap fails. A contiguous range keeps the single view.

Left as before:
- a range with a page that is not a shared view, such as flexible memory, is still refused;
- `importAllocation` still imports one registered range at a time; imports of views spanning several registered ranges are not added here.

### Tested
Windows 11 Pro, Intel Core i7-12700K, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070, 32 GB, MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0.
- `guest_memory` (`core/libs/tests/GuestMemory.cpp`; the three new checks are Windows only):
  - `CheckAliasAcrossDirectAllocations`: allocations of 32 KiB and 16 KiB, adjacent and mapped with one call. The alias has one view per allocation, reads and writes all three pages, and unmapping it frees them;
  - `CheckAliasOfReorderedSharedPages`: two pages remapped in reverse physical order. The alias reads and writes both;
  - `CheckAliasRefusesPagesThatAreNotSharedViews`: a range whose second page is flexible memory is still refused.

  On `main`, each of the first two fails with the message above (address aside); the third passes on both.
- `agc_driver_dcc_keys_first_write` (also maps an alias), `agc_write_watch_coverage`, `agc_driver_typed_heaps`, `guest_heap_rounding_overflow` and `application_heap_*` pass.
- `tools/check_conventions.py --base origin/main` passes.
- Poppy Playtime: Chapter 4 (PPSA25063) aborted once with this error in a presentation compute shader (`0x3008540000+0x400000`), in a local build that also imports buffer views spanning several registered ranges, which this PR does not add. The log does not show whether that range was one registered range or several. With an earlier revision of this change (one view per page) in that build, the title reaches gameplay and the error did not recur in 12 later runs. The error was rare, and the logs do not show whether an alias of several views was created, so this does not show that the change prevents it.
- Not tested:
  - this revision (one view per run) in any title; the Poppy runs above used the one-view-per-page revision with other local changes;
  - a Vulkan host import of an alias made of several views (a failed import falls back to copies);
  - the rollback when mapping a run fails, and an unmap that fails (the alias is still forgotten);
  - Linux (the change is Windows only).
