body:
### What
Every draw copies its index range and each of its vertex ranges out of guest memory into a new host buffer (`CopyDrawInput`) before the GPU can read them. A range that lies in a host import is now bound from the import itself, at its offset in it. That's also how the console reads them: the input assembler fetches straight from guest memory, with no copy step.

- A range is bound in place only when nothing could still write over it: no recorded or in-flight GPU write after the pending results are flushed (the same `FlushGpuWrites` the copy does, which waits for such a write), no completion label, no queued label store, no copied buffer a dispatch or draw writes back. Otherwise it's copied as before.
- Its offset in the import has to suit the reader: a multiple of the index size for indices, and for vertices the strictest format alignment of the attributes that share the range. A copy starts its range at offset 0, so only an in-place range can end up misaligned; `PlanVertexCopies` now records that alignment per range (`VertexCopyPlan::alignments`).
- The read is noted on the batch (`Recorder::ReadKind::DrawInput`), so a CPU store into the range waits for the draw like the other in-place readers, and the barrier validation sees it. The import's buffer stays alive until the batch completes the same way it does for those readers (`retireImport`).
- Host imports gain `VERTEX_BUFFER` and `INDEX_BUFFER` usage.

#1968, #1969 and #1769 change the same loops in `prepareDrawInputs` (the index scan, and zero buffers for some V#s). They don't do what this does, but whichever lands first, the other needs a rebase. With #1968 the in-place index scan should use its `HighestDrawIndex` too, and I'll do that if it merges first.

### PPSA36082
Hades II issues thousands of small draws a frame from vertex and index data in GPU-mapped memory. On main f1451396 with the fixes it needs to reach gameplay, it ran at about 2 fps, and the frame time went to copying draw inputs. With this change it ran at 27-30 fps in the same scene (MangoHud). This exact commit, on current main with the rest of what Hades needs (including #1810), runs gameplay at 40-45 fps with no skipped draws, so the alignment check doesn't cost it anything.

### Tested
Linux (CachyOS), x86-64, GCC, 7800X3D / RTX 4090.
- `agc_driver_graphics` (new checks): a merged vertex range takes the strictest alignment of its attributes.
- `agc_driver_recorder_tests` (new `drawInputInPlaceTests`, over a write-watched block registered and imported like the other draw input tests):
  - An aligned imported range is bound in place, and its read is noted on the open batch as a draw input read. It's gone once the batch completes.
  - A range misaligned for its format is copied; the same range is bound in place for a 2-byte reader.
  - A range under a pending GPU write is bound only after the write completed.
  - A range under a queued label store is copied; a disjoint range still binds in place.
  - Memory without an import, and a draw without a recorder, are copied.
- `agc_driver_recorder_tests` isn't registered with ctest (it's in `KNOWN_UNRUN`), so I ran it by hand. All its checks before `storageRefreshTests` pass; that one fails with "the refresh's store of the results did not reach guest memory", the same as on main without this change.
- Mutations, each failing a check: alignment ignored, queued label stores ignored, read not noted, a range keeping its first attribute's alignment, an import bound without a recorder.
- The linux job of current `build.yml` run locally (SPIRV tools on, test registration check, build, libs, ctest) on this head, which is current main d70b8998 plus this commit: 515/516. The one failure is `agc_driver_dcc_keys_first_write`, which fails the same way on main without this change on this machine (RTX 4090) and passes in GitHub's CI.

### What

On a host whose kernel has no IPv6, `socket(AF_INET6)` fails with `EAFNOSUPPORT`, so `guest_sce_net` aborted at its first IPv6 socket in `CheckUnspecifiedIpv6` and never ran the TCP, UDP, epoll, `sceNetSendmsg`/`sceNetRecvmsg`, resolver and NetCtl checks after it.

### What

`agc_driver_shader_clock` failed in a parallel ctest run with `memtime: lane 24 went back from 4294921902 to 3823`. llvmpipe builds the high dword of the shader clock with a left shift: `emit_clock` in Mesa's [`src/gallium/auxiliary/gallivm/lp_bld_nir_soa.c`](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/-/blob/main/src/gallium/auxiliary/gallivm/lp_bld_nir_soa.c) does `LLVMBuildShl(builder, result, 32)` and then truncates to 32 bits, so the high dword is always 0 (unchanged in Mesa `main` of 2026-10-07). `s_memtime` and `s_memrealtime` therefore wrap every 2^32 ns (about 4.3 s) at subgroup and device scope alike, and a pass whose two reads straddle a wrap fails.

On llvmpipe the test now compares the two reads' low dwords modulo 2^32, which stays correct if Mesa fixes the shift; every other device keeps the 64-bit comparison. The host limitation is recorded in TechnicalDebt next to the RADV `s_memtime` entry.

### Tested
Ubuntu 24.04, GCC 13.3, lavapipe (Mesa 25.2.8, LLVM 20).
- Printing the raw reads on llvmpipe: the high dword of both clocks is always 0 and the low dword counts nanoseconds.
- Dispatching right before a 2^32 ns boundary (32 passes sweeping the lead time) to force the wrap: on `745b775e`, 24 lanes read a wrapped clock; the 64-bit comparison rejects all 24 and the modular one none (on `a8b032b2`: 32 of 32 and none).

body:
### What

`nid_patcher` turns the `_nid_postfix` names of a library into NIDs for ELF and PE. This adds Mach-O, so that a library built on macOS gets its NIDs too. It is the piece of the macOS port that `ninja libs` needs there; the build changes that use it come in separate PRs. Nothing changes for ELF and PE.

- A Mach-O dylib keeps its exports in a dyld export trie and its imports in the chained fixups, so the patcher works on those. The trie is read, every exported C name (without Mach-O's leading underscore) is resolved to its NID, and the trie is rebuilt the way ld64 lays it out: node offsets are uleb128, so the layout is repeated until it is stable. A trie that no longer fits is appended to `__LINKEDIT`, which has to end the file, and a signed image is refused.
- Weak definitions that are not marked `_nid_postfix` or `_nid_no_patch` keep their names, because dyld coalesces those across images by name.
- In the chained imports, names bound to a `.prx` dylib that are guest facing (a `_nid_postfix` name or an `sce` prefix) are patched in place. A name that would grow, or that shares storage with another import, is an error. An image that uses bind opcodes instead of chained fixups is refused.
- `--preserve-exports` reads a reference Mach-O the way it reads ELF and PE references.

### Tested

- New test `nid_patcher_macho`: builds small Mach-O dylibs byte by byte and runs `nid_patcher` on them. It checks the rebuilt export trie (including a weak export that must stay), the patched and untouched chained imports, a trie that grows and is appended to `__LINKEDIT`, `--preserve-exports`, and the three refusals (signed image, bind opcodes, an import NID longer than its name). It needs no macOS. I also ran it against two copies of the patcher with a deliberate break each (no import patching, weak exports patched), and both fail it.
- macOS 26.5 (M5 Max): the patcher turns all 121 libraries of the macOS port into the same bytes the port builds, checked with `cmp`, and the port's `patched_libraries` test loads them all.
- Linux and Windows: the full build and `ctest`, run by manual dispatch on my fork: https://github.com/mugurc/AnyPS5/actions/runs/37931715161 (Linux 508 of 508, Windows 517 of 517, `nid_patcher_macho` included). The relinker jobs on a pull request do not build `nid_patcher`, so they do not cover this change.
- No commercial title was tested; I have no PS5.

body:
### What

When a queue worker fails, `Driver::run` calls `ReportFailure(error)` and only then calls `Fail` on the flips of the submission it was executing. `ReportFailure` publishes the failure and wakes the idle waiters, so a thread returning from `AgcDriverWaitIdle` with the failure can still see one of those flips neither completed nor failed. `agc_driver_flip` hits this in `testFailure`: `failed flip was completed successfully`.

This fails the executing submission's flips first, as `ReportFailure` already does for the pending submissions it drops before it notifies. One line moved in `QueueWorker.cpp`.

The only `IFlipRequest::Fail` outside the tests (VideoOut's `FlipRequest::Fail`) takes only its own config mutex and does not call into the driver, and the only `AgcDriverWaitIdle` call outside the guest is the VideoOut constructor, before its threads start, so failing the flips first cannot deadlock.

body:
### What

`EhFrameReader::leb` accepts a tenth-byte payload of `1` for both unsigned and signed 64-bit LEB128. In the signed case, nine `0x80` bytes followed by `0x01` encode positive 2^63, which does not fit in `int64_t`. The reader accepts it and returns the bit pattern of `INT64_MIN`.

Use separate overflow limits: the tenth payload may be `0` or `0x7F` for SLEB128, and `0` or `1` for ULEB128. This matches the [LLVM 20.1.8 decoder](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/llvmorg-20.1.8/llvm/include/llvm/Support/LEB128.h#L169-L171). The existing error reports malformed unwind data instead of silently accepting the overflow.

Add a regression to the registered `strict_nid_filter` test. It reads a complete EH frame header, CIE and FDE through `ReadExceptionFunctions`. The fixture checks all 128 terminating payloads with two prefixes, in signed and unsigned CIE fields: 512 boundary combinations plus a normal short encoding. Accepted encodings must preserve the function range and targets; rejected ones must produce the overflow diagnostic.

This is independent of #1944, which changes LSDA handling in the same reader. `git merge-tree` combines the two branches without conflicts. No dependency.

### Tested

Windows x64, WinLibs MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0 UCRT POSIX SEH r7, Ninja Release, Python 3.12.14. Based on upstream `d70b8998`; contribution `682d6f62`.

```text
cmake -S . -B build-relinker -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DANYPS5_RELINKER_ONLY=ON -DBUILD_TESTING=ON
cmake --build build-relinker --parallel 4
ctest --test-dir build-relinker --output-on-failure --timeout 120 --no-tests=error --parallel 2
python tools/check_test_registration.py build-relinker
python tools/check_conventions.py --base origin/main
git diff origin/main --check
```

All 40 registered test groups passed. Registration, conventions and whitespace checks passed. `strict_nid_filter` took 0.28 seconds. The existing `tls_function_coverage` test took 67.63 seconds; no repository timeout was changed.

With only the regression added to the original implementation, `strict_nid_filter` fails with `Overflowing CIE LEB128 value was accepted`. It passes with the one-line fix.

body:
### What

`patched_libraries` (added in #1828) calls `LoadLibraryExW` on each patched `.prx`. On Windows, when one of them has an import the loader cannot resolve, the loader shows its "Entry Point Not Found" message box, and `LoadLibraryExW` does not return until someone closes it. The test then waits on the dialog until ctest's timeout (300 s) and reports `Timeout` instead of naming the libraries that failed.

The test now calls `SetErrorMode(SEM_FAILCRITICALERRORS)` at start on Windows, as `GuestHeapRounding.cpp` already does. The loader then returns the error to the caller instead of showing the box. Microsoft documents this for `LoadLibraryEx`: "To enable or disable error messages displayed by the loader during DLL loads, use the `SetErrorMode` function." `SEM_FAILCRITICALERRORS` is described as: "The system does not display the critical-error-handler message box. Instead, the system sends the error to the calling process." The Linux path is unchanged.

### Tested

Windows 11, WinLibs GCC 15.2.

I hit this by accident. An unrelated program's old `libstdc++-6.dll` (2021) sits in my system `PATH` ahead of WinLibs'. The patched libraries resolved their `libstdc++-6.dll` import to it, and it lacks `_ZNKSt25__codecvt_utf8_utf16_baseIwE10do_unshiftER9_MbstatetPcS3_RS3_`.

- After, with the same `PATH`: no dialog. The test exits 1 after 1.3 s, printing each failing library (`libkernel.prx: LoadLibraryEx failed with error 127`, ...) and `14 patched libraries loaded, 102 failed`.

body:
### What

Windows conversion only patches guest TLS accesses (`mov %fs:0x0, ...`) in instructions that code analysis reaches. #1117 added roots for code that no root reaches. A function whose only reference is a 64-bit RIP-relative `LEA` is still missed: a constructor, callback or thread entry whose address is stored and later called indirectly. Its TLS access stays unpatched, and the first call reads `FS:0` as a null pointer on Windows.

A REX.W `LEA` with a RIP-relative displacement that resolves to executable code now adds that target as a code root. This applies both in the main instruction walk and while following the control-flow graph of unreached code. `BuildControlFlowGraph` gets an opt-in `followCodeAddresses` flag for the second case. Existing callers keep their behaviour.

A new `tls_function_coverage` case, `address-taken-tls-callback`, puts a TLS access in a function that is only reached through `lea rax, [rip+fn]; call rax`. It fails on current `main` (the access is not rewritten to a jump) and passes with this change.

### Tested

Windows 11, MinGW-w64 GCC (project toolchain), Release/Ninja on upstream main `d70b8998`.

- `tls_function_coverage` passes; on unchanged production code the new case fails with `AssertionError: address-taken-tls-callback`.

- `tools/check_conventions.py` and `git diff --check` pass.
- A retail Unreal Engine title: converted with current `main`, the title crashes early with a null read at a raw `mov %fs:0x0, %rax` in a function installed by address (`OutputDeviceRedirector` thread). With this change that site is patched and startup continues.

body:
### What

`sceKernelReleaseDirectMemory` and `sceKernelCheckedReleaseDirectMemory` free the physical pages and forget their direct mappings, but the virtual ranges that mapped them stay registered as guest allocations. A later `sceKernelVirtualQuery` then reports those ranges as committed flexible memory at offset 0.

A title that frees GPU memory by walking a virtual range with `FIND_NEXT` and releasing `offset + (start - info.start)` for each region it finds then frees physical offset 0. That stops with `direct memory range 0x0+0x200000 references unallocated physical page 0x0`.

With this change, releasing direct memory also unmaps every virtual view of the released pages, aliases included, so the range is free afterwards. The views are collected before the pages are freed and unmapped through the existing `UnmapRegistered` path. The checked variant unmaps only when the release succeeds.

This follows shadPS4's `MemoryManager::Free`, which releases "any dmem mappings that reference this physical block": https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4/blob/main/src/core/memory.cpp

`CheckReleaseDirectMemoryClearsMappings` asserted the old behaviour, where a fully released mapping still answered queries. It now checks that both the mapping and a second alias stop answering queries, and that `FIND_NEXT` from them does not return them. It no longer depends on how a hole inside an allocation is reported, which #1731 changes.

### Tested

Windows 11, MinGW-w64 GCC (project toolchain), Release/Ninja on upstream main `d70b8998`.

- `guest_memory` passes with the change. On unchanged production code the updated test fails at the released-mapping query (`GuestMemory.cpp:288`).

body:
### What

Implement nine libc exports: `rint`, `rintf`, `rintl`, `lrint`, `lrintf`, `lrintl`, `llrint`, `llrintf`, and `llrintl`.

The functions honor the active floating-point rounding mode and preserve floating-point exception behavior. Guest `long` results use the host `llrint` overloads to retain 64-bit values on Windows. Extended-precision overloads retain the guest x87 `long double` representation. Compile only this translation unit with `-frounding-math`; without it GCC's optimized `rint` gives incorrect negative results under directed rounding.

Behavior references: FreeBSD [rint(3)](https://man.freebsd.org/cgi/man.cgi?manpath=FreeBSD+15.0-RELEASE&query=rint&sektion=3) and [lrint(3)](https://man.freebsd.org/cgi/man.cgi?manpath=FreeBSD+14.0-RELEASE&query=lrint&sektion=3). Export names are present in the [shadPS4 aerolib table](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4/blob/0fe263a4760dfbfa973366890061749b4af0de97/src/core/aerolib/aerolib.inl).

body:
### What

`Buffer` and `DeviceBuffer` created their `VkBuffer` at the pool's size class (`BufferPool::Capacity`: the next power of two, at least 256 bytes), not at the size the caller asked for. With `robustBufferAccess`, a shader read past the requested size therefore stayed inside the `VkBuffer` and returned whatever an earlier user of the pooled memory left there, instead of an out-of-range result (zero or a value inside the buffer).

Each `VkBuffer` now has exactly the requested size, bound to memory sized for the class so the allocation stays reusable. `BufferAllocation` records the size its `VkBuffer` was created with (`bufferBytes`). A buffer taken from the pool for a different size gets a new `VkBuffer` over the same memory, and a same-size reuse keeps the existing one.

Open PR #1896 also changes `BufferPool.cpp`, but only its eviction bookkeeping; it doesn't touch these functions.

### Tested

Windows 11, RTX 5070 (driver 595.x), MinGW-w64 GCC, Release, `BUILD_TESTING=ON`.

- New execution test `agc_driver_pooled_buffer_range`:
  - A 256-byte buffer is filled with `0xabababab` and released. A 100-byte buffer then takes the same pooled memory, and a compute shader reads word 28 (byte 112) through a `VK_WHOLE_SIZE` storage descriptor with `robustBufferAccess` enabled. On `main` this returns `0xabababab`, the earlier user's bytes; with the fix it returns zero or a value inside the buffer.
  - The test also checks the size of every `vkCreateBuffer`: fresh, pooled-at-another-size and same-size-reused `Buffer` and `DeviceBuffer`.
  - Fails on `main` (`d70b8998`), passes with this change.
- `ctest -R "^agc_driver"`: 213/213 pass with this change.
- Minecraft Dungeons II (PPSA16064, UE5) title screen, with the other changes that title needs: same capture points with and without this change. No visible difference on the title (its visible symptoms of this bug, translucent blocks and texture noise, came together with the stride-0 fetch fixed in #1769), and no regression.

body:
### What

Guest code can now start an export session, import JPEG/PNG/GIF images from a guest file or a data-provider callback, import an explicit image thumbnail, and finish the session. The five exports previously threw unconditionally. Imports preserve source bytes and publish media plus metadata into a persistent host catalog that a separate content-search change can query.

The catalog lives under the launch root's `/data/anyps5-content`. Each successful import receives its own guest-readable path. An exclusive pending directory reserves the content ID; complete media and metadata are published by directory rename. Native file locks serialize publication and catalog snapshots across processes. A generation assigned at publication advances the update ID even when two exports finish in the opposite order from their start.

Guest allocator callbacks supply the streaming copy buffer and receive their original user data. Callback imports enforce the declared byte total and the 0/more, 1/done protocol; malformed callbacks, allocation failures and failed imports leave the output and published catalog unchanged. Live sessions enforce the ten-execution limit, and an active callback cannot finish, terminate or reenter its own session.

Scope: image imports. PNG/JPEG use the existing source-built decoders; GIF uses the existing stb submodule and validates its first frame. Video imports and nonzero bytes in the ambiguous reserved/comment field throw. Automatic thumbnails, console gallery notifications and sharing are not implemented. Host storage paths, session-limit application, error precedence and all recovered ABI contracts remain unverified on PS5 hardware; these gaps are recorded in TechnicalDebt.

ABI evidence:

- [Orbital PS4 signature database](https://github.com/AlexAltea/orbital/blob/cc408367da6a6ebbf5ac1ac559fefeadc73b2831/tools/ida/db_types.json): all five export signatures.

Its middle 257 bytes are called `comment`; SharpProspero calls them reserved, so a nonzero value throws.

body:
### What
A depth surface is a host image that AnyPS5 clears once, when it creates the image, to the DB_DEPTH_CLEAR value it sees then. RADV (and real hardware) clears depth differently: it doesn't touch the depth memory, it rewrites the HTILE metadata so every tile reads as "cleared" (ZMASK = 0), and the DB returns DB_DEPTH_CLEAR for those tiles. AnyPS5 doesn't model HTILE, so after the first frame the host depth image is never cleared again.

vkQuake (PPSA99010, the homebrew Vulkan port, through RADV) shows this as a black 3D view. It uses reverse Z (GREATER_OR_EQUAL, clear to 0.0), so the depth buffer keeps the largest depth of every earlier frame, and once the camera moves nearly every world draw fails the depth test. The HUD, the 2D draws and the post-process pass are unaffected.

- `DepthTarget` carries the surface's HTILE address (DB_HTILE_DATA_BASE / _HI) when DB_Z_INFO.TILE_SURFACE_ENABLE is set and the base register has been written. 0x005 and 0x01e are added to `DrawKeyRegisters`.
- RADV writes HTILE with its `clear_htile_mask` compute kernel (17 GFX10 words: `htile = (htile & user[5]) | user[4]` over the buffer at user[2..3]). `HtileDepthClearAddress` recognizes it by its code and 64x1x1 groups, and returns the HTILE address when the update leaves ZMASK at 0. The dispatch still runs, so guest memory is unchanged.
- `DepthSurfaceView` clears the depth aspect of that surface to the draw's DB_DEPTH_CLEAR the next time the surface is bound, through `Recorder::Commands()` (which ends any open render pass) with barriers around the clear.

HTILE initialization (ZMASK 0xf, "expanded") and the stencil-only update RADV issues alongside it are left alone.

Limits: this matches one RADV kernel. Fast clears done some other way (the SDK's own paths, CP DMA fills, stencil HTILE clears) aren't covered.

Tests:

### What

Depends on #2224.

Implement `sceUsbdSubmitTransfer` and `sceUsbdCancelTransfer` on the source-built libusb backend introduced by #2224. Submitted transfers now reach native USB I/O, completions copy status, byte counts and isochronous packet results back to the guest object, and cancellation completes through the same callback path. A separate native transfer invokes the original guest callback through the System V ABI, including on Windows. Supporting allocation/free changes preserve resubmission and freeing from callbacks, prevent freeing pending transfers, and release auto-free buffers through the guest heap.

This contribution adds **2** implementations beyond #2224: CPU libraries move from 2600/3044 (85.41%) to 2602/3044 (85.48%). The 22 synchronous implementations and dependency files visible in the current diff belong to #2224; they are inherited unchanged. This branch is based on its exact head `3dbf85f0d9be6a45baa955d28528b46058426e27` and should merge after it. `sceUsbdCheckConnected` still throws.

The asynchronous signatures follow [OpenOrbis Usbd.h](https://github.com/OpenOrbis/OpenOrbis-PS4-Toolchain/blob/master/include/orbis/Usbd.h) and [shadPS4 declarations](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4/blob/0fe263a4760dfbfa973366890061749b4af0de97/src/core/libraries/usbd/usbd.h). Transfer ownership, flags and completion behavior follow [libusb 1.0.30](https://github.com/libusb/libusb/tree/v1.0.30). There is no additional third-party dependency in this follow-up.

PS5 hardware ABI, Windows asynchronous execution, game behavior and physical control/interrupt payloads remain unverified. Linux native tests enumerate devices and read descriptors; transfer completion tests use a deterministic native submission/event backend. These limits are recorded in TechnicalDebt.

### Tested

Linux x86-64, GCC 13.3.0, Release, BUILD_TESTING=ON:
- Full CMake configure/build and `--target libs`: passed.
- `guest_usbd`, `guest_usbd_control`, `guest_usbd_async`: passed. Native tests enumerated 17 host devices and read descriptors. The new asynchronous tests use real libusb allocations/context, wrapping only native allocation/free accounting and submit/cancel/event delivery. They verify error translation, double submission rejection, pending-free rejection, cancellation, guest callback identity and data, resubmission, freeing from callbacks, isochronous results, and guest-heap auto-free ownership.
- AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer asynchronous suite: passed.
- Full `ctest --parallel 2 --timeout 30`: 512 passed, 1 skipped (`agc_driver_storage_cache_budget`), 2 failed (`agc_driver_dcc_keys_first_write` assertion and `agc_driver_flat_store` timeout). Neither involves USB.

On the exact #2224 parent, after normal configure/full build/libs, the identical DCC assertion reproduced and flat-store passed in 29.14 s. That test is close to the fixed 30-second limit; no AGC code or timeout was changed.

### What

`windows_import_modules` fails intermittently on Windows under a parallel ctest run, at about 31.6 s:

```
  File "test_windows_import_modules.py", line 291, in main
    run_status = shell_execute_exit_code(output)
  File "test_windows_import_modules.py", line 159, in shell_execute_exit_code
    raise TimeoutError('ShellExecuteExW child did not exit')
...
PermissionError: [WinError 5] Access is denied: '...\missing-symbol-gui\app0\prx\a.prx.guest.prx'
```

The same failure is mentioned in #2079 ("timed out waiting for the unrelated windows_import_modules GUI child, followed by a temporary-file cleanup PermissionError") and #2020 (the cleanup `PermissionError` on a `.prx.guest.prx` the test has just run).

Cause: the two `--windows-gui` fixtures (#1153) were started with `ShellExecuteExW`. A process the shell starts gets the default error mode, so the `RaiseException` with which the entry stub reports `0xc0000139`/`0xc0000135` goes to Windows Error Reporting as an `APPCRASH`. The Application log shows one `Windows Error Reporting` event per launch (`P1: output.exe`, `P4: KERNELBASE.dll`, `P7: c0000139`). Collecting the report delays the child's exit: about 2 s per launch here, 10.9 s once in 60 launches, and past the test's 30 s wait under load. WerFault also keeps the image open, which is the `PermissionError` at cleanup.

The fixtures now start through `CreateProcessW` with `STARTF_USESTDHANDLES` and no standard handles, and with `SEM_FAILCRITICALERRORS | SEM_NOGPFAULTERRORBOX` added to the test's error mode, which the child inherits. The condition #1153 tests is unchanged: the stub's diagnostic has no handle to write to, and the raised status must still be the exit status. Nothing outside the test changes; a title started from Explorer still reports through the system as before.

### Tested

Windows 11 Pro 25H2 (10.0.26200.9457), MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0 (WinLibs r7), Python 3.14, Release, full build on `main` d70b8998.

- Before: in repeated full `ctest -j8` runs the test failed 3 times in about 25, always as above. Launching the GUI missing-symbol fixture 60 times through `ShellExecuteExW` took 1.9-2.6 s per launch (once 10.9 s), and each launch logged a WER event. Through a handle-less `CreateProcessW` the same fixture exits in under 35 ms with `0xc0000139` (`0xc0000135` for the missing-module one).
- After: `windows_import_modules` takes 1.24 s alone (5.1 s before) and 1.3-1.9 s in six full `ctest -j8` runs, 510/510 each. No WER event is logged during the test.
- `tools/check_conventions.py --base upstream/main` passes.

Depends on #1915. Only the last commit, ab09a0a9, is this PR; the first three are #1915's (its head af9e60b6).

### What

Ratchet & Clank: Rift Apart (PPSA01474) writes `PA_SC_CONSERVATIVE_RASTERIZATION_CNTL = 0xe6000` on its first draws. Decoded with the field shifts in the kernel's `gc_10_3_0_sh_mask.h`:

| Bits | Field | Value |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `OVER_RAST_ENABLE` | 0 |
| 5 | `UNDER_RAST_ENABLE` | 0 |
| 13, 14 | `OVERRIDE_{OVER,UNDER}_RAST_INNER_TO_NORMAL` | 1, 1 |
| 17:16 | `UNCERTAINTY_REGION_MODE` | 2 |
| 18, 19 | `OUTER_` / `INNER_UNCERTAINTY_EDGERULE_OVERRIDE` | 1, 1 |

Both rasterization enables are clear, as in libSceAgc's `0x6000`. On top of #1915's disabled mask (`0x00106000`), this also accepts bits 19:16, the uncertainty-region mode and its two edge-rule overrides:
- With either enable set, anything other than `0x6001` is still rejected. `0xe6001` and `0xe6020` are rejected.
- It is the narrow shape discussed on #1915.

I have no source that says these fields do nothing when both enables are clear. RADV never writes them; it sets `PBB_UNCERTAINTY_REGION_ENABLE` only for overestimation. So the TechnicalDebt entry records it as an assumption from the field names, not a measurement.

### Tested

Linux (CachyOS, GCC), RX 9070 XT, RADV / Mesa 26.2.4.

- `agc_driver_graphics`: `0xe6000` decodes as disabled and is not rejected; `0xe6001` and `0xe6020` are still rejected. #1915's cases are unchanged.
- `tools/check_conventions.py` passes.
- **Ratchet & Clank: Rift Apart** on `main` 43972e69, with #1673, #1339, #1836, #1837, #1893, #2105 and #2184, plus a local placeholder for `munlock`:
  - Before this change, the run stops about 19 s in on `PA_SC_CONSERVATIVE_RASTERIZATION_CNTL=0xe6000: only 0x6000 (off) and 0x6001 (overestimation) are supported`.
  - After it, the same draws go through. The run stops a moment later on `depth/stencil clear, copy, resummarize or decompress draws (DB_RENDER_CONTROL) is unsupported (register 0x0 = 0x00000001)`.
  - No frame has been presented yet, so I can't show a visual comparison. With both enables clear, the host pipeline is the same as for `0x6000`: no conservative rasterization.

body:
### What

`GuestImageReader::Read` scans both full relocation tables for every INIT_ARRAY/FINI_ARRAY entry. With R relocations and A lifecycle entries, this validation is O(A × R), despite already having an ordered target index for overlap checks.

Reuse that same map to retain validated input-file relocation offsets instead of target end addresses. Each lifecycle entry needs one lookup, followed by reading info/addend from the immutable input bytes: O(A log R). No second index or increase in the map key/value size. Overlap, executable-address, symbol-type, addend, and unrelocated-pointer checks are preserved. No runtime exports, relaxed checks, or silent stubs are added.

Base: `d70b89989473ba1f6ae13e44e079e67f1f8a44b0`; head: `7b7326907001e65e0c243bebd3a08d9317511671`. Targeted open-PR searches for lifecycle/GuestImageReader found no competing lifecycle-index implementation. Related module-discovery and initializer-delivery contributions are not included.

The registered `guest_lifecycle_relocations` regression covers 46 Linux/Windows conversions: empty and larger arrays, reverse-ordered relocations, relative/symbol function pointers, invalid GLOB_DAT/PLT entries, nonzero symbol addends, object symbols, non-executable addresses, unrelocated pointers, and overlapping targets. Valid Linux x86-64 synthetic modules are also loaded with `ctypes.CDLL`, and their constructor-updated counter is checked through an actual exported function call.

### Tested

Ubuntu 24.04 x86-64, GCC 13.3.0, Python 3.12. Original synthetic ELF fixtures only; no game binaries, firmware, or proprietary assets.

- Built all 65 production translation units from the CMake target source inventory with `-std=c++20 -O3 -g -DNDEBUG -DAPS5_ENABLE_TIMING_LOG=0` and the project static-link flags. Baseline and candidate use identical flags: baseline Reader from the pinned main, all other unchanged production objects shared.
- **44/44 Linux-applicable registered test groups passed when compiled/invoked manually**, including C++/Python relinker groups and four root Python groups. Test C++ translation units have assertions enabled (`-O1 -g -UNDEBUG`). This was **not a CMake/CTest run**: CMake/Ninja were unavailable. `hardware_oracle` reports 8 subtests with 1 optional assembler-dependent subtest skipped; no GPU/console oracle is claimed.
- New 46-conversion group passed in 0.208 s; slowest group was `tls_function_coverage`, 8.50 s. No timeout increased.
- **240 differential comparisons** (seed 5909), including shuffled tables and invalid types/addends/targets: identical exit codes, diagnostics, and generated executable/module hashes, including **88 matching rejections**.
- Semantic-preservation tests also pass unchanged main, as expected for an optimization. A mutation of the final implementation that looks up `address + offset + 8` instead is rejected by the regression.
- Final Reader built with AddressSanitizer/UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer: large fixture with 4096 initializer and 4096 finalizer entries read successfully, no sanitizer report. This is an instrumented reader harness, not an instrumented full runtime.
- `python3 tools/check_conventions.py --base origin/main` and `git diff --check origin/main HEAD` pass on the committed head.

**Conversion benchmark, not gameplay/FPS:** synthetic module, 262144 relocations, 4096 entries in each lifecycle array, three alternating baseline/candidate runs. Both production builds use O3.

| Build | Raw seconds | Median |
|---|---|---|
| Pinned main | 11.483600, 11.167935, 6.399533 | 11.167935 s |
| Candidate | 0.196453, 0.216516, 0.159082 | 0.196453 s |

Median ratio: 56.85x **for this fixture on this host**. Host-load variation is visible in the raw samples; this is not a fixed performance guarantee. Converted module bytes are identical in every run, SHA256 `d938902fcdcd9a68e0c8444c63696a6d72fae81c8a5476fedb0b28924c15c0c6`.

Reproduce from the contribution checkout with separately built baseline and candidate relinkers:

```bash
python3 - /path/to/baseline/relinker /path/to/candidate/relinker <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import hashlib, statistics, subprocess, sys, tempfile, time
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path('core/relinker/relinker/tests').resolve()))
from test_guest_lifecycle_relocations import fixture
from test_guest_intel_trampolines import main_fixture
binaries = [Path(p).resolve() for p in sys.argv[1:]]
assert len(binaries) == 2
times, hashes = [[], []], set()
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
    work = Path(directory)
    (work / 'sce_module').mkdir()
    (work / 'sce_module/module.prx').write_bytes(fixture(262144, 4096))
    (work / 'input.elf').write_bytes(main_fixture())
    for repeat in range(3):
        for which in ((0, 1) if repeat % 2 == 0 else (1, 0)):
            start = time.perf_counter()
            subprocess.run([str(binaries[which]), str(work / 'input.elf'),
                            str(work / 'output.elf')], check=True,
                           capture_output=True, timeout=25)
            times[which].append(time.perf_counter() - start)
            artifact = work / 'app0/sce_module/module.prx.guest.prx'
            hashes.add(hashlib.sha256(artifact.read_bytes()).hexdigest())
assert len(hashes) == 1, hashes
for label, samples in zip(('baseline', 'candidate'), times):
    print(label, samples, 'median', statistics.median(samples))
print('identical module SHA256:', hashes.pop())
PY
```

Not tested: native Windows/macOS execution, full system-library build, real titles, graphics, GPU performance. This PR does not claim to make a specific title playable.

body:
### What

Replace 22 throwing `libSceUsbd` exports with a synchronous host USB backend using libusb 1.0.30. Previously the library always returned an empty device list and threw on all device operations. It now enumerates real host devices, reads device/configuration/string descriptors, manages device references and handles, claims/releases interfaces, performs control transfers, and exposes native configuration/reset/driver operations.

Add libusb as a pinned submodule (`libusb/libusb-cmake`, tag `v1.0.30-0`, commit `c8477c10ac2ac6b1718d4d498e102b9f18b776f5`) and build it statically from source. Linux uses the bundled netlink enumeration backend rather than a system libudev dependency. Hide native libusb exports from the guest library.

Use the signatures, native descriptor layouts and USB error conversion documented by [shadPS4 usbd.h](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4/blob/0fe263a4760dfbfa973366890061749b4af0de97/src/core/libraries/usbd/usbd.h) and [usbd.cpp](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4/blob/0fe263a4760dfbfa973366890061749b4af0de97/src/core/libraries/usbd/usbd.cpp), with locally written wrappers. Own a separate reference-counted libusb context and convert the guest's 64-bit timeval fields to the host representation.

Transfer allocation/free and interrupt-transfer preparation work, preserving the guest callback pointer. Asynchronous submit/cancel and `sceUsbdCheckConnected` remain throwing stubs. Host permissions and USB drivers apply; console lifecycle and invalid-argument error precedence remain unverified. Record these limits in TechnicalDebt and remove the obsolete no-device silent-stub entry.

The progress scanner changes from 2578/3044 (84.69%) to 2600/3044 (85.41%), +22 implementations and +0.72 percentage points.

### Tested

Windows, WinLibs GCC 15.2.0, Release, BUILD_TESTING=ON:

- Native USB tests enumerated 9 host devices, read cached device descriptors and available configuration descriptors, checked device/list reference lifetimes, repeated initialization/exit, transfer allocation/preparation, SysV guest callback invocation, invalid arguments, and remaining throwing paths.
- Deterministic control-transfer tests replace only the native libusb control-transfer call at link time. They verify setup fields, byte counts and buffer output, error conversion (including OTHER), zero/maximum/invalid lengths, string-descriptor requests, and that invalid calls never reach the backend.
- Native libusb functions are not exported from the built guest library.
- Test registration and conventions checks passed.

- `cmake --build build --parallel 12` completed successfully, as did `cmake --build build --target libs --parallel 12`.
- `ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure --parallel 4 --timeout 30`: 506 passed, 1 skipped (`guest_video_out_wqhd_detection_no_vulkan`), 1 timed out (`agc_driver_flat_store`). The timeout was 30.06 s; no timeout setting was raised.
- Re-ran `agc_driver_flat_store`, `guest_usbd` and `guest_usbd_control` sequentially with the same 30-second limit: all 3 passed (24.19 s, 0.10 s, 0.01 s respectively).

No game or homebrew was tested. Physical devices were enumerated and their descriptors read; control-transfer payload tests used the test backend. Linux has not been tested locally.

body:
### What

`agc_driver_storage_cache_budget` (#1059) computed its expected budget from a device other than the one it ran on. `SelectDevice` ranked the physical devices itself and always took the discrete GPU's memory heaps, while `OpenVulkanTestDevice` honours `ANYPS5_GPU`. It now takes the heaps of the physical device whose name matches `VulkanDevice::DeviceName()`.

On a machine with an RX 9060 XT (16 GiB heap) and a Ryzen 9 7950X iGPU (32 GiB shared heap), a run on the iGPU expected a 4076 MiB budget while the driver used 8083 MiB:

```
texture cache budget 4076 MiB; each 4096x4096 32_UINT surface holds 64 MiB; cyclic set of 33 surfaces (2112 MiB)
AGC graphics: surface 0 is still cached after 65 surfaces under a budget of 63 of them
```

With the change, the same run reports `texture cache budget 8083 MiB` and passes. Machines with a single device are unaffected.

### Tested

Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26300, MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0 (WinLibs r7), Release, `-DBUILD_TESTING=ON -DANYPS5_ENABLE_SPIRV_TOOLS=ON`, on `main` at d70b8998.

- `ANYPS5_GPU="Radeon(TM) Graphics"` (RDNA 2 iGPU, driver 32.0.21045.5002): passes. On `main` this run first stops on the #2138 `OpSelect` validation error, so it was run with #2191 applied to the working tree, then without it for the commit.
- `ANYPS5_GPU="RX 9060"` (RDNA 4, driver 32.0.31041.1004): passes with and without this change (4076 MiB budget, eviction checked), with `VK_EXT_memory_budget` reporting a 15416 MiB heap budget.

While another process held about 10.7 GiB of the RX 9060 XT's VRAM, `VK_EXT_memory_budget` reported a 2197 MiB heap budget and the 2112 MiB cyclic set failed with `vkAllocateMemory storage texture: Vulkan result -2`, with and without this change. The storage image cache budget is `TextureCacheBudget` (a quarter of the heap size) and does not follow `VK_EXT_memory_budget` as the sampled cache does, so the test fails rather than skips when other processes use the device memory. Not changed here.

body:
### What

Validate complete `DT_RELA` and `DT_JMPREL` relocation table ranges before parsing them.

Malformed ELF metadata could declare a relocation table extending beyond its file-backed `PT_LOAD` segment. The parser could then interpret bytes outside the segment as relocation entries.

This change:

- Validates the full relocation table against its containing `PT_LOAD`.
- Validates the resulting file range against the ELF byte buffer.
- Rejects relocation sizes that are not multiples of 24 bytes.
- Uses overflow-safe checks for virtual and file offsets.
- Applies the checks to both `DT_RELA` and `DT_JMPREL`.
- Adds regression coverage for overextended, unaligned, and near-`UINT64_MAX` metadata.

Fixes #2221

### Tested

Linux x86-64 (Ubuntu 26 LTS)

Tests use synthetic ELF byte arrays only. No PS5 hardware, controller, firmware, title, or game files are required.

Commands run:

    cmake --build build --target strict_nid_filter_tests --parallel
    ctest --test-dir build -R strict_nid_filter --output-on-failure

body:
### What

Exports `wcstok` on the guest's 16-bit `wchar_t`, next to `wcsspn` and using the same `Contains` helper. The behaviour follows FreeBSD's three-argument `wcstok` (`lib/libc/string/wcstok.c`):
- leading delimiters are skipped;
- the token ends at the next delimiter, which is overwritten with 0, and `*last` points past it;
- when the string is exhausted, `*last` becomes NULL, both after the last token and when only delimiters remain;
- with `text == NULL` it continues from `*last`, and returns NULL when that is NULL.

Code units are compared one by one, so a surrogate pair is never split by a BMP delimiter.

Exports `rand_r`. In FreeBSD, `rand` and `rand_r` share one generator step (`do_rand` in `lib/libc/stdlib/rand.c`): `rand` advances the global state, and `rand_r` advances the caller's `unsigned int`. On Linux, any executable import or guest-module import whose NID two bundled modules export is a hard error, even when the import declares one of them. Windows already binds such imports to their declared module (#684).

This branch carries #846, #1503 and #1529 so the fix is reviewable with its demo; merge those first. Only the last commit is mine.

### What

Exports `__inet_ntoa` (the symbol behind `inet_ntoa`). It formats the four address bytes in network (memory) order as dotted decimal, as FreeBSD's `lib/libc/inet/inet_ntoa.c` does. The `struct in_addr` argument is passed by value; under the SysV ABI that is the 32-bit integer in `edi`, so the parameter is declared `unsigned int`.

FreeBSD returns a static buffer; this uses a per-thread buffer like `basename` in the same file, so concurrent callers don't overwrite each other's result. Each call still reuses the same buffer, which the test checks.

```
FAIL: Forbidden syscall instruction at code offset 0xb03d47
```

The fixed stubs set the number with a constant right before the instruction (`48 C7 C0 09 00 00 00` is `mov rax, 9`, FreeBSD `link`; `B8 39 00 00 00` is `mov eax, 57`, `symlink`). `SyscallScanner` now looks back for a constant load into rax and adds it:

```
FAIL: Forbidden syscall instruction at code offset 0xa: syscall number 9 (offset 0xa)
```

The number is only reported when it can be established. The constant load must be the instruction directly before the syscall, or one `mov r10, rcx` (the SDK's first-argument move, which does not write rax) in front of it. Any other intervening instruction stops the inference rather than returning a stale value, so `mov rax, 9; add rax, 1; syscall` reports no number instead of 9. A stub that takes the number from a register — the SDK's generic `syscall()` / `__syscall()` wrapper reads rax from rdi — also reports no number and keeps today's text. The check still throws and nothing else changes; `--skip-syscall-check` is unaffected.

This does not pick one of the three directions in #2136, and the relinker still refuses the title. It makes the failure say which call it hit, which all three directions need, and it is the number #2136's author had to recover by hand with a disassembler.

### Tested

Linux x86-64, relinker-only build (`-DANYPS5_RELINKER_ONLY=ON -DBUILD_TESTING=ON`), GCC 16.2.1: `ctest` 45/45. `syscall_scanner` covers all four forbidden opcodes — the 64-bit constant stub → number 9, the 32-bit constant stub → number 57, `int 0x80` → number 11, `sysenter` → no number, `sysret` with a constant load in front of it → no number, a stub that loads rax from a register → no number, and a stub whose intervening instruction writes rax → no number (the regression for the review). `test_syscall_number` covers the same contract through the Python harness, so it also runs on Windows and macOS, where the C++ fixture helpers do not build. `tools/check_conventions.py --base origin/main` and `tools/check_test_registration.py` both pass.

Windows: not run here. @rmz-24 built `529476c7` (the previous head, unchanged in this respect) onto `main` `d70b8998` with MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0 and reported 510/510 on the full `ctest`.

body:
### What

Refs #1666, which asks to review the adjacent table reads for the same arithmetic pattern; this is one such finding.

The CFG/GOT filter (`unused-filter=1`, which runs on non-PLT references) collects entry points in `UnusedNidFilter/EntryPointCollector.cpp`. It checked every position as `offset + size > file size` or `<= file size`: the program headers, `PT_DYNAMIC`, the init/fini arrays, the section headers, the section name table, the `sh_link` header and the symbol entries. With an offset near 2^64 the sum wraps, the check passes, and the unchecked `read*` helpers `memcpy` from outside the input. The relinker validates none of these section header fields before this point.

Measured on `main` (`d70b8998`), with the read helpers temporarily instrumented to report out-of-range reads:

- `e_shoff = 2^64 - 32` with two section headers reads 8 bytes at offset -8 and 4 bytes at -28, both before the input buffer, and the relink still exits 0.
- Wrapping can also land on an in-bounds table. With `e_shoff = 2^64 - 64` and `e_shentsize = 0x840`, section 1 is read from file offset 0x800. A `SHT_SYMTAB` there adds a function that nothing else reaches to the entry points, so the `GLOB_DAT` reference it loads is kept (`CFG/GOT filtering: 1 -> 1`). The same happens with an in-bounds section header whose symbol table offset wraps (`sh_offset = 2^64 - 24`).

The fix checks each position by subtraction (`base <= size && offset <= size - base && length <= size - base - offset`), the same form `RelinkerPipeline` uses for RELA entries since #917. Out-of-range tables keep their existing handling: program headers and `PT_DYNAMIC` still throw, and the best-effort section and array scans still stop.

`RelativeRelocationIndex.cpp` has the same pattern (`pos + RelaEntSize`, `phPos + 56`, `segOff + segSz`), but it is not reachable: by the time it runs, the pipeline has already rejected a wrapping `e_phoff` (`FileByteOffset out of bounds`), `PT_DYNAMIC` (`Dynamic segment out of bounds`) and RELA table. I checked by instrumenting its read helpers the same way. So it is left unchanged.

### Tested

Windows 11, WinLibs GCC 15.2.0 r7, relinker-only Release build, `-DBUILD_TESTING=ON`:

- New `entry_point_bounds` test (Python, relinker fixture, `--windows unused-filter=1`), with a `GLOB_DAT` reference loaded only by a function that only a symbol makes reachable:

  | Case | `main` | This PR |
  |---|---|---|
  | no section headers (control) | `1 -> 0` | `1 -> 0` |
  | symbol table in bounds (control) | `1 -> 1` | `1 -> 1` |
  | section header table offset wraps onto it | `1 -> 1` | `1 -> 0` |
  | symbol table offset wraps onto the symbol | `1 -> 1` | `1 -> 0` |

- `ctest` on the relinker-only build: 41/41 passed.
- `tools/check_conventions.py` and `tools/check_test_registration.py` pass, and `tools/pr_overlap.py --branch` reports no overlap.

### What

Exports `strsep` with FreeBSD's semantics (`lib/libc/string/strsep.c`):
- It returns the token at `*stringp`, ending at the first delimiter.
- The delimiter is overwritten with NUL, and `*stringp` advances past it.
- Empty fields are returned, unlike `strtok`.
- When no delimiter is left, `*stringp` becomes NULL; with `*stringp == NULL` it returns NULL.

body:
### What

On Windows, receiving after local `shutdown(SHUT_RD)` or `shutdown(SHUT_RDWR)` reports guest `EIO` when Winsock returns `WSAESHUTDOWN`. Handle that receive error as a successful zero-byte receive in libkernel `recv`, `recvfrom` and `recvmsg`, and their libSceNet counterparts. Guest errno and data/address/control buffer bytes are preserved. `recvfrom` returns a zero source length when an address is supplied; `recvmsg` also clears the control length and returns the accepted input flags, following FreeBSD's EOF path.

Related to #1786, whose description explicitly defers the receive case to a separate PR. This change does not alter either shared native error map or the send functions and does not depend on #1786.

The behavior comes from [FreeBSD 11.4 `soshutdown` and `soreceive`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/releng/11.4/sys/kern/uipc_socket.c) and [`kern_recvit` / `sys_recvmsg`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/releng/11.4/sys/kern/uipc_syscalls.c). [Winsock documents `WSAESHUTDOWN` after disabling receives](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winsock/nf-winsock-recv). No FreeBSD implementation code was copied. The hardware validation gap and scope limits are recorded in TechnicalDebt.

### Tested

Windows x64 (10.0.26300), WinLibs MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0 UCRT/POSIX/SEH, Python 3.12.14, Release, `BUILD_TESTING=ON`, `ANYPS5_ENABLE_SPIRV_TOOLS=ON`; base `d70b89989473ba1f6ae13e44e079e67f1f8a44b0`.

- Six new Windows CTest groups fail on the unmodified receive implementation with errno 5 and pass with the change. They cover 72 shutdown scenarios across TCP, connected UDP and kernel stream/datagram socketpairs, blocking/nonblocking sockets, `SHUT_RD`/`SHUT_RDWR`, repeated receives and `MSG_PEEK`. They also check untouched data/guard/address/control bytes, errno, source/control lengths, message flags and receives without an address.
- Controls cover normal data, zero-byte UDP datagrams with a source address, `SHUT_WR` preserving receives, `SHUT_RD` preserving sends, send errors after `SHUT_RDWR`, invalid flags/buffers, closed descriptors and would-block errors.
- Relevant existing socket tests plus the new groups: 11/11 passed. Ten repetitions of each new group: 60/60 passed. Longest new group in the focused run: 0.089 s, with a 20 s timeout.
- An independent local harness resolves the generated NIDs in the built, patched `libc.prx`, `libkernel.prx` and `libSceNet.prx` and runs the same behavioral cases for all six receive functions: passed. The harness and logs are local artifacts, not repository additions.
- Full build and `libs` target: passed. Full CTest with the existing CI 120 s global timeout: 515 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped (516 registered tests). An earlier run with a 30 s global timeout passed 513/514 and timed out only `tls_function_coverage` at 30.05 s; its source and registration are unchanged by this patch. This is the existing test addressed separately in #1913. No repository test timeout was increased; all six new groups have a 20 s timeout.
- Skipped full-suite tests: `guest_video_out_wqhd_detection_no_vulkan`.
- Working-tree conventions, test registration and `git diff --check`: passed.

Linux, PS5 hardware and games: not tested. This is specifically the translation of `WSAESHUTDOWN`; other host errors and existing behavior for queued data, zero-length stream requests and an already blocked receive are unchanged. These tests do not establish hosted CI timing.

### What

Ratchet & Clank: Rift Apart (PPSA01474) reads its thread id straight from the pthread object. It calls `pthread_self()` and loads the first 32 bits it points to. That matches FreeBSD's libthr, which PS5 libkernel derives from: `struct pthread` starts with `long tid`.

The title then uses that id to find a per-thread allocator in its own table:
- a worker thread registers itself under its id;
- the main thread looks up its own id later.

On Linux, `PthreadPrivate` currently starts with `std::thread _thr`:
- **created threads:** the title reads the low 32 bits of the glibc `pthread_t`;
- **adopted main thread:** `_thr` is empty, so the title reads 0. It matches an empty table slot, gets a null allocator and crashes with SIGSEGV about 19 s in.

Changes:
- `PthreadPrivate` now starts with `long tid`, taken from a process-wide counter that starts at 100000, the first FreeBSD thread id. Every thread object gets one, including adopted threads.
- `scePthreadGetthreadid` returns the calling thread's `tid`, as FreeBSD's `pthread_getthreadid_np` returns `TID(curthread)`. Before, it returned a hash of `std::thread::id` on Linux and `GetCurrentThreadId()` on Windows, so the two ids could disagree.

### Tested

Linux (CachyOS, GCC), RX 9070 XT.

- `guest_thread_self` now checks three things:
  - the first `long` of the main thread's and a created thread's pthread objects is non-zero, and differs between the two threads;
  - on each thread, it equals `scePthreadGetthreadid()`;
  - without the change, the test aborts.
- Full `ctest`: 511/512. The failing test is `import_audit`, which can't read the commit hash in my worktree and is unrelated.
- `tools/check_conventions.py` passes.
- Ratchet & Clank: Rift Apart, on `main` 43972e69 + #1673, #1339, #1836, #1837, #1893, #2105, plus a local placeholder for `munlock`:
  - Before this change, the main thread crashes about 19 s in, at `cmpq $0x0,(%rbx)` with `rbx = 0`, inside the title's `hashmap32<T>` construction. The allocator came from that thread-id lookup.
  - After it, the title gets past that point, registers its shaders and reaches its first draws. It then stops on an unrelated `PA_SC_CONSERVATIVE_RASTERIZATION_CNTL=0xe6000` check.

body:
### What

`sceNetGetsockopt` rejects SO_ERROR, so a caller waiting for a nonblocking connection cannot query its completion result. Implement guest SO_ERROR (0x1007), translate the host socket error to guest errno, return the output size, and preserve thread errno on successful queries.

On Windows 10 build 19045.7417, Winsock returns WSAECONNREFUSED repeatedly after a failed asynchronous connection. Track the consumed completion error per native socket, serialize connect/error queries, and reset it when another connection attempt starts. Successful connections stop this tracking once getpeername confirms a peer. Established-socket and UDP errors continue to use host behaviour.

The regression covers successful and refused loopback connections, invalid query arguments, output bounds, errno preservation, receive EAGAIN, and Windows same-socket retries with concurrent readers. The pending-connect errno mapping is already provided by merged #1448 and is not reintroduced here. FreeBSD-derived guest behaviour and unverified console semantics are recorded in TechnicalDebt.

Overlap review: 456 open PR titles/bodies checked, with diffs inspected for the open libSceNet changes. #1786 extends the same host-error mapping and #1588 changes the global synchronization used by the same exports; neither implements SO_ERROR. Resolver and pool-statistics changes have since merged and are preserved in the final rebase. No dependency on an unmerged PR.

### Tested

Candidate Windows validation and final rebase:

- macOS arm64, isolated native-ABI diagnostic: current unmodified source fails the SO_ERROR query with guest EOPNOTSUPP (45); candidate passes successful connection, asynchronous refusal and read-and-clear checks. The diagnostic supplies an isolated poller-registration hook and is not a supported-platform integration build.
- Windows 10 build 19045.7417, WinLibs GCC 15.2.0 r7, normal CMake/Ninja Release build on `f145139676a48306681d3a4d5fabf83938759daf`: both networking targets compiled and `guest_sce_net` plus `guest_sce_net_connect` each passed three CTest repetitions (six executions, 0 failures, 12.85 seconds). This uses the project guest ABI.
- Final rebase onto `51f69aa2182f28ef3b91cdc20e57431d065e3e65` preserves the same SO_ERROR implementation and tests, incorporates upstream resolver/pool-statistics changes, and resolves the TechnicalDebt conflict while retaining upstream entries. The macOS isolated loopback regression passed after this rebase. Windows/Linux integration on this final base remains pending maintainer-triggered CI; the earlier Windows run is not presented as a final-head result. Upstream Build run 37919912528 is action_required with no jobs started. The conventions check passed.
- Linux and PS5 title/hardware execution: not performed.
- Final author commit: `b7a6823f`. Diff and repository conventions checks passed.

Earlier Windows validation on `df16c4c256be3c44e03eb9149a6ce5f8e8a038b2`, before narrowing the patch for current main:

- Windows 10 build 19045.7417, WinLibs GCC 15.2.0 r7, Release, AMD Radeon RX 6800 XT. Normal build and library build completed. Existing `guest_sce_net` and new `guest_sce_net_connect` passed three repetitions, including Windows refusal clearing, concurrent readers and successful same-socket retry.
- Full CTest: 402/405 passed in 240.38 seconds. `agc_driver_sdwa_float_selectors`, `agc_driver_sdwa_ldexp_f16`, and `guest_system_font` failed. Temporarily removing the patch and rebuilding reproduced all three failures on the same upstream revision and machine. The two graphics mismatch values were identical; the font test ended at the same point in its output. Restoring the patch and rebuilding made both networking tests pass again.

### What

#453 (48ebf3195e, "skip depth and stencil tests whose plane is absent") renders depth and stencil tests without a depth target when `DB_Z_INFO` and `DB_STENCIL_INFO` both have FORMAT INVALID: with no plane, there is nothing to test, and every test passes.

The depth bounds test (`DB_DEPTH_CONTROL` bit 3) reads the same absent depth plane, but such a draw still threw:

```
[videoout] presentation failed: AGC graphics: depth bounds without a depth surface
```

Depth bounds now follow the same rule when both planes are absent: no depth target, and no bounds test. The change is in `DecodeState` and `DrawRejection`, `core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/State.cpp`.

With an absent depth plane beside a present stencil plane, the bounds test still throws `depth bounds without a depth plane`, as before.

This is the same claim #453 makes for the depth and stencil tests. It also matches the Vulkan rule that the bounds test passes without a depth attachment. It is not checked on hardware.

body:
### What

A draw with `DB_RENDER_CONTROL.RESUMMARIZE_ENABLE` (bit 4) recomputes the HTILE summary of the bound depth surface from its depth values. HTILE is not modeled: depth surfaces live in their resident images. So a resummarize draw with depth and stencil tests off (`DB_DEPTH_CONTROL` bits 0-1 clear) and no color writes changes no modeled state. `DepthMaintenanceRejection` now passes it, and the draw precheck draws nothing for it. Before, it threw:

```
DB_RENDER_CONTROL depth copy, resummarize or decompress is unsupported (register 0x0 = 0x00000010)
```

These still throw:
- a resummarize draw with a depth or stencil test, with color writes, or without `DB_DEPTH_CONTROL`/`CB_TARGET_MASK`/`CB_SHADER_MASK` set;
- depth/stencil copy and other maintenance bits.

TechnicalDebt records the rule.

#### For the reviewers

#1371 (`f2fe3f7165`) made maintenance draws reject before shader compilation, and its test listed resummarize among the rejected modes. This changes that one case. If the intent is to reject every resummarize draw until HTILE is modeled, this PR should not be merged.

### Tested

- Linux (CachyOS, GCC 16.2, RTX 4090, NVIDIA 610.57), on `main` a8b032b236: ctest 495/495. `tools/check_conventions.py` passes.
- `agc_driver_graphics`, `depthMaintenanceTests`: a resummarize draw with no depth/stencil test and no color writes passes, with every clear combination. The same draw with `Z_ENABLE` or with color writes still rejects. Copy, compress and other modes still reject as before.
- A heavier title issues such draws (`DB_RENDER_CONTROL` 0x10, no depth test, no color) in its title passes, and stopped there with the line above. With this, it reaches its title screen.

body:
### What

Normalize negative texel indices in the emulated color-comparison wrap path before converting them to unsigned image coordinates. Add a point-filtered wrap case to the execution regression, which includes negative coordinates. The implementation follows repeat addressing (`VK_SAMPLER_ADDRESS_MODE_REPEAT`) and uses the SPIR-V-defined signed remainder semantics (`OpSRem` takes the dividend's sign) with an explicit correction to the nonnegative texel range. See the [Vulkan specification](https://registry.khronos.org/vulkan/specs/latest/html/vkspec.html) and [SPIR-V `OpSRem`](https://registry.khronos.org/SPIR-V/specs/unified1/SPIRV.html#OpSRem). The technical-debt entry records that PS5 behavior has not been measured.

This is distinct from #2092, which expands supported color-comparison descriptor formats and views; it does not change address wrapping.

### Tested

- Linux x86_64, GCC 12.2, Release: built `agc_driver_emulated_color_compare_tests` from PR head `72c6f987696f5de02fdebea45d6ee96a9eb4e809`.

body:
### What

A draw build that is not address-based and whose every guest buffer element has a memory offset slot (a push constant byte, or a shader data byte inside its data buffer) binds a region whose offset in its host import is DWORD aligned in place (`GuestBufferMemory::AllowAdjustedRegions`, `bindableInPlace`), like a region at `minStorageBufferOffsetAlignment`:

- `Descriptor` binds the view from the aligned offset below it and the shader gets the remainder through its memory offset slot, as it already does for misaligned views;
- read-only views are snapshotted per draw by `PrepareDrawBindings` at `address - adjustment`;
- the import serial keys the template and `Revalidate` proves it per use, as for aligned regions.

Dispatches keep the copy: they read in-place inputs at execution, not at record.

### Why

Such a region was copied per build: a new buffer, an input snapshot, and a `vkCmdCopyBuffer` that ends the open render pass. `DirectRegions` also refused the build as a template. In the level measured below, binding them in place more than doubles the draws that continue an open render pass.

### Tested

- Linux (CachyOS, GCC 16.2, RTX 4090, NVIDIA 610.57), on `main` a8b032b236: ctest 495/495. `tools/check_conventions.py` passes.
- `agc_driver_recorder_tests`, new `misalignedRegionTests`: a misaligned read-only draw region is read in place and the build is reusable (on `main` it is copied and the check fails); the push constant carries the adjustment; the per-draw snapshot starts at the aligned offset below the view and holds the view's bytes after a CPU store. ctest builds this executable but does not run it; run by hand, it passes `misalignedRegionTests` and stops later at `importWindowTests` "(w) a cache over the pages the import reported sees no change", which fails the same way on `main`.
- A heavier title, one level, frames per second over level start +30 to +150 s, warm caches, two runs with the change and four of the base. It does not reach the level on `main` alone, so this was measured with the fixes needed for the title to reach the level: `main` 4b6ab6bb73 plus the boot fixes, #425 (with a depth-plane read fix), #1274, #1745, #1059 and an import budget like #290's. The base is that build:

  | build | level fps | `Graphics::Draw` per draw packet | draws continuing a render pass per 10 s |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | base (4 runs) | 0.455 / 0.448 / 0.415 / 0.436 | 180-199 µs | 4.4k |
  | base + this | 0.596 / 0.558 | 99 / 117 µs | 10.2k |

  Level frames show the same scene, geometry and brightness as the base.
- A lighter title that runs at 60 fps: unchanged, 60.0 fps menu, 59.9 fps gameplay, no skipped draws, all screen checks pass.

body:
### What

`CachedPipeline`'s LRU bound goes from 256 to 1024 pipelines. A cached pipeline is a pure function of its key, so only memory and time change.

### Why

A level whose draws use more than 256 pipelines thrashes the LRU, and every miss creates a new `VkPipeline` (modules, layout, render pass and a driver compile). Since #639 shaders are compiled at registration, but pipelines are still created on demand here.

### Tested

- Linux (CachyOS, GCC 16.2, RTX 4090, NVIDIA 610.57), on `main` a8b032b236: ctest 495/495. `tools/check_conventions.py` passes.
- No new test: the bound is a constant, and counting cache misses needs a device and a scene with more than 256 pipelines.
- A heavier title, one level, frames per second over level start +30 to +150 s, warm caches, two runs with the change and four of the base. It does not reach the level on `main` alone, so this was measured with the fixes needed for the title to reach the level: `main` 4b6ab6bb73 plus the boot fixes, #425 (with a depth-plane read fix), #1274, #1745, #1059 and an import budget like #290's. The base is that build:
  - At 256, `[pipecache]` shows 1,488 misses and 1,488 evictions per 10 s; the level's working set is 538 pipelines. At 1024: 0-4 misses per 10 s, nothing evicted.

  | build | level fps | `Graphics::Draw` per draw packet |
  |---|---|---|
  | base (4 runs) | 0.455 / 0.448 / 0.415 / 0.436 | 180-199 µs |
  | base + this | 0.461 / 0.497 | 161 / 142 µs |

- A lighter title that runs at 60 fps: unchanged, 60.0 fps menu, 59.9 fps gameplay, no skipped draws, all screen checks pass.

body:
### What

Exports `__isinf(double)` next to `__isnan` and `__isfinite`. Like the existing `__isinff`, it returns 1 for either infinity and 0 otherwise, which is what FreeBSD's `lib/libc/gen/isinf.c` does. glibc's `isinf` returns -1 for negative infinity instead, so the test pins the sign behaviour.

Titles: open-source homebrew from the #1578 catalog audit imports it from `libSceLibcInternal` (resolved through `libc.prx`): PPSA74126 Stremio Plus, PPSA92280 Capy Mobile, PPSA99003 ProsperoTV, PPSA99039 EVO Player, PPSA99082 OpenNOW, PPSA99169 RetroArch, PPSA99177 PS5VR, PPSA99420 PS5MC, PPSA99505 Jelly5 and PPSA99515 Emby5. I haven't run any of these titles.

### What

Exports `log1p`, `log1pf` and `expm1`. Each one forwards to the C++ standard library, like `log` and `exp`. Only the variants that titles import are added.

Titles: open-source homebrew from the #1578 catalog audit imports them from `libSceLibcInternal` (resolved through `libc.prx`):
- `log1p`: PPSA68091 Ruffle, PPSA99169 RetroArch
- `log1pf`: PPSA68091 Ruffle
- `expm1`: PPSA99169 RetroArch, PPSA99764 Porpoise

I haven't run any of these titles.

### Tested

Windows 11, WinLibs GCC 15.2.0 r7, Release, `-DBUILD_TESTING=ON`:

- New checks in `guest_math_tests`, next to `log10f`:
  - signed zero (`log1p(-0)` and `expm1(-0)` are `-0`);
  - limits: `log1p(-1) == -inf`, `log1p(inf) == inf`, `expm1(-inf) == expm1(-1000) == -1`;

body:
### What

Guest file descriptors currently contain host descriptor numbers. A guest can therefore read, seek or close a private runtime file by supplying its host descriptor. This change gives guest files their own descriptor table, shared by libc, libkernel, POSIX file operations and AIO.

Descriptors 0-2 retain their guest meanings through owned duplicates of the host standard streams. Ordinary guest descriptors occupy 3-32767, preserving the existing signed 16-bit FILE prefix. Operations hold a native ownership lease, so a concurrent guest close retires the logical descriptor while an in-flight operation can finish. FILE wrappers retain the original descriptor identity; after close and slot reuse, a stale stream reports EBADF without accessing or closing the replacement. Pipe adoption publishes both guest descriptors atomically and releases native resources on failure.

Existing platform backends remain in place, including the Windows/Linux ftruncate error handling. Existing tests now obtain file descriptors through the guest API. The same new isolation fixture runs against both the ordinary libraries and the actual NID-patched libc.prx/libkernel.prx.

The overlap bot reported eight other PRs. Their current heads were read and fetched for three-way merge simulations against `b14cd621`. Each of the eight produces a textual conflict; none implements the guest descriptor namespace, ownership leases or stale-FILE identity mechanism introduced here.

| PR | Other change | Integration when combining |
|---|---|---|
| [1804](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/pull/1804) | Linux routing for guest wide printf arguments | Keep guest-stdout routing and its wide-conversion logic together in vfprintf. |
| [1807](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/pull/1807) | Sandbox random-word export | Preserve both independent CMake test-registration blocks. |
| [2019](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/pull/2019) | gethostname | Preserve both independent CMake test-registration blocks. |
| [2030](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/pull/2030) | fsync result/errno translation | Acquire the guest descriptor lease, then preserve that PR's native flush/error mapping. |
| [2033](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/pull/2033) | FreeBSD fopen/freopen mode parsing | Keep its parser; derive the registry access mode from the parsed native mode and preserve FILE identity/ownership. |
| [2109](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/pull/2109) | Wide-format UTF-8 validation | Keep its EILSEQ catch while writing through the owned guest stdout stream. |
| [2129](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/pull/2129) | sceKernelFdatasync | Its added export currently uses a raw host descriptor. A combined version must resolve the logical guest descriptor and hold its lease; tests must use guest-owned descriptors. |
| [2144](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/pull/2144) | Scalar kernel I/O errors | Preserve its native error/buffer handling and our logical lookup/lease. Its pipe tests must obtain guest descriptors. Both changes cover invalid-descriptor EBADF behavior, using different mechanisms. |

These are not functional prerequisites for this standalone branch, so Depends on remains none. Merge order matters: after any of these lands, rebase and validate the combined behavior rather than selecting one side of a conflict. The simulations above only examine merges; no combined-branch build or runtime pass is claimed.

Previously reviewed [scalar POSIX I/O errors](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/pull/1307) and [Windows positioned I/O](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/pull/2029) also touch file APIs, without implementing the ownership registry. [File/pipe polling](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/pull/1832) will need logical-descriptor lookup if both changes land.

### Tested

- Windows, WinLibs GCC 15.2.0 r7, Release: full `all` and `libs` build; 13 selected tests passed covering ordinary and patched isolation, standard streams, file positioning, filesystem operations, vector I/O, directory buffers/close, AIO, guest memory and narrow/wide formatting. The new socket-pair test also passed. After cleanup and the final upstream rebase, the full build and all 13 selected tests passed again. One intermediate parallel run timed out after the isolation fixture printed its success message; the immediate isolated run and the repeated parallel selection passed without code or timeout changes.
- Linux, Ubuntu 26.04.1 under WSL, GCC 15.2.0, Release: built libc, libkernel, their NID-patched libraries and the relevant test targets. All 26 selected tests passed, including private host descriptor rejection, stale FILE identities, ownership, close races, blocked reads, pipe rollback, stdio errno, directory entries and the shared isolation fixture against actual patched libraries. No full Linux graphics build or game/homebrew run was performed.
- `python tools/check_conventions.py --base upstream/main` and the whitespace check passed. No full CTest suite was run.

The runtime/build results above were obtained at `2b12fd51`, based on upstream `51f69aa2`. The subsequent conflict-free rebase onto `d70b8998` brings upstream AGC profiling/video-output build changes; libc, libkernel, the NID patcher and the file test sources are unchanged. ### What

Depends on #419. Its prerequisite commits are included; the follow-up is `feat(agc): support uniform custom MSAA sample locations`.

After multisampled targets are supported, 3D MiniGolf (PPSA03647) aborts while loading its first course because its four PA_SC_AA_SAMPLE_LOCS_PIXEL registers contain `0x22eea66a`, rather than Vulkan's standard four-sample pattern. Preserve the guest's sample indices and signed sixteenth-pixel offsets through VK_EXT_sample_locations for uniform 2x, 4x and 8x patterns.

Query the device's sample counts, coordinate range, subpixel precision and grid support before enabling the extension. Include the pattern in pipeline and render-pass continuation keys, check the actual depth format and sample count with vkGetPhysicalDeviceImageFormatProperties, create compatible depth images, and supply sample locations at pipeline creation and render-pass begin. Depth attachments retain GENERAL throughout their use. Spatially varying 2x2 patterns and unsupported devices throw. CB resolves validate sample counts independently of raster sample locations.

Vulkan behavior follows the official [sample-location pipeline state](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkPipelineSampleLocationsStateCreateInfoEXT.html), [render-pass state](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkRenderPassSampleLocationsBeginInfoEXT.html), and [depth-attachment requirement](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkCmdDraw.html). The guest coordinate interpretation is unchanged from #419; PS5 coverage and interpolation equivalence remain unmeasured and are recorded in TechnicalDebt.

### Tested

Rebased onto main `f8c2f072`. Subsequent main commits only change PR-intake workflows; the tested runtime/relinker source is unchanged. Windows, MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0, Release, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050 6GB Laptop GPU.

- Independent build of this stacked contribution branch: production `libSceAgcDriver` and `agc_driver_graphics_tests` build successfully. `agc_driver_graphics` passes in 6.03 seconds.
- Regression cases cover custom coordinates and sample indices, signed endpoints for 2x/8x, the normalized standard 4x coordinates, spatially varying pattern refusal, missing extension/count support, unsupported depth formats and depth sample counts, exact image-query flags and usage, and standard-pattern fallback. Unexpected Vulkan query errors propagate. Capability queries run at pipeline creation, rather than on each draw.
- `tools/check_conventions.py --base origin/main` passes.
- Earlier MiniGolf (PPSA03647) integration test: course loading changes from `nonstandard sample locations are unsupported` to a rendered course and HUD. The separate unwritten-pixel-program blocker is covered by #2022. A completed shot is not confirmed; this PR alone does not provide all title startup fixes.

### What

`guest_ajm` fails on macOS, as mugurc reported on #1. the first mono block of `TestMultichannelAt9`, header `0x00` filled with `0x07`, makes LibAtrac9 read a gradient end unit above 31, and `CreateGradient` then writes past `Block::Gradient[31]` into `GradientMode` and the fields after it. what the decoder reports as used for the 27-byte block depends on the compiler: 27 with GCC at `-O1` and above, 24 with GCC at `-O0` and with clang, 20 with the array widened to 48. on macOS the second frame is parsed from offset 24 and fails with `ERR_UNPACK_GRAD_START_UNIT_OOB`

filled with `0xA5` the block is still 27 bytes, decodes the same everywhere, stays in bounds and is audible. the overrun itself is in `Block` in shadps4-emu/ext-LibAtrac9 and in the upstream library, only a malformed block reaches it
