body:
### What
`DecodeColorTileMode` accepted only 2D (`RESOURCE_TYPE` 1, depth 0) and 3D (`RESOURCE_TYPE` 2) color targets. A 1D target (`RESOURCE_TYPE` 0) threw "unsupported color depth, dimension, resource level or metadata mode".

In addrlib, `RESOURCE_TYPE` 0 is `ADDR_RSRC_TEX_1D`. On GFX10 a 1D surface may use the linear and render swizzle modes (`Gfx10Rsrc1dSwModeMask`), and it gets its swizzle pattern the same way as a 2D surface: `GetSwizzlePatternInfo` only tells 3D apart. So a 1D color target one row high is laid out exactly like a 2D target one row tall.

- `DecodeColorTileMode` accepts `RESOURCE_TYPE` 0 with depth 0, like 2D. It rejects a 1D target with a standard swizzle mode (`SW_4KB_S`, `SW_64KB_S`), which addrlib does not allow for 1D.
- `DecodeColorBuffer` decodes a 1D target as that one-row 2D target. One taller than a row (`CB_COLOR_ATTRIB2.MIP0_HEIGHT` not 0) is rejected as unsupported: addrlib only limits 1D to one row on its linear paths (`HwlComputeSurfaceInfoLinear`, `ComputeSurfaceAddrFromCoordLinear`), so a tiled one is not modeled.

### PPSA36082
Hades II renders into a 512x1 sRGB 8_8_8_8 target with `CB_COLOR_ATTRIB3` = `0x4cc6c000` (`RESOURCE_TYPE` 0, `SW_64KB_R_X`, resource level 1) while it loads a level. Plain main stops earlier than that. On main f1451396 (where I tested the game; this branch is rebased on current main) with the fixes it needs to get there (#861, #1367, #1249, #1905, #1961, #1959, #1960, #1928 and a fix for the null pixel program miss from #1901), it threw at that draw; with this change it renders it and goes on to the next problem (MSAA, #419).

### Tested
Linux (CachyOS), x86-64, GCC, 7800X3D / RTX 4090.
- `agc_driver_graphics` (new checks):
  - The game's descriptor decodes as a render target. A linear 1D target decodes. A 1D target with depth, `RESOURCE_TYPE` 3, or `SW_4KB_S` / `SW_64KB_S` is rejected.
  - A 1D target decodes to a one-row extent at its base address. One with a taller `CB_COLOR_ATTRIB2` is rejected.
- Mutations, each failing a check: 1D still rejected; no height check; 1D arrays accepted; standard swizzles accepted.
- ctest: 494/494.

### What

Translate host EILSEQ to guest FreeBSD EILSEQ when asprintf_nid_postfix fails to format an invalid wide character. On Linux, host vasprintf returns errno 84, but the guest ABI uses 86. The change handles only this failed conversion; successful formatting and other errors retain their existing behavior.

The error is specified for the printf family by [FreeBSD vfprintf(3)](https://man.freebsd.org/cgi/man.cgi?manpath=FreeBSD+11.1-RELEASE&query=vfprintf&sektion=3), and [stable/11 errno.h](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/stable/11/sys/sys/errno.h) defines EILSEQ as 86. Open #1804 changes the separate vasprintf wrapper's wide-format routing in Formatting.cpp; it does not change asprintf_nid_postfix in AllocatingStrings.cpp.

### Tested

- Direct Linux baseline-versus-fixed verification passed in [run 37902555693](https://github.com/STUPIDCONTEM/AnyPS5/actions/runs/37902555693), head 0a51258403b46780650706a26a615124b79c8f18. With the unchanged upstream implementation, the regression reports expected guest errno 86 but got 84. Restoring the candidate makes all three focused runs pass.
- The regression uses an invalid surrogate in the C locale, checks negative return/null output/guest errno, then verifies successful formatted allocation, content, matching release and null-destination EINVAL. It explicitly registers the standalone test's default allocator.

body:
### What

`CallSiteResolver::ResolveCallSites` takes `lower_bound(address)` and `lower_bound(address + size)`. For a jump slot whose `r_offset` is `0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF8` or higher, `address + 8` wraps, the upper iterator lands before the lower one, and the loop walks past the end of the map. On main the relinker dies with SIGSEGV (exit 139) in both Linux and `--windows` mode instead of failing with an error. Under ASan:

```
ERROR: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow
    #0 in Relinker::CallSiteResolver::ResolveCallSites(...) CallSiteResolver.cpp:104
    #1 in Relinker::RelinkerPipeline::Relink(...) RelinkerPipeline.cpp:336
```

The resolver now throws `RelinkerException("Relocation target range exceeds the address space")` when the range does not fit, with the same `size > max - begin` check as `EhFrameReader.cpp:173` and `StrictNidFilter.cpp:26`. `0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF7` still reaches the existing PT_LOAD containment check.

`test_jmprel_table_bounds.py`: the fixture's jump slot `r_offset` becomes a parameter; targets `0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF8`, `0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFC` and `0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF` must exit 2 with the new message and write no output.

No open pull request touches `CallSiteResolver.cpp` or this test.

### What

PICO-8 for PS5 (PPSA99808 v0.1.2, [RafaelNGP/pico8-ps5](https://github.com/RafaelNGP/pico8-ps5), GPL-3.0) stops at start-up on `environ` once `__inet_aton` (#1848) resolves:

`+2thxYZ4syk` is `environ`. FreeBSD's libc `getenv` reads it and `setenv`/`putenv` replace it, so the export is a writable `char**`.

The fixed-ID set comes from the [public PS5 payload SDK FreeBSD time header](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk/blob/master/include/freebsd/sys/time.h#L384-L402). [FreeBSD stable/11 kern_clock_gettime and kern_clock_getres](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/stable/11/sys/kern/kern_time.c#L316-L478) reject unknown nonnegative IDs and separately dispatch negative CPU-clock encodings. This change preserves the existing unsupported negative-encoding path and null-pointer behavior. SCE error encoding follows the project's KernelErrors.hpp conventions.

### What

Path-based sceKernelTruncate now returns encoded EISDIR for an existing directory instead of collapsing the resize failure to EIO. On Windows, filesystem resize reports a generic permission error for this case, so recognize a directory only after a successful status query. Keep the existing negative-length check first and leave other resize-error mappings unchanged.

The behavior and negative-length precedence are verified in [FreeBSD stable/11 kern_truncate](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/stable/11/sys/kern/vfs_syscalls.c#L3022-L3061): negative lengths fail before path lookup; a resolved directory is rejected with EISDIR before ordinary write checks. This is a narrow directory classification fix, not a complete rewrite of path-truncation error handling or host filesystem race semantics.

### Tested

Windows 10 Pro 19045, WinLibs GCC 15.2.0 UCRT posix SEH r7, Release, BUILD_TESTING=ON; independent branch from main f145139676a48306681d3a4d5fabf83938759daf.

- GuestFilesystem verifies directory truncation returns encoded EISDIR, preserves guest errno and leaves the directory intact. Negative length still takes precedence with encoded EINVAL and unchanged guest errno.
- Regular-file path truncation covers shrinking, preserved prefix bytes, growth size and zero-filled new bytes. Existing missing-path behavior is retained.
- The directory-error regression fails on unchanged upstream. Parent corrected temporary-directory cleanup so the pre-existing root-removal test remains meaningful. Three focused runs passed, default and explicit libs builds passed, and full CTest passed 488/488 in 25.55 seconds.
- Parent reviewed the kernel source and final change; independent review checked status-query failure guarding, symlink-following behavior and test lifetime. Conventions, whitespace and test registration passed.

No Linux or title run was performed for this branch. #2041 fixes descriptor-based ftruncate and uses a different path; #2001 removes write-watch recording in the same function but does not implement this directory-error behavior. No open PR duplicating this change was found.

body:
### What

`FillClearColor` refuses half and B10G11R11 fill patterns that hold a denormal code, because an implementation may flush denormals in a clear. A fill like that over a resident image goes the CPU way instead: the pattern is written into guest memory and the image is uploaded again.

Astro's Playroom (PPSA01325) fast-clears its 3840x2160 `R16G16_SFLOAT` target `0x515390000` every frame with a denormal half. That is a 33 MiB guest write plus a re-upload every frame.

This change:

- `ClearKeepsDenormals(context, format)` (declared in `Texture.hpp`) probes the device once per format and caches the answer per device:
  - it clears a 1x1 image of the format with denormal codes (half `0x0001`, `0x83ff`, `0x0200`, `0x8001`, one per channel; 11/10-bit `0x001`);
  - it reads the texel back and compares the bits.
- `StorageTexture::FillClear` tries a refused pattern again with denormals decoded exactly (`SmallFloat`, `FillClearColor`), but only when the probe says this device's clears keep them. The clear then stores the guest's bits.
- NaNs, float32 denormals and the SNORM minimum stay refused, as before. Formats without small floats probe as not keeping.

The probe runs in its own `CommandBatch` with `SubmitAndWait`, once per format per device, the same way `StorageTexture` already does its synchronous uploads.

### Tested

Windows 11, WinLibs GCC 15.2, RTX 3060 Laptop. The NVIDIA driver keeps denormal halves in clears; the test prints `denormal half clears are kept by this device`.

- `agc_driver_recorder_tests` has a new case, `denormalClearTests`. It clears a 64x64 `R16G16_SFLOAT` resident image with three patterns:
  - a normal half pattern: accepted, bits exact;
  - a denormal pattern `0x83ff0001`: cleared exactly when the probe says the device keeps it, and checked bit for bit when cleared;
  - a NaN pattern: refused.
  It also checks that the probe is stable and that `R32G32B32A32_SFLOAT` probes as not keeping.
- `agc_driver_tests` passes, and `tools/check_conventions.py --base upstream/main` passes.
- PPSA01325, A/B on the title screen with this commit as the only difference: 8.66 -> 14.30 FPS (115.5 -> 69.9 ms per frame), mean of three runs per side; the per-frame clear of `0x515390000` runs as a GPU clear instead of the CPU write. Current `main` does not reach the title, so both sides ran on an integration branch; details and per-run numbers are in the comments.

body:
### What

Astro's Playroom (PPSA01325) runs a 64-thread compute kernel (69 dwords) every frame to fill DCC keys, HTILE and other metadata. It ran as a shader. Before the fill, every key read of those surfaces waited for a drain (on the UI target `0x534830000`, among others).

What the kernel does, read from its code and confirmed by the new test against the translated kernel:

- It covers every `i` below `min(launched threads, s8, num_records)`. The group id is in `s10`, so the kernel has exactly 10 user SGPRs.
- Into dword `i` of a 4-byte-stride buffer (`s[0:3]`) it stores `pattern[min(i % s9, 3)]`, where the pattern is `s4..s7` and `s9` is the period.
- The modulo is computed with a float reciprocal. Remainders 0, 1 and 2 select `s4`, `s5` and `s6`; anything else stores `s7`.

`MatchDwordPatternFill` (new header `Driver/Memory/DwordPatternFill.hpp`) recognizes the exact code and accepts only one shape:

- a direct, non-partial 1-D dispatch;
- a 4-byte-stride, unswizzled, non-add-tid buffer;
- a period of 1, 2 or 4 dwords;
- whole 16-byte units into a 16-byte aligned destination.

That shape is a 16-byte pattern fill, and `fillBuffer` takes it the same way it takes the existing fill kernel: clear path, `FillBuffer`, key memo. Everything else still runs the kernel. `APS5_NO_FILL_HLE` turns both matchers off.

#1335 recognizes a different, typed pattern-fill kernel (18 dwords, pattern and control read from buffers). Both PRs touch `fillBuffer`, so whichever merges second needs a small rebase.

### Tested

Windows 11, WinLibs GCC 15.2, RTX 3060 Laptop:

- New `agc_driver_dword_pattern_fill_tests` (`tests/execution/DwordPatternFill.cpp`):
  - the matcher accepts the kernel, and refuses every single-bit change of its code, a truncated copy, periods other than 1/2/4, partial units, unaligned destinations, add-tid descriptors, other user SGPR counts, partial dispatches and a missing group id;
  - it clamps to the descriptor's records;
  - ten cases run through `Submit`: matched ones and unmatched ones (periods 3 and 5, a count of 250, a partial dispatch).
- The test passes as is. With `APS5_NO_FILL_HLE=1`, the translated kernel meets the same expectations, which is where the `min(i % s9, 3)` reading comes from.
- `agc_driver_tests` and `agc_driver_pm4_tests` pass, and `tools/check_conventions.py --base upstream/main` passes.
- PPSA01325, A/B on the title screen with this commit as the only difference: 12.68 -> 13.96 FPS (78.9 -> 71.6 ms per frame), mean of three runs per side, B ahead in every pair. Current `main` does not reach the title, so both sides ran on an integration branch; details and per-run numbers are in the comments.

body:
### What

Nonblocking connect now translates a pending host connection to guest EINPROGRESS (36), and a repeated pending connection to EALREADY (37). Previously Windows WSAEWOULDBLOCK became EAGAIN (35), while POSIX EINPROGRESS/EALREADY fell through to EIO (5). Applications checking the expected pending status could incorrectly treat an ordinary connection attempt as failure.

Translation is specific to connect, preserving ordinary send/receive would-block behavior and existing fallback errors. The contracts are [FreeBSD stable/11 connect(2)](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/stable/11/lib/libc/sys/connect.2) and [Microsoft Winsock connect](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winsock2/nf-winsock2-connect). Windows WSAEINPROGRESS describes a separate blocking Winsock operation; it is not reclassified as a pending nonblocking connect.

### Tested

Windows 10 Pro 19045, WinLibs GCC 15.2.0 UCRT posix SEH r7, Release, BUILD_TESTING=ON; independent branch from main f145139676a48306681d3a4d5fabf83938759daf.

- GuestTcp calls the actual nonblocking connect wrapper over loopback, accepts immediate success or requires EINPROGRESS, waits with bounded polls for client/listener readiness, and transfers data. It fails on unchanged upstream at the pending-error assertion and passes with this change.
- The deterministic guest_connect_error test covers initial pending, repeated pending and fallback selection for platform error constants.
- Both focused tests passed 50 repetitions each. Default and explicit libs builds passed; full CTest passed 489/489 in 26.28 seconds.
- Parent independently reviewed the mapping and rejected an overbroad Windows error translation and unnecessary test abstraction before verification. Conventions, whitespace and test registration passed.

An earlier fourteen-proposal integration passed full Linux verification with SPIRV Tools and lavapipe enabled: [run 37898813460](https://github.com/STUPIDCONTEM/AnyPS5/actions/runs/37898813460), exact head 8740893d8db1f13169cb0923d0445dec0a21ba42, 479 tests passed three times and 25 graphics feature tests were skipped (504 registered tests, zero failures). Two unrelated graphics tests exceeded the project 30-second target on their cold run; no timeout occurred. No title run was performed. The repeated-pending case is covered at the mapper level; loopback timing is not used to force a second connection attempt to remain pending.

Open #2079 fixes accepted socket mode in the same runtime and test file; both TCP regression blocks are retained in the integration. #1091 implements readiness events and #1832 descriptor polling. No duplicate pending-connect fix was found.

Current Windows integration, based on upstream `d70b89989473ba1f6ae13e44e079e67f1f8a44b0`, contains the 19 still-open proposals and excludes the three declined changes and the superseded build fix. Default and explicit libs builds passed at `8f0190c793c6dfa2b7a3a3f33f3d2cbe2509937c`; 513 tests passed and one was skipped (514 registered, 52.66 seconds). Five affected I/O and socket tests each passed ten repetitions. Removing only the production ConnectError call reproduced the public TCP pending-error failure on this Windows host; restoring it gave ten passes. Loopback may complete immediately on other hosts, so this is Windows call-site evidence rather than a guarantee that every Linux run exercises the pending path.

The complete external #1091 (f94f0300 and exact tip 7f5f456585e9a112ac468726c43df636d711a1d8), #1832 (f782e4ad175527cb1ca63ee0c0d0fbe58024db5d), and #1676 (942a105c396828f5ab734cfad68cee1c07ca49ef) were also combined locally, preserving their authors. ### What

Accepted TCP connections now inherit the listener's guest nonblocking mode. Previously the accepted socket's cached mode always started as blocking; on Windows this disagreed with the inherited native mode, while Linux's native accept does not inherit O_NONBLOCK. Set both the accepted native socket and its guest cache from the listener mode before publishing the descriptor.

The contract follows [FreeBSD stable/11 accept(2)](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/stable/11/lib/libc/sys/accept.2). The accepted socket remains independently configurable after creation. Mode-setting errors close the newly accepted native socket through the existing guard.

### What

### What

Prepare the combined vertex/pixel shader layout in `sceAgcLinkShaders` after both register sets are available. Previously the helpers prepared stages separately, leaving the pixel stage without the cumulative push-constant offset required by a draw after a vertex stage that uses push data.

This addresses the missing preparation path behind the static-ABI failure reported by johnmaia for EVO PLAYER's `ui_sdf` shader in [#1578](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/issues/1578#issuecomment-6072163434). It uses the existing combined-stage resolver inside the existing preparation transaction. Null-pixel linking retains its single-stage path; exceptions still prevent publishing partial results. No instruction semantics or permissive draw fallback is added.

body:
### What

`ElfReader::TranslateVirtualAddress` could wrap a `PT_LOAD` file offset and return a location in unrelated input bytes. A synthetic ELF with `p_offset=0xfffffffffffff000`, `p_vaddr=0x2000`, `p_filesz=0x2000` and `DT_STRTAB=0x3600` translates to file offset `0x600` after wrapping. On unmodified main, Linux conversion succeeds and emits `DT_NEEDED=libwrongx.prx` from those unrelated bytes. The valid control emits `libkernel.prx`.

Check the selected load segment's complete file range with the existing subtraction-based `_rangeFits` helper before adding the address displacement. The malformed input now exits 2 with `Segment offset out of bounds (offset 0xfffffffffffff000)` and creates neither an executable nor a registry. Windows also rejects it in the shared parser, before its existing PE-specific validation.

The [ELF gABI, sections 7.1 and 7.2](https://gabi.xinuos.com/elf/07-pheader.html) defines `p_offset` as the start of a segment's file image and `p_filesz` as its extent. The check follows the existing `ElfReader::ReadSegment` contract, which rejects a segment whose complete file range exceeds the input. This deliberately rejects truncated segments even when the requested byte itself is inside the file.

Extend the already registered `elf_offsets` test with 20 conversions: valid mappings, the first file-backed byte, a segment ending exactly at EOF, wrapping/past-EOF offsets, truncated and oversized extents, an address at the segment's exclusive end, and an empty segment. Invalid cases require exit 2, the expected diagnostic, and no output or registry. Valid Linux controls inspect the emitted dynamic table and dependency name; Windows controls verify successful PE generation. Existing assertions are retained.

This is the deferred file-offset translation gap recorded in #1690. It does not duplicate that PR's symbol-boundary tests or #1272's symbol guard. Open #1087 and #1956 change other `ElfReader` methods; #1446 bounds RELA tables and #1943 handles Linux layout-address overflow. The audit reviewed all 558 open PRs and current relinker/ELF issues on 9 October 2026; no equivalent implementation was found. No prerequisite is needed.

### Tested

macOS 26.6.2 (25G83), x86-64; AppleClang 21.0.0; CMake 4.4.4; Ninja 1.13.2; Python 3.13. Relinker-only Release build, without third-party submodules or system libraries. Base: `f145139676a48306681d3a4d5fabf83938759daf`, refreshed from upstream main before final review.

- Built and ran all existing tests before selecting the task: **34/34 passed** (37.08 s).
- Ran the extended `elf_offsets` against a saved, unmodified baseline binary: **failed** at `translation-offset-wrap`, because Linux returned 0 and wrote an executable instead of rejecting the input. All three new valid controls passed in both output modes before that failure.
- After the fix, focused `elf_offsets`: **passed** (1.84 s).
- Complete patched suite: **34/34 passed** (25.10 s); extended `elf_offsets` took 1.67 s.
- `python3 tools/check_conventions.py --base origin/main --title 'fix(relinker): validate translated load segment file ranges' --body <PR-description-file>`: passed.
- `python3 tools/check_test_registration.py ../build-relinker`: all five test executables registered.
- `git diff --check` and final diff review: passed; two source/test files, three production lines, no added comments, dependencies or investigation files.

Build and test commands from the repository root:

```sh
cmake -S . -B ../build-relinker -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DANYPS5_RELINKER_ONLY=ON -DBUILD_TESTING=ON
cmake --build ../build-relinker --parallel 4
```

### What

Positive `nanosleep` requests can wrap during conversion to nanoseconds and return immediately: `(1LL << 55)` seconds becomes zero. Sleep in bounded 24-hour intervals, then the remaining seconds and nanoseconds, so the full positive request is retained without overflowing the conversion or a Windows millisecond fallback.

The shared implementation serves `sceKernelNanosleep`, `nanosleep`, and `_nanosleep`. Existing invalid-nanosecond, negative-second, return-value and errno behavior remains covered.

### Tested

Windows 10 Pro 19045, WinLibs GCC 15.2.0 UCRT posix SEH r7, Release, BUILD_TESTING=ON. Independent branch from `f145139676a48306681d3a4d5fabf83938759daf`.

- Extended `guest_nanosleep` launches a child, waits for readiness, verifies that an overflowing positive request remains active, then terminates and reaps it. Startup and observation waits are bounded; POSIX polling retries interruptions against a fixed deadline.
- Corrected regression fails against unchanged upstream and passes three focused runs with the fix (0.43 seconds each).
- Default and explicit `libs` builds passed; full CTest passed **488/488** in 28.94 seconds. After the POSIX-only test interruption adjustment, rebuilt and repeated the focused Windows test three times.
- Committed-head conventions, whitespace and test-registration checks passed. Parent independently reviewed production code and corrected the child test's readiness/output handling before accepting results.

Open #1576 changes sub-millisecond waits in other libraries and #1588 changes epoll waits; neither changes this conversion. Linux, console hardware and PS5 titles were not run locally. No claim is made about hardware behavior for centuries-long requests.

### What

Exports `sceSystemServiceLaunchWebBrowser` (NID `-+3hY+y8bNo`) from libSceSystemService. AnyPS5 launches no web browser, so it fails with the kernel's `EOPNOTSUPP` (0x8002002D) for any arguments, the same choice as `sceTextToSpeech2Initialize` (#1374).

- RommPS (PPSA76677) 1.1.0, released today, declares `int sceSystemServiceLaunchWebBrowser(const char *uri, void *param)` ([credits.cpp L16](https://github.com/s0liton/RommPS/blob/754d4d60f25938a5136b9e2efcd074313c4386c5/platform/ps5/app/rommps/examples/rommps/kit/credits.cpp#L16)) and calls it as `sceSystemServiceLaunchWebBrowser(url, nullptr) == 0` ([L86-L95](https://github.com/s0liton/RommPS/blob/754d4d60f25938a5136b9e2efcd074313c4386c5/platform/ps5/app/rommps/examples/rommps/kit/credits.cpp#L86-L95)).
- When the call fails, RommPS's message becomes "The browser didn't open. Scan the code to watch on your phone", pointing at the QR code it shows for the YouTube video ([L396-L411](https://github.com/s0liton/RommPS/blob/754d4d60f25938a5136b9e2efcd074313c4386c5/platform/ps5/app/rommps/examples/rommps/kit/credits.cpp#L396-L411)).
- Opening the host's browser would not help here: the page RommPS opens, `http://127.0.0.1:8780/video?v=...`, is served by its own payload on the console ([L239-L242](https://github.com/s0liton/RommPS/blob/754d4d60f25938a5136b9e2efcd074313c4386c5/platform/ps5/app/rommps/examples/rommps/kit/credits.cpp#L239-L242)).

- PSXS5 (PPSA97510), SwanStationPS5 (PPSA98510) and ScreenTester5 (PPSA69420) import it too, behind earlier stops.

RommPS 1.1.0, from its [GitHub release](https://github.com/s0liton/RommPS/releases/tag/v1.1.0) (the [homebrew catalog](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-homebrew-catalog) reserves PPSA76677 for it; the 1.1.0 listing is pending), relinked with `--windows` and run on Windows 10:

body:
### What

`strerror_r` replaced EINVAL with ERANGE when the error number was unknown and the output buffer was also too short. Preserve EINVAL for unknown numbers, matching [FreeBSD stable/11 strerror_r](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/stable/11/lib/libc/string/strerror.c), which checks buffer truncation for valid error numbers only. Known errors still return ERANGE when their messages do not fit. Existing truncation, NUL termination, and errno preservation remain intact.

### Tested

Windows 10 Pro 19045, WinLibs GCC 15.2.0 UCRT/posix/SEH r7, Ninja Release, BUILD_TESTING=ON, SPIRV-Tools disabled. Independent branch from `f145139676a48306681d3a4d5fabf83938759daf`.

- New `guest_strerror_r` fails against unchanged upstream at `short unknown buffer still returns EINVAL`.
- Regression covers known/unknown errors; negative, positive and extreme unknown numbers; ample, exact, short, one-byte and zero-byte buffers; NUL termination, adjacent sentinel bytes, and guest errno preservation.
- Parent independently inspected the exact FreeBSD reference and reviewed the patch, then built and ran the regression in the full runtime.
- Full default and explicit `libs` builds passed; full CTest: **489/489 passed**, 31.78 s.

The separate regression leaves `GuestErrors.cpp` unchanged, avoiding the test-only change in #1712. #1729 uses strerror_r in syslog but does not change this implementation. Linux and PS5 hardware/titles were not run.

body:
### What
On Windows, direct memory was always mapped as views of a section. Views have no page write watch, so the GPU driver tracked CPU writes to them by arming pages read-only and taking a write fault. With live AVX state, the exception frame Windows builds for such a fault overwrites the stack from RSP-0x20 down. That is most of the System V red zone, where guest leaf functions keep live values. Measured on Windows 11 with AVX2; without live AVX state the frame starts at RSP-0x120.

PPSA29141 took about 5,000 such faults a second, 80,000 of them with AVX state live in 75 s. It crashed in roughly a quarter of 90-second runs, in a Unity job, on a red-zone slot read back as 0.

- A physical page mapped at one address is now private `MEM_WRITE_WATCH` memory, one allocation per mapping, with the section as its store.
  - Its content goes to the section when the mapping ends while the page stays allocated, and comes back when it is mapped again.
  - A second mapping turns the private one into views first.
  - Unmapping part of a private mapping re-commits the kept parts as their own allocations, with their content and protections.
  - During either switch, accesses to the range wait in the vectored handler (`GuestArenaAwaitRetarget`) and retry.
- `WindowsMappings::Collect` finds Commit's write-watched allocations without `VirtualQuery`.
- `HostWrite` also refuses private pages the guest left read-only (reads into them return `EFAULT`).
- `APS5_DIRECT_MEMORY_VIEWS=1` restores views-only mapping. `APS5_TRACE_FAULTS=1` counts the faults the handler resumes from and how many had AVX state live.
- The crash report prints the words around RSP and the register state of every thread.
- Note for review: main's new private-mapping observer is not called for the parts a partial unmap re-commits. Their pages are rewritten in full, so the write watch reports them as changed.

### Tested
Windows 11, i7-13650HX, RTX 4070 Laptop.
- `guest_memory` gains tests for:
  - a page mapped once is private and never armed;
  - content survives an unmap and remap;
  - a second mapping converts to views while another thread keeps writing;
  - a partial unmap while another thread writes.
- The existing view tests now alias their pages.
- LEGO Party! (PPSA29141): 0 write faults (was ~383,000 in 75 s). Four two-minute runs and a five-minute run without a crash. Frame rate unchanged against views-only (15–35 fps both).
- Full suite passes on this branch.

body:
### What
- **HTILE fast clears.** A depth target with `DB_Z_INFO.TILE_SURFACE_ENABLE` and an HTILE base is cleared before a draw when the title wrote its HTILE since the last look and every word reads cleared (ZMask 0, plus SMem 0 for a tracked stencil plane). The planes are cleared to `DB_DEPTH_CLEAR` / `DB_STENCIL_CLEAR` and the words stored back as expanded. PPSA29141 clears depth only through HTILE with a compute kernel (`InvokeHTileClearComputeShader` in Unity's `ClearMRT`). Without this, depth kept every earlier frame and moving objects left black trails ("stuck motion" in the LEGO PARTY title scene). Word layouts are radv's for GFX10.
- **Depth surface reuse.** A depth surface answers texture and storage lookups only at its own extent, and is superseded once a color target or written storage image covers its memory: the title freed the depth target and reused the memory. Before, sampling such reused memory failed or aborted with "sampling the depth/stencil plane … is not implemented".
- **Unreachable V#s read as null**: a base with no readable page, or a size over `maxStorageBufferRange` over memory that is not readable that far (SRT slots a shader declares but does not reach). A V# of another resource type still throws, as on `main`.
- **Stencil clears through `DB_RENDER_CONTROL`** draw with a stencil test that always passes and replaces with `DB_STENCIL_CLEAR`.
- Debug aids: `APS5_TRACE_MARKERS=<seconds>|msaa` (marker/draw/dispatch timeline), `APS5_DUMP_FRAMES_AFTER`, thread names and `APS5_SAMPLE_THREADS_AFTER` in the thread sampler.
- Gaps recorded in TechnicalDebt: partial HTILE clears, draw-side HTILE compression state, depth slices other than the first.

### Tested
Windows 11, i7-13650HX, RTX 4070 Laptop. LEGO Party! (PPSA29141): title scene, menus, studio audience and several minigames render correctly in frame dumps (before: black trails and stuck motion over the whole scene). New decode/HTILE unit tests in `agc_driver_graphics`. Full suite passes on this branch.

body:
### What
- An ATRAC9 run job stops after the gapless total of output samples counted from the start of the current segment and leaves the rest of its input unconsumed; the next run starts the next segment with the decoder as it is, without a second skip. A reset (`SetGaplessDecode` with the reset flag, `ClearContext`, initialization) starts a new segment.
- Run jobs decode until the input or the output is exhausted, with or without `RUN_MULTIPLE_FRAMES`.
- FMOD (PPSA29141) sets a gapless total shorter than a sound's frames and reads the frames after it on later runs. With the output held at the total, its stream reader waited forever and the last buffer looped audibly ("stuck" audio).
- Debug aid: `APS5_DUMP_AUDIO=<file>` writes the AudioOut2 mix (raw 48 kHz stereo float), used to check for repeated audio.
- Both behaviours are recorded in TechnicalDebt.

### Tested
Windows 11, i7-13650HX. LEGO Party! (PPSA29141): 148 s of the dumped mix from intro to menus, with no quarter-second of loud audio repeating earlier audio exactly (before: the music and voice lines looped). Full suite passes on this branch.

body:
### What
- `_umtx_op`: `UMTX_OP_WAIT`, `UMTX_OP_WAIT_UINT` and `UMTX_OP_WAKE` following FreeBSD's `kern_umtx.c` (64-bit or zero-extended 32-bit compare, relative `timespec` timeout, `-1` and `errno` on failure). Other operations, `_umtx_time` timeouts, misaligned addresses and wake counts below 1 throw. PPSA29141's `libc.prx` and Unity's `PS5Util.prx` reach it only through these wrappers. Recorded in TechnicalDebt.
- `scePthreadMutexLock` / `scePthreadMutexTimedlock` / `scePthreadRwlockWrlock` wait in short slices inside an `InterruptibleScope`, so `sceKernelRaiseException` reaches a thread blocked on a guest mutex or rwlock. Unity's GC stop-the-world signals every thread; a thread blocked on a mutex never ran the handler and the game deadlocked during loads.

Windows 11, i7-13650HX, RTX 4070 Laptop. New `guest_umtx` test; `guest_raise_exception` gains delivery-while-blocked tests for mutex lock, timed lock and rwlock write lock. Full suite passes on this branch. LEGO Party! (PPSA29141) no longer deadlocks in its GC during level loads.

body:
### What

`_FSinh` and `_FCosh` evaluated the unscaled float hyperbolic function before multiplication, so representable scaled results overflowed. For example, `_FSinh(100.0f, 0x1p-40f)` returned infinity instead of a finite result near `1.22e31`.

Evaluate finite intermediates in double and narrow only after scaling. Handle zero, NaN and infinite arguments explicitly according to the scaled CRT routines, including signed-zero behavior, and report ERANGE for actual final float overflow. Tiny products that round to zero preserve errno.

Semantics are sourced from Microsoft's primary CRT implementations [xsinh.cpp, _FSinh](https://github.com/microsoft/STL/blob/main/stl/src/xsinh.cpp) and [xcosh.cpp, _FCosh](https://github.com/microsoft/STL/blob/main/stl/src/xcosh.cpp), whose stated scale domain is `|y| <= 1`. No implementation code or polynomial tables were copied. PS5 hardware behavior has not been measured.

### Tested

Windows 10 Pro 19045, WinLibs GCC 15.2.0 UCRT/posix/SEH r7, Ninja Release, BUILD_TESTING=ON, SPIRV-Tools disabled. Independent branch from `f145139676a48306681d3a4d5fabf83938759daf`. Open #1844 adds ordinary libm test coverage without changing these implementations; this regression has a separate test file and target.

- New `guest_scaled_hyperbolic` built and run against unchanged upstream: failed finite scaled-result, errno, and special-value assertions.
- Six finite reference cases (x=0.25, 1, 90, 100, 150, 192), all argument/scale signs, including subnormal scales. Fixed expected float values independently verified with 100-digit decimal arithmetic.
- Signed zero, tiny products, NaN/infinite arguments, zero scale with huge finite arguments, and actual overflow at x=100/y=1 and x=193/minimum-subnormal scale.
- Parent independently reviewed the implementation, corrected tiny-product errno behavior, and ran the new regression in the full project runtime.
- Full default and explicit `libs` builds passed.
- Full CTest suite: **489/489 passed**, 26.87 s.
- Committed-head conventions, whitespace and test-registration checks passed.

Linux and PS5 hardware/titles were not run. Tests use the default floating-point rounding mode; alternate rounding modes were not validated.

body:
### What

Windows `getargc`/`getargv` always exposed just the executable path, dropping all supplied arguments. Initialize the UCRT wide argument vector without wildcard expansion and copy its entries into the existing stable guest argument storage as UTF-8. This preserves the CRT's argument quoting rules, empty arguments, and Unicode. The Linux `/proc/self/cmdline` path is unchanged.

The implementation uses the supported Windows UCRT toolchain's `_configure_wide_argv(_crt_argv_unexpanded_arguments)` before reading `__argc`/`__wargv`; normal narrow-main executables do not otherwise initialize the wide vector. See Microsoft's [CRT argument variables](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/c-runtime-library/argc-argv-wargv?view=msvc-170) and [C command-line parsing rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/c-language/parsing-c-command-line-arguments?view=msvc-170).

fix(shader): flush v_mullit_f32 denormals in the float modes that flush them

### What

Part of #981 (FLOAT_MODE family), a follow-up to #1850. With f32 denormals flushed, `v_mullit_f32` gave other bits than the hardware when a source was a denormal:

| src0, src1, src2 | hardware | `main` (NVIDIA, RADV) |
|---|---|---|
| `0`, `0x3f800000`, `0x00000001` | `0xff7fffff` | `0x00000000` |
| `0xbfc00000`, `0x00000001`, `0x3f800000` | `0x00000000` | `0x80000000` |
| `0x7f800000`, `0x00000001`, `0x3f800000` | `0x00000000` | `0x7fffffff`, `0xffc00000` |

TechnicalDebt said only the denormals-kept behaviour was modelled. On hardware `v_mullit_f32` flushes like `v_mul_f32`: all three sources and the product are flushed, so a positive denormal limit (src2) counts as zero and selects -FLT_MAX, and tininess is detected before rounding.

`v_mullit_f32` is now in the "inputs and result flushed" group of `f32DenormalFlushFor`. It reads its sources through `flushF32Denormal` and passes the product through `flushTinyProduct`, both from #1850. The existing NaN, zero and limit rules are unchanged, so a flushed source now takes the zero-operand path and gives `+0`. The product flush and tininess (`0x3f7fffff * 0x00800000` gives `0`, not `0x00800000`) already match NVIDIA's and RADV's default behaviour, but not a driver that keeps denormals, such as lavapipe. With f32 denormals kept nothing changes.

Measured on RDNA2 (gfx1036, the same family as the gfx1035 used for #1850) with the HW oracle, all float controls set: 6907 rows (19 values per operand, 5 of them denormals, plus 48 products near 2^-126) with f32 denormals flushed and kept, at IEEE=0 and IEEE=1. This rule matches every row. Flushing only src2 misses 723 rows per flushing mode, and flushing the inputs but not the product misses 69.

### Which title needs it

Titles run their shaders with f32 denormals flushed: TechnicalDebt's float mode entry records it for Astro's Playroom's 0xc0, and a shader without a known float mode is translated the same way. This changes the result of `v_mullit_f32` in that mode. No specific title run was done: we have no title copy to run.

### Tested

CachyOS Linux, GCC 16.2, RTX 4070 Ti (NVIDIA 615.71.09) and Radeon 610M (RADV, Mesa 26.2.4).
- `agc_driver_f32_denormal_flush` gets two results on the test's 32 rows, captured on hardware with f32 denormals flushed: `v_mullit_f32 v26, v4, v5, v6` for the limit, and `v_mullit_f32 v27, v4, v5, 1.0` for the product, since the rows with a tiny product all have a zero src2. 31 of the 64 new cells differ from the hardware's result with denormals kept. On `main` it fails on both drivers (`lane 1 no float mode v_mullit_f32 v26, v4, v5, v6 is 0x80000000, expected 0x00000000`); with the change it passes, in under a second.
- Without the tininess check the test still passes on NVIDIA and RADV, which already flush a tiny product before rounding; as in #1850, only lavapipe tells them apart. Not run on lavapipe locally.
- Full Release ctest: 498/498 on NVIDIA and on RADV, including `agc_driver_nan_quieting`, which runs `v_mullit_f32` in 0xc0.
- A local differential run of 2744 rows against the hardware: 208 rows differed in each flushing mode on `main`, none now, on NVIDIA and RADV. With denormals kept, 91 rows still differ, as on `main`: both drivers flush f32 denormals by default, which TechnicalDebt already records.
- `check_conventions.py` and `git diff --check` pass.

Not tested: a title run; f32 denormal modes 1 and 2 now throw for `v_mullit_f32`, like the rest of its group.

body:
### What

For #1458. Astro Bot stops at submission validation after about 20 s when part of its command memory has no host import:

```
AGC driver: unsupported PM4 packet type: header 0x00000001 at DWORD 8730 of 10340
```

A label whose memory the device has no host import of was stored by a completion action of its batch, so it landed only when the batch was reaped. Labels recorded after it were stored by the GPU and became visible first. The title saw those, reused the earlier label's memory for its next command buffer, and the late store then wrote the label's `1` over a `RELEASE_MEM` header there (EdouardSence traced the write to `Recorder::AfterCompletions` with a [watchpoint](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/issues/1458#issuecomment-6055410168)).

On the console the CP stores labels in stream order: a later `RELEASE_MEM` value is never visible before an earlier one. The Linux amdgpu driver relies on this. Its gfx10 fences are `RELEASE_MEM` writes ([`gfx_v10_0_ring_emit_fence`](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/6c377d19d4a5116d9bec5203aa3c6c11523e7898/drivers/gpu/drm/amd/amdgpu/gfx_v10_0.c)), and [`amdgpu_fence_process`](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/6c377d19d4a5116d9bec5203aa3c6c11523e7898/drivers/gpu/drm/amd/amdgpu/amdgpu_fence.c) signals every fence up to the last sequence number it reads.

As [oneandonlydean diagnosed](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/issues/1458#issuecomment-6057226059), a label the GPU can't store has to be stored at its place in the stream. `WriteLabelOnGpu` now answers "memory not imported" for such a label in every case, not only with `APS5_DRAIN_COMPLETION_LABELS=1`. The callers then wait for the recorded work and store it on the CPU. Labels in imported memory are unchanged, and so is a label behind a pending write-back, which the GPU also stores in order. The cost is one wait per label the GPU cannot reach. That is listed in TechnicalDebt. Open #1747 and #1896 add `reason == 6` checks, which never match after this change; #1864 edits neighbouring lines in `PacketMemory.cpp` and `DeferredLabels.cpp`.

### Which title needs it

PPSA21567 (Astro Bot, v01.019.000), from #1458. EdouardSence's [runs](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/issues/1458#issuecomment-6059891851) were on `main` 6b573862 with #759 merged locally (without #759 it stops earlier, on another error) and `APS5_HOST_IMPORT_MIB=64`. There it stops at the line above in 3 runs out of 3, and with `APS5_DRAIN_COMPLETION_LABELS=1` it runs to the 100 s timeout in 3 runs out of 3. That debug variable stores these labels the same way as this change, and it also turns off label queuing, which this change keeps. We do not have this title and could not run it with this change.

### Tested

CachyOS Linux, GCC, RTX 4070 Ti (NVIDIA) and Radeon 610M (RADV).

- New `agc_driver_unimported_label_order` test. It records a fill, then a label in memory the device has no import of, then a later label in imported memory, and waits for the later one to land. The guest then writes a `RELEASE_MEM` header over the first label's word, and the test waits for the device to go idle. On `main` the first label still holds `0` when the later one has landed, and the reused word ends up `0x00000001`, the #1458 symptom (3 runs out of 3 on each GPU). With the change it passes 3 runs out of 3 on each GPU.
- Full ctest: 498/498 on each GPU.
- `check_conventions.py --base origin/main` and `git diff --check`: clean.
- Not tested: the title itself.

### What

Part of #981, a follow-up to #1867. In a shader with `IEEE_MODE`=1, the cube instructions return a signaling NaN unchanged:

```
v_cubesc_f32 v10, 0, 0x7fc12345, 0xff812345   hardware 7fc12345, recompiler 7f812345
v_cubetc_f32 v10, 0, 0, 0xff812345            hardware ffc12345, recompiler ff812345
v_cubema_f32 v10, 0xff812345, 0, 0            hardware ffc12345, recompiler ff812345
```

With IEEE=1 the hardware quiets a signaling NaN result of `v_cubesc/cubetc/cubema_f32`, and keeps the sign the instruction gives it (`cubesc` above returns `-z`). With IEEE=0 the bits pass through. This is the rule #1867 measured for the unary instructions. `floatCube` picks the NaN operand itself, so these bits never came from the driver: #1867 recorded `v_cubema` as "left to the driver", but the code always returned the signaling NaN as it was. `floatCube` now passes a NaN result through `quietNan32`. IEEE=0, shaders without a known float mode and `v_cubeid_f32` behave as before. With `DX10_CLAMP`=1 a clamped NaN still becomes 0; with `DX10_CLAMP`=0 it keeps its sign and payload and is quieted only with IEEE=1 (row 2 `v_cubema_f32 ... clamp`: `7f800001` at IEEE=0, `7fc00001` at IEEE=1 on gfx1036).

### Which title needs it

No known title needs it yet. It extends the rule #1867 measured to three more instructions, and it only changes shaders running with IEEE=1, which titles we know do not use (they use 0xc0, IEEE=0).

### Tested

Frames are written as a linked list of records: next pointer, u32 module offset, then the module name at +0x10. `GetBufferSize` reports the count and the bytes `Self` will need. The signatures and record layout are inferred from the title and listed in TechnicalDebt, including the unknown u32 at +0xC (written as 0). Windows throws.

### Tested

### What

PPSA28997 (God of War Sons of Sparta) imports `lrand48` and `srand48`. They follow FreeBSD libc:

body:
### What

The f16 and f64 min/max family ignored the shader's `IEEE_MODE`, so a NaN operand gave a different result than on the console:

```
v_min_f16(0x3c00, 0x7c01), IEEE=1:              hardware 0x7e01, main 0x3c00
v_min_f64(+0, 0x7ff0000000000001), IEEE=0:      hardware +0,     main 0x7ff8000000000001
```

#1826 and #1867 made the f32 forms and the unary instructions follow `IEEE_MODE`; TechnicalDebt still listed "the f16 and f64 min/max/med3" as following a single mode. This PR covers those forms: `v_min_f16`, `v_max_f16`, `v_min3_f16`, `v_max3_f16`, `v_med3_f16`, `v_min_f64` and `v_max_f64`. RDNA2 has no f64 min3, max3 or med3.

The f16 forms now choose the NaN result on the f16 bits, like the packed f16 forms already do. The f64 forms keep their current lowering at IEEE=1 (it already matched) and get the IEEE=0 rule. The f32 path and `ieeeMinMaxF32` are unchanged. Shaders with no known float mode follow IEEE=0, as elsewhere.

Measured with the [hardware oracle](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/blob/main/docs/dev/HW_ORACLE.md) on RDNA2. I used gfx1036 (Radeon 610M), not the gfx1035 of #1826; both are RDNA2. Every float control was set explicitly, at IEEE=0 and IEEE=1, with f32 denormals kept and flushed:

| | IEEE=0 | IEEE=1 |
|---|---|---|
| f16 | a NaN operand returns the other operand unchanged, src0 when both are NaN | as IEEE=0, but a signaling NaN operand returns that NaN quieted, src0 checked first; min3/max3 are two nested pairs, med3 is min3 when any operand is NaN (same rule as f32) |
| f64 | src1 NaN: src0 unchanged, even a signaling NaN; otherwise src0 NaN: src1 | a signaling NaN operand returns that NaN quieted (already the case on `main`) |

Measured rows (gfx1036):

| instruction | operands | IEEE | hardware | `main` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `v_min_f16` | `0x0000`, `0xfd23` | 1 | `0xff23` | `0x0000` |
| `v_med3_f16` | `0x0000`, `0x0000`, `0xfd23` | 1 | `0xff23` | `0x0000` |
| `v_min_f16` | `0x7c01`, `0xfe55` | 0 | `0x7c01` | `0x7e01` RADV, `0x7fff` NVIDIA |
| `v_min_f64` | `0x7ff0000000000001`, `+0` | 0 | `+0` | `0x7ff8000000000001` |
| `v_max_f64` | `0x7ff0000000000001`, `0x7ff8000000000000` | 0 | `0x7ff0000000000001` | `0x7ff8000000000001` |

The TechnicalDebt float mode line now lists these forms with their rule. It also records a separate gap: when f16/f64 denormals are flushed, the hardware flushes denormal inputs of these instructions (`v_min_f16(0x0001, 0x8001)` gives `0x8000`), and this lowering does not, before or after this PR.

### Which title needs it

No title yet. This completes the `IEEE_MODE` series (#1826, #1867) for the f16 and f64 min/max forms that TechnicalDebt still listed as following a single mode. Most titles use `FLOAT_MODE` 0xc0 with IEEE=0, where `v_min_f64`/`v_max_f64` now return the non-NaN operand as the console does instead of a NaN, and f16 min/max keep src0's NaN bits when both operands are NaN. No title is known to hit either case.

### Tested

CachyOS Linux, RTX 4070 Ti (NVIDIA) and Radeon 610M (RADV), Release build.

- New `agc_driver_f16_min_max_nan`, laid out like `agc_driver_f32_min_max_nan`: 128 rows of ±0, ±1, ±inf, quiet and signaling NaNs with payloads and denormals, with garbage in the high halves, through the five f16 ops and `-`/`|x|` modifiers. Each row runs with no float mode and with IEEE=1, against tables captured on the oracle. It passes on both GPUs. On `main` it fails at `row 94 v_min_f16 v10, v4, v5 is 0x00007e01, expected 0x00007c01`.
- `agc_driver_f64_arithmetic` held the IEEE=1 results (its table matches gfx1036 exactly at IEEE=1) but ran without a float mode. It now runs both ways, and its min/max columns at IEEE=0 come from the oracle.
- Every row of the f16/f64 min/max cases from our oracle sweep (424 to 2,221 rows per op, with clamp and neg/abs variants) matches the hardware on both drivers in the four mode combinations (IEEE 0/1, DX10 clamp 0/1, f32 denormals kept/flushed).
- The SDWA forms follow too: `v_min/max_f16_sdwa` with WORD_0/WORD_1 selects, clamp, `mul:2` and neg/abs, 400 rows each in two IEEE=1 modes (DX10 clamp on and off), match the hardware on both drivers with this branch (`main`: 64 of 400 differ).
- Full ctest on both GPUs, `check_conventions.py`, `git diff --check`.
- With f16/f64 denormals flushed, these forms still differ from the hardware (measured, recorded in TechnicalDebt, see above).
- Not tested: lavapipe, gfx1013 hardware, rounding other than to nearest even.

body:
### What

Part of #981, follow-up to #1867. The f64 unary instructions always set the quiet bit on a signaling NaN input:

```
v_fract_f64 0x7ff00000_00000001, IEEE=0: hardware 0x7ff00000_00000001, recompiler 0x7ff80000_00000001
```

The SPIR-V lowering quiets every f64 NaN, but the hardware does that only with `IEEE_MODE`=1, the same rule #1867 measured for f32 and f16. Translation now follows `GuestContext::floatMode.ieeeMode` through a third helper, `quietNan64`, next to `quietNan32` and `quietNan16`.

- **Changed here:** `v_sqrt/rcp/rsq/fract/floor/ceil/trunc/rndne/frexp_mant_f64`, `v_ldexp_f64`, `v_div_fixup_f64` and `v_cvt_f64_f32` return a signaling NaN unchanged with IEEE=0 and quieted with IEEE=1. A shader without a known float mode follows IEEE=0.
- **Recorded, not changed:** `v_add/mul/fma_f64` follow the same rule on hardware, but their NaN bits stay with the driver, as for f16 (#2083 now chooses them for f32). `v_cvt_f32_f64` always quiets, like `v_cvt_f16_f32`, and the code already does that.

TechnicalDebt: the "Signaling NaN inputs" line now names the f64 forms and the two conversions.

### Which title needs it

No single title. This applies #1867's measured rule to the f64 forms of the same instructions. Most titles run with IEEE=0, where the f64 forms were still quieting.

Measured on RDNA2 (gfx1036, Radeon 610M) with the HW oracle. #1867 was measured on gfx1035, which is the same family. Settings: f32 denormals flushed, f16/f64 denormals kept, round to nearest even, DX10 clamp on.

| Instruction, input | IEEE=0 | IEEE=1 |
|---|---|---|
| `v_floor_f64 0xfff00000_12345678` | `0xfff00000_12345678` | `0xfff80000_12345678` |
| `v_ldexp_f64 0x7ff40000_00000000, 0` | `0x7ff40000_00000000` | `0x7ffc0000_00000000` |
| `v_rcp_f64 0x7ff00000_00000001` | `0x7ff00000_00000001` | `0x7ff80000_00000001` |
| `v_div_fixup_f64 1.0, 0x7ff00000_00000001, 1.0` | `0x7ff00000_00000001` | `0x7ff80000_00000001` |
| `v_cvt_f64_f32 0xff812345` | `0xfff02468_a0000000` | `0xfff82468_a0000000` |
| `v_cvt_f32_f64 0x7ff00000_00000001` | `0x7fc00000` | `0x7fc00000` |

### Tested

CachyOS Linux, GCC 16.2, RTX 4070 Ti (NVIDIA 615.71) and Radeon 610M (RADV, Mesa 26.2.4).
- `agc_driver_nan_quieting` runs two more kernels, 13 f64 instructions × 8 rows captured on hardware, with no mode, IEEE=0 and IEEE=1, bit for bit. For `v_rcp/rsq/sqrt_f64` only the NaN cells are compared, because their finite results are approximations. The f64 part runs only when the device has Float64, like the other f64 tests; otherwise it prints that it was skipped and the f32/f16 checks still run. Checked with a copy of the test that removes Float64 from the target: it skips the f64 part and passes on both drivers.
- `agc_driver_f64_arithmetic`, `_conversions`, `_division`, `_division_modifiers`, `_nan_conversions` and `_transcendental` expected quieted NaNs. Their tables predate the oracle's explicit modes, so they now pin `FLOAT_MODE` 0xf0, IEEE=1, as #1867 did for its tests. The tables are unchanged.
- Negative checks, each fails: quieting always (the old behaviour) and quieting never.
- A hardware-vs-recompiler comparison of these instructions at IEEE=0 and IEEE=1, with DX10 clamp and f32 denormals each on and off: no NaN row differs on either driver.
- Full ctest 498/498 on NVIDIA and on RADV. `check_conventions.py` and `git diff --check` pass.
- Not tested: gfx1035, lavapipe.

body:
### What
`ReadRawComputeShader` (the fallback for compute programs that were never registered) reads a growing prefix of guest memory, 64, 128, 256 words and so on, and decodes it. When the decoder throws `std::out_of_range`, it reads more. The instruction-length check, the scalar decoder and the vector decoders throw `std::out_of_range` for an instruction cut off by the end of the span.

The memory decoders (SMEM, DS, MUBUF, MTBUF, FLAT, through `requireTwoWords` and the generic memory check), the image decoder (MIMG and its NSA payload) and the export decoder threw `std::runtime_error` instead. So when a two-word instruction of those families lay across a window boundary, the read failed instead of growing. Whether it happened depended on where the program's instructions fell. vkQuake (PPSA99010) terminated with `truncated FLAT instruction` in some runs and not others.

Those five throw sites now use `std::out_of_range`, like the rest of the decoder. The messages are unchanged. Nothing in the tree catches `std::runtime_error` around decoding; the one test that matches a truncation message (`LdsCondxchg`, `truncated DS instruction`) catches `std::exception`.

Test (`agc_driver`): a raw program of 63 `s_nop`, a two-word `s_load_dword` in words 63 and 64, and `s_endpgm` reads back as 66 words. It fails (`truncated SMEM instruction`) without the change.

body:
### What
vkQuake (PPSA99010, the homebrew Vulkan port) opens `history.txt` with mode `"rt"` at startup, and AnyPS5 threw from `fopen`.

FreeBSD's `__sflags` ([`lib/libc/stdio/flags.c`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/releng/11.0/lib/libc/stdio/flags.c)) reads the access character (`r`, `w`, `a`), then `b`, `+`, `x`, `e` and `v`, and **stops at the first other character without failing**, so on the console `"rt"` opens for reading. On Windows, AnyPS5's `fopen` inserted `b` after the first character and passed the rest on: `"rt"` became `"rbt"`. The CRT rejected that with `EINVAL`, and `fopen` throws for any error other than `ENOENT`. `freopen` accepted only a fixed list of 15 modes.

Both now parse the mode like `__sflags` (`ParseFileMode`):
- The native mode is the access character, then `+` if seen, then `b` on Windows, then `x` if seen.
- An unknown access character, or `x` on a read-only stream, returns NULL with `EINVAL`, as `__sflags` does.
- `x` on an existing file returns NULL with `EEXIST` instead of throwing.
- `e` (close-on-exec) and `v` (verify) are accepted and ignored.
- Whether a stream writes (for the written-path record) comes from the parsed mode, so `"rt+"`, which FreeBSD opens read-only, no longer counts as writing.

Tests (`guest_standard_streams`):
- The byte-exact mode matrix, run through both `fopen` and `freopen`, adds `"rt"`, `"r+t"`, `"wt"`, `"w+e"`, `"ae"` and `"rbv"`.
- `""`, `"q"`, `"tr"`, `"rx"` and `"rbx"` return NULL with `EINVAL` from both.
- `"wx"` on an existing file returns NULL with `EEXIST`, and on a new file creates and writes it.
- `"rt+"` opens read-only: a write fails.
- The test fails (an exception from `fopen` on `"rt"`) with the old `FileAndHeap.cpp`.

### Tested
Windows 11 Pro (26200), MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0 (WinLibs r7), Release.

- The full suite (488 tests) passes on this branch alone. It was run from the generated `CTestTestfile.cmake` commands because antivirus blocks `ctest.exe` on this machine.
- `tools/check_conventions.py --base origin/main` passes.
- vkQuake gets past its `history.txt` open with this, on a local branch with my other pending changes.

Not tested on Linux or macOS. The `b` insertion stays Windows-only as before.

body:
### What

`sceKernelFsync` returned the host's `-1` on failure instead of an encoded kernel error. It also sent guest socket descriptors to the host CRT, which could only report an invalid descriptor.

Translate native failures through the existing kernel error mapping and preserve the caller's errno in the kernel entry point. The POSIX `fsync` wrapper now decodes the kernel result into `-1` plus guest errno. Open guest sockets return EINVAL, and invalid/closed descriptors return EBADF.

The socket/invalid-descriptor distinction follows [FreeBSD 11 fsync](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/stable/11/lib/libc/sys/fsync.2); the kernel encoding is the project's existing KernelErrors/SceErrorFromErrno convention. Regular files still use the existing host flush operation.

### Tested

Windows 10 Pro 19045, WinLibs MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0 UCRT/posix/SEH r7, Ninja Release, BUILD_TESTING=ON, SPIRV-Tools disabled. Based directly on `f145139676a48306681d3a4d5fabf83938759daf`; independent of #2029.

- New `guest_fsync` fails against upstream at `kernel result encodes the guest error`.
- With the fix, it checks negative/large invalid descriptors, closed regular descriptors, open/closed sockets, successful regular-file flushes, kernel errno preservation, and POSIX errno translation.
- Focused `guest_fsync`, `guest_filesystem`, and `guest_kernel_sync`: 3/3 passed.
- Full default and explicit `libs` builds succeed.
- Full CTest suite: **489/489 passed**, 27.52 s.
- Committed-head conventions, whitespace, and test-registration checks pass.

Linux and PS5 hardware/title behavior were not tested. The regression checks API results, not crash/power-loss durability.

Overlap review: #1738 registers a terminal test at the same CMake insertion point; it changes different production functions and is not a dependency. #2001 deletes the POSIX fsync wrapper as part of broader removals; it does not implement the error translation here. This PR remains independently based on main; overlapping hunks need reconciliation if either change lands first.

An [external review](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/pull/2030#pullrequestreview-5466099238) approved this exact head and reports a Linux/GCC 12.2 build plus passing `guest_fsync` (1/1). This is reviewer-reported validation, separate from the local Windows results above.

title: fix(libkernel): translate fsync errors for guest callers

body:
### What

Concurrent positional I/O on Windows saved and restored the shared file pointer. A simultaneous sequential read could observe the positional transfer's offset, and restoring it could discard another thread's progress.

`NativePositioned` now uses a separately reopened file object for each transfer. It checks the original handle's granted access before reopening, so a read-only descriptor cannot gain write access (or vice versa). The original file pointer is never moved. EOF behavior is retained; reopen failures return an I/O error without a seek-and-restore fallback.

The new `guest_positioned_io` regression exercises all four scalar/vector positional APIs concurrently with sequential reads, including a duplicated descriptor. It checks exact file contents through an independent native reader, permission failures, short reads, EOF, zero-length transfers, and exclusive-sharing failures. TechnicalDebt records the sharing/locking limitation.

Host behavior follows Microsoft's [ReOpenFile](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winbase/nf-winbase-reopenfile) and [NtQueryObject](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winternl/nf-winternl-ntqueryobject) documentation.

Scope: synchronous positional I/O only. #1135 concerns the separate AIO implementation. Inspected #1777 and #1518; their Stdio.cpp changes address random devices and timestamps rather than this helper.

### Tested

Windows 10 Pro 19045, WinLibs MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0 UCRT/posix/SEH r7, Release, Ninja, BUILD_TESTING=ON, SPIRV-Tools disabled. Base: `f145139676a48306681d3a4d5fabf83938759daf`.

- Before the fix: the new concurrency regression fails at `concurrent transfers preserve sequential data and positioned results`; existing guest_filesystem and guest_file_vector pass.
- With the fix: expanded concurrency/permission/EOF regression passes five consecutive runs (~0.33 s each).
- Final regression also includes native full-file verification and exclusive-sharing failures.
- Full default build and explicit `libs` build succeed.
- Full CTest suite: **489/489 passed**, 55.75 s, including the final regression and GPU execution tests.
- Committed-head conventions check, whitespace check, and test-registration check pass.

Linux and a PS5 title/homebrew were not run. No game compatibility or performance improvement is claimed. Reopening for each transfer has overhead; restrictive host sharing/locks can prevent a transfer.

Overlap review: #1807 adds an adjacent sandbox documentation entry; there is no functional dependency. #2001 also changes `NativePositioned`, but removes the shared-position save/restore while retaining transfers on the original handle; it does not implement the separate-handle isolation in this PR. This PR remains independently based on main; those overlapping hunks need reconciliation if either change lands first.

An [external review](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/pull/2029#pullrequestreview-5466115518) approved this exact head and reports a Linux/GCC 12.2 build plus passing `guest_positioned_io` (1/1). This is reviewer-reported validation, separate from the local Windows results above.

body:
### What

`sceKernelGetModuleList` (`IuxnUuXk6Bg`, libkernel) is missing on `main`. Ruffle Flash (PPSA68091) stops at it once its `lstat` stop (#1624) is fixed.

It now returns the handles of the loaded guest modules: the main program and every loaded `.prx` image, in load order. Host runtime libraries are left out. Each handle is the id `sceKernelGetModuleInfoFromAddr` already reports for that image, so the two agree, and it is the `sceKernelLoadStartModule` handle when the image was opened through the loader. On Linux the images come from `dl_iterate_phdr`, on Windows from `EnumProcessModules`.

The `(int32_t* handles, size_t count, size_t* actual)` signature and the errors follow shadPS4 ([process.cpp](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4/blob/0fe263a4760dfbfa973366890061749b4af0de97/src/core/libraries/kernel/process.cpp#L244-L264)):
- a null `handles` or `actual` returns `EFAULT`;
- when more images are loaded than `count`, the first `count` handles are written and it returns `ENOMEM` without writing `actual`.

The ENOMEM case, the filtering, and handles that are AnyPS5 ids rather than the console's are listed in TechnicalDebt.

### Log

@babyhuey's runs of the homebrew catalog release with #1624 merged (thanks):

- Linux, `main` d64134f0 + #1624 ([comment](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/pull/1624#issuecomment-6070702243)): on `main` it stops at `app.elf: symbol lookup error: app.elf: undefined symbol: DRGXpDDh8Ng` (`lstat`), and with #1624 the next stop is `IuxnUuXk6Bg`.
- Windows, `main` f1451396 + #1624 ([comment](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/pull/1624#issuecomment-6072367960)):
  ```
  FAIL: unresolved ELF import IuxnUuXk6Bg from libkernel.prx
  ```

Both of those builds also had babyhuey's other open PRs merged. Only #1624 exports `lstat`.

The call site is in Ruffle's own `eboot.bin` (release 1.2.0, `PPSA68091.zip` sha256 `b34b40b69da30dafce4ea67ee312a55b6bd9b07b59849741253b2c46147076be`). I unwrapped the SELF and disassembled it:
- At 0xa54 it calls `sceKernelGetModuleList(handles, 0x200, &count)` with a 4-byte handle array.
- A nonzero result logs `Ruffle PS5: module list -> %#x`, and the title then loads `/system/common/lib/%s.sprx` itself.
- On success it calls `sceKernelGetModuleInfo` on each handle. It tries `st_size` 0x160, 0x1a8, 0x1b0, 0x158 and 0x200, and matches names with `strstr`. `sceKernelGetModuleInfo` is also absent on `main`. A rig run has since shown it is the next stop, and the second commit adds it (see below).

### Tested

aarch64 Debian 13 host. The full project can't be built here because it needs x86-64.

- Extended `core/libs/tests/GuestModuleInfo.cpp` (`guest_module_info`, Linux):
  - the list starts with the main program's id;
  - it holds `libkernel.prx` exactly once, leaves out the dlopened non-`.prx` fixture, and has no duplicate ids;
  - with one slot too few it returns `ENOMEM`, fills the slots it has and leaves `actual` alone;
  - null pointers return `EFAULT`.
- I ran the test natively against `ModuleInfo.cpp` and `DynamicLoader.cpp` built as a shared `libkernel.prx`, with Zig 0.17 clang, also under UBSan, and it passes. Two mutants each fail at the expected check: one without the `.prx` filter, and one that writes `actual` on `ENOMEM`. In that harness the existing `invalid_argument` checks need `catch (...)`, because libc++ is linked statically into both binaries. That applies to `main`'s test as well.
- `ModuleInfo.cpp` and the test compile for x86_64-linux-gnu and x86_64-windows-gnu with `-Wall -Wextra` (Zig 0.17 clang). The only warning is the existing `-Wreturn-type-c-linkage` from `General.hpp`. The Windows path is compile-checked only; it was not run.
- `python3 tools/check_conventions.py --base origin/main` passes.
- Not run with the title.

### Follow-up: `sceKernelGetModuleInfo`

On my x86-64 Linux box (Ubuntu 24.04, lavapipe), `main` f1451396 with #1624 and this PR merged (ref d973cd6f), Ruffle Flash PPSA68091 1.2.0 gets past `lstat` and `sceKernelGetModuleList` and stops at:

```
./app.elf: symbol lookup error: ./app.elf: undefined symbol: kUpgrXIrz7Q
```

That NID is `sceKernelGetModuleInfo`; the second commit adds it. With both commits it moves on to `sigemptyset` (claimed by #1641), and the `guest_module_info` test passes on x86-64 (ctest, 1/1):

```
./app.elf: symbol lookup error: ./app.elf: undefined symbol: +F7C-hdk7+E
```

The call site is the loop from the description, in Ruffle's unwrapped `eboot.bin` (capstone):

```
0x0a54  call [sceKernelGetModuleList]          ; rdi = int32 handles[0x200], esi = 0x200, rdx = &count
0x0ae0  memset(info + 8, 0, 0x500)             ; info at rbp-0x660
0x0af6  mov edi, [handles + i*4]
0x0b07  mov qword [info], 0x160
0x0b12  call [sceKernelGetModuleInfo]          ; rax == 0 -> 0xbd8 (use the name)
0x0b3c  mov qword [info], 0x1a8 ; call ; je    ; then 0x1b0, 0x158, 0x200
0x0bd4  jne 0xc52                              ; every size failed: next handle, first rc kept for the log
0x0bdc  strlen(info + 8) ; strcat into a summary of the first 12 names
0x0c40  strstr(info + 8, needle) ; jne 0xe08   ; match: sceKernelDlsym(handle, ...) for Init/Open/Read/Close
```

- It reads only `name`, at offset 8. Nothing reads the segments, the count or the fingerprint.
- `size` 0x160 is tried first. A nonzero return is not fatal: the title tries the next size, then the next handle. When no name matches, it logs `Ruffle PS5: %s not in %zu modules (%d named, info rc %#x): %s` and loads `/system/common/lib/%s.sprx` itself.
- The loop only runs when the GOT entries for the mouse (or keyboard) `Init`/`Open`/`Read` functions are null (0x0a1a). The import is what stops the load. The loop itself is a fallback path.

`sceKernelGetModuleInfo(int32_t handle, ModuleInfo* info)` fills the 0x160-byte `SceKernelModuleInfo`: `st_size` (u64) at 0, `name[256]` at 8, four `{u64 address, u32 size, s32 prot}` segments at 0x108, `segment_count` at 0x148 and `fingerprint[20]` at 0x14c. The layout is the same in [fpPS4](https://github.com/red-prig/fpPS4/blob/04cefd43e6fddd1ab033e7980cd356d14c964905/sys/sys_types.pas#L319-L337) (packed record, `size:QWORD` … `fingerprint:array[0..19] of Byte`) and [shadPS4](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4/blob/0fe263a4760dfbfa973366890061749b4af0de97/src/core/module.h#L15-L31) (`OrbisKernelModuleInfo`). The [OpenOrbis docs](https://github.com/OpenOrbis/OpenOrbis-PS4-Toolchain/blob/master/docs/MD/PS4%20Libraries/Libkernel.md) give the same layout. prosper (643ad45e) does not implement this export. `static_assert`s in `SceTypes.hpp` pin the offsets.

- The handle has to be one that `sceKernelGetModuleList` returns, so the two agree. Name and segments come from the same code `sceKernelGetModuleInfoFromAddr` uses: the shared part of `Fill` moved into a template, with no change in behaviour.
- The errors follow [shadPS4](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4/blob/0fe263a4760dfbfa973366890061749b4af0de97/src/core/libraries/kernel/process.cpp#L190-L205) and the other functions in this file:
  - a null `info` returns `EFAULT`;
  - any `st_size` other than 0x160 returns `EINVAL` and leaves the buffer alone;
  - an unknown handle returns `ESRCH`, as `sceKernelDlsym` does here.
  
  [fpPS4](https://github.com/red-prig/fpPS4/blob/04cefd43e6fddd1ab033e7980cd356d14c964905/kernel/ps4_libkernel.pas#L203-L220) also returns `EFAULT` and `ESRCH` but does not check the size.
- The fingerprint is left zero. Segment `prot` uses the 1/2/4 bits that `sceKernelGetModuleInfoFromAddr` already reports, while fpPS4 and shadPS4 copy the ELF `p_flags`. Windows calls `NotImplemented_nid_no_patch`, like `sceKernelGetModuleInfoFromAddr`. All of this is listed in TechnicalDebt.

Tested (aarch64 Debian 13, Zig 0.17 clang), extending `GuestModuleInfo.cpp`:
- `libkernel.prx`'s info matches `sceKernelGetModuleInfoFromAddr` (name, segments) and has a zero fingerprint.
- Every listed handle resolves, and the main program's name matches.
- Sizes 0x158, 0x1a8, 0x1b0, 0x200 and 0 return `EINVAL` and leave the buffer alone.
- Null returns `EFAULT`. The dlopened non-`.prx` fixture's handle and -1 return `ESRCH`.
- It passes natively, also under UBSan. Four mutants each fail at the expected check: any size ≥ 0x158 accepted, the handle ignored, no segments for `ModuleInfo`, and `EINVAL` for null.
- `ModuleInfo.cpp`, `Module.cpp` and the test compile for x86_64-linux-gnu and x86_64-windows-gnu with `-Wall -Wextra`. The only warning is the existing one from `General.hpp`.
- `check_conventions.py` passes.
- Not run with the title yet.

### What

`agc_driver_storage_cache_budget` uploads and flushes 64 MiB images to test a multi-gigabyte cache. Cold Linux lavapipe runs in #1059/#1971 took 40–60 seconds, exceeding the 30-second test limit, and CPU devices skipped the eviction assertions.

Use the existing `APS5_TEXTURE_CACHE_MIB` override for a 32 MiB test cache and 512×512 R32_UINT images (1 MiB each). Size the retention and eviction sets from the actual accounted allocation. Keep shader marker readback, object-identity, retained-entry, exact two-oldest-entry eviction and cleanup checks; execute eviction on CPU Vulkan too. Set the test's CTest timeout to 30 seconds. Existing graphics unit tests retain coverage of the physical-heap budget formula.

**#1059 has merged. This branch has been rebuilt directly on `main` `d70b8998`: one commit, two files.** The final diff contains only the bounded storage test and its timeout. All #1971, #1265, #1986, #1999 and #1913 prerequisite changes have been removed; none is needed for this patch. This addresses the review request to isolate the diff.

Duplicate review inspected #1059/#1971 and #1971's `e3180e13` update: that update fixes sampled-texture identity and does not bound this storage test. The broader #2001 removal proposal is not an implementation dependency.

### Tested

Exact source head `68072d60`: [independent validation](https://github.com/kali113/AnyPS5/actions/runs/37925995362) passes on native GitHub Linux and Windows runners, Release / GCC, including full default builds, all-library packaging and three repetitions of the relevant runtime tests under a 30-second limit. Linux lavapipe executes the storage test three times with distinct empty Mesa caches: **4.63, 1.43 and 1.37 s**; graphics unit tests also pass. Hosted Windows runs the graphics tests and skips the storage Vulkan test because no usable device is available. No Windows GPU execution is claimed.

These are fork validation jobs, not collaborator-dispatched upstream checks. Unrelated tests from the full suite were not run in this validation.

Earlier pre-PR Linux validation on the prerequisite integration branch took **0.44, 0.42 and 0.40 s** for separate cold caches. Ignoring the configured cache budget deliberately failed the eviction assertion in **0.42 s**, confirming that the test checks eviction. body:
### What

Part of #981. `FP16_OVFL` was decoded into `GuestContext::floatMode`, serialized and part of the cache key (#1816), but nothing read it: every f16 result overflowed to infinity. Translation now follows `floatMode.fp16Overflow`.

Measured on RDNA2 (gfx1036, a Ryzen 7 7700X iGPU, not the PS5's gfx1013) with the HW oracle, 32 f16 instruction forms (add, sub, mul, fma, fmac, div_fixup, med3, max, pk_mul, pk_add, pk_fma, fma_mixlo, mul with clamp, mul with `mul:2`, add through SDWA to `WORD_1`, fma with clamp, exp, log, rcp, rsq, sqrt, sin, cos, ldexp, cvt_f16_f32, cvt_f16_u16, cvt_f16_i16, cvt_pkrtz_f16_f32, rcp with `mul:2`, exp with clamp, frexp_mant, floor) over 32 rows each, at IEEE=0 and IEEE=1 with f16 denormals kept, and at IEEE=0 with them flushed, `DX10_CLAMP`=1, f32 denormals flushed, round to nearest even, `FP16_OVFL`=0 and =1 (`--ieee I --dx10-clamp 1 --denorm32 0 --denorm16 D --round32 0 --round16 0 --fp16-overflow O`):

- `FP16_OVFL`=1: an f16 result that would round to ±infinity is written as ±0x7bff, in every form above, unless a source operand is infinite, in which case the infinity passes through (`inf + 1`, `inf * 2`, `fma(65504, 2, -inf)`, `ldexp(inf, 1)`, `exp(inf)`, `cvt_f16_f32(inf)`). A zero source is not exempt: `v_rcp_f16`, `v_rsq_f16` and `v_log_f16` of ±0 give ±0x7bff, and so do `v_exp_f16` of 16 or more and `v_rcp_f16` of 2^-16, whose f32 intermediate overflows or not. The threshold is the nearest-even one: 65504 + 16 (a tie) overflows, 65504 + 15.99 does not. The sign is kept (`-65504 - 16` gives 0xfbff).
- `v_div_fixup_f16` keeps the infinity it writes for a zero denominator or an infinite numerator and clamps any other infinite quotient, including the one it writes for a NaN quotient.
- `v_cvt_pkrtz_f16_f32` never overflows and is unchanged. NaN results, the clamp modifier and `DX10_CLAMP` are unaffected; with `mul:2` applied (f16 denormals flushed, IEEE=0) the doubled result is clamped the same way.
- `IEEE_MODE` and the f16 denormal mode do not change the rule: the IEEE=1 runs differ from the IEEE=0 ones only in signalling NaN quieting, the flushed runs only in the flushed denormals.

Changes:
- `clampF16Overflow` applies the rule to an f32 value before it is converted to f16, given the source values whose infinity exempts the result. `writeF16` takes those sources, so the scalar binary, ternary, mix, SDWA, convert and `v_interp_p2_f16` paths get it, as do the packed lanes, the unary instructions, `v_ldexp_f16` and `v_div_fixup_f16` on its bits.
- A shader without a known float mode, and `FP16_OVFL`=0, keep the previous lowering.
- `HW_ORACLE.md`: the `fp16_overflow` row said division by zero still produces infinity; the measurement above says `v_rcp_f16` of zero is clamped and only `v_div_fixup_f16` keeps it. TechnicalDebt: the float mode entry lists `FP16_OVFL` as read, and a new entry records the rule and what it leaves open (`v_fma_mix*_f16` with f32 sources and `v_interp_p2_f16` with infinite inputs follow the rule unmeasured; round modes other than nearest even are not modelled).

Raw data (bodies, rows and the results in all six modes): https://gist.github.com/snoozedDev/9174fac268859aba2e9ff790b5dabe6b

### Tested

Arch Linux (kernel 7.2.5), GCC 16.2.1, Release, RTX 3090 (NVIDIA 610.57.04) and the RADV iGPU (gfx1036, Mesa 26.2.2), `main` f1451396.

- New `agc_driver_fp16_overflow`: 16 instructions (add, sub, mul, fma, div_fixup, pk_mul, pk_add, fma_mixlo, add through SDWA, exp, log, rcp, rsq, ldexp, cvt_f16_f32, cvt_f16_u16) × 32 rows captured on gfx1036 with `FP16_OVFL`=0 and =1, IEEE=0, `FLOAT_MODE` 0xc0, `DX10_CLAMP`=1; 109 of the 512 cells differ between the two settings. The test runs with no mode and with `FP16_OVFL`=0 (checked against the first table) and with `FP16_OVFL`=1 (the second). Where the NaN bits come from a driver op any NaN is accepted; where translation chooses them (`v_div_fixup_f16`, packed, `v_ldexp_f16`) they are compared bit for bit. Passes on both GPUs; with `main`'s translation it fails on both at `lane 0 FP16_OVFL=1 v_add_f16 is 0x00007c00, expected 0x00007bff`.
- Full Release ctest: 498/498 on the RTX 3090, and the 24 f16, modifier, SDWA, packed and division tests on RADV.
- Not run on lavapipe.

body:
### What

A depth/stencil-only draw whose pixel program address (`SPI_SHADER_PGM_LO/HI_PS`) was never written is rejected on `main` with:

```text
AGC graphics: depth/stencil-only draws without a pixel shader are not implemented
```

The draw decoder already reads an unwritten address as 0 and binds the null pixel program for it (`DecodeGraphicsPrograms`, since #469). Only `PixelProgramSkipped` required both registers to be present and 0, and the precheck in `DrawPrecheck.cpp` rejected the never-written case before the draw got there.

- `PixelProgramSkipped` now reads an unwritten `SPI_SHADER_PGM_LO/HI_PS` as unset, like a written 0. `NullPixelProgramRejection` then applies to such a draw too, so one that writes color is rejected as "a draw without a pixel program writes color", as with a written 0.
- The precheck no longer rejects these draws. It still drops the ones that test neither depth nor stencil, as before.
- The graphics test fixture `makeState()` now names a pixel program at 0x100. Its draws relied on an absent address being read as a real pixel program.

### Tested

Ubuntu 26.04, GCC 15.2, Release build, AMD Radeon R9 380 (RADV, Mesa 26.0.8).

- `agc_driver_graphics` passes. New checks: with both registers erased, the draw is read as having no pixel program, is rejected if it writes color, and is accepted as depth-only otherwise. Without the `PixelProgramSkipped` change the new check fails with `an unwritten pixel program address was not read as unset`.
- Full `ctest`: 492/494. `agc_driver_emulated_color_compare` (needs `shaderResourceMinLod`, which GFX8 lacks) and `agc_driver_f32_denormal_flush` (`v_fma_f32` denormal result on GFX8) fail the same way on `main` on this card.
- Sonic Origins (PPSA05324), with #2004 and local workarounds for its earlier stops (see #2021): its depth/stencil clear draws have no pixel program and never write `SPI_SHADER_PGM_LO_PS`. Before, they stopped at the precheck above. With this change they reach the null pixel program variant, `prepared shader artifact is missing for the requested static ABI ... stage=5 wave=64`, which #1902 covers.
- `tools/check_conventions.py --base origin/main` passes.
