body:
Closes #1927

### What

A rect-list draw needs a prepared rectangle for its (front, vertex variant, fragment variant). Rectangles are built only when the title resolves the graphics ABI through `sceAgcCreateInterpolantMapping`. A fragment variant prepared at the draw (the null pixel program, or a shader deferred at registration) therefore has none, and the draw throws `prepared rectangle artifacts are missing`.

There are two commits:
1. `refactor(agc): look up a rect-list draw's rectangle through DrawRectangle` moves the lookup into `DrawRectangle(front, fragment, vertexId, fragmentId, target)`. Behaviour is unchanged.
2. `fix(agc): prepare a rect-list draw's missing rectangle at draw from its prepared stages`: when the lookup misses, `DrawRectangle` logs it, calls `ResolvePreparedGraphics(front, fragment, 17, target)` and looks it up again. Any other failure still throws.

### Tested

Linux (Nobara 44, GCC), RTX 5070 Ti, NVIDIA 595.91.07.

The new check in `tests/execution/PreparedGraphics.cpp` prepares a fragment variant that was never linked to the front through the ABI, then draws a rectangle with it through `DrawRectangle`.

| | `ctest -R agc_driver_prepared_graphics` |
|---|---|
| `main` 1be6f9f1 + commit 1 (lookup moved, no behaviour change) + the test | fails: `AGC driver: prepared rectangle artifacts are missing` |
| this branch | passes, logging `Rect-list draw of shader ... has no rectangle for fragment shader ...; preparing it at draw` |

The test can't run on `main` without commit 1. The draw path has no function a test can call short of a full GPU draw, and the ctest suite has no harness for that. Commit 1 adds that function without changing behaviour, so the test builds and fails there because of the bug, not because it doesn't compile. I can squash the two commits if you prefer one.

The `agc_driver_prepared_shaders*` tests and `pixel_ancillary` also pass on the combined branch.

Stray, with #1902: without this change it aborts on the first rect-list draw that uses the null pixel program. With it, the log shows `Rect-list draw of shader 0x200bbe0000 has no rectangle for fragment shader ...; preparing it at draw` and the run continues to a later, unrelated error.

### What

A window close ends in `std::exit` on a helper thread (`LibcRequestExit_nid_postfix`), and `std::exit` destroys the host libraries' statics while the title's threads are still running. AJM and APR keep their state in namespace-scope statics, so a title thread that calls them during exit reads freed memory:

- `libSceAjm.native`: `g_instances` and `g_batches` (and their mutexes). A job on a freed `Instance` decodes a garbage codec, `sceAjmBatchWait` returns `SCE_AJM_ERROR_INVALID_BATCH` for a batch it just started, and `sceAjmInstanceDestroy` frees an instance twice.
- `libkernel` APR: `g_files`, `g_idsByPath`, `g_directories`, `g_counterWrites` and the AMM state from `_amm()`. A read resolves its file id through the freed vector.

All of these are now allocated once and never destroyed, the same approach #1197 took for NGS2. Callers don't change: the namespace-scope names are now references to the heap objects.

Closes #1925

### Tested

Nobara 44 x86-64 (Linux 7.2), GCC 16.2, RTX 5070 Ti, driver 595.91.07. Base: `main` f1451396.

- New test `guest_ajm_teardown` (UNIX only, it needs `dlopen`). It registers an `atexit` handler, then `dlopen`s `libSceAjm.native` and creates an instance. Because the library is loaded after the handler is registered, its statics are destroyed before the handler runs. The handler then runs a batch on the instance, waits for the batch and destroys the instance. With `main`'s `Ajm.cpp` it aborts 3 of 3 times (`free(): double free detected in tcache 2`). With this change it passes.
- `ctest -j1 --timeout 60`: 494 of 495 pass. The one failure, `guest_dynamic_loader`, also fails here without this change. `tools/check_conventions.py` and `tools/check_test_registration.py` pass.
- Demon's Souls PPSA01341 v1.07, closed with the window's close button at the attract movie after 150 s. These runs used our test stack (`main` from 10-07 with #1071, #1202, #1184 and local performance changes) with this commit on top. Before: 15 of 15 closes crashed (SIGABRT on `AJM: decoding codec 4026830656 is not implemented`, `APR: cannot open <garbage>` or `double free or corruption`, or SIGSEGV after `NCA DecoderManager: sceAjmBatchWait() failed with error code 0x80930004`), and 3 of 3 with #1658. After: 5 of 5 closes exit 0 with no core. One more run aborted at boot, before any close, on an X RandR error (`BadRROutput`) and `VideoOut: presentation thread cannot stop itself`. That is unrelated to this change.
- Windows: not built. The change is plain C++.

Other libkernel state lives in namespace-scope statics too (`Equeue.cpp`, `SyncOnAddress.cpp`, `DirectMemory.cpp`). Demon's Souls didn't hit those in these runs, so they are left as they are.

body:
### What

`decodeDepthBias` rejected a draw that rasterizes both faces when the front and back depth bias differ (`depth bias differing between front and back faces`). Vulkan has one depth bias per draw, and the cull mode is baked into the pipeline.

Such a draw is now recorded twice in the same render pass:

- `DecodeState` keeps the front values in `depthBias*`, puts the back values in the new `backDepthBiasConstant`/`backDepthBiasSlope`, and sets `depthBiasPerFace`. A face whose offset enable bit (PA_SU_SC_MODE_CNTL bit 11 or 12) is clear gets bias 0, which is the same as no bias.
- `Pipeline` creates a second `VkPipeline` for that state. The first one culls back faces, the second culls front faces, and `depthBiasPerFace` is part of the pipeline key.
- Both draw paths in `Draw.cpp` record the draw with the first pipeline and then call `ContinueBackFaces` (bind the second pipeline, set the back bias) and record it again. Both pipelines share one layout, so descriptor sets and push constants stay bound.
- When one face is culled, nothing changes: the decoder already used the remaining face's values.
- `APS5_REJECT_PER_FACE_DEPTH_BIAS=1` brings back the rejection.

The TechnicalDebt entry records the difference from hardware: the vertex stages run twice, and all front faces land before all back faces instead of in primitive order. That only matters for blending or stencil updates that depend on the order, or for a vertex shader that writes memory.

Closes #1923

### Tested

Nobara 44 x86-64 (Linux 7.2), GCC 16.2, RTX 5070 Ti, driver 595.91.07. Base: `main` f1451396.

- `agc_driver_graphics`: the depth-bias block now decodes differing front/back bias with no culling, front-only and back-only bias, and cull-front with the back bias. On `main` it fails, because the decode throws.
- New GPU test `agc_driver_depth_bias_per_face` (`tests/execution/DepthBiasPerFace.cpp`): a front-facing and a back-facing triangle at depth 0.5, a `LESS` test against a surface cleared to 0.5, opposite biases on the two faces. Only the face that is pulled closer passes, in both directions. Equal biases and front-only bias are checked too. With a single pipeline that draws both faces with the front bias, it fails (`the back-facing triangle at (20, 4) is 255, expected depth-rejected`).
- `ctest -j1 --timeout 60`: 494 of 495 pass. The one failure, `guest_dynamic_loader`, also fails here on a branch without this change. `tools/check_conventions.py` and `tools/check_test_registration.py` pass.
- Demon's Souls PPSA01341 v1.07: not run with this branch. In the tutorial level about 4.3k shadow-caster draws per 10 s hit this rejection (PA_SU_SC_MODE_CNTL 0x01001a48, front slope -17.6, back slope -480000). A local stopgap that drew both faces with the front bias removed those rejections with no new errors.

body:
### What
RADV on the PS5 ([mihawk-99/PS5_Mesa](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Mesa)) builds its own command streams, as on Linux. Its preamble, draws and dispatches use packet forms the PM4 validator refused, so ccleste's (PPSA59322) command buffers were rejected.

Two commits.

**Graphics preamble and draws:**
- `CONTEXT_CONTROL` that only updates the load and shadow enables to zero, which RADV emits when it does not shadow registers. It is a no-op. Any enable bit, a compute queue, or a short packet is still rejected.
- `SET_UCONFIG_REG_INDEX` of `VGT_PRIMITIVE_TYPE` with index 1, next to the index-2 `VGT_INDEX_TYPE` write already accepted.
- `WRITE_DATA` to memory (`DST_SEL` 5) from the graphics queue.
- `EVENT_WRITE` `PIPELINESTAT_START` (25), `PIPELINESTAT_STOP` (26), `SQ_NON_EVENT` (38) and, on the graphics queue, `VGT_FLUSH` (36). The statistics counters are not modelled, and the events that would read them stay rejected.
- `ACQUIRE_MEM` over the full 48-bit range (`COHER_SIZE_HI` and `COHER_BASE_HI`); the bits above 48 are still rejected.

**Dispatches and register loads:**
- `DISPATCH_DIRECT` and `DISPATCH_INDIRECT` with the `SHADER_TYPE` header bit, which RADV sets on every dispatch, as other packets already may.
- `FORCE_START_AT_000` in the dispatch initiator. The driver never offsets dispatches by `COMPUTE_START_X/Y/Z`, so they already start at zero.
- `LOAD_CONTEXT_REG_INDEX`, `LOAD_SH_REG_INDEX` and `LOAD_UCONFIG_REG_INDEX` in their consecutive-register form (a register offset and a count, `DATA_FORMAT` 0). RADV uses it to load `DB_STENCIL_CLEAR` and `DB_DEPTH_CLEAR` from an image's clear values. The offset-and-data form keeps its old checks.

**Added after review started** (four commits, found running vkQuake, PPSA99010, the homebrew Vulkan port, through RADV):
- **Partial last thread group.** For an unaligned direct dispatch RADV sets `PARTIAL_TG_EN` in the initiator and puts each axis's last-group size in the upper half of `COMPUTE_NUM_THREAD_X/Y/Z`. The dispatch now runs `(groups - 1) * full + last` threads per axis through the dispatch-size limit `USE_THREAD_DIMENSIONS` already uses, or plain groups when every last group is complete. A zero or oversized last group throws (`Pm4::PartialGroupThreads`). `DecodeComputeStageInfo` reads only `NUM_THREAD_FULL` (bits 15:0); it read the whole register, so a partial size would have widened the workgroup.
- **`COPY_DATA` from memory to context registers.** Where it doesn't use `LOAD_CONTEXT_REG_INDEX`, RADV loads clear values into `DB_STENCIL_CLEAR`/`DB_DEPTH_CLEAR` and `CB_COLORn_CLEAR_WORD0/1` with `COPY_DATA` to a register (`DST_SEL` 0, one or two dwords). It isn't a memory store, so the packet drains like other `COPY_DATA` the driver can't record on the GPU, and executing it reads the source then and writes the registers. Register, GDS, immediate and clock sources, and destinations outside the context registers, are still rejected.
- **`COPY_DATA` to memory through `DST_SEL` 5** (`COPY_DATA_DST_MEM` in Mesa's `sid.h`), the current form of the deprecated GRBM-synchronized `DST_SEL` 1 already accepted. RADV uses it for every memory destination; vkQuake's timestamp writes hit it.
- **In-order dispatches.** RADV clears `ORDER_MODE` for a dispatch that needs in-order wave launch. That is the stricter guarantee and the driver doesn't reorder waves, so a direct or indirect dispatch now needs only `COMPUTE_SHADER_EN`.

Tests (`agc_driver_pm4`): each accepted form, and next to it the neighbouring form that is still rejected (an enable bit in `CONTEXT_CONTROL`, a wrong index bank, event indices on the statistics and `VGT_FLUSH` events, `VGT_FLUSH` on a compute queue, an unrelated event type, dispatch modifiers beyond `FORCE_START_AT_000`, `ACQUIRE_MEM` range bits above 48, and an out-of-range register in the consecutive load form). For the later commits: `PartialGroupThreads` for complete, partial, empty and invalid last groups; `DecodeComputeStageInfo` ignoring the partial half; `COPY_DATA` writing one and two context registers, not resolving as a store, and rejecting an immediate source, a non-context register, an overflowing range and a misaligned source; `DST_SEL` 5 with an immediate and a 64-bit timestamp; initiators `0x2047`, `0x2007` and indirect `0x2005` accepted and `0x40` rejected. Each new check fails with its change reverted.

**Two more commits**, also from vkQuake:
- **Indirect draw register location 0.** RADV writes 0 as the start-instance location of `DRAW_INDIRECT` and `DRAW_INDEX_INDIRECT` when the vertex shader doesn't read the base instance, and as the draw-index location of the multi forms when draw IDs are off. The validator accepted only `0x280` as "no register"; 0 is now accepted and decoded as `0x280`.
- **4-byte-aligned indirect argument bases.** RADV sets the draw and dispatch indirect base with `SET_BASE` to the argument buffer address plus the command's offset, which Vulkan only requires to be a multiple of 4 (vkQuake's ends in `0x14`). The validator required 8-byte alignment; the records are read as 32-bit words, so a 4-byte-aligned base is now accepted and a 2-byte-aligned one still rejected.

Tests for these two (`agc_driver_pm4`): location 0 in `DRAW_INDIRECT` and in the multi form resolves to `0x280`, and an out-of-range location (`0x200`) is still rejected; a `SET_BASE` ending in `0x14` is accepted and one ending in `0x12` rejected. Each fails with its change reverted.

RADV's other packet, `DMA_DATA` to `DST_SEL` NOWHERE (its L2 prefetch of shader code), is not here: #1709 implements it, and ccleste needs that too.

### Tested
Windows 11 Pro (26200), MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0 (WinLibs r7), Release, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti.

- The full suite (488 tests) passes on this branch alone with all eight commits (on `main` as of the last two). `agc_driver_pm4`, `agc_driver_graphics` and `agc_driver` pass again on the pushed head. It was run from the generated `CTestTestfile.cmake` commands because antivirus blocks `ctest.exe` on this machine.
- `tools/check_conventions.py --base origin/main` passes.
- ccleste renders with the first two commits (and an equivalent of #1709's prefetch), and vkQuake gets through startup and plays its demo with all eight, on a local branch that also carries my other open RADV PRs (#1732, #1733-#1736, #1819, #1825, #1914, #1915 and others).

Not tested on AMD, Intel, Linux or macOS.

body:
### What
Implements `sigaction` (libkernel, NID `KiJEPEWRyUY`). @hikazey reports in #1578 that EVO-PLAYER PPSA99039 v0.11.0 stops here once its earlier imports resolve (#1838, #1634, #1714, #1641, #1857 merged locally). At start-up, `projects/evoplayer/main.cpp` installs:
- a crash handler for `SIGSEGV`, `SIGBUS` and `SIGABRT` (`SA_SIGINFO | SA_NODEFER`);
- a quit handler for `SIGTERM`, `SIGINT` and `SIGHUP` (flags 0).

```c
int sigaction(int sig, const struct sigaction* act, struct sigaction* oact);
```

- **Layout:** FreeBSD's `struct sigaction`, which is the handler union at 0, `sa_flags` at 8, the 128-bit `sa_mask` at 12, and 32 bytes in all. `static_assert`s pin it.
- **Recording:** the handler, flags and mask of every signal from 1 to 128 are recorded and returned through `oact`.
  - As FreeBSD's `kern_sigaction` does, other signal numbers return `EINVAL`, and so does any handler but `SIG_DFL` on `SIGKILL` or `SIGSTOP`.
  - `signal` now shares this table and records `SA_RESTART`, as FreeBSD's libc `signal` does, so mixing the two calls reports consistent results.
- **Delivery:** handlers without `SA_SIGINFO` on the six signals `signal` already delivers (`SIGINT`, `SIGILL`, `SIGABRT`, `SIGFPE`, `SIGSEGV`, `SIGTERM`) run exactly as `signal` handlers do. `SIG_IGN` and `SIG_DFL` are applied to the host signal as before.
- **Recorded only:** `SA_SIGINFO` handlers and the other signals (`SIGBUS`, `SIGHUP`, ...) are recorded but never called. Calling them needs FreeBSD's `siginfo_t` and `ucontext_t`; #1431 builds the context for `sceKernelRaiseException`. For a signal like that, `raise` throws instead of terminating the process. `sa_mask` and the flags are not applied to delivery. All of this is in TechnicalDebt.

**Overlap:** none on exports. #1431 changes signal masks and exception delivery in other files (`Exception.cpp`, `Thread.cpp`), not `Signals.cpp`.

### Tested
- `guest_signals`, extended:
  - `oact` after `signal(SIGTERM, SIG_DFL)` reports `SA_RESTART`.
  - A plain `SIGTERM` handler with a mask in words 0 and 3 is delivered by `raise`, and round-trips through `oact`.
  - `signal` returns the handler `sigaction` set, and the reverse.
  - `SA_SIGINFO` handlers on 10, 1, 64 and 128 round-trip.
  - `raise(SIGABRT)` with an `SA_SIGINFO` handler throws.
  - Signals 0 and 129, and handlers on 9 and 17, return -1 with errno 22, while `SIG_DFL` on 9 and 17 succeeds.
  - Null `act` and `oact` are accepted.
- Linux (Ubuntu 24.04.5, GCC 13.3, RX 7600): full ctest passes, 497/497.
- Windows 11 (WinLibs GCC 15.2.0 r7): the signal and exception tests pass, 5/5.

### What
RADV on the PS5 ([mihawk-99/PS5_Mesa](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Mesa)) programs two raster registers with values that mean "off" but that AnyPS5 rejected. ccleste's (PPSA59322) draws were rejected because of them.

Three commits:

1. **`PA_SC_MODE_CNTL_1` `OUT_OF_ORDER_WATER_MARK`.** RADV sets the watermark to 7 on every GFX10 draw, also when `OUT_OF_ORDER_PRIMITIVE_ENABLE` is off. The watermark only tunes out-of-order rasterization, which stays rejected, so the field (bits 30:28) is accepted on its own.
2. **`PA_SC_CONSERVATIVE_RASTERIZATION_CNTL` when disabled.** RADV writes `NULL_SQUAD_AA_MASK_ENABLE` alone (`0x100000`), where libSceAgc writes the two `INNER_TO_NORMAL` overrides (`0x6000`). A value made only of those bits, including 0, now decodes as disabled. Overestimation (`0x6001`) keeps its checks, and every other mode is still rejected.

3. **Point and line depth bias enable on triangle draws** (added later, found running vkQuake, PPSA99010). With depth bias on, RADV sets `POLY_OFFSET_PARA_ENABLE` in `PA_SU_SC_MODE_CNTL` next to the front and back enables whatever the topology (vkQuake's draws carry `0x3a46`). That bit applies the offset to points and lines, so it changes nothing for triangles, and Vulkan applies depth bias only to polygons. It is now accepted with depth bias on triangle topologies; point and line draws with it are still rejected.

Tests (`agc_driver_graphics`):
- A watermark of 7 without out-of-order rasterization is accepted, and with `OUT_OF_ORDER_PRIMITIVE_ENABLE` set the draw is still rejected.
- `0x6000`, `0x100000` and 0 decode as disabled and are not rejected. Two enabled modes (`0x00e00001`, `0x01e00022`) are still rejected.
- `0x3a46` on a triangle list keeps its depth bias and back-face culling; the same value on a point or line topology is still rejected. It fails with the change reverted.

body:
### What
`CB_COLOR_ATTRIB` had to be zero, so any draw whose color target set `FORCE_DST_ALPHA_1` (bit 17) was rejected. RADV on the PS5 ([mihawk-99/PS5_Mesa](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Mesa)) sets it for color formats without alpha, so blending reads the destination alpha as 1, as for an RGBX surface. In ccleste (PPSA59322) six draws per frame were skipped this way.

The bit is now accepted, and the target's blend factors are rewritten to what they become when the destination alpha is 1:

- Color equation: `DST_ALPHA` becomes `ONE`, `ONE_MINUS_DST_ALPHA` becomes `ZERO`, and `SRC_ALPHA_SATURATE` (`min(As, 1 - Ad)`) becomes `ZERO`.
- Alpha equation: `DST_ALPHA` and `DST_COLOR` become `ONE`, and `ONE_MINUS_DST_ALPHA` and `ONE_MINUS_DST_COLOR` become `ZERO`, since the destination color's alpha component is the destination alpha.

Other factors are unchanged. Every other `CB_COLOR_ATTRIB` bit is still rejected.

Test (`agc_driver_graphics`, `OpaqueDestinationAlphaTests`): without the bit, the destination-alpha and destination-color factors decode unchanged. With it they become `ONE` or `ZERO` as above, `SRC_ALPHA_SATURATE` becomes `ZERO` in the color equation and stays in the alpha equation, and another `CB_COLOR_ATTRIB` bit (18) is still rejected.

Related: #419 (multisampled targets) also relaxes the `CB_COLOR_ATTRIB` check, for the sample and fragment fields. The two edit the same line, so whichever merges second needs a small rebase; they don't conflict in behaviour.

### What
A title built with `-fstack-protector` reads its stack guard from `fs:0x28` even when it has no thread-local data and its linker emits an empty `PT_TLS`. The Windows TLS builder refused any guest TLS access in that case: `Guest TLS access with empty PT_TLS`. ccleste (PPSA59322) failed to relink because of it.

body:
### What
An address-based build put every readable registered range in its BDA table and imported or mirrored it, including memory the guest mapped for the CPU only. On the console a mapping reaches the GPU only if its protection has GPU access (`0x10` read, `0x20` write).

- The guest allocation registry records whether a range has GPU access. libkernel sets it from the protection at `sceKernelMapDirectMemory`, flexible maps, fixed remaps and `sceKernelMprotect`. Reservations and the main image have none; a title's mprotect with GPU bits gives the image pieces access.
- An address-based build leaves out ranges without GPU access. Nothing else changes: stores are still decided by CPU write access and in-place import, and AnyPS5's own libc heap is still registered with GPU access.
- `GuestAllocations::Mutation::Add` and `Protect` take the flag.

Sources:
- The protection bits: shadPS4 `src/core/memory.h` `MemoryProt` (`CpuRead = 1`, `CpuWrite = 2`, `GpuRead = 16`, `GpuWrite = 32`).
- GPU page table entries exist only for ranges with GPU access: KytyPS5 `src/kernel/memory.cpp` `CountPageTableEntries(bool gpu)` counts a range for the GPU only if its protection has `PROT_GPU_READ` or `PROT_GPU_WRITE`, and `sceKernelGetPageTableStats` reports the CPU and GPU counts separately.
- PPSA36082 maps memory the CPU uses with `3` and sets the GPU bits where the GPU reads: its bundled `libc.prx` maps the malloc heap with `sceKernelMapNamedFlexibleMemoryInternal` (`4h6F1LLbTiw`), protection `3`, at both call sites (`+0xb2eb`, `+0xb4fd`); its executable's segments carry only R/W/X flags, and it mprotects the two pieces the GPU reads with `0x12` and `0x11`.

### PPSA36082
During loading and the main menu it registers: the 1 GiB malloc heap at `0x200000000` with `3`, 6784 MiB of direct memory with GPU read and write, and the two 32 KiB image pieces. Its first address-based draw runs on the queue the loader's fence waits on. That draw imported the heap; the import fails to pin (the kernel logs `Cannot map memory with base addr 0x200000000 and size of 0x40000 pages`), the fence is late, and the 512 MiB upload pool overflows (eboot `0x28fba9`). With this change the heap is not in the table and nothing fails to pin.

In my local build I bypassed both problems by hand: a driver option, `APS5_GPU_EXCLUDE=0x200000000+0x40000000`, kept that address range out of address-based builds, and a patched executable got through loading with a 2.5 GiB upload pool instead of 512 MiB. Both are specific to this title. This change replaces the first: the title maps its heap with `3`, which has no GPU access, so address-based builds leave it out without an option. Loading with the original 512 MiB pool also needs the changes below.

It also needs #861, #1367, #1249, #290 and a follow-up I will open after this one, which imports GPU-mapped memory when it is mapped and depends on this PR. With those, on main df16c4c2 with an earlier version of the follow-up, 40 s runs to the main menu: 4/5 pass with this change (the other overflowed at 4.1 s; the pool's margin is thin and that is separate work), 0/3 without it (each overflowed at 503 MiB with the pin failure above).

### Local changes not in this PR
I also have these on local branches. They finish making the GPU follow the guest's protection, but I am not opening them because no title I can run needs them. Do you want PRs for them?

- GPU read and write kept apart: the registry records GPU read and GPU write separately; the BDA table grants reads only with GPU read and stores only with GPU write (today CPU write decides stores); AnyPS5's own libc heap is registered without GPU access, as the console's `libc.prx` maps its heap with `3`. PPSA36082's only range where CPU and GPU write differ (an image piece mprotected with `0x12`) gets no GPU stores, and it allocates nothing through AnyPS5's libc heap.
- GPU access on every path, not just address-based builds: buffer descriptors read zeros from memory without GPU read and drop stores to memory without GPU write (memory with GPU write only is copied in so stores are exact); the command processor (command buffers, `WRITE_DATA`, `DMA_DATA`, labels, waits, fills), render targets, index and vertex inputs, DCC keys, display buffers and shader code fault on such memory; texture reads see zeros. The driver's GDS backing and AvPlayer's fallback frames are mapped with GPU access. A counted PPSA36082 run made no access to memory without GPU access.
- Mappings with GPU access but no CPU read (`0x10`, `0x30`) reach address-based builds, and AMM PRT pages with no physical memory read zero and drop GPU stores, through an unbound Vulkan sparse buffer (strict residency). Sources: amdgpu `AMDGPU_PTE_PRT`, which turns off faults on unmapped PRT accesses (`gmc_v8_0_set_prt`), and RADV reporting `sparseResidencyNonResidentStrict`. PPSA36082 makes no such mappings and imports no `sceAmpr*` function.
- The main image is registered when the process starts on both OSes. Today Linux registers it at any mprotect and Windows only at an mprotect of the image. PPSA36082 mprotects its image, so it is registered either way.

### Tested
Linux (CachyOS), x86-64, GCC, 7800X3D / RTX 4090.
- `guest_memory`: a direct map with `3` has no GPU access, `0x32` has; `sceKernelMprotect` to `0x13` adds it and back to `3` removes it; flexible maps with `3` and `0x33` likewise; the main image has none. Mapping with the GPU bits ignored fails it, and so does registering the image with GPU access.
- `agc_driver_graphics`: an address-based build includes a range with GPU access and leaves out one without. Dropping the check fails it.
- Test blocks that GPU work reads are registered with GPU access.
- ctest: 494/494.
- Windows: cross-built with MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0 and run under Wine 11.19. `agc_driver_graphics` and `agc_driver_flat_store` pass; `guest_memory` passes the new checks, then stops at `CheckMlock` (the working-set query), as it does without this change.

body:
Closes #1903

Depends on #1179. This branch is #1179's head b4e02e2d plus one commit, 46e17bfe. Review that commit only.

### What

#1179 lowers the packed pixel ancillary word in one pass after the fold loop, and only when every reader of the word extracts a modelled field. In real shaders the word also has an exec-masked `SelectU32` copy. `MaskedSelectEliminator` removes that copy, but it runs after `ConstantFolder` and the fold does not run again. So while the fold runs, the copy is still a reader, #1179's check refuses the whole word, and `ShaderInfoCollector` then throws on the extract that still reads it.

When the check refuses the word, each in-range `BitFieldUExtract` / `BitFieldSExtract` that reads it (directly or through `Identity` copies) is now rewritten on its own, and the other readers keep the word. When every reader is an extract, #1179's whole-word lowering runs unchanged.

### Tested

Linux (Nobara 44, GCC 16), RTX 5070 Ti with NVIDIA 595.91.07, and RADV on a Ryzen 5 7600X iGPU with Mesa 26.2.1.

New check `ExtractVectorMaskedCopy()` in `core/libs/tests/PixelAncillary.cpp`: the IR a vector `v_bfe_u32` produces (masked offset, clamped count) plus a `SelectU32(lane < 16, word, 0)` copy of the word. After the fold, the extract must read the Layer (16, 11) or SampleId (8, 4) builtin. `ExtractVector()` is the same without the copy.

| | `pixel_ancillary` |
|---|---|
| #1179 b4e02e2d + the tests only | `ExtractVector` passes, `ExtractVectorMaskedCopy` fails |
| this branch | passes |

body:
Closes #1901

### What

The driver's null pixel program is prepared only in its registration variants (0 user SGPRs). A draw without a pixel program uses the queue's `SPI_SHADER_PGM_RSRC2_PS` user count and `SPI_PS_IN_CONTROL` wave bit for it. When those differ from the registration variant, `SourceHandleFor` and `InvocationFor` throw `prepared shader artifact is missing for the requested static ABI`.

The root cause, found by @Raghav314: since #1178 the two `emplace` calls at registration did nothing, so the null program was registered with the wrong inputs, and a null pixel draw took the last bound pixel shader's user SGPR count.

- Registration moves into `PrepareNullPixelProgram(device)`, which uses `insert_or_assign` for the program address, `SPI_PS_INPUT_ENA/ADDR` and RSRC2 (no user SGPRs).
- A null pixel draw gets 0 user SGPRs (RSRC2 is not read) and an empty export mapping, so it matches the variant prepared at registration.
- The unregistered compute path in both functions moves into `PreparedAtUse`. For the null program it prepares a variant at the draw only for wave32, which registration doesn't prepare. Every other miss still throws as before.

### Tested

Linux (Nobara 44, GCC), RTX 5070 Ti, NVIDIA 595.91.07.

d83e608e adds `NullPixelMatchesRegistration` to `agc_driver_prepared_graphics`: a null pixel draw with a previous shader's leftover state (4 user SGPRs, other inputs, a bound export mapping) must use the artifact prepared at registration. It fails without the fix and still fails with only part of it; it passes with all of it. `ctest -R agc_`: 248/248 on the RTX 5070 Ti and on RADV (Mesa 26.2.1). `tools/check_conventions.py` passes.

The earlier at-draw check and its results:

New check `NullPixelAtDraw()` in `tests/execution/PreparedShaders.cpp`. It prepares the registration variant of the null pixel program, then requests a wave32, 4 user SGPR fragment variant at push offset 20 / capacity 108.

| | `ctest -R agc_driver_prepared_shaders` |
|---|---|
| `main` 1be6f9f1 + the test only | 4 of 5 fail with `prepared shader artifact is missing for the requested static ABI: ... stage=5 wave=32 pushOffset=20 pushCapacity=108 preparedLayouts= [0,128]`. `_debug_failure` passes, as it expects a failure. |
| this branch | 5/5 pass, and `agc_driver_prepared_graphics` passes too |

Stray: without this change it aborts on the first such draw (above). With it, the log shows `The null pixel program has no artifact for this draw (wave 64, 4 user SGPRs); preparing it at draw` and the run continues to a later, unrelated error.

### What

Closes #1897.

This makes the recompiler accept `clamp` on VOP3 `v_add_nc_u32`, `v_sub_nc_u32`, `v_subrev_nc_u32`, `v_add_nc_u16`, `v_sub_nc_u16`, `v_add_nc_i16` and `v_sub_nc_i16`, and saturates the result.

For u32, `vAddSubNcU32` already saturated for SDWA, so the three opcodes only needed adding to `usesIntegerSaturateClamp`.

For the 16-bit ops, a new `isVop3Integer16AddSubOpcode` lets clamp through `checkNativeVop3Modifiers` and keeps it in `supportsNativeVop3Clamp`, and `integer16Binary` now passes its result through the existing `saturateInteger16`. The i16 forms now read their operands sign-extended. That doesn't change the low 16 bits when clamp is off.

The semantics were measured with `tools/hw-oracle` on a Ryzen 5 7600X iGPU (gfx1036, RDNA2, wave32). The settings were IEEE=0, DX10_CLAMP=1, denorm32=0, denorm16=3, round32=0, round16=0, fp16_overflow=0. A second run with IEEE=1, DX10_CLAMP=0, denorm 3/3, round toward zero and fp16_overflow=1 gave the same results. The new test, `tests/execution/Vop3AddSubClamp.cpp`, pins all 32 measured rows for the 7 clamped ops plus an unclamped `v_add_nc_u32` control. The rows include u32 wrap, the u16/i16 boundaries, and inputs with junk in bits 31:16.

The carry ops with clamp still throw. See the issue.

body:
### What

With #1201/#1202, queue 0's direct draws become commit items on @MichonGoddijn231849's committer, but every indirect draw drains the pipeline and records inline on the packet worker. In #1202 Michon said indirect draws weren't on his list and offered them to us ([comment](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/pull/1202#issuecomment-6064423707)). This PR takes that part and builds on his committer as it is.

With `APS5_PIPELINE_INDIRECT=1` (off by default):

- An indirect draw no longer drains at the start of `Driver::draw`.
- GPU-side indirect draws (the device reads the arguments) are enqueued like direct draws. `commitDraw` records them in packet order, so the arguments are read by the GPU after every earlier commit.
- CPU-side indirect draws read their argument records on the worker. Before the read, the argument range and the count dword are checked against the writes of pending commit items, label items included (`DrawPipeline::DrainIfOverlaps`); an overlap drains first. The expanded records are enqueued as one commit item.
- A draw whose cache hit was validated against guest memory drains and translates again when any of its captured or decoded ranges overlaps a pending write, so a hit can't be validated against bytes a pending commit is about to change. Fresh captures were already covered by `queryPendingWrite`.
- Pipeline depth defaults to 64 instead of 8 when the knob is on. At depth 8 the worker waited for room on most draws.
- `[draw] pipelined` also reports committer busy %, indirect commits and argument-overlap drains.

body:
### What

Adds an opt-in `APS5_THREAD_PRIORITY` that raises the AGC queue workers and the VideoOut presenter above the title's threads. Guest priorities don't reach host scheduling, so a title whose job system busy-waits on every hardware thread can keep the queue 0 worker off a core and make the driver the bottleneck (#1788).

- `=high`: nice `APS5_THREAD_NICE` (default -10). On Linux through rtkit (`MakeThreadHighPriorityWithPID`) over a dlopen'd libdbus-1, the way SDL does it. On Windows, `THREAD_PRIORITY_HIGHEST`.
- `=rt`: real-time priority `APS5_THREAD_RT` (default 10) through rtkit's `MakeThreadRealtimeWithPID`. On Windows, `THREAD_PRIORITY_TIME_CRITICAL`.
- The mode picks one path before any call, with no fallback between them (#182). If rtkit or `SetThreadPriority` refuses, the thread throws with the refusal. The presenter passes it back to the VideoOut constructor.
- Each queue worker calls it, and so does the presenter, through a new C export from the driver. Each raised thread logs its priority once as `[thread-priority]`. Unset means no change.

`RLIMIT_RTTIME` handling for `=rt` (second commit, after @MarcZX100's review in #1788): rtkit's `verify_process_rttime` reads the hard limit from `/proc/<pid>/limits` and refuses when it is above `RTTimeUSecMax` ([source](https://github.com/heftig/rtkit/blob/c295fa849f52b487be6433e69e08b46251950399/rtkit-daemon.c#L592-L637)). Lowering only the soft limit is not enough. With soft 100000 us and hard unlimited, `MakeThreadRealtimeWithPID` returns "Access denied"; with hard 200000 it succeeds. So the code now:

- reads rtkit's `MaxRealtimePriority` and `RTTimeUSecMax` first. If rtkit is unreachable or the priority is above its maximum, the limit is not touched.
- keeps a hard limit that is already at most `min(APS5_THREAD_RTTIME_US, RTTimeUSecMax)`, and otherwise lowers it to that value. The soft limit goes to at most half of the hard one.
- logs when it lowers the hard limit.

An unprivileged process cannot raise the hard limit again, so once lowered it stays lowered even if rtkit then refuses (burst limit, user or start-time checks). That is listed in TechnicalDebt and in BUILD.md. The log also reports the policy rtkit applied: `SCHED_RR` by default, not `SCHED_FIFO` as the issue says.

Why opt-in: it changes host scheduling for every title, rtkit is not on every system, and under `=rt` a queue worker that runs past `RLIMIT_RTTIME` without blocking gets the process a SIGXCPU. #626 (P-core pinning on hybrid CPUs) is complementary.

Closes #1788.

### Tested
Linux 7.2 (Nobara 44), GCC 16, RTX 5070 Ti, driver 595.91.07, Ryzen 5 7600X. Rebased on `main` d70b8998.
- `ctest -R agc_ -j1`: 259 of 260 with the variable unset, and the same with `APS5_THREAD_PRIORITY=high` and with `=rt`. The one failure, `agc_driver_dcc_keys_first_write`, fails the same way on `main` d70b8998.
- `agc_thread_priority_refused_rt` and `_high` run the raise with the system bus pointed at a missing socket and pass only if it throws.
- Earlier run, before the fallbacks were removed: `ctest -R agc_driver -j1` 202 of 202, unset and with `=rt`. In the `rt` run the queue workers log `SCHED_RR 10 via rtkit`, and the hard limit is lowered from unlimited to 200000 us once per process.
- A standalone harness around `RaiseWorkerThreadPriority` (`=rt`): hard limit unlimited is lowered to 200000 (soft 100000); a preset soft 30000 / hard 150000 is left as is and rtkit grants; `APS5_THREAD_RT=99` (above `MaxRealtimePriority` 20) and an unreachable system bus leave the limit untouched (that run predates the throw).
- `python3 tools/check_conventions.py --base origin/main`: passes.
- Demon's Souls (PPSA01341 v1.07), from #1788 on an earlier base: with `=high` the PS Studios movie went from 254-255 to 345 presents per 10 s, and the attract movie from 429-447 to 520-536 presents per 10 s. With the priority on, the boot-time capture race from #1787 became more likely; with that fix, 15 of 15 runs were clean.
- Windows (by @popcoder565, on the earlier revision): Windows 10, RTX 3060 Laptop, driver 616.92. `agc_thread_priority` passes, and the threads log `highest` / `time-critical` in the two modes.

body:
### What

`MakeTextureKey` copies the eight raw T# words into the sampled-texture cache key. Three fields in those words are texture-streaming feedback: MIN_LOD_WARN (word 5 bits 8-19), MIP_STATS_COUNTER_EN (word 5 bit 25) and MIP_STATS_COUNTER_ID (word 6 bits 0-7). `DecodeTextureResource` reads and ignores them, so they never change the texture, but they do change the key. Demon's Souls rotates the counter fields per use, so each streaming texture ends up under about six keys. Every new key is a fresh snapshot (about 5 MiB for a 2048x2048 BC texture), and the stale variants push live textures out under the budget.

`MakeTextureKey` now clears those three fields before the words go into the key, so two descriptors that differ only in them share one entry.

Closes #1790.

### Tested
Linux 7.2 (Nobara 44), GCC 16, RTX 5070 Ti, driver 595.91.07.
- Rebased on current `main` (ae91d978), no conflicts.
- `ctest -R "agc_driver|guest_agc_driver"`: 202 of 202 pass, without `APS5_WRITE_WATCH_IMPORTS`. `agc_driver_lds_atomics64` and `agc_driver_scalar_sop1` are excluded; they fail on unmodified `main` on this GPU too (the first one hangs it).
- `python3 tools/check_conventions.py --base origin/main`: passes.
- There's no new test: the cache has no hook a test can observe the key through.
- Demon's Souls (PPSA01341 v1.07), tutorial level, per 10 s, with an 8 GiB texture budget:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| budget evictions | 656-1017 | 0 |
| texture cache | churning at the budget | 1260 entries, 8162 MiB, all resident |
| draw resource binding | 1856 ms | 54 ms |
| level fps | 0.80 | 1.10 |

Before the change, every evicted entry was a stale key of a texture still cached under another key (711 of 711, 780 of 780 and 948 of 948 in three windows). These numbers come from a local build (an older `main` with #861 and other patches) that also raised the pipeline store's 256-entry bound, so the fps change isn't from the key alone. The eviction and binding numbers are. The level's texture set is about 8 GiB, so it still won't fit `main`'s fixed 2 GiB budget; #1059 sizes the budget from device memory. Without this change the six variants of each texture compete for whatever budget there is.

body:
### What

A compute queue worker passes a `WAIT_REG_MEM` as soon as another queue's worker has recorded the label store it waits on, before the GPU has executed that store. The dispatches behind the wait are then captured from guest memory the title has not written yet. On hardware the CP cannot pass the wait that early, so titles fill the tables a gated dispatch reads after they submit, and GPU latency keeps it ordered. Demon's Souls does this every frame, and it crashes 20-90 s into boot with `guest memory is not readable at 0x60`, bad V#s or null texture bases on a compute queue. #1787 has the traces.

Two commits:

1. Land cross-queue waits before a guest read. A wait that a worker passes on another queue's recorded store (not yet in memory) stays on the worker. Before its next dispatch, draw, COND_EXEC or predicated packet, the worker polls until memory satisfies the wait or no unfinished batch writes the label any more. The second condition covers a label the title re-arms after the store lands. A wait on a label the same queue wrote earlier orders no title write, so it isn't kept; `LabelStore` records the writing queue for that check. The graphics queue is exempt by default, because landing its waits on the compute queues' labels took the attract from 50-54 to 36-39.5 fps, and this title fills its graphics buffers before submitting them. `APS5_LAND_WAITS_ALL_QUEUES=1` includes it, `APS5_NO_LAND_WAITS=1` turns landing off. A landing wait restarts its timeout only when packets finish, since it runs inside a packet that is itself in flight. A TechnicalDebt entry records the graphics-queue exemption.
2. Resolve the gated group at the gate. Landing alone left a late read: the worker captured dispatch k of the group 11-25 ms after the gate, waiting on the GPU mutex between dispatches, and by then the title had re-armed the gate and reused the slots (4 of 8 boots still failed). Once a compute queue's wait has passed on memory, the worker now resolves every dispatch up to the next unsatisfied wait before issuing any of them: dispatch-cache lookup, capture and recompile, against a scratch copy of the queue state driven through the `SET_*` packets. The real dispatch adopts the parked result if the program address and cache key still match. The lookahead stops at a packet that writes guest memory other than a label, at conditional or predicated packets, and at a dispatch that reads a label or buffer an earlier dispatch of the run writes. CPU-path indirect arguments are read at the gate too. If the device later finds the memory changed (`guest snapshot differs from registered memory`), the dispatch is resolved again from current memory, as on `main`. `APS5_NO_GROUP_CAPTURE=1` disables it.

One gap is left. The capture now holds gate-time memory, but the GPU still reads the live import later. Queue 0's next frame overwrites a few structs the group reads, so the device check rejects about 5 dispatches per frame, and those are resolved live (708 in 150 s). Binding gate-time snapshots for those regions would close the gap; it isn't in this PR.

Closes #1787.

### Tested
Linux 7.2 (Nobara 44), GCC 16, RTX 5070 Ti, driver 595.91.07.
- Rebased on current `main` (ce64d8eb). The only conflicts were in the TechnicalDebt list; both sides are kept.
- `ctest -R "agc_driver|guest_agc_driver"`: 203 of 203 pass, without `APS5_WRITE_WATCH_IMPORTS`. `agc_driver_lds_atomics64` and `agc_driver_scalar_sop1` are excluded; they fail on unmodified `main` on this GPU too (the first one hangs it).
- `python3 tools/check_conventions.py --base origin/main`: passes.
- Demon's Souls (PPSA01341 v1.07), boot to the opening cinematic, with driver threads at high priority (`APS5_THREAD_PRIORITY=high`, #1788), which makes the race more likely:

| | failed boots |
|---|---|
| `main`, normal priority | about 3 of 35 |
| `main`, high priority | 9 of 15 |
| commit 1 only (landing) | 4 of 8 (4 of 4 on the day of the runs below) |
| both commits | 0 of 15 (each ran its full 150 s) |

The 15 runs include 4 with a 48x24 depth copy that made the crash 2 of 2 before. The group capture costs 25-75 ms per 10 s on queue 0x20, and the parked result is adopted 0.35-0.65 ms after the gate on average. Movie and attract frame rates are unchanged (305-346 presents per 10 s in the movie).

Those runs were measured on an older `main` (c1241ad0) with #861 and a few other local patches. The settle condition and the landing timeout in commit 1 came after them, when a landing wait on a re-armed label hung the title past the main menu, so they weren't in the build behind the 15 runs.

body:
### What
Step 1 of #1581. `0xffff1000` is a type-3 NOP with count 0x3fff, which the command processor reads as one dword. `sceAgcDcbResetQueue` writes it at the start of every call (measured on a PS5 in #1581), and the driver read it as a 16385-dword packet ("invalid PM4 packet size").

`Pm4::FillerPacket` now also matches exactly `0xffff1000`, so every walker (validation, submission, COND_EXEC ranges, execution) steps over it as one dword. The match is on the whole header, as in Mesa: `src/amd/common/ac_parse_ib.c` checks `header == PKT3_NOP_PAD`, and `sid.h` defines `PKT3_NOP_PAD` as `PKT3(PKT3_NOP, 0x3fff, 0)`. A NOP with count 0x3fff and other header bits set is still sized by its count. d4f7ddaa used the wider `0x3fffff00` mask for range predication; this PR keeps the exact header from Mesa.

Refs #1581

### Tested
Fork CI on c975fe54, before rebasing onto current main (84703ca7, same diff) (Linux and Windows build + ctest, relinker on Ubuntu, Windows and macOS): https://github.com/aashishaxo/AnyPS5/actions/runs/37848985909
- `testNopPad`: Validate accepts the pad on graphics and compute queues and rejects it with a trailing dword; NOPs with count 0x3fff and header flags, and the largest counted NOP, are still sized by their count.
- `testNopPadSubmission`: the measured `op = 0` envelope from #1581 submits and the packets after it run; a COND_EXEC range containing the pad counts it as one dword.

body:
### What

`libkernel` does not export `shm_open` (`QuJYZ2KVGGQ`). ccleste (PPSA59322) stops on it at load on `main`.

Its bundled Mesa calls it in two places, both with `SHM_ANON`:

- At 0x480750: `shm_open(SHM_ANON, O_RDWR | O_CREAT | O_CLOEXEC, 0600)`, then `ftruncate`, then `close` on failure. This is Mesa's FreeBSD `os_create_anonymous_file`. Its caller then `mmap`s the descriptor `MAP_SHARED`.
- At 0xb853ce: `shm_open(SHM_ANON, O_RDWR [| O_CLOEXEC], 0600)`.

`shm_open` is added in the new `libkernel/File/src/SharedMemory.cpp`, following FreeBSD 11's `kern_shm_open` ([`sys/kern/uipc_shm.c`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/stable/11/sys/kern/uipc_shm.c)):

- The access mode must be `O_RDONLY` or `O_RDWR`. Flags other than `O_ACCMODE | O_CREAT | O_EXCL | O_TRUNC | O_CLOEXEC` are rejected. Both return `EINVAL`, before the path is looked at.
- `SHM_ANON` with `O_RDONLY` returns `EINVAL`.
- `SHM_ANON` with `O_RDWR` returns a new descriptor for a zero-length object. Each object is a host anonymous file: a `memfd` on Linux, and on Windows a delete-on-close temporary file opened with `_O_TEMPORARY | _O_SHORT_LIVED`. Because the guest descriptor is the host CRT descriptor, the existing `ftruncate`, `read`/`write`, `pread`/`pwrite`, `fstat` and `close` work on it unchanged.
- `EMFILE`, `ENFILE` and `ENOMEM` from the host are returned as the guest errors; any other host failure throws. The guest `errno` is kept on success.
- A named object throws (`NotImplemented_nid_no_patch`). No title is known to open one.

`mmap` is unchanged. It accepts only private anonymous mappings and fails a mapping of a descriptor with `EOPNOTSUPP`. So `os_create_anonymous_file` now succeeds, and the caller's `MAP_SHARED` mapping fails on its error path (it checks for `MAP_FAILED`) instead of the title failing to load. Shared file mappings are a separate change. `docs/dev/TechnicalDebt.md` records this, the ignored mode and the named-object gap.

### Log

I don't have a console, and I couldn't run the title here: the host is aarch64 and the project needs x86-64. The stop is from @SleglJan's run of the homebrew catalog on `main` 4b6ab6bb in #1578 ([comment](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/issues/1578#issuecomment-6068281866)). Each title was relinked with `--registry` and run for 8 s on Linux. In the table of first stops, `shm_open` is the stop for PPSA59322 ccleste, with no open PR. That run reports the stop as `app.elf: symbol lookup error: app.elf: undefined symbol: QuJYZ2KVGGQ`.

- PPSA59322: [PS5_Celeste 1.00](https://github.com/darkxex/PS5_Celeste/releases/tag/1.00), `PPSA59322.zip`, sha256 `96861b81…fb43`, matching the [catalog record](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-homebrew-catalog/blob/main/apps/PPSA59322.json)

The call sites and arguments come from its unwrapped `eboot.bin`: the relocation for `QuJYZ2KVGGQ`, then the `call`/`jmp qword ptr [rip+…]` through that slot. The `ftruncate` (`ih4CD9-gghM`), `close` and `mmap` (`BPE9s9vQQXo`) slots were resolved the same way.

If someone with the title can post the next stop with this PR applied, I'll add it here.

### Tested

aarch64 Debian 13 host. The full project cannot be built here because it needs x86-64.

- New `core/libs/tests/GuestShmOpen.cpp` (`guest_shm_open`) checks:
  - three anonymous objects (Mesa's flags, plain `O_RDWR`, and `O_CREAT | O_EXCL | O_TRUNC | O_CLOEXEC`) give distinct descriptors and leave `errno` unchanged
  - after `ftruncate` to 16 KiB, data written with `pwrite` reads back, the last byte is zero and a read at the end returns 0
  - a second object is still empty, so objects are not shared
  - all three close
  - `EINVAL` for `O_RDONLY`, `O_CREAT` alone, `O_WRONLY`, access mode 3, `O_APPEND` and `O_NONBLOCK`, and for bad flags on a named path
  - a valid named open throws
- It passes natively on aarch64 (Zig 0.17 clang, glibc 2.36), and on x86_64-linux-musl under qemu-user. Both builds use `SharedMemory.cpp` with host-backed stand-ins for the guest `ftruncate`/`pread`/`pwrite`/`close`, which the CMake test takes from `libkernel`.
- Negative check: without the change the test does not link. Three mutants each make it abort: anonymous `O_RDONLY` accepted, no flag check, and a named path accepted.
- `SharedMemory.cpp` and the test compile for x86_64-linux-gnu and x86_64-windows-gnu with `-Wall -Wextra`. The only warnings are the existing `-Wreturn-type-c-linkage` ones from `General.hpp`. The Windows `_wsopen_s` path is compiled but not run.
- `python3 tools/check_conventions.py --base origin/main` passes.
- Not run with a title.

body:
### What

`libkernel` does not export `system` (`Jc6E7N+dHz0`). Yamagi Quake II (PPSA99007) stops on it at load on `main`, and ccleste (PPSA59322) imports it too.

In both titles the only caller is the bundled Mesa. A small function runs `system("clrxdisasm --version > /dev/null 2>&1")` and returns whether the result is 0, which tells Mesa whether the CLRX disassembler is installed. It sits on the shader-disassembly dump path, at 0x4608d0 in the PPSA99007 executable and 0x826270 in PPSA59322 (the single `call [system]` site in each).

`system` now follows FreeBSD 11's `lib/libc/stdlib/system.c` ([source](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/stable/11/lib/libc/stdlib/system.c)) for a process with no `/bin/sh`:

- A null command returns 1. That version returns 1 without checking for the shell (`if (!command) return(1);`).
- Any other command runs nothing and returns `0x7f00`. In FreeBSD, the child that cannot `execl(_PATH_BSHELL, ...)` calls `_exit(127)`, and `system` returns its wait status. So `WIFEXITED` is true and `WEXITSTATUS` is 127, and Mesa's probe sees that CLRX is not available.
- The guest `errno` is not touched.

No host command is ever run. A new line in `docs/dev/TechnicalDebt.md` says what is assumed: that the console's application sandbox has no shell, and that `vfork` succeeds there (FreeBSD returns -1 when it fails).

### Log

I don't have a console, and I couldn't run the titles here: the host is aarch64 and the project needs x86-64. The stop is from @SleglJan's run of the homebrew catalog on `main` 4b6ab6bb in #1578 ([comment](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/issues/1578#issuecomment-6068281866)). Each title was relinked with `--registry` and run for 8 s on Linux. In the table of first stops, `system` is the stop for PPSA99007 Yamagi Quake II, with no open PR. That run reports the stop as `app.elf: symbol lookup error: app.elf: undefined symbol: Jc6E7N+dHz0`. Closed #3 also reported a Quake II build stopping at `Jc6E7N+dHz0` (`system`) before guest entry.

- PPSA99007: [ps5-yamagi-quake2 v0.2.0-alpha.1](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-yamagi-quake2/releases/tag/v0.2.0-alpha.1), `PPSA99007.zip`, sha256 `4fa5da07…9a70`, matching the [catalog record](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-homebrew-catalog/blob/main/apps/PPSA99007.json)

The call sites come from the unwrapped `eboot.bin` of each release: the relocation for `Jc6E7N+dHz0`, then the only `call qword ptr [rip+…]` through that slot.

With this PR applied, @CouchRiv ran PPSA99007 on Linux (NVIDIA, `main` f1451396 plus this PR, 90 s timeout) ([comment](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/pull/1859#issuecomment-6074519487)). body:
### What

Adds `msync` to libkernel, next to `mmap`, `munmap` and `mprotect` in `DirectMemory/PosixMemory.cpp`. It follows FreeBSD 11's [`kern_msync`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/stable/11/sys/vm/vm_mmap.c) and [`vm_map_sync`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/stable/11/sys/vm/vm_map.c) over the guest's mappings as `sceKernelVirtualQuery` reports them:

- The address is rounded down to the page and the length rounded up, with the same unsigned arithmetic as `kern_msync`. A range whose end wraps is `EINVAL`.
- `MS_ASYNC | MS_INVALIDATE` is `EINVAL`. Other flag bits are not checked, as in FreeBSD.
- An unmapped start, or any unmapped page in the range, is `ENOMEM`. Length 0 checks the mapping that holds the address (`vm_map_sync` widens `start == end` to that entry). Reservations count as mapped, since FreeBSD has a map entry for them.
- Success writes nothing back: the guest's `mmap` only creates private anonymous mappings, so there are no file mappings to sync.
- `MS_INVALIDATE` on a mapped range throws. FreeBSD returns `EBUSY` there when the range holds `mlock`ed pages, and locked pages are not tracked. The `ENOMEM` check comes first, as in `vm_map_sync`.

One limitation is recorded in TechnicalDebt with the rest: a page `munmap`ed from inside a larger mapping still counts as mapped, because `sceKernelVirtualQuery` keeps reporting the whole mapping after a partial unmap (on `main` too).

EVO-PLAYER PPSA99039 v0.11.0 ([sainsaji/EVO-PLAYER-PS5](https://github.com/sainsaji/EVO-PLAYER-PS5)) imports it for a mapped-file benchmark (`projects/evoplayer/src/evo_iobench.c`, `msync(p, len, MS_SYNC)`). It's also in the absent lists of other titles in #1578, where it was claimed.

### Tested

  - with it, it gets past and stops at `KiJEPEWRyUY` (`sigaction`, #1431).
- **New `guest_msync` test** (Windows and Linux): success for the whole range, `MS_ASYNC`, an unaligned address inside the mapping, a range crossing a page boundary, length 0, an unknown flag bit and a reserved range, with errno untouched on success; `EINVAL` for `MS_ASYNC | MS_INVALIDATE` and a wrapping range; `ENOMEM` after `munmap` for the start, a range, length 0 and `MS_INVALIDATE`; the `MS_INVALIDATE` throw on a mapped range.

body:
### What

Part of #1668's shader-mode workstream and #981. MODE rounding reads currently return zero even when the shader declares a nonzero initial mode, and MODE writes can silently leave that declared state inconsistent with the shader's instructions.

For example, with `FLOAT_MODE=0xc5`, reading MODE bits 0..3 now returns `5`. An immediate write of `5` preserves the state and is accepted; writing `0` reports the instruction and program counter as an unsupported runtime transition.

- Read any subfield confined to MODE bits 0..3 from the initial mode already carried by `GuestContext::floatMode`.
- Accept `s_setreg_imm32_b32` only when its selected rounding bits remain unchanged, masking source bits above the selected width. Apply the same rule to the low four bits of `s_round_mode`; its upper immediate bits are ignored.
- Reject SGPR-sourced MODE writes and state-changing immediate writes. Runtime transitions need control-flow-aware state and matching arithmetic lowering.
- Document the data flow, supported contract and remaining gaps in [Architecture](https://github.com/Sanjaysrinivas/AnyPS5/blob/fix/shader-mode-registers/docs/dev/ARCHITECTURE.md#shader-mode-register-access) and [TechnicalDebt](https://github.com/Sanjaysrinivas/AnyPS5/blob/fix/shader-mode-registers/docs/dev/TechnicalDebt.md).

Semantics follow AMD's RDNA2 ISA sections 5.8 and 6.4, Table 24, cross-checked against LLVM 20.1.8's `AMDGPUBaseInfo.h`, `SIModeRegister.cpp` and GFX10 assembler tests. Exact source links are in Architecture. No console or GPU execution measurements are claimed. Missing metadata retains the existing nearest-even assumption; other MODE fields remain unsupported, and non-MODE `s_setreg_b32` writes retain their existing no-op behavior, recorded in TechnicalDebt.

This is partial progress on #1668; it does not complete the category issue or add arithmetic support for every initial mode. Initial-mode propagation (#1816), output-modifier mode handling (#1851) and f32 denormal flushing (#1850) are already on main. No open PR prerequisite.

Coordination with #1811: both PRs initially edited the same CMake test-list line. The MODE test is now registered separately, with its normal-build inclusion, Windows runtime path and timeout preserved. Combining the two changes merges cleanly in either order; neither PR depends on the other. The MODE documentation also sits within the existing Graphics section so it can merge independently of #1802's appended kernel documentation.

### Tested

Release builds on Windows 11 Pro (build 26300, WinLibs GCC 15.2.0 r7) and Ubuntu 24.04 under WSL2 (GCC 13.3.0). Four focused CTest cases passed on each host, with no skips: `agc_shader_mode_register`, `agc_shader_control_flow`, `agc_shader_disk_cache`, and `agc_validate_program`.

The new regression uses production decoding, control-flow construction and translation, with requirements active in Release:

- 5,120 known-mode subfield read comparisons across all 256 FLOAT_MODE bytes and wave32/wave64, plus legacy unknown-metadata reads.
- 1,024 masked immediate-write combinations and 512 `s_round_mode` combinations, including ignored upper bits and preservation of untouched rounding bits.
- SGPR writes, unsupported selectors, branch-local writes with diagnostics at PC 4, and initial-mode propagation through full `Recompile`.
- A 20-second CTest timeout; the new test took about 0.13 seconds on Linux and 0.99 seconds on Windows.

LLVM 18.1.3's assembler independently verified 23 instruction encodings for both gfx1013 and gfx1030. Replacing the production fix with upstream code makes the final regression fail; restoring it returns all four Linux cases to passing.

Local builds used an untracked CMake parent importing the production libc/recompiler source lists and the four production test target definitions, with SPIRV-Tools disabled. After rebasing onto main `ce64d8eb`, all four cases passed again on each host; the parent also evaluates the production MODE test registration and checks its inclusion in normal builds. This covers compiler regressions, not the full application build, GPU execution, a title or console behavior. Full repository CI passed on Linux and Windows at `4344bbfd`; the updated head needs a fresh CI run.

cmake --build <local-build> --target agc_shader_mode_register_tests agc_shader_control_flow_tests agc_shader_disk_cache_tests agc_validate_program_tests --parallel 6

### What

PICO-8 for PS5 (PPSA99808 v0.1.2, [RafaelNGP/pico8-ps5](https://github.com/RafaelNGP/pico8-ps5), GPL-3.0) stops at start-up on `main`:

```
FAIL: unresolved ELF import a7ToDPsIQrc from libSceLibcInternal.prx
```

`a7ToDPsIQrc` is `__inet_aton` (`tools/nid_names.py`). It is the only title in @SleglJan's run of the catalog (#1578) that stops there.

The parser follows FreeBSD's `inet_aton` (`lib/libc/inet/inet_addr.c`):
- one to four parts, each in decimal, octal (leading `0`) or hex (`0x`);
- the last part fills the remaining bytes (`a.b` → `a.0.0.b` with `b` up to 24 bits, `a.b.c` with `c` up to 16 bits, a single number for all 32 bits);
- the input ends at a NUL or a whitespace character;
- it returns 1 and writes the address in network order, or returns 0 and leaves the output untouched;
- a null address only validates.

Windows has no `inet_aton`, and glibc's differs in its overflow checks, so the parser is written out instead of calling the host's. It is in `StringExtensions.cpp` rather than a new file, so it does not collide with the `Network.cpp` that #1766 (`__inet_addr`, `__inet_ntoa`) adds.

body:
### What

`std::set_new_handler` was implemented in libc but `operator new` never called the handler. When the allocator returned null, `operator new` threw `bad_alloc` straight away. The C++ standard ([new.delete.single]) says `operator new` loops on failure: it calls the current new handler and tries again, and it only throws `bad_alloc` once there is no handler. A title that frees a cache or a reserve inside its handler, which is the usual reason to install one, would crash on the first out of memory condition instead of recovering.

`Allocate` in `StdioExtras.cpp` now follows that loop for `operator new`, `operator new[]` and the two nothrow forms. The handler runs outside the allocator callback, so it may allocate, free or reinstall itself. A handler that throws `bad_alloc` propagates from the throwing forms and gives a null pointer from the nothrow ones. The handler slot is atomic now, since `set_new_handler` and `get_new_handler` are required to be thread safe.

### Tested

Ubuntu 26.04, GCC 15.2. The new `guest_new_handler` test installs a replacement allocator that fails a chosen number of times and checks each form: no handler (throws, or null for nothrow), a handler that returns (retried exactly as often as it fails), a handler that uninstalls itself after three calls, a handler that throws `bad_alloc`, a handler that allocates, the previous handler returned by `set_new_handler`, and a zero byte request. It passes with the change, and without the change it dies with an uncaught `bad_alloc`. The non-GPU suite passes (241 tests) and the convention checks pass. Not run on Windows locally, so the Windows job is the first run there.

body:
### What

Correct two Windows calling-convention mismatches in libc's guest exception runtime. Guest calls pass the object pointer in RDI under System V, but the registered message-destructor lambdas and exception vtable entries previously used native Windows function pointers expecting RCX.

- Register an explicit `APS5_VABI` message-destructor adapter for standard message throws and `regex_error`. The adapter calls the unchanged native destruction helper. The legacy destructor pointer storage and native/guest allocation markers remain unchanged.
- Give guest `what`, non-deleting destructor and deleting destructor slots explicit `APS5_VABI` types and use guest adapters for all plain/message exception vtables. Each adapter calls the correctly declared native helper.

Normal Release previously happened to leave the same object in RDI and RCX, masking the registered-callback defect. Deliberately supplying a different object in RCX reproduced destruction of the wrong message; clearing RCX reproduced an invalid read. Virtual calls showed the same mismatch.

Object and RTTI layouts, message reference counting, existing malloc/free ownership, native host helpers and native exception routing are preserved. Deleting-destructor tests use standalone malloc-owned objects; they do not delete exceptions owned by the exception allocator. No new exception export aliases are added.

The two commits form one runtime ABI fix: the second extends the regression fixture introduced by the first. There is no dependency on the separate math or hardware-concurrency changes.

Potential overlap: #1551 also edits `core/libs/prx/libc/CMakeLists.txt`. Its `precise_wait` registration and this PR's MinGW exception-test block are in different current hunks. There is no functional dependency, but the shared file should be checked when either PR is merged.

### Tested

Windows 10 x86-64, MinGW GCC 15.2, Ninja, Release, `BUILD_TESTING=ON`. Validation was repeated on this independent PR branch, head `05e1cf9d`, based on upstream `04477932`.

- Built only libc, libkernel and the relevant regression targets in a separate build directory, with at most four parallel jobs. No full repository build.
- Passed 27 CTests three consecutive times: **81/81 executions**. This includes 12 virtual-call cases, 10 guest message-destructor cases, `windows_exceptions`, `guest_thread_callback_abi`, `guest_exception_handler`, `guest_raise_exception` and `guest_unwind_module_info`.
- Covered mismatched and zero RCX, correct message/object selection, shared and final-release messages, typed guest catches, rethrow, cleanup and normal Release. A test-process-only wrapper around libc's native free import checks actual object/message frees and rejects duplicate or foreign frees.
- Existing native exception, virtual what, cleanup, exception_ptr and cross-thread rethrow regressions passed. Windows disassembly confirms RDI object access and native-call register/shadow-space bridging.
- Before the original fixes, four registered-message callback cases failed and 10/12 vtable cases failed. Plain non-deleting destructor cases had no observable failure because their helper ignores the object pointer. These earlier baseline results are distinct from the fresh PR-branch validation above.
- `git diff --check`, the official conventions check against `origin/main`, and the test-registration check passed. The registration checker reports no newly unregistered executable targets.

Linux source compatibility was reviewed: `APS5_VABI` is empty there, native helper semantics are unchanged, and the Windows assembly/IAT regressions are MinGW-only. **Linux build and runtime tests were not run because no usable Linux environment was available.** These self-authored guest fixtures validate AnyPS5's runtime model, not proprietary PS5 SDK layouts or physical-console behavior.

body:
### What

The static, graphics and rectangle ABI resolvers look up the registered shader by its code address. #639 made them require the bound `Shader` header to be at the registered header's address, and otherwise throw `... refers to a replaced shader header`.

Astro Bot (PPSA21567) registers a vertex shader with its header at 0x50000e500, then binds it for a draw through a copy at 0x307ae3920. The copy's 96 fixed `Shader` bytes match the registered header except `user_data`: 0x50000e668 in the registered header, null in the copy. The `cx_registers`, `sh_registers`, `specials` and semantic pointers still point into the registered header. body:
### What

Since #639, `RegisterShader` prepares every registered shader up front, and the first one that can't be prepared ends the run. Before that, such a shader only failed when it was dispatched, so titles that never dispatch it, or dispatch it late, kept running.

Several titles now stop at registration on compute shaders that call a user-data function pointer with `s_swappc_b64`, which is not implemented (#1817): Astro Bot, Ghost of Yōtei, Rise of the Ronin, Epic Mickey: Rebrushed, Stray and GTA V. Silksong and Ratchet & Clank: Rift Apart also register headers without their program address registers.

This change marks those shaders `deferred` instead of preparing them, and prepares them when they are first used. The deferral is decided before any preparation starts, and only in two cases:

- **The stage's program address registers are missing from the header.**
- **The program has an `s_swappc_b64` whose target the call analysis can't resolve.** `ShaderRecompiler::UnresolvableSwappcTarget` is the condition that `GraphBuilder::Build` throws on today. It is shared with the analysis through a new `isFetchCall` helper, so fetch-shader calls are still accepted.

Every other error, including any `GraphBuilder`, `Structurizer` or `PrepareShader` failure, still throws at registration. There is no retry after an error.

`SourceHandleFor` and `InvocationFor` prepare a deferred shader at dispatch, the path unregistered compute shaders already take. So the original error is raised there if the shader is really used.

### Tested

Linux (CachyOS, GCC), RX 9070 XT, Mesa 26.2.4 RADV. Head 52b77c20 on `main` 43972e69.

- **`agc_driver_prepared_shaders_deferred`** registers a compute shader made of `s_swappc_b64 s[4:5], s[4:5]`.
  - Registration succeeds, and logs `its s_swappc_b64 at program counter 0x0 calls a computed target`.
  - The dispatch fails with `not statically resolvable`.
  - The test now returns the skip code when no Vulkan device can be opened, like the other device tests.
- **`agc_driver`** (`tests/Submit.cpp`, `testHeaderWithoutProgramAddress`, contributed by @lubaxe) registers a type 4 header without `SPI_SHADER_PGM_LO/HI`. On `main` it fails with `missing static shader ABI register 201`.
- **Full `ctest`:** 512/513. The failing test is `import_audit`, which can't read the commit hash in my worktree and is unrelated.
- **`tools/check_conventions.py`** passes. `UnresolvableSwappcTarget` is added to `shaderCacheReviewedNames`: it only decides whether to prepare at registration and doesn't change what a recompile produces.
- **Astro Bot**, scripted input, headless:
  - Without this change it stops at its first shader registration on `computed/data-dependent s_swappc_b64 call target at program counter 0x00000074`.
  - With it, 96 shaders are deferred for an unresolvable `s_swappc_b64` and 1 for missing program registers.
  - The run then reaches `rectangle ABI refers to a replaced shader header`, which #1837 fixes. No frame is presented yet.

body:
### What

Initial implementation of the offline Apple ARM64 compiler discussed in #1553. Ready for architecture and coverage review of this experimental compiler-only implementation.

With `ANYPS5_NATIVE_AOT=ON`, declared x86-64 ELF functions are lowered to LLVM IR and compiled to ARM64 Mach-O objects. The emitted code uses native function calls, callbacks, stack arguments and resolved tail calls. The object gate rejects remaining virtual-register allocations or unresolved machine-state values; no x86 interpreter, JIT or runtime decoder is linked into the output.

The implementation includes:

- ELF/SCE dynamic metadata, sectionless symbol tables, relative pointers and native function import slots.
- Input-hash-bound function/data contracts, scalar SysV-to-Apple ABI reconstruction and a conservative native-pointer provenance check. Unproved literal addresses, pointer-cell contents and callback targets reject.
- Scalar integer operations, legacy SSE and a bounded VEX integer/bitwise subset, with explicit floating-point and division qualifications.
- Symbol/unwind/companion-object recovery evidence. Function signatures and indirect target sets remain explicit annotations; the helper does not infer or prove them.
- Pinned Capstone 5.0.6 and pyelftools 0.32 source submodules, opt-in CMake integration, reproducible tests and an Apple Silicon CI workflow.

This update fixes two defects in the proposed compiler: repeated native test compilations now load distinct dylibs instead of reusing the first loaded image, and pointer-cell invalidation follows the compiler's store semantics rather than Capstone operand access flags. This prevents SSE stores from leaving stale native-pointer proofs. Supported instruction coverage and runtime scope are unchanged.

This PR is **compiler-only**. Objects need a native entry-point caller and native implementations of their imports. It does not provide a complete PS5 runtime or a runnable game package. TLS, guest C++ exceptions, aggregates/varargs, general computed jumps, x87, atomics, concurrent memory semantics and module lifecycle remain open. Pointer-cell proofs are invalidated by possibly aliasing writes/calls; repeated GOT use and arbitrary struct-pointer loads can reject until typed memory-effect contracts are added. These limits are recorded in BUILD and TechnicalDebt.

The existing `hello_notify` and `gpu_cube` research inputs currently reject at a later startup import after the preceding call invalidates import-pointer proofs. They need typed pointer-cell/effect contracts and fresh qualification. Earlier integration executions are not evidence that this stricter PR runs those complete programs.

The regular relinker and runtime targets are unchanged when the option is off.

### Tested

Head `142a7ab2` retains the `745b775e` main base, including merged #2099 and #2151. The new commits correct the existing test harness and pointer analysis.

- Native Apple M5 Max, macOS 27.2, AppleClang 21, Python 3.13: all **212 CTest cases pass** (54.53 seconds with two processes). Conventions, registration and whitespace checks pass.
- Reproduced both defects before the fixes: a second dylib returning 42 still executed the previous function returning 17; a non-pointer SIMD overwrite could retain a spilled native-pointer proof.
- The loader regression executes two different compiled libraries and verifies that the first remains unchanged. Store regressions cover 22 supported SSE/VEX encodings, partial/full stack-pointer and import-slot overwrites, a non-pointer vector payload, and a read-only vector load.
- The CLI regression emits and links an ARM64-only executable, verifies `sysctl.proc_translated` is not set, then executes 1,000 arithmetic cases. Existing callback, tail-call, ABI, relocation, malformed metadata and vector/oracle tests also pass.
- The optional AMDGPU assembly case is skipped when Clang lacks that backend, as required by #2151. SSE references use Rosetta on this host; generated ARM64 artifacts do not. AVX2 uses independent integer/lane oracles. No console compatibility or performance claim is made.
- Hosted CI passes at head `142a7ab2`: [Native ARM64 AOT](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/actions/runs/37962616682), [relinker on Linux/Windows/macOS](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/actions/runs/37962616680), and [Conventions](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/actions/runs/37962616634). Full Linux/Windows PR builds require a maintainer to dispatch **Build** on main with `pr=1835`. Skipped full-build jobs do not count as passes.

body:
### What

A draw snapshot can corrupt storage-buffer array bounds on MoltenVK 1.4.2. Updating a short buffer at array element 1 also changes the shader-visible length of element 0: MoltenVK's auxiliary-size update uses the element index without the write's destination offset ([source](https://github.com/KhronosGroup/MoltenVK/blob/v1.4.2/MoltenVK/MoltenVK/GPUObjects/MVKDescriptorSet.mm#L1051)). In a native macOS integration test, a 128-byte constant buffer replaced an 864-byte vertex buffer's reported length.

Cache each original buffer descriptor when constructing the set. Draw snapshots now rewrite each affected array from element zero, substituting snapshot descriptors and retaining the original handle, offset and range for untouched elements. Unaffected bindings still use the descriptor-set copy. This adds one descriptor-info entry per allocation and writes complete affected arrays.

The regression covers changes to element 0, element 1 and both, with distinct data and ranges. It checks untouched descriptors, unrelated binding copies and resource lifetime through `PrepareDrawBindings`.

This is independent of the ARM64 compiler work. #1580 changes descriptor limits/layout allocation in the same files; it is not a dependency and does not address these partial-write bounds.

### Tested

Current head `a2fe737e` is rebased onto `main` at `745b775e`, which includes #2099 and resolves the previous missing SPIRV-Headers failure. `git range-diff` confirms this PR's fix and regression patch are unchanged. Conventions and whitespace checks pass.

- Earlier focused native ARM64 validation of the descriptor-only test failed on its unmodified base and passed with this patch. Previous head `ae1699ac` also passed full upstream Linux/Windows CI, including all 488 Linux tests and `agc_driver_graphics`.
- On this new base, the production source and regression compile in the focused native harness, but that harness's older native-runtime support archive no longer provides a coherent runtime for changed upstream texture/guest-memory interfaces. Its current-head execution attempt failed before the descriptor assertion. This is **not** a passing current-head runtime check; full validation is still required.
- Earlier integration-only MoltenVK 1.4.2 GPU tests passed after the full-array fix. That branch has macOS/shader changes outside this PR and does not substitute for current-head validation.

body:
### What

Fixes items 1 and 5 of #1794 (traced in [this comment](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/issues/1794#issuecomment-6068608707)).

A title's executable can name a bundled module differently from the file it ships. Dying Light 2 (PPSA02262) needs `EOSSDK-PS5-Shipping.debug_prx` and ships `EOSSDK-PS5-Shipping.prx` beside the executable. Needed names were matched by exact filename, so the relinker skipped the module without an error, and start-up stopped with `Failed to load module: ...\libs\EOSSDK-PS5-Shipping.debug_prx`. Renaming the file is not a workaround. The title later calls `sceKernelLoadStartModule("/app0//EOSSDK-PS5-Shipping.prx")`, and `dlopen` looks for `app0/EOSSDK-PS5-Shipping.prx.guest.prx`. That load fails with `ENOENT`, so the title's EOS lobby backend fails and `CGame::Initialize` asserts `Net_StartUp failed`.

`GuestModuleBuilder` now resolves a needed name that no file has exactly to a module whose name differs only in its `.prx`, `.sprx` or `.debug_prx` extension. This applies both in the module directories and in the search under the input. The output keeps the shipped file name (`EOSSDK-PS5-Shipping.prx.guest.prx`), so run-time loads by that name find it. The needed name is added as another name of that guest module, so the executable binds to it instead of asking for a host library. An exact filename still wins. Two candidates for one needed name are ambiguous, as for exact names.

### Tested

Windows 11, MinGW GCC 15.2.0, RTX 3070:
- `guest_needed_modules` has new cases. An executable needs `needed.debug_prx` while `needed.prx` is shipped, once in `Media/Modules` and once in `sce_module/`, on both the Linux and the Windows output. The guest output is `needed.prx.guest.prx`, the Linux executable's `DT_NEEDED` is that path and no host `needed.debug_prx`, and the Windows output runs and returns 42. `needed.prx` and `needed.sprx` side by side are reported as ambiguous. Without the change the new cases fail; with it they pass.
- Full build and `ctest`: 479/479 pass.
- `python tools/check_conventions.py --base origin/main` passes.
- Dying Light 2: relinked without renaming anything, `EOSSDK-PS5-Shipping.prx.guest.prx` is produced, and with the title's logging enabled it reports `[Lobby.Backend.Eos] > [StartUp] ok` and `[Lobby] > [Initialize] all backends are up`. `Net_StartUp` passes. The title then stops in EOS's `RtcNetworkThread`, which is the socket descriptor / `fd_set` question raised in #1794 and is not part of this PR. Other #1794 items were worked around locally for this run.

Linux output is covered by the test; I did not run a title on Linux.
