body:
### What
RADV on the PS5 ([mihawk-99/PS5_Mesa](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Mesa)) enables NGG culling by default on GFX10 and GFX10.3 (`radv_physical_device.c`, `use_ngg_culling`). Its vertex shaders are then ACO's NGG culling programs:
- They share vertex data through LDS with `s_barrier`.
- They count surviving vertices with `v_mbcnt` and a prefix sum, and read the wave's total with `v_readlane_b32` of lane 63.
- They allocate and export their own primitives (`s_sendmsg` `GS_ALLOC_REQ`, prim export).

AnyPS5 runs a PRIMGEN draw without GS on the vertex path, a Vulkan vertex shader with one guest lane per invocation. It has no workgroup memory or barrier, and on a 32-lane host it cannot read lanes 32-63. Every such draw failed with `v_readlane_b32 of lane 63 is outside the 32-lane host subgroup`. ccleste (PPSA59322) only rendered with `RADV_DEBUG=nonggc`.

The geometry path already provides what these programs need:
- A mesh workgroup with LDS.
- Two guest lanes per invocation for wave64 on a 32-lane host (`SpirvEmitter.cpp`, `laneCount`).
- `GS_ALLOC_REQ` and primitive exports.

This PR sends such a draw there.

- `decodeDraw` routes a draw to the geometry path when all of these hold:
  - `VGT_SHADER_STAGES_EN` has `PRIMGEN_EN` without `GS_EN`, `PRIMGEN_PASSTHRU_EN` or `HS_EN`.
  - The vertex program is unregistered (no AGC header).
  - The program uses LDS or `s_barrier`.

  Passthrough programs and every program that works today stay on the vertex path. RADV's own blits are passthrough, as are ps5-opengl's vertex shaders.
- `ProgramUsesWorkgroup` decodes the program once per snapshot (DS instructions or `s_barrier`) and caches the answer on it.
- `DecodeShaderStages(queue, vertexWorkgroup)` builds the mesh configuration from the NGG registers for such a program:
  - The subgroup is bounded by the vertex budget (`GE_MAX_OUTPUT_PER_SUBGROUP`) instead of the GS output budget.
  - Each input primitive yields at most one output primitive.
  - The GS and ES VGPR count checks are skipped. The merged inputs keep their positions whatever the counts, and the mesh entry loads v0-v8 either way. vkQuake's (PPSA99010) culling vertex shaders load only the vertex ID (`ES_VGPR_COMP_CNT` 0); ccleste's load all.
  - Asking for this with `GS_EN`, passthrough or tessellation throws.
- Registered programs keep today's routing. Routing them would also change registration-time preparation (`PrepareRegistered`, `ResolveGraphicsStagesAbi`), so I left that for a follow-up.
- Tests:
  - `agc_driver_graphics` (`NggVertexWorkgroupTests`), using ccleste's culling-draw registers (`VGT_SHADER_STAGES_EN` 0x00012010, `GE_NGG_SUBGRP_CNTL` 0x10080, `GE_MAX_OUTPUT_PER_SUBGROUP` 0x80, `VGT_ESGS_RING_ITEMSIZE` 1):
    - Without the flag, the draw stays on the vertex path.
    - With it, a triangle list becomes a mesh configuration of 42 primitives, 126 vertices and 128 threads.
    - A strip becomes 126 primitives over 128 vertices.
    - A program with vkQuake's `SPI_SHADER_PGM_RSRC1_GS`/`RSRC2_GS` (`0x222c0005`, `0x00400030`) takes the mesh path.
    - A vertex budget below one primitive, `GS_EN`, passthrough and tessellation are rejected.
  - `agc_driver` (`testProgramWorkgroupUse`): an LDS write and an `s_barrier` need a workgroup, a plain program does not, the result is cached, and the check starts at the program's entry.

There is no GPU execution test of a culling program on the mesh path; ccleste exercises it, below.

### Tested
Windows 11 Pro (26200), MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0 (WinLibs r7), Release, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti.

- The full suite (478 tests) passes on this branch. It was run from the generated `CTestTestfile.cmake` commands because antivirus blocks `ctest.exe` on this machine.
- ccleste renders its title screen and levels with RADV's NGG culling on (no `RADV_DEBUG`), on current `main` with this PR, #1819 and my other pending changes on a local branch. Earlier, on an older `main`, it was also play-tested this way.

Not tested on AMD, Intel or Linux.

### What

[SharpProspero](https://github.com/SvenGDK/SharpProspero/blob/5dfdb4b0b166e83dc9ae275001afb695f12c7174/src/SharpProspero/Interop/Compression/Zlib.cs) supplies the caller ABI and output limits. Linux x86-64. `guest_zlib` passes independent compressed fixtures, plaintext checks, checksum/truncation failures, exact and insufficient capacity, alignment, output canaries, request IDs and lifecycle guards. Standalone ASan/UBSan passes. Existing JPEG and PNG decoder tests also pass.

### What

Linux guest modules always received a run path rebased by two parent directories. That works for `app0/sce_module`, but a required module emitted under `app0/Media/Modules` searches `app0/libs` instead of the executable's `libs` directory. A module from the game root overshoots in the other direction.

Rebase `$ORIGIN` paths from each emitted module's actual directory to the executable directory. Preserve the configured suffix and leave absolute paths unchanged. Discovery, original game files and Windows import resolution are unchanged.

The regression converts fixtures with providers at the input root, in `sce_module`, and at two deeper nonstandard paths. Each conversion also includes a standard-directory module, so modules at different depths must resolve the same configured host-library directory. It checks default, bare `$ORIGIN`, custom paths containing a space, and absolute paths, with separate input and output directories.

### Tested

Windows 11, MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0, Release, `ANYPS5_RELINKER_ONLY=ON`, based directly on main `4b6ab6bb7371869f85837ff824f409b49f1e8081`:

- The same regression fails on unchanged main with nine incorrect resolutions and passes with the fix for all 32 module/path combinations.
- Final relinker build, conventions and `git diff --check` pass. All 36 groups other than `tls_function_coverage` pass within 30 seconds, including the new `guest_runpath` group.
- The initial full suite passed 36/37 and timed out the unchanged TLS group at 30 seconds. That complete group passes separately on both unchanged main and the final candidate. Its runtime exceeds 30 seconds on this machine; no repository timeout was raised, and these diagnostics do not establish CI's time limit.
- Generated Linux ELF dynamic strings are inspected on Windows. No Linux host execution, game startup or performance result is claimed.

[Upstream CI at this exact head](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/actions/runs/37840342766) passes the Linux and Windows full builds/tests and the relinker jobs on Linux, Windows and macOS. This supplements the local Windows checks above; it is not a title-playability result.

Reviewed related #732, #1165/#1232, #716 and the open discovery changes; none implements this path-depth correction. Trial merges against the inspected heads of #846, #1462, #1503, #1506, #1529, #1597, #1617, #1782 and #1815 are clean. None is included or required.

### What
`DecodePixelStageInfo` rejected any `SPI_PS_INPUT_ENA`/`ADDR` with `LINE_STIPPLE_TEX_ENA` (bit 7) or `POS_FIXED_PT_ENA` (bit 15): `unsupported SPI_PS_INPUT_ENA/ADDR bit combination`. RADV on the PS5 ([mihawk-99/PS5_Mesa](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Mesa)) sets both. In Mesa's `radv_compute_spi_ps_input` (`src/amd/vulkan/radv_shader.c`):

- `LINE_STIPPLE_TEX` is the required pixel input of a shader that reads no interpolants: "At least one of PERSP_* (0xF) or LINEAR_* (0x70) or LINE_STIPPLE_TEX must be enabled. LINE_STIPPLE_TEX uses the least number of initialized VGPRs". ccleste's (PPSA59322) present shader is one; with #1732 on current `main`, every frame stopped there (`presentation failed`).
- `POS_FIXED_PT` is enabled when a shader reads integer pixel coordinates (`reads_pixel_coord`): X in bits 15:0, Y in bits 31:16.

Changes:
- Both bits join the supported inputs in `DecodePixelStageInfo`. `PERSP_PULL_MODEL` and `SAMPLE_COVERAGE` are still rejected.
- `ShaderInputInfoBuilder` places both VGPRs whenever `SPI_PS_INPUT_ADDR` has the bit. `inputAddr` is already part of every cache, draw and request key, so no key or serializer changes are needed.
- The pixel entry fills them:
  - `POS_FIXED_PT` is `uint(FragCoord.x) | uint(FragCoord.y) << 16`.
  - `LINE_STIPPLE_TEX` is 0, because line stipple is not emulated. The TechnicalDebt entry under Functional records this.
- Tests:
  - `agc_driver_graphics` (`PixelInputLayoutTests`):
    - ENA/ADDR 0x80 decodes, with `LINE_STIPPLE_TEX` in v0.
    - With 0x8082, `LINE_STIPPLE_TEX` takes v2 and `POS_FIXED_PT` v3, after the perspective-center pair.
    - A shader exporting the `POS_FIXED_PT` VGPR reads `FragCoord`, and one exporting `LINE_STIPPLE_TEX` does not.
    - 0x8 and 0x4000 are still rejected.
  - New GPU test `agc_driver_pixel_fixed_point_position`:
    - A pixel shader splits the `POS_FIXED_PT` VGPR into X and Y and converts them to float. It exports them with the `LINE_STIPPLE_TEX` VGPR into a linear 64x16 `32_32_32_32` float target.
    - Every pixel must read back `(x, y, 0, 1)` for three ADDR layouts: the input alone, after `LINE_STIPPLE_TEX`, and after the perspective-center pair and `LINE_STIPPLE_TEX`.

body:
## Summary

Fixes #1791.

On Linux, `describePages` previously queried `PROCMAP_QUERY` (or `/proc/self/maps`) but did not store the discovered readable pages in the existing page table. As a result, subsequent uncached guest-range checks repeatedly performed `PROCMAP_QUERY`.

This change:

- Adds a shared `PageStates::record()` helper for populating cached page state.
- Reuses the existing page-table caching behavior already used by the Windows `VirtualQuery` path.
- Stores Linux `PROCMAP_QUERY` results in the page table.
- Applies the same behavior to the `/proc/self/maps` fallback.
- Preserves the existing generation/invalidation mechanism.
- Avoids changing memory validation semantics.

## Dependency

Depends on #861.

On current Linux `main`, the guest arena is not initialized into the Linux page-state arena span, so the new Linux cache population remains inactive until #861 lands. The relevant Linux test path is likewise gated when `GuestArenaAvailable_nid_postfix()` is false.

## Testing

Passed:
- `python -m unittest discover tools/tests` — 14/14 tests passed
- `python tools/check_conventions.py --base upstream/main` — passed

Not run locally:

### What

Adds `sceKernelGetFsSandboxRandomWord` to libkernel, in a new `System/src/Sandbox.cpp`. On the console a title's sandbox root holds `app0` and a directory with a random-looking name under which system files are exposed; the function returns that name, and the open-source SDKs splice it into paths: `/<name>/common/cert/CA_LIST.cer` ([ProsperoEden](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ProsperoEden/blob/main/headless/update_check/console_curl.c)), `/<name>/common/lib/libc.sprx` ([tiny-ps4-shell](https://github.com/john-tornblom/tiny-ps4-shell/blob/master/kern_orbis.c)), `/<name>/common/lib/mscorlib.dll` ([ps4-hen-plugins](https://github.com/Scene-Collective/ps4-hen-plugins/blob/main/plugin_mono/source/mono.c)). The kernel keeps the name per process and `randomized_path` (syscall 602) reads it back, as [obliteration](https://github.com/obhq/obliteration/blob/main/legacy/src/process/mod.rs) implements it, with `/system/common/lib` mounted at `<name>/common/lib`.

- The name is fixed, `gkbHtXc3Wq`, so a path built from it is the same across runs. It is recorded in TechnicalDebt: nothing is mounted under the name here, so `/gkbHtXc3Wq/common/...` resolves under the guest root like any other path and does not exist.
- The pointer is to static storage and the same on every call and every thread; the function cannot fail.

Of the 34 relinked titles in the homebrew catalog (#1578), 12 import the function and 5 stop at it on `main` b858fdc4: each dies in the loader with `app.elf: symbol lookup error: app.elf: undefined symbol: JGfTMBOdUJo`. They are PPSA17641 SymphonyStation5, PPSA74126 Stremio Plus, PPSA97510 PSXS5, PPSA99009 ProsperoLichess and PPSA99082 OpenNOW PS5 - Prototype, which makes it the most common next stop in the catalog. With this change each of them reaches its next missing import: `sceVideoOutGetResolutionStatus` (#1714), `socketpair` (#1711), `geteuid` (#1650), `geteuid` (#1650) and `sysctlbyname` (#1685).

Overlap: none by `tools/pr_overlap.py` against the open pull requests. #1748, #1650 and #1675 change `System/src/Process.cpp`, which this does not touch; the source line goes after `Process.cpp` in `libkernel/CMakeLists.txt`, the test block after `guest_file_vector`, and the TechnicalDebt entry after the `sceKernelPread` one, clear of #1802's rewrite of the `sceKernelRaiseException` entries.

body:
### What

On Linux the narrow printf family passes `%ls`/`%S` guest strings to the host formatter, which reads 32-bit wchar_t elements instead of the guest's 16-bit units. Route formats containing `%ls`, `%S`, `%lc` or `%C` through the existing guest formatter. Formats without guest wide conversions retain their native Linux path, including positional arguments and escaped percent signs. Guest va_list inputs remain unchanged.

The common formatter also dropped a NUL `%lc`/`%C` argument because it passed that character through `%s`. Format that one case through `%c`, preserving the byte and output count. This follows [FreeBSD 11 vfprintf](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/stable/11/lib/libc/stdio/vfprintf.c), whose wide-character branch emits the complete `wcrtomb` result, including a converted NUL.

Extend the existing guest_formatting regression on both platforms and update TechnicalDebt. The UTF-16-to-UTF-8 conversion policy is the existing Windows policy: it does not establish console locale behavior or validate invalid UTF-16. Positional or other unsupported conversions in a format that needs the guest formatter still throw; ordinary Linux formats keep host support.

Independent of #1507 (wcsrtombs), #1511 (swprintf), #1573 (Windows numeric flags), #1614 (locale character conversions) and #1708 (large collate storage). Merge simulations with the current heads of #1511 and #1573 are clean. #1708 conflicts only in adjacent TechnicalDebt entries; the implementation files merge cleanly. Rebase the second PR after the first merges, preserving both debt updates. No functional dependencies.

### Tested

Windows x64 Release, portable GCC 15.2.0 and CMake/Ninja in the existing virtualenv, SPIRV-Tools disabled: all 34 libc CTests pass. The real-DLL PoC covers all 14 formatting exports, C and UTF-8 host locales, mixed argument types, output capacities, precision, Unicode surrogate pairs, NUL characters, protected page boundaries, allocation and file/stdout output, preserved va_list state and concurrent calls.

[Linux validation](https://github.com/gdrosa/AnyPS5/actions/runs/37830862982) on Ubuntu 24.04, GCC 13.3, Release, SPIRV-Tools enabled, exact commit `21d21da3857e`: the same regression on unpatched main fails only guest_formatting (36/37 tests pass). The fix passes 37/37 libc tests, repeated three times. The full suite, requested with repeat until-fail:3, has 291 passes, 194 GPU-dependent skips and 1 failure(s) out of 486 tests. The complete project, patched libraries and test-registration check pass. The Linux real-library PoC passes 5,974 checks; Windows passes 5,976. Full Windows project suite not rerun for this contribution. Build tools are installed in virtualenvs or taken from the existing portable toolchain; no system installations.

The full suite has one failure: `agc_driver_flip` reports "failed flip was completed successfully". This is consistent with a pre-existing notification race: [QueueWorker.cpp](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/blob/b858fdc48e29c3ab7476782199d8a41999d46d59/core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Execution/src/Driver/Queues/QueueWorker.cpp#L168) calls ReportFailure before failing the active submission's flip requests; [Lifecycle.cpp](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/blob/b858fdc48e29c3ab7476782199d8a41999d46d59/core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Execution/src/Driver/Lifecycle.cpp#L81) publishes the exception and wakes idle waiters. [Flip.cpp](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/blob/b858fdc48e29c3ab7476782199d8a41999d46d59/core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/tests/Flip.cpp#L181) then reads the callback counter after those waiters return, which can happen before the callback. These three files are byte-identical to the unpatched base. This diagnosis is source analysis; the unpatched base was not rerun locally to reproduce the failure. [Upstream Build on that base](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/actions/runs/37829320117) passed, so this result should not be presented as a deterministic base failure. The printf change does not modify the AGC path.

body:
### What

Fixes item 4 of #1794. On Windows, `sceKernelMprotect` accepted only the executable's image and threw `Memory protection of a foreign image is not supported` for any other image. Bundled title modules are relinked into DLLs named `<module>.guest.prx`, so a title that reprotects pages of its own bundled module could not start. Dying Light 2's bundled `libNRD` does this at start-up (`prot=0x12` over 0x11278 bytes, then `0x11` over 0x178540 bytes).

`DoMprotect` now also accepts images whose file name ends in `.guest.prx`. It registers their committed pages in `GuestAllocations` the same way as the executable's: `RegisterMainImage`'s Windows walk becomes a per-image registration, and the executable is one caller. Any other image (system DLLs, AnyPS5's own `.prx` libraries) is still refused.

### Tested

Windows 11, MinGW GCC 15.2.0, RTX 3070:
- `guest_memory` has a new Windows case. It loads a small DLL named `guest_memory_module.guest.prx` and reprotects a data page read-only, then writable (writes and checks a byte), then read-only again, checking the host protection each time. body:
### What

Hades (PPSA03355, v01.003) stops at load on `main`:

```
./app.elf: symbol lookup error: ./app.elf: undefined symbol: 9HzfhdtESio
```

`9HzfhdtESio` is `pthread_getname_np`. The executable imports it from libkernel and calls it once: `pthread_getname_np(pthread_self(), buffer)`, with a 32-byte stack buffer that was zeroed first. No length is set before the call.

I measured the console function on a PS5 (firmware 13.60) by calling libkernel's export through `dlopen` from a homebrew payload, with the buffer filled with `0xAA` before each call:

| Call | Console |
|---|---|
| thread named `""`, `"A"`, `"AnyPS5Probe"`, a 31-character name | 0; writes the name and its terminator, nothing after |
| a third argument of 0, 1, 4 or 64 | ignored: the whole name is written |
| a new thread that was never named | 0, `""` |
| a joined thread, or a null thread | 3 (`ESRCH`), nothing written |
| a null buffer | 14 (`EFAULT`) |

So on the PS5 it takes `(thread, buffer)`, not FreeBSD's `(thread, buffer, length)`. This adds `pthread_getname_np` with that signature on top of `scePthreadGetname`, which already writes the stored name truncated to 31 characters and terminated, and returns `ESRCH` and `EFAULT` for the two measured errors.

A joined thread cannot be detected here: `scePthreadJoin` frees the thread object, so the pointer is indistinguishable from a live one. The TechnicalDebt entry records that. Hades only passes `pthread_self()`.

With this branch, Hades gets past load and runs until `sceKernelDebugRaiseException` (`0xa0020013`), before it reaches the `pthread_getname_np` call. That stop is unrelated and is not touched here.

A fork branch (`budhilaw/AnyPS5`, `feat/macos-uncharted`, not in a PR) has a three-argument version that would read the length from `rdx`. Hades never sets that register before this call.

Measured in passing, and not changed here: the console's `pthread_rename_np` refuses a name of 32 characters or more with 63 (`ENAMETOOLONG`) and keeps the old name, while `main` stores any length.

### Tested

- PS5 firmware 13.60: every row of the table. The probe source and the raw output are in the comment below.
- Hades (PPSA03355) on Linux: stops at load on `main` with the line above, and gets past load with this branch.
- Linux: build, `libs`, full CTest 480/480. The new `guest_pthread_getname` covers every row except the joined thread.
- Windows Server 2025 VM, WinLibs GCC 15.2, CI configure flags: build, `libs`, CTest 0 failed of 474, `guest_pthread_getname` included (GPU execution tests skipped, the VM has no GPU).
- Mutation check: 5 mutations each make `guest_pthread_getname` fail. They drop the null-thread or null-buffer check, return `EINVAL` for the buffer, drop the terminator, or pad the buffer past the name.

body:
### What

Implements `gethostbyname` in `libScePosixForWebKit`, one of EVO-PLAYER-PS5's missing imports reported in #1578.

Parses numeric IPv4 addresses with FreeBSD semantics before native hostname lookup. Supports decimal, octal and hexadecimal forms, one through four components, trailing whitespace and FreeBSD 64-bit accumulation. For example, `0x7f.1` resolves to `127.0.0.1`. Copies the name, aliases and address list into per-thread storage with the guest `hostent` layout. Linux uses reentrant lookup. Windows converts its 16-bit host fields into guest 32-bit fields. Failures update `sceNetErrnoLoc`, the error location used by the public SDK's `__h_errno`. A successful numeric lookup clears that error.

The ABI and SDK error location follow [SDK v0.43 netdb.h](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk/blob/v0.43/include/freebsd/netdb.h), [SDK netdb.c](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk/blob/v0.43/libc/netdb.c), and [FreeBSD 11 netdb.h](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/releng/11.0/include/netdb.h). Numeric parsing and success errors follow FreeBSD 11.4 [inet_aton](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/releng/11.4/lib/libc/inet/inet_addr.c) and [fakeaddr](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/releng/11.4/lib/libc/net/gethostnamadr.c). Exact PS5 semantics remain unverified and are recorded in TechnicalDebt. Windows conversion follows [Microsoft HOSTENT](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winsock2/ns-winsock2-hostent).

### Tested

- Arch Linux, GCC, Release build. The new behavioral check first failed with `undefined reference to gethostbyname_nid_postfix`.
- `guest_resolver` and `guest_sce_net` pass. Checks cover numeric address bytes, guest field widths, names, aliases, address lists, per-thread result lifetime, and the SDK error location.
- Loaded the NID-patched module and called `5T4SHQqzoGo`: numeric lookup and shared error reporting pass.
- The new `0x7f.1` regression check failed before the compatibility fix and passes after it. Sixteen numeric fixtures cover shorthand, octal, hexadecimal, whitespace, wrapping and component boundaries.
- 2,009 numeric inputs match a locally compiled FreeBSD 11.4 `inet_aton` reference.
- A consumer compiled for FreeBSD against SDK v0.43 headers passes guest `hostent` layout, numeric lookup and error-slot checks. It uses the SDK's actual `__h_errno` function. SDK tooling remains outside the repository.
- Native Windows 11 Pro (build 26300), MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0 (WinLibs r7), Release: reproduced the reported guest_resolver_tests link failure with undefined reference to __gxx_personality_v0 on a1e2781f. Linking libc and applying configure_windows_unwind fixes the build. guest_resolver, guest_sce_net and windows_exceptions pass (3/3); the resolver executable has the required .ehfram section.
- WSL2 Arch Linux, GCC 15.2.1, Release: built the same patched source. guest_resolver, guest_sce_net, exception_runtime, exception_personality and exception_c_cleanup pass (5/5). Linux .eh_frame and .eh_frame_hdr sections remain intact.

### What

Fixes #1785. Both Windows error maps, libkernel `NativeError` and libSceNet `native_error`, translate `WSAESHUTDOWN` to 32 (`EPIPE`), as FreeBSD `send(2)` reports and as the Linux maps already do for the host's `EPIPE`. ### What

Implements the C locale wide character class functions in libc on top of the rune locale from #1781: `iswalnum`, `iswalpha`, `iswblank`, `iswcntrl`, `iswdigit`, `iswgraph`, `iswlower`, `iswprint`, `iswpunct`, `iswspace`, `iswupper`, `iswxdigit`, `iswctype`, `wctype`, `towlower`, `towupper`, `btowc` and `wctob`.

Following FreeBSD 11 `_ctype.h`, `wctype.c`, `btowc.c`, `wctob.c` and `none.c` for the C locale, the only one `setlocale` accepts:

- `isw*` and `iswctype` test `_CurrentRuneLocale->__runetype[c]` for 0..255 and are false above 0xFF and for `WEOF` (the `_ext` ranges are empty). `iswalnum` is `_CTYPE_A|_CTYPE_N`.
- `wctype` returns FreeBSD's `_CTYPE_*` masks for the twelve standard names and the BSD `ideogram`, `special`, `phonogram`, `number` and `rune`, and 0 for any other name.
- `towlower`/`towupper` map 0..255 through `__maplower`/`__mapupper` and return anything else unchanged.
- `btowc(EOF)` is `WEOF`; any other value is `(unsigned char)c`. `wctob` returns the value for 0..255 and `EOF` otherwise, including `WEOF`.

Found with `tools/import_audit.py` on the catalog homebrew titles: each of these is absent in 9 or 10 of 36 audited titles.

body:
### What

When the executable needs a module that is not in `sce_module`, `sce_modules` or `prx`, the relinker searches the input tree for it and relinks it. The modules that this found module needs in turn were not looked up. They were left as host libraries, which no host provides, so the title failed to load.

The needed names of every module found this way are now searched for the same way, round by round, until no new module turns up. Each name is searched once, so a dependency cycle ends the search. Names that nothing in the input provides stay host libraries, as before. Ambiguity, exclusion (`--exclude-sce-module`) and the skipped module directories work as before. Each found module is parsed once, and the parsed image is reused when the modules are relinked.

The scope is kept narrow. Only modules found by this search have their needs followed. Modules in `sce_module`, `sce_modules` and `prx` are unchanged, and their needs resolve as before.

Example: Planet Coaster (PPSA01736) needs `libcohtml.Prospero.prx` at the package root, and that module needs `libChakraCore.prx` and `libRenoirCore.PS5.prx` beside it. Before, only cohtml was relinked; now all three are.

### Tested

Windows 11, MinGW-w64 15.2.0. `test_guest_needed_modules.py` adds two cases, each for both Linux ELF and Windows PE output:
- A found module needs a second module elsewhere in the tree: both are relinked. The Linux DT_NEEDED order puts the dependency first, and the Windows output runs and returns 42.
- The second module needs a library the input lacks: it stays a host library in DT_NEEDED.

The first case fails without the fix. The relinker-only build passes its tests (36/36), and so does the full build (476/476). `tools/check_conventions.py --base origin/main` passes. Converting PPSA01736 now relinks cohtml, ChakraCore and RenoirCore, and the title loads them. Not built or run on Linux or macOS.

body:
### What

Exports the FreeBSD C rune locale from libc: `_DefaultRuneLocale` (`lWGF8NHv880`), `_CurrentRuneLocale` (`chlN6g6UbGo`) and `__mb_sb_limit` (`fGYLBr2COwA`). Titles built against FreeBSD `<ctype.h>`/`<wctype.h>` read `_CurrentRuneLocale->__runetype[c]` inline, bounded by `__mb_sb_limit`, and fall back to `&_DefaultRuneLocale`; they import these as `libSceLibcInternal` data.

- `_RuneLocale` follows FreeBSD 11 `include/runetype.h`, checked with `static_assert`s: `__runetype` at 64, `__maplower` at 2112, `__mapupper` at 3136, ranges at 4160, 4224 bytes.
- The C table is generated, not copied. It matches FreeBSD 11 `lib/libc/locale/table.c` for all 256 `__runetype`, `__maplower` and `__mapupper` entries (compared offline against a parse of that file): ASCII classes, the digit value in the low byte of digits and hex letters, no class above 0x7f, magic `RuneMagi`, encoding `NONE`, `__invalid_rune` 0xFFFD, empty `_ext` ranges.
- `_CurrentRuneLocale` points at `_DefaultRuneLocale`, and `__mb_sb_limit` is 256, as in FreeBSD `table.c` and `none.c` for the C locale, the only locale `setlocale` accepts.

Found with `tools/import_audit.py` on the catalog homebrew titles: `_DefaultRuneLocale` is absent in 11 of 36 audited titles, `_CurrentRuneLocale` and `__mb_sb_limit` in 9.

body:
### What

`/dev/random` and `/dev/urandom` resolved to files under the guest root that do not exist, so `open` failed. Titles that read entropy from them then read from the failed descriptor: Planet Coaster (PPSA01736) aborts in `sceKernelRead` with `fd=-1, errno=9`.

Opening either path for reading now returns a descriptor backed by the host's null device. `read`, `pread`, `readv` and `preadv` on it fill the buffer from `std::random_device`, the source `sceRandomGetRandomNumber` already uses. As on FreeBSD, both devices behave the same and positioned reads ignore the offset. Opening them for writing (adding entropy) throws. Closing a descriptor, through `close` or `sceKernelClose`, forgets it.

### Tested

body:
### What
A compute program whose LDS is larger than `maxComputeSharedMemorySize` was compiled to a `Workgroup` array of that size, which Vulkan does not allow (NVIDIA reports 48 KiB and lavapipe 32 KiB; a PS5 workgroup can have 64 KiB).

- When the LDS plus the 64-bit atomic lock dword exceeds the target's `maxWorkgroupSharedMemoryBytes`, the whole LDS moves to a storage buffer at set 1: one slice per workgroup (LDS and lock dword), indexed by the flattened `WorkgroupId`. Bounds stay as they were; barriers and LDS atomics add `UniformMemory` semantics, and the buffer is `Coherent`.
- The driver binds a device-local buffer sized by the group count (rounded up to 1 MiB). An indirect dispatch of such a program reads its group counts on the CPU; more than `maxStorageBufferRange` throws.
- Smaller programs compile as before. The size travels in `ShaderInfo::sharedMemoryBytes`, which the disk cache already encodes (cold cache, same format); the LDS size and the limit are both known when the shader is registered.
- PPSA26344 v1.008: four ray-traversal kernels declare 63.5 or 60.5 KiB. On `main` an RTX 3080 runs such arrays up to 96 KiB and hangs at 112 KiB.
- Overlap: #1190's shared-aperture arm uses the same LDS element pointer, so it follows.

### Tested

body:
### What

Implements `getifaddrs` (NID `j-gWL6wDros`) and `freeifaddrs` (NID `N2OjwJJGjeQ`) in libc. 16 of the homebrew titles in the #1578 audit import both from libSceLibcInternal, which resolves through libc.

- One entry per host IPv4 or IPv6 address, in FreeBSD's 56-byte `struct ifaddrs` with FreeBSD `sockaddr_in` / `sockaddr_in6` (length byte, `AF_INET` 2, `AF_INET6` 28). Every entry has a netmask. Broadcast interfaces get the IPv4 broadcast address, point-to-point interfaces the destination address. Flags use FreeBSD's values (`IFF_MULTICAST` is `0x8000`, not Linux's `0x1000`).
- Linux reads the host's `getifaddrs`. Windows reads `GetAdaptersAddresses`: names from `ConvertInterfaceLuidToNameA` (NDIS names such as `loopback_0`), netmask from `OnLinkPrefixLength`, broadcast from the address and netmask.
- As on FreeBSD, the list is one allocation, so `freeifaddrs` is a single `free`.
- Errors return -1 with FreeBSD `errno`, as `getcwd` here does: a null list pointer gives `EFAULT`, and host or allocation failures give `ENOMEM`, `ENOBUFS`, `EMFILE` or `ENFILE`. Any other host failure throws.
- Linux edge cases: a point-to-point address without a peer loses `IFF_POINTOPOINT`, and an IPv4 broadcast address the host omits is computed from the netmask, so a flag always comes with its address, as on FreeBSD.
- Windows edge cases:
  - The flags are only `IFF_UP`, `IFF_RUNNING`, `IFF_LOOPBACK`, `IFF_BROADCAST` and `IFF_MULTICAST`, derived from the adapter.
  - A prefix length the host reports as unspecified (255) gets a host mask.
  - PPP and tunnel adapters get neither `IFF_BROADCAST` nor `IFF_POINTOPOINT`, since their peer address is not reported and FreeBSD always fills `ifa_dstaddr` with `IFF_POINTOPOINT`.
  - An NDIS name longer than 15 bytes (FreeBSD's `IFNAMSIZ` is 16) becomes `if<index>`.
  - The adapter query is retried at most 4 times.
- Recorded in TechnicalDebt:
  - FreeBSD's per-interface `AF_LINK` entries and their `if_data` are not produced, so interfaces without an address are omitted.
  - Names are the host's.
  - The Windows flag and prefix rules above apply.

### Tested
<!-- OS, title or homebrew, what was checked. "Not tested" is a valid answer. -->

- New `guest_interfaces` test, registered in ctest:
  - **Host comparison:** compares every guest entry, in order, with a snapshot from the same host API (`getifaddrs` on Linux, `GetAdaptersAddresses` on Windows). Family, address, netmask and IPv6 scope id must match, with up to 3 attempts in case DHCP or a VPN changes an address between the two snapshots.
  - **Per entry:** name length, FreeBSD-only flag bits, sockaddr layouts (zero port, flowinfo and padding), and 8-byte alignment. A broadcast or point-to-point flag must come with a destination address.
  - **Loopback:** requires `127.0.0.1/8` with `IFF_UP | IFF_LOOPBACK` and no `IFF_BROADCAST`.
  - **Errors:** `getifaddrs(nullptr)` must return -1 with `EFAULT`, and `freeifaddrs(nullptr)` must return.
- The test fails against 16 deliberate breakages, among them:
  - flag translation (Linux's `IFF_MULTICAST` leaking through, the loopback flag dropped, loopback marked broadcast);
  - sockaddr length and family bytes, and the netmask (taken from the address, or a prefix mask off by one bit);
  - dropped IPv4 or IPv6 entries, a truncated list, a dropped IPv6 scope id;
  - a broadcast flag without a broadcast address, a non-zero port or flowinfo, and the null-pointer `errno`.
- Windows 10, MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0 (WinLibs `15.2.0posix-14.0.0-ucrt-r7`), Release, merged with `main` d70b8998: `guest_interfaces` passes (`--repeat until-fail:3`), and so does the full suite. The NID-patched `libc.prx` exports both NIDs.

body:
### What

A vertex attribute whose V# has stride 0 and fewer `NUM_RECORDS` bytes than one element made the draw throw ("vertex fetch exceeds descriptor byte range"), so the draw was skipped.

With stride 0 the range check depends on `OOB_SELECT` (V# word 3, bits 28-29). The GFX10 table in Mesa [`ac_descriptors.c`](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/-/blob/main/src/amd/common/ac_descriptors.c) gives:

- `OOB_SELECT 2`: out of range only when `NUM_RECORDS == 0`.
- `OOB_SELECT 3` (swizzle off): out of range when `offset >= NUM_RECORDS`.

This change:

- `VertexFetchOutOfRange` (`VertexInput.hpp`) is true for a stride-0 `OOB_SELECT` 2 or 3 V# with no records. `Draw` binds a zeroed buffer of one element for such an attribute instead of planning a guest copy.
- `ZeroStrideAvailableBytes` makes `VertexBufferReadSize` and `VertexBufferExtent` (the indirect-draw path) read the whole element for a stride-0 `OOB_SELECT 2` V# with nonzero records. This goes through the normal guest copy, so pending GPU writes are flushed and the render-target alias check runs.
- `OOB_SELECT 3` with a fetch that only partly fits still throws, because the source does not say whether each dword is checked separately. `OOB_SELECT` 0 and 1 keep the current structured checks.
- The rules are recorded in TechnicalDebt as taken from Mesa, not measured on hardware.

Why it matters: Unreal Engine binds its per-draw PrimitiveId vertex stream as a stride-0, one-record, `OOB_SELECT 2` V# (`V# xxxxxxxx 0000001e 00000001 20014204` in PPSA16064). The vertex shader uses the id to fetch the primitive's transform. With the draw skipped, or with the id read as zero, every mesh is placed with primitive 0's transform.

Relation to #1426: #1426 handles the same short zero-stride case. It keeps only the whole dwords below `NUM_RECORDS` (`records & ~3`), so a one-record PrimitiveId stream reads as 0. A downstream branch with that rule renders PPSA16064's title scene with every terrain chunk drawn on top of the first one: the depth prepass covers about 13% of the frame and the base pass shows see-through blocks. Reading the whole element as `OOB_SELECT 2` defines fixes it: depth coverage goes to about 37% of the 2848x1600 target, about 80% of the 1920x1080 view. The new execution test's "OOB_SELECT 2, one record" case expects the element itself, so it separates the two rules.

### Tested

Windows 11, MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0, Release, `BUILD_TESTING=ON`, NVIDIA RTX 5070.

- New execution test `agc_driver_zero_stride_vertex_fetch`. It draws through a fetch-shader vertex attribute and stores the fetched registers. Cases: `OOB_SELECT 2` with one record reads the whole element; `OOB_SELECT 2` with none reads zeros; `OOB_SELECT 3` with a whole element in range reads it; `OOB_SELECT 3` with none reads zeros; `OOB_SELECT 0` with a whole element in range is unchanged. It fails on `main` with "vertex fetch exceeds descriptor byte range" and passes with this change.
- `agc_driver_graphics` has new unit checks for `VertexBufferReadSize`, `VertexBufferExtent` and `VertexFetchOutOfRange` across the `OOB_SELECT` modes.
- All `agc_driver` tests: 196/196 pass.
- PPSA16064 (Minecraft Dungeons II) title scene: verified on a downstream branch with an equivalent change (the PrimitiveId case reads the full 4-byte element), comparing prepass depth coverage before and after. This exact branch was not run in the title.
- Not tested on Linux or on an AMD GPU.

body:
### What

Fixes #1754. On Windows, `flock` now tracks the one lock each descriptor holds ([FileLock.cpp](core/libs/prx/libkernel/File/src/FileLock.cpp)), as FreeBSD `flock(2)` defines it:

- `LOCK_UN` without a lock and a repeat of the held mode return 0.
- A conversion between `LOCK_SH` and `LOCK_EX` releases the held lock and takes the new one. As on FreeBSD, the conversion is not atomic, and a failed `LOCK_NB` conversion leaves no lock.
- `close` and `sceKernelClose` forget the descriptor's lock, so a reused descriptor number starts unlocked.
- The operation is decoded as FreeBSD [`sys_flock`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/39f7dbff606d/sys/kern/kern_descrip.c#L4053-L4066) does, before either host sees it: `LOCK_UN` over `LOCK_EX` over `LOCK_SH`, other bits ignored, and an operation with none of the three fails with `EBADF`. Before, Linux rejected such operations with `EINVAL` and Windows took them as a shared lock. An invalid descriptor sets `EBADF`.
- The state lock is not held during a blocking `LockFileEx`, so a wait on one descriptor does not block `flock` on others.

Contention still throws from `flock_nid_postfix`, as before and as on Linux. On Linux only the operation decoding changes.

### Tested

Windows 11 (10.0.26200), MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0 (WinLibs r7), Release, RTX 4070 Laptop:

- `guest_filesystem` gains `flock` cases: unlock without a lock, repeated `LOCK_EX`, `LOCK_EX` → `LOCK_SH` → `LOCK_EX` conversions, shared locks on two descriptors, repeated `LOCK_SH` released by one `LOCK_UN`, descriptor reuse after `close` and `sceKernelClose`, and malformed operations (`0` and `LOCK_NB | 0x10` fail with `EBADF`, `LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB | 0x10` locks, `LOCK_UN | LOCK_EX` unlocks).
- On main the new cases abort at the first `LOCK_UN` (`error=158`); with the change they pass. Without the decoding commit the malformed cases abort (`error=87`).
- Full `ctest` with `ANYPS5_REQUIRE_VULKAN=1 --repeat until-fail:3`: 506/507 passed on `d70b8998`. `libs` target builds. The failure, `pr_overlap_encoding`, also fails on main locally: it patches `subprocess._text_encoding`, which Python 3.10 does not have.
- Linux: not run locally. CI Linux passed `guest_filesystem` on the earlier head, and nauroth ran it on Ubuntu 24.04 in #1764.

body:
### What
Part of #1578. Implements `seteuid` (`HTxb6gmexa0`) and `setegid` (`4oKwKmeOKjM`) in libkernel. In the #1578 audit, `seteuid` is an absent import of 11 of the relinking homebrew titles (ProsperoRadio, ProsperoLight, ProsperoTV, PS5MC, Prospero Win and others) and `setegid` of 4. No open PR implements them or any other `set*id` function.

The guest process is assumed to run as root, with real, effective and saved ids 0; #1650 reports the same identity through `getuid`/`geteuid`/`getgid`/`getegid`. In FreeBSD 11.0 `sys_seteuid` and `sys_setegid` (`sys/kern/kern_prot.c`), an id equal to the real or saved id passes without a privilege check, and the credential changes (and `P_SUGID` is set) only when the id differs from the current effective one. So:
- `seteuid(0)` and `setegid(0)` return 0, change nothing and leave errno untouched.
- Any other id would change the effective credential, which nothing models, so it throws. EPERM would be wrong, since root is allowed.

The known callers are the sandbox-elevation clients these homebrew share (the ps5-native-app-boilerplate example vendored in ProsperoLight, ProsperoTV and ProsperoStore; Porpoise; prospero-win; PSXS5). They call `seteuid(geteuid())`, and `setegid(getgid())` only when `getegid() != getgid()`. With a root identity, both pass id 0. The assumed identity is recorded in `TechnicalDebt.md`.

There is no build dependency on #1650: the two change different lines and merge in either order. If #1650's identity changes, the accepted id here follows it. Whichever lands second can fold the two `TechnicalDebt.md` entries into one and move these exports next to the getters.

### Title
Callers do `seteuid(geteuid())` and imports resolve in name order, so on `main` these titles stop at `geteuid` first; with #1650 they stop here. Runs posted by others:
- CouchRiv on #1650, Linux `main` f1451396 + #1650: PPSA99003 ProsperoTV 01.000.030 stops at `undefined symbol: HTxb6gmexa0` (`seteuid`), PPSA99002 ProsperoLight 01.000.090 at `4oKwKmeOKjM` (`setegid`).
- LeandroLP23 on #1578, Windows `main` f1451396 with each stop's PR merged in turn: PPSA99808 PICO-8 v0.1.2 resolves `seteuid` with this PR and stops next at `sigaction`.
- Own Windows runs, `main` 0fdda7be + #1650: PPSA99003 ProsperoTV stops at `HTxb6gmexa0` and PPSA99002 ProsperoLight at `4oKwKmeOKjM`; with this PR they stop next at `JGfTMBOdUJo` (`sceKernelGetFsSandboxRandomWord`) and `+F7C-hdk7+E` (`sigemptyset`). Details in the comments.

### Tested

body:
### What
With pipelined draws (#1201, on by default since #1202), every compute dispatch on queue 0 still drains the pipeline before it runs, so the committer goes idle and the worker waits. Titles with many dispatches between draws pay that on each one: Demon's Souls issues about 3,800 queue-0 dispatches per frame in its tutorial level, most of them one chain of small ones (measured by @fisherjoey on #1202).

`APS5_PIPELINE_DISPATCH=1` (off by default; needs pipelined draws) makes a `DISPATCH_DIRECT` whose dispatch-cache entry hits with a recipe an ordered commit item, like the draws around it. The capture and the cache lookup run on the worker; the recording runs on the committer in order. A dispatch still drains, as today, when:
- its cache lookup misses or the entry has no recipe;
- what it reads overlaps a write still pending in the pipeline (the read-side rule: its captured inputs would be checked against memory a queued item is about to change);
- the hit is a verified data hit, or its writes cannot be ranged.

`DrawPipeline::DrainRequestsByOpcode` counts drains per opcode and `DrawPipeline::QueuedItems` reports the queue size, both for the tests. `DispatchWriteRanges` gives the commit item the dispatch's write ranges, so later draws that read them wait for it.

Tests (`tests/execution/PipelinedDispatch.cpp`):
- `agc_driver_pipelined_dispatch` (switch off): a dispatch after an immediate fill of its input, in one DCB, over several rounds; each dispatch drains once and reads the fill.
- `agc_driver_pipelined_dispatch_item` (switch on): repeated dispatches that read nothing pending do not drain; a round whose descriptor table a pending fill retargets drains and reads the new buffer. That round holds the committer behind a gate item, waits until the fills are queued, and only then submits the dispatch, so the order is exact rather than timed. With the read-side check removed it reads the buffer the table named before the fill (0x6a6a0002 for 0x6b6b0003), every run; with the commit-item path removed, the first round fails ("a dispatch that reads nothing pending drained the pipeline").

### Tested
Windows 11 Pro, AMD Ryzen 5 7600, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5080 (driver 32.0.16.1074), 32 GB, MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0.
- On this branch: builds; all `agc_` tests pass with the switch off and on.
- GTA V PPSA04264 (01.005), Performance mode, the prologue bank, on my integration branch with the same change: 26.2 fps with the switch against 26.4 without, i.e. no change. GTA V issues few dispatches between draws; the expected gain is in titles like Demon's Souls, which I have not measured yet.

body:
### What

This PR addresses two concurrency and stability issues in `core/libs/prx/libkernel/Pthread/src/Thread.cpp`:

1. **Prevent TLS nullptr crash in `scePthreadCreate`**:
   `scePthreadCreate` on Linux (`#else` branch) previously used `std::promise<bool> start` and `start.set_value(true)` to synchronize the creator and newly spawned threads.
   Under Linux GCC/glibc, `std::promise::set_value` invokes `std::call_once`, which relies on libstdc++ thread-local storage (`_ZSt15__once_callable`). When host tests or client code run across the boundary between the PRX shared library and test executables, the trampoline function executed via `pthread_once` / `__once_proxy` can dereference a null TLS pointer (`_ZSt15__once_callable` is `0x0` due to dual runtime / TLS model mismatch), resulting in an immediate `SIGSEGV` in `std::once_flag::_Prepare_execution::_FUN` at `mov (%rax), %rdx`.
   
   This change replaces `std::promise<bool>` on Linux with C++20 `std::atomic<int>` wait/notify synchronization (`wait(0)`, release store + `notify_one()`), avoiding any call to `std::call_once` or libstdc++ TLS.

2. **Preserve configured thread stack size and bounds in `SetStackFromHost`**:
   When a thread was created via `scePthreadCreate` with specific stack attributes, the child thread's `RunThread` executed `SetStackFromHost(self)` which unconditionally overwrote `thread->stackSize` with the host thread stack size (typically 8 MB).
   
   `SetStackFromHost` now preserves the configured stack size when non-zero. In addition, because x86-64 stacks grow downwards from `high` to `low`, it sets `thread->stackAddress = reinterpret_cast<void*>(high - thread->stackSize)` (matching the Windows behavior in `StartNativeThread`), ensuring guest thread local variables fall cleanly within the reported stack bounds.

### Tested

- Linux x86-64 (CachyOS, GCC 16, Release).
- Built target `libs`: 0 errors.
- `ctest --test-dir /tmp/anyps5_build -R "guest_" -V`: all 152 guest tests pass 100%.
- Verified over 50+ stress test iterations of `guest_kernel_is_stack`, `guest_thread_self`, and `guest_pthread_attr` without failure.
- `python3 tools/check_conventions.py --base origin/main`: all convention checks passed.

body:
What

A title that paces itself on pending flips can get further ahead of the queue 0 worker than its per-frame memory allows, and the worker then records a frame from memory the title has already rewritten.

Astro Bot (PPSA21564) keeps per-frame data in a ring of three slots, polls sceVideoOutIsFlipPending, and submits the next flip as soon as fewer than three are pending. On hardware a pending flip is a frame whose commands have been read. Here submissions waited 98 to 110 ms in queue 0, so the worker was still recording frame N while the title wrote frame N+3 into the same slot. A block of per-frame constants that holds the title's frame counter read 0x17e in the frame right after one that read 0x17a: the worker recorded frame 0x17b from the slot of frame 0x17e. When the slot was half rewritten the draw bound the wrong block, and the frame came out black, without the movie quad, or with the quad at half size: 8 to 16 of 48 window captures in each of five runs. APS5_FLIP_READ_CHECK=1 counted 141,478 of 158,640 in-place reads as overwritten before execution. The same overrun produced guest snapshot differs from registered memory in compute shader 0x5005e7b00.

A submission on queue 0 that carries a flip now waits until the worker has reached the flip of every earlier one. The wait ends early when queue 0 is blocked on memory that no running, held or pending work writes, the criterion orderReleased uses, since only the title can end that wait. The presenter stays asynchronous: the title still has three flips pending when the display is the limit. APS5_NO_FLIP_HOLD=1 submits as before.

tests/Flip.cpp gains a case: a flip behind a closed rendering wait holds the next flip submission until the wait opens, and a flip behind a WAIT_REG_MEM on a label only the test stores does not hold it.

Not established: what the console returns from sceVideoOutIsFlipPending while its GPU is behind. The change does not depend on it.

Tested

  • Windows 11, RTX 5070 Ti, Astro Bot (PPSA21564, 01.007.000), built from b3fcd6d6 (an older main) with this change. 45 s runs through the intro, 48 window captures each in bursts 70 ms apart:
    Build | Odd captures | Frames presented -- | -- | -- Without the change (five runs) | 8 to 16 | 730 to 795 With the change (two runs) | 0 | 868, 999 With the change and APS5_NO_FLIP_HOLD=1 | 12 | 795
    With the change the snapshot check passes through the whole intro without APS5_NO_SNAPSHOT_CHECK. The title still needs a local workaround for an unrelated failure in the same shader at the first frame (guest memory is not readable at 0x30) and APS5_HOST_IMPORT_MIB=16384.
  • Linux, on 4ddbf049 (this branch's base): agc_driver_flip, agc_driver_pm4 and agc_driver_pm4_failure pass; agc_driver is skipped there because the machine has no Vulkan device. The new case fails with APS5_NO_FLIP_HOLD=1 and passes without it. tools/check_conventions.py --base origin/main passes. The rest of the test suite was not built or run.
  • Not tested: the title on 4ddbf049 itself (the Windows runs used the older base; rebasing needed two textual conflict resolutions next to the new timing fields), any title on Linux, any title other than Astro Bot.

body:
### What

`tools/pr_overlap.py` took every added line with `APS5_VABI` before a name and a parenthesis as an export, so a declaration such as `extern "C" int* APS5_VABI __error_nid_postfix();`, which many source files add to reach the guest errno, made each pull request that adds it "implement the same function" as all the others. The reports of #1641 and #1727 each list five such rows.

The export collection moves into `exports(diff)`, which skips a line that ends in a semicolon. In the tree every declaration the pattern matches ends that way (206 lines), and a definition's first line ends in `{`, `}`, `(` or `,` (3086 lines); no declaration is split over lines, so none is lost.

Overlap: #1325 changes `open_prs` in the same file and adds `tools/tests/test_pr_overlap.py`, #988 changes its `__main__` output; this change is in `scan` and its own test file, so they merge in any order. #1662 and #1623 add an `add_test` at the same place in the root `CMakeLists.txt`; whichever merges second rebases two lines.

### Tested

- `python3 tools/tests/test_pr_overlap_exports.py` and `ctest -R pr_overlap_exports`: three cases over one diff: definitions of a POSIX export, an `sce` export with `noexcept`, a one-line body and a signature with the brace on the next line are exports; two declarations (one with `noexcept` and trailing spaces, kept in a separate string so an editor cannot strip them), a `_nid_no_patch` helper, a removed line and a context line are not. Written before the change; it fails on `main` with `AttributeError: module 'pr_overlap' has no attribute 'exports'` and passes with it.
- `--branch` runs against the 200 newest open pull requests (the tool's current limit, which #1325 lifts), Linux, Python 3.12:
  - `feat/libkernel-socket-read-write` (#1727): `main`'s tool reports 9 rows, 6 of them `__error_nid_postfix` only (#1613, #1616, #1627, #1641, #1675, #1729); this one reports the 3 rows with conflicting lines (#1708, #1711, #1738) and nothing under "Same exports".
  - `feat/libkernel-mlock` (#1673): 1 row, #1633's conflicting line, with both.
- `tools/check_conventions.py --base upstream/main` passes; `progress_report` and `import_audit` still pass.

body:
### What

Refs #1668. **Depends on #1141**. Add cancellation recovery regressions and technical documentation to complement its implementation. This is the cancellation workstream only; #1668 remains open for shader modes, Linux exception delivery, and the cancellation limits recorded below.

The branch includes #1141's original commits through `6d380536ede30d889d1d1cafba5929fb10d464c7`, preserving their author and history so CI exercises the complete stack. It is based on current main `6b56175a4290a03ab28ebc6697beeffe6fe9be8d`. Once #1141 merges, rebase this branch so the remaining review contains only the four complementary files in `a4cd66803cbf41786e1f9973dc09b7f43aa1fac0`. No alternative cancellation implementation is added. The prerequisite merge resolves one TechnicalDebt conflict by retaining main's MIMG behavior and #1141's cancellation entry.

- Pending cancellation before ordinary/timed SCE and POSIX semaphore waits must preserve an available token. Repeated requests must produce one exit. A fresh guest thread must consume that same token successfully and start with enabled/deferred defaults.
- Cancellation must run cleanup in reverse push order, permit cancellation points inside cleanup without a second exit, and run thread-specific destruction afterward, exactly once.
- Cancel an enrolled timed condition waiter while another thread holds its mutex. Cleanup must wait for mutex reacquisition and unlock it. With cancellation disabled, the wait must return after a real signal; enabling deferred cancellation must return before explicit testcancel acts on the pending request. Reuse the same mutex/condition in a fresh successful waiter.
- A pending cancellation at join must preserve the result output sentinel and target ownership. Another join must obtain the target's original result, followed by another successful create/join. Invalid setters must preserve state and output arguments.

Host atomic gates and guest mutex handshakes establish ordering without scheduling sleeps or internal cancellation-field inspection. Checks remain active in Release. Register normal and `APS5_COARSE_TIMED_WAITS=1` executions, each bounded to 20 seconds against 60-second guest waits.

Update existing `ARCHITECTURE.md` with the request/wait/cleanup/join lifecycle and pinned FreeBSD references; update existing `TechnicalDebt.md` with the remaining limits. No tracked investigation notes or new infrastructure.

Overlap audit, 9 October 2026, at main `f8c2f072`: #2067 avoids overflow in large `nanosleep` durations by splitting them into bounded intervals. The conflicting `Time.cpp` change in this branch belongs to the included #1141 prerequisite, which routes sleeps through `CancellableSleep`; the complementary recovery tests/documentation do not add a competing sleep implementation. A combined implementation must use cancellable sleep for each bounded interval and the remainder while retaining existing argument/errno behavior. Run both cancellation recovery and large-duration nanosleep regressions after reconciliation. A virtual merge confirms the text conflict; this audit does not claim that combined code was built or tested. The implementation dependency remains **Depends on: #1141**.

### Tested

Synthetic guest-API programs linked to production libc/libkernel; no console, title, or homebrew measurements. Both local builds use the production library CMake source lists and test registrations through a temporary parent project, building only the relevant runtime targets without graphics dependencies.

| Host/toolchain | Checks | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ubuntu 24.04/WSL2, GCC 13.3.0, C++20, Release, Ninja | Six selected CTest cases, 50 repetitions each, four parallel jobs | 300 executions passed, 9.07 s |
| Windows 11, WinLibs MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0 (`15.2.0posix-14.0.0-ucrt-r7`), C++20, Release, Ninja | Same six cases and repetitions, including normal and coarse waits | 300 executions passed, 14.26 s |

Cases: `guest_pthread_cancel`, `guest_pthread_cancel_recovery`, `guest_pthread_cancel_recovery_coarse`, `guest_pthread_key`, `guest_pthread_sem`, `guest_cond_timedwait`.

Reproduction with the normal repository build:

```sh
cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DBUILD_TESTING=ON
cmake --build build --target guest_pthread_cancel_tests guest_pthread_cancel_recovery_tests guest_pthread_key_tests guest_pthread_sem_tests guest_cond_timedwait_tests --parallel 6
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure -R '^(guest_pthread_cancel.*|guest_pthread_key|guest_pthread_sem|guest_cond_timedwait)$' --repeat until-fail:50 --parallel 4
python tools/check_conventions.py --base origin/main
git diff --check
```

Conventions and whitespace checks pass. Three temporary Linux production mutations were each detected by the new recovery test: removing the pre-acquisition semaphore cancellation check, allowing cancellation to re-enter during cleanup, and discarding a disabled pending request on enable. Original sources were restored byte-for-byte; all six cases then passed another 50 repetitions (300 executions, 8.91 s). Full GitHub CI on combined head `a8875ddc14e23f3eaf3cffdb16f6dfaaf53c5390` passes: [Linux](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/actions/runs/37820511966/job/113460084313) and [Windows](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/actions/runs/37820511966/job/113460084270), including three repetitions of both new recovery cases. Conventions and progress checks pass; the relinker job is intentionally skipped by the path filter. Capability-based skips in the full suites are retained.

The reference contract is FreeBSD stable/11 at immutable `5ed7eb0d97ba4436218e810f61bd059acba984c2`, not measured console behavior. The included prerequisite still accepts asynchronous mode with mostly deferred behavior, does not interrupt sleeps, and omits file/socket cancellation points. Condition signal conservation, cancellation versus exit/detach, and safe non-null invalid/reclaimed handles remain unverified. This PR documents those limits and does not claim the complete #1668 cancellation contract is implemented.

body:
### What

Adds `tcgetattr` and `tcsetattr` to libkernel, in a new `File/src/Terminal.cpp`, on the assumption that a title's descriptors are never terminals: a title runs without a controlling terminal, and what the console gives it as descriptors 0 to 2 is unknown (recorded in TechnicalDebt). The errors are the ones FreeBSD 11's [`termios.c`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/stable/11/lib/libc/gen/termios.c) and `ioctl` path give for a descriptor that is not a terminal:

- A file or pipe descriptor is `ENOTTY`, and `tcgetattr` leaves the `termios` untouched, as `TIOCGETA` copies out only on success. A guest socket gets what its protocol's control routine returns to a termios ioctl, `EADDRNOTAVAIL` for `AF_INET` (`in_control` without an interface) and `EOPNOTSUPP` otherwise (`in6_control`, `pru_control_notsupp`).
- `tcsetattr` gives `EINVAL` for an action other than `TCSANOW`, `TCSADRAIN` or `TCSAFLUSH`, with or without `TCSASOFT`, before anything else; `EFAULT` for a null `termios`, which `sys_ioctl` copies in before it looks at the descriptor. With `TCSASOFT` and a null `termios` FreeBSD's libc faults while copying it, so that case throws.
- A descriptor is invalid (`EBADF`) when it is negative, a closed guest socket, or a host descriptor the host does not know: `fcntl(F_GETFD)` on Linux, `_get_osfhandle` on Windows under the thread-local invalid-parameter handler, as `NativeClose` in `Open.cpp` does.

Of the 34 relinked titles in the homebrew catalog (#1578), 16 import `tcgetattr` and `tcsetattr` and one stops at `tcgetattr` on `main` 4b6ab6bb, PPSA99728 OpenRCT2 Native Port: relinked with `main`'s relinker and run for 8 s in a bubblewrap sandbox on Linux, it dies in the host loader with `app.elf: symbol lookup error: app.elf: undefined symbol: 5kBfZ40bAuk`.

Overlap: #1613 adds `isatty` to libScePosixForWebKit through the host's `isatty`, which can say yes to a host terminal on descriptors 0 to 2 where this says no; the two should agree once either lands. #1645 and #1192 insert source lines next to `Stdio.cpp` in `libkernel/CMakeLists.txt`; this one goes after `NativeStat.cpp`, so none of the three overlap. #1727 and #1091 add declarations to `SocketRuntime.hpp` where this adds `Family`; whichever merges second rebases one line.

### Tested

- Linux (CachyOS, kernel 7.2.9, GCC 16.2.1), full build with `BUILD_TESTING=ON` and `ANYPS5_ENABLE_SPIRV_TOOLS=ON` on this branch (based on `main` 2b297842): `ctest --repeat until-fail:3` 468/468; `tools/check_test_registration.py` and `tools/check_conventions.py --base upstream/main` pass.
- New `guest_terminal` test: `ENOTTY` with an untouched `termios` from `tcgetattr`, and from `tcsetattr` with every valid action, on a file opened through `open`, descriptors 0, 1 and 2 and both ends of a `pipe`; `EADDRNOTAVAIL` on an `AF_INET` socket with the `termios` untouched; `EINVAL` for actions 3, -1 and `TCSASOFT | 3` even on an invalid descriptor; `EFAULT` for a null `termios` even on an invalid descriptor; `EBADF` for -1, a closed socket and a closed file. Written before the implementation; it failed on the two unresolved exports and passes with it.
- The patched `libkernel.prx` exports the NIDs (`5kBfZ40bAuk`, `La7xW-jcZwQ`).
- `tools/import_audit.py` on five of the 16 catalog titles, absent imports on `main` 4b005b22 → this branch: PPSA17641 SymphonyStation5 35 → 33, PPSA97510 PSXS5 72 → 70, PPSA99000 ProsperoStore 40 → 38, PPSA99009 ProsperoLichess 37 → 35, PPSA99039 EVO Player 24 → 22. None of them loads yet; the remaining imports are listed in #1578.
- Windows: the same Build workflow run on this commit in the fork's Actions (merged onto `main` 6b56175a), [run 37822114975](https://github.com/SleglJan/AnyPS5/actions/runs/37822114975): `guest_terminal` passes its three repeats, full suite 474/474. The only host call there is `_get_osfhandle` under the invalid-parameter guard; the UCRT keeps descriptors 0 to 2 open in a child process, so the test's `ENOTTY` checks on them hold.

body:
### What
`COLOR_8_8_8_8` with number type UINT threw `unsupported color format 10 number type 4 component swap 0`. RADV renders into `R8G8B8A8_UINT` images through it. With #1073, ccleste (PPSA59322) writes such a target with a `UINT16_ABGR` export, and it was the last draw ccleste dropped.

This builds on #1073, which accepts that export and validates the `uvec4` output. Its first commit is #1073's and drops out once that merges.

- `COLOR_8_8_8_8` UINT decodes to `VK_FORMAT_R8G8B8A8_UINT` for component swaps 0, 2 and 3, with the same reversed export mappings as the other 8_8_8_8 types.
- The alternate swap (1) still throws. It would need `B8G8R8A8_UINT`, which Vulkan does not require as a color attachment, unlike `R8G8B8A8_UINT`.
- Tests:
  - `agc_driver_graphics` (`uint8x4TargetTests`): the target decodes as `R8G8B8A8_UINT` with `uintExport` set, swaps 2 and 3 decode, and swap 1 throws.
  - New GPU test `agc_driver_uint8x4_color_target` draws a compressed `UINT16_ABGR` export into a linear 256x64 `8_8_8_8_UINT` target. It requires every channel's byte inside the scissor and the untouched bytes outside it. It fails with `unsupported color format 10 number type 4 component swap 0` without this change.

body:
### What
This is the color-target half of #1734, which it builds on. Its first commit is that PR's and drops out once it merges. It has two parts.

**Pipe/bank XOR.** Mesa ORs the pipe/bank XOR into `CB_COLOR_BASE` (`cb_color_base |= tile_swizzle` in `ac_set_mutable_cb_surface_fields`, `src/amd/common/ac_descriptors.c`). `DecodeColorBuffer` passed the unaligned address to `GuestMemory::CheckRange` with the block alignment, which threw `null or misaligned address`. Under RADV on the PS5, ccleste (PPSA59322) dropped its off-screen render passes this way.

- For XOR modes, `DecodeColorBuffer` splits the base into the block-aligned `address`/`surfaceAddress` and `ColorTarget::pipeBankXor`. The new field is placed at the end of the struct, because tests initialize it positionally.
- `ColorTargetLayout` takes the XOR and applies it to the in-block offset, as addrlib does, for the CPU paths in `ColorTargetTransfer`. It rejects an XOR for non-XOR modes, values that are not whole 256-byte units, and values beyond the block.
- The two `SW_64KB_R_X` detile and retile dispatches in `Draw.cpp` pass it to the detiler.
- `SurfaceForTarget` copies it into the resident surface. A texture that samples the target then finds the same image through `SurfaceKey`, and the draw key includes it.

**`SW_4KB_S_X` and `SW_4KB_D_X`.** `DecodeColorTileMode` accepted only linear, `SW_4KB_S`, `SW_64KB_S` and `SW_64KB_R_X`. RADV renders small surfaces in `SW_4KB_D_X`. ccleste's three such draws failed earlier, at the FMASK check (`ATTRIB3` 0x0da58000: `COLOR_SW_MODE` 0x16, `FMASK_SW_MODE` 0x14).

- Both 4 KiB XOR modes decode and become `ColorTileMode::S4KBX`/`D4KBX`, mapping to the texture modes the detiler already handles. Resident targets take the existing storage-image path.
- `ColorTargetLayout` builds their block tables from the same `kTextureSwizzleEquations` entries as `SW_64KB_R_X`. Its 4 KiB alignment is used for `CheckRange`. The XOR split uses the 4 KiB mask.
- The FMASK check also accepts `FMASK_SW_MODE == COLOR_SW_MODE & ~3`. Mesa sets this for every color surface without FMASK (`ac_surface.c`: "CMASK fast clear uses these even if FMASK isn't allocated. FMASK only supports the Z swizzle modes, whose numbers are multiples of 4"). The existing 0 and 0x18 stay accepted; 0x18 is what a logged AGC descriptor uses with `SW_4KB_S`.

**Tests:**
- `agc_driver_graphics` (`ColorTargetLayout`):
  - With XOR 0x5600, `SW_64KB_R_X` offsets equal the unswizzled ones XORed inside each block, across two blocks.
  - Tile and detile round trips are exact.
  - Invalid XORs are rejected.
  - A 2x2 transfer with XOR 0x3200 writes the pixels at 0x3200/0x3210 and reads them back.
  - ccleste's `ATTRIB3`, its `S_X` twin and a `D_X` target without FMASK decode. An FMASK mode that matches neither rule is rejected.
  - For both 4 KiB XOR modes, offsets follow the swizzle equation plus XOR 0xa00, the block geometry is 32x32, round trips are exact, and an XOR of a whole block is rejected.
- `agc_driver_graphics` (`ColorPipeBankXorTests`): `DecodeState` splits `SW_64KB_R_X` bases with XOR 0, 0x5600 and 0xff00, and `SW_4KB_D_X` bases with 0, 0xa00 and 0xf00.

There is no GPU draw test of the XOR'd color paths. The detile shader they use is covered by the GPU test in #1734.

title: feat(agc): render into XOR-swizzled color targets with a pipe/bank XOR, and into SW_4KB_S_X/D_X

body:
### What
On GFX10 the XOR swizzle modes (`SW_4KB_*_X`, `SW_64KB_*_X`, `SW_64KB_*_T`) add a per-surface pipe/bank XOR to the offset inside each block. AMD addrlib, `Gfx10Lib::ComputeSurfaceAddrFromCoordMacroTiled`:

```
pOut->addr = sliceSize * sliceId + mipInfo[pIn->mipId].macroBlockOffset + (blkIdx << blkSizeLog2) + (blkOffset ^ pipeBankXor);
```

Every mip and slice uses the same `pipeBankXor`, masked to the block. Mesa stores it in the low bits of the descriptor base: `desc[0] |= swizzle` in `ac_set_mutable_tex_desc_fields`, and `cb_color_base |= tile_swizzle` in `ac_set_mutable_cb_surface_fields` (`src/amd/common/ac_descriptors.c`). `DecodeTextureResource` threw `combines an XOR swizzle with a pipe/bank XOR base which is not implemented` for those descriptors. Under RADV on the PS5, ccleste (PPSA59322) dropped one such draw every frame: the blit of its rendered image to the display buffer.

- For XOR modes, `DecodeTextureResource` splits the base into the block-aligned `baseAddress` and `pipeBankXor`, which is the address bits below the block size. Nothing that addresses guest memory moves.
  - A base that is only XOR bits (block address 0) still throws `null base address`.
- `DetileWindow::pipeBankXor` reaches `TextureDetile.comp` as a new push constant. The equation family XORs it into the block offset, the same place as addrlib, tail mips included. All eight texture detile and retile dispatches in `Texture.cpp` pass it.
- Windows and covered-byte ranges stay valid, because they are built from whole blocks and the XOR only permutes 256-byte units inside a block.
- `SurfaceKey` folds the XOR into its address word, which is zero there for an aligned base. The view check in `Texture.cpp` compares it too, so two descriptors that differ only in their XOR do not share an image.
- Tests:
  - `agc_driver_graphics` (`GuestTextureResource`):
    - `SW_64KB_R_X`, `SW_4KB_D_X` and `SW_64KB_D_T` bases split into the expected base and XOR.
    - A non-XOR mode keeps its base.
    - An aligned base has no XOR.
    - An XOR-only base throws.
  - `agc_driver_graphics` (`TextureDetiler`): a dispatch without a window pushes 0, and the window's XOR reaches the push constant.
  - New GPU test `agc_driver_image_pipe_bank_xor`:
    - Fills a 160x70 RGBA8 texture (several blocks) with addrlib's equations, XORing the pipe/bank value into each block offset.
    - Samples it through `image_load` with the descriptor base raised by that value.
    - Cases: `SW_4KB_D_X` with XOR 0 and 0xa00, `SW_64KB_S_X` with 0x5600, `SW_64KB_R_X` with 0xf100.
    - With the shader's XOR removed, it fails on the first nonzero case.

Color targets with such a base still throw `null or misaligned address`; #1735 follows on top of this one.

body:
### What
`DecodeTextureResource` rejected any nonzero `BC_SWIZZLE` (T# word 3, bits 27:25). The field only reorders the border color, so the border lands in the right channels after `DST_SEL`. Mesa sets it from the format's channel order on every image descriptor (`ac_border_color_swizzle` in `src/amd/common/ac_formats.c`, used by RADV and radeonsi). So every texture whose format is not stored as XYZW was dropped, for example ccleste's (PPSA59322) under RADV.

Mesa's own comment there gives the rule: "For the pre-defined border color values (white, opaque black, transparent black), the only thing that matters is that the alpha channel winds up in the correct place."

- `BC_SWIZZLE` values 0-5 decode into `GuestTextureResource::bcSwizzle` (enum `SQ_IMG_RSRC_WORD3__BC_SWIZZLE` in `gfx10-rsrc.json`). The reserved values 6 and 7 still throw.
- `RequireBorderSwizzle` runs next to `RequireFilterMinmax`, for each sampled image and its paired samplers.
  - It throws only when the swizzle moves W (`XWYZ`, `WZYX`, `WXYZ`, `YXWZ`) and a paired sampler clamps to an opaque black border.
  - Transparent black and opaque white are the same under any channel order, as is any sampler that never reads its border. Border color tables already throw in `DecodeSamplerResource`.
  - With `XYZW` or `ZYXW` the sampled values are exactly those of the unswizzled case.
- Tests:
  - `agc_driver_graphics` (`GuestTextureResource`): values 0-5 decode and keep their value; 6 and 7 are rejected.
  - `agc_driver_graphics` (`GuestSamplerResource`): `ReadsOpaqueBlackBorder` is true only for clamp-to-border with opaque black. Every swizzle passes with transparent black, opaque white, or no border addressing. The four alpha-moving swizzles throw with opaque black, and `XYZW`/`ZYXW` pass. An unbound sampler element throws.

body:
### What
A draw resolves each stage's program address (`SPI_SHADER_PGM_LO/HI_*`) against the shaders registered through `sceAgcDriverRegisterShader`. An address outside every registration threw `graphics program does not belong to a registered shader`. Dispatches already fall back to reading the code from guest memory, and since #639 an unregistered compute program is prepared at its first dispatch.

RADV on the PS5 ([mihawk-99/PS5_Mesa](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Mesa)) never registers its shaders. It uploads ACO's code to GPU memory and programs the registers directly, as on Linux. Every RADV draw was dropped: ccleste (PPSA59322) presented only black frames.

- **Decode.** `ProgramSnapshot(registry, address)` returns the registration that covers the address, or reads the code from guest memory (`ReadRawComputeShader`, renamed `ReadRawShader`). Dispatches and draw-time decoding use it.
  - Decoding for a registration-time static ABI (`DecodeGraphicsPrograms` with `staticAbi`) still requires registered programs, with the same errors as before.
- **Header-less programs.**
  - The binary-type check is skipped, because the type only says which AGC binary kind a registration holds.
  - On the geometry path such a front program counts as a single-stage program (type 2), so the merged user-data pointer is optional.
  - `Draw` leaves out empty memory regions, so no empty header region reaches `RequestMemoryView`.
  - `DecodeVertexStageInfo` returns no embedded fetch for an empty header. RADV vertex shaders load their own attributes.
- **Preparation (#639).**
  - `InvocationFor` and `SourceHandleFor` prepare an unregistered program at first use for every stage, not only compute, and keep the artifact on its snapshot as the compute fallback does.
  - For a rect-list draw whose programs are unregistered, `Draw` calls `ResolvePreparedGraphics(front, fragment, 17, …)` before `PreparedRectangle`. Registration would otherwise have prepared the rectangle shaders.
- **Draw cache.** The register draw key identifies an unregistered program only by its address, and a key hit reused the entry's decode without reading the program again. A different program uploaded to the same address with the same registers would have run the old compiled shader. A key hit now checks the decode's unregistered programs against guest memory (`DecodeProgramsCurrent`, through the by-value check `ReadRawShader` already does) and drops the entry when one changed. Registered programs are not checked.
- **Behaviour change.** At draw time, an address past a registration's code is now read from memory instead of throwing `graphics program is outside registered shader code`. This matches dispatches.
- **Tests.**
  - `agc_driver` (`testProgramSnapshots`):
    - A registered entry resolves to its registration, also from inside its code.
    - An unregistered address and an empty registry read raw code with an empty header.
    - An unmapped address throws.
  - `agc_driver_graphics` (`HeaderlessVertexStageTests`): a header-less vertex program gets no fetch table, and a truncated non-empty header still throws.
  - New GPU test `agc_driver_prepared_unregistered_graphics`:
    - A vertex and a fragment program in memory, with an empty registry, decode as raw code.
    - `InvocationFor` prepares each stage once and reuses it, also for a relocated push-constant block.
    - `PreparedRectangle` finds the rectangle shaders after `ResolvePreparedGraphics`.
    - It fails with `unregistered program is not a compute shader` when the compute-only restriction is restored.
  - `agc_driver` (`testProgramSnapshots`): a decode stays current while its programs are unchanged and after a registered program is rewritten, becomes stale when its unregistered program is rewritten, and is current again with the new snapshot. It fails without the check.
  - `agc_driver_prepared_graphics` still checks that the static-ABI decode rejects an unregistered program.

### Tested
Windows 11 Pro (26200), MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0 (WinLibs r7), Release, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti.

- The full suite (478 tests) passes on this branch. It was run from the generated `CTestTestfile.cmake` commands because antivirus blocks `ctest.exe` on this machine.
- ccleste renders its title screen on current `main` with this PR. The test branch also carried #1733-#1736, #1073, my other pending changes, and a local port of the `LINE_STIPPLE_TEX`/`POS_FIXED_PT` pixel inputs; RADV's present shader enables the former, and I will open that separately. `RADV_DEBUG=nonggc` was set: RADV's NGG culling shaders are a separate gap.
- With the draw-cache check, on the same local branch with RADV's NGG culling on (#1825), ccleste's register-key hit rate is unchanged (every draw after the first 10 s hits; no entry is dropped). Per-draw validation went from about 6.3 to 7.8 µs.

Not tested on AMD, Intel or Linux.

body:
### What
Implements `syslog` (NID `s-e0hFe21FA`) and `vsyslog` (NID `rzvf5zicF88`) in libc. Two of the homebrew titles in #1578 import `syslog` from libSceLibcInternal, which resolves through libc: ps5-opengl (PPSA99005) and ProsperoRadio (PPSA99001).

- Output: each message is written to `stderr` as `[syslog:<priority>] <message>`, under a lock and flushed, with a newline added when the message has none. This is the same convention `sceKernelDebugOutText` uses (`[debug:<channel>]`).
- Format and priority follow FreeBSD's `vsyslog`:
  - `%m` expands to the guest errno's message (FreeBSD numbering via `strerror_r`), with any `%` in it doubled, and `%%m` stays a literal `%m`.
  - Bits outside `LOG_PRIMASK | LOG_FACMASK` produce `syslog: unknown facility/priority: <hex>` and are then masked off.
  - A missing facility becomes `LOG_USER`.
  - errno is preserved.
- Formatting uses the same paths as `vfprintf`: SysV `va_list` on Linux and `LibcDetail::FormatWindows` on Windows.
- Recorded in TechnicalDebt: messages go to `stderr` instead of the console's system log, and `openlog`, `setlogmask` and `closelog` are not implemented, so identity, options and mask are not applied. Neither title imports them.

### Tested
- New `guest_syslog` test, registered in ctest. It captures `stderr` and checks the exact output for:
  - plain formatting;
  - `%m` with errno 2, a literal `%%m` and `%%`;
  - unknown priority bits (`0x10004`, the warning line followed by the masked message);
  - the default facility;
  - an empty message.
  
  It also checks that errno is unchanged.
- Linux (Ubuntu 24.04.5, GCC 13.3) and Windows 11 (WinLibs GCC 15.2.0 r7): `guest_syslog`, `guest_errors`, `guest_formatting` and `guest_filesystem` pass.
