body:
### What

`read`, `write`, `_read` and `_write` on a guest socket descriptor (0x10000000 and up) went to the host as if the number were a host descriptor, so `sceKernelRead` and `sceKernelWrite` threw (`sceKernelWrite: write failed, fd=…, errno=9`) on the first byte a title moved through a socket that way. On the console both are the socket's `recv` and `send` without flags ([`soo_read`/`soo_write`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/stable/11/sys/kern/sys_socket.c)).

- `GuestSockets::Read` and `GuestSockets::Write` in the socket runtime forward to `recv` and `send` with flags 0, so the socket layer's errno applies: `EAGAIN` (35) on an empty non-blocking socket, `EPIPE` (32) after the peer closed, `EBADF` (9) on a closed descriptor. A zero-length `read` returns 0 without touching the socket, as `dofileread` does, and a read longer than `INT_MAX` is clamped.
- `read`, `write`, `_read` and `_write` route descriptors at or above `GuestSockets::FirstDescriptor` to them; `sceKernelRead` and `sceKernelWrite` do the same, before their null-buffer check, and return the kernel error (`0x80020023` for `EAGAIN`, `0x80020009` for `EBADF`) instead of throwing.
- Recorded in TechnicalDebt: `EPIPE` raises the host's `SIGPIPE` on Linux, which the guest can neither ignore nor suppress, and nothing on Windows (the console raises it unless `SO_NOSIGPIPE`); a `write` above `INT_MAX` bytes is `EMSGSIZE`; `readv`, `writev`, `pread`, `pwrite`, their `sceKernel` forms and AIO on a guest socket still go to the host.

The 15 catalog titles whose OpenSSL QUIC notifier creates a `socketpair` (#1711, open) signal it with `write` and drain it with `read` (`rio_notifier.c` through `writesocket`/`readsocket`); the same applies to any TCP socket a title reads with `read`.

Overlap: #1307 rewrites the four wrappers in `Stdio.cpp` (the socket branch has to stay first); #1711 and #1708 insert a TechnicalDebt line at the same place; #1091 and #1738 add declarations to `SocketRuntime.hpp`, and #1091 code to `Udp.cpp` near the table, where this adds two declarations and two functions at the end. Whichever merges second rebases. The pr-overlap report's `__error_nid_postfix` rows (#1613, #1616, #1627, #1675) are the shared `extern "C"` declaration of the errno accessor that `Open.cpp` now adds, not an export.

### Tested

- Linux (CachyOS, kernel 7.2.9, GCC 16.2.1), full build with `BUILD_TESTING=ON` and `ANYPS5_ENABLE_SPIRV_TOOLS=ON` on this branch (based on `main` b83e849f): `ctest --repeat until-fail:3` 467/467; `tools/check_test_registration.py` and `tools/check_conventions.py --base upstream/main` pass.
- New `guest_socket_read_write` test over a TCP loopback pair: `write`/`read`, `_write`/`_read` and `sceKernelWrite`/`sceKernelRead` carrying data both ways; `EAGAIN` and `0x80020023` on an empty non-blocking socket; zero-length reads returning 0; 0 from both forms after the peer closed; (Linux) `EPIPE` on `write` after the peer closed, with the host's `SIGPIPE` ignored by the test since a title cannot; `EBADF` and `0x80020009` from every entry point on a closed descriptor. Each receive waits with `poll` first, accepting `POLLHUP` after the close. Written before the change: on `main` it aborts with the `sceKernelWrite` throw above; it passes with the change.
- Windows: the same Build workflow run on this commit in the fork's Actions (merged onto `main` 6b56175a), [run 37822108157](https://github.com/SleglJan/AnyPS5/actions/runs/37822108157): `guest_socket_read_write` passes its three repeats, full suite 474/474; the test excludes only the `EPIPE` case there, like `guest_tcp`.

The fork's Build workflow on this head merged into `main`, [run 37932709308](https://github.com/SleglJan/AnyPS5/actions/runs/37932709308): `guest_socket_read_write` and the full suite pass on Linux and Windows; the first Windows attempt failed on `guest_video_out_wqhd_detection` (a `main` test, SEGFAULT) and passed unchanged on rerun.

### What
Implements `sceVideoOutGetResolutionStatus` (NID `6kPnj51T62Y`). Three of the homebrew titles in #1578 import it and stop at start-up without it: ps5-opengl (PPSA99005), EVO-PLAYER-PS5 (PPSA99039) and ProsperoRadio (PPSA99001). It was the most-needed import in that list without a pull request.

```c
int sceVideoOutGetResolutionStatus(int32_t handle, SceVideoOutResolutionStatus* status);
```

- Layout: the 48-byte `VideoOutResolutionStatus` follows the two title declarations, which agree: EVO-PLAYER-PS5 (`projects/common/include/evo_ps5.h`, `fullWidth`, `fullHeight`, `paneWidth`, `paneHeight`, `uint64_t refreshRate`, `float screenSizeInInch`, `uint16_t flags`, reserved) and ps5-opengl (`src/platform/ps5_agc_native_runtime.c`, with `_Static_assert` size 48 and `refresh_rate` at 16). A `static_assert` pins the size and both offsets.
- Values: the full and pane size are the port's `width` and `height`, and `refreshRate` is the refresh rate ID chosen exactly as `sceVideoOutGetOutputStatus` does (3 for 59.94 Hz, 13 in the 119.88 Hz output mode; EVO-PLAYER-PS5 reads 13 as 120 Hz). The pane equals the full size because `sceVideoOutSetWindowModeMargins` applies no margins. `screenSizeInInch` is 0, the value EDID uses for an undefined size, since the host display's size is not read; shadPS4 returns a fixed 50. `flags` and the reserved fields are 0; the whole struct is written.
- Errors: a null `status` or an invalid or closed handle throws, as in the other VideoOut status getters.
- The layout, the screen size and the flags are recorded in TechnicalDebt as not confirmed on a console.

### Tested
- New `guest_video_out_resolution_status` (registered in ctest): status prefilled with `0xff` bytes, then 1920x1080 full and pane, the same `refreshRate` as `sceVideoOutGetOutputStatus`, zero screen size, flags and reserved fields; null status, handles 0, -1, a never-opened handle and a closed handle all throw.
- The built `libSceVideoOut.prx` exports `6kPnj51T62Y`, the NID shadPS4 binds to `sceVideoOutGetResolutionStatus`.
- Linux (Ubuntu 24.04.5, GCC 13.3, RX 7600) and Windows 11 (WinLibs GCC 15.2.0 r7): the VideoOut tests pass (`guest_video_out_wqhd_detection`, `guest_video_out_resolution_status`, `guest_videodec2`).
- No title run: each of the three still has other absent imports listed in #1578.

Overlap: #1496 adds a test to the same place in `libSceVideoOut/CMakeLists.txt` and edits the neighbouring VideoOut lines of TechnicalDebt, so whichever merges second needs a small rebase. It does not change how the refresh rate is reported.

body:
### What

`DMA_DATA` with `DST_SEL` 2 (`V_411_NOWHERE` in Mesa's `src/amd/common/sid.h`) reads its source into L2 and stores nothing. libSceAgc emits it as an L2 prefetch, with the source address repeated as the destination (`c0055000 60200000 8038e000 1d 8038e000 1d 8000caf0`). The validator rejected it with "DMA_DATA register or prefetch destination is not implemented", so a title that prefetches aborts.

A prefetch of a memory source (`SRC_SEL` 0 or 3) is now accepted and writes nothing:
- `ResolveStore` returns it as an empty store, so the packet stays ordered without a drain.
- `DecodeMemoryCopy` still rejects it, so no buffer copy is recorded.
- `Execute` returns before reading the source.

A prefetch of a register, GDS or immediate source still throws ("DMA_DATA prefetch of a register, GDS or immediate source is not implemented"), and so does a register destination (`DAS`).

Source of the semantics: Mesa `src/amd/common/sid.h` (`S_411_DST_SEL`, `V_411_NOWHERE`). Not measured on hardware: a prefetch has no visible memory effect to measure.

### Tested

Windows 11, RTX 3060. `agc_driver_pm4` covers the new path: a prefetch resolves as an empty store, does not decode as a copy, leaves memory unchanged, and the immediate-source and register-destination forms throw. All 183 `agc_driver` tests pass, and `tools/check_conventions.py --base origin/main` passes. PPSA07906 (Unreal Engine 5) issues these packets at startup and aborted on them; with the change it gets past them and renders its intros.

body:
### What
On Linux, shared direct memory is imported through `/dev/udmabuf` (#943) when the driver imports dma-buf memory. Many distributions create the node as `root:kvm` with mode `0660` (#943's checklist notes this, and its test machine had a per-user ACL), so a user outside the `kvm` group cannot open it. The ranges are then copied instead of imported, and GPU stores through FLAT/GLOBAL addresses to them fail. The only trace was the import step and a Vulkan result, which hides `errno`:

```
[gpu] host import of 0x7b76a9e00000+0x2000000 failed at open /dev/udmabuf (-1000072003); falling back to copies
[gpu] deferred write-back failed: BDA access failed: address=0x7b76a9e00000 instruction=0x260 bytes=4 stage=4 reason=2; the store hit 0x7b76a9e00000+0x2000000, read-only in the BDA table: ...
```

DOOM PPSA99666 (homebrew) presents through a compute kernel that stores into a 32 MiB direct memory range, so on such a machine it logs `video: GPU presentation failed, switching to the CPU scaler`.

- `udmabufDevice` prints the open error once, with the fix for `EACCES`:
  ```
  [gpu] open /dev/udmabuf: Permission denied; shared direct memory is copied instead of imported, and GPU stores through FLAT/GLOBAL addresses do not reach it (give the user read-write access to /dev/udmabuf, for example through the kvm group)
  ```
  The device is only opened where `context.dmaBufImport` is set, so nothing is printed on the NVIDIA proprietary driver (#1329).
- `docs/user/USAGE.md` documents the requirement next to the Windows direct memory note, including the 64 MiB `size_limit_mb` above which ranges are copied anyway (#943).

No behaviour change.

### Tested
Linux, Ubuntu 24.04.5, GCC 13.3, RX 7600 (RADV, Mesa 25.2.8), `/dev/udmabuf` `root:kvm 0660`.

| run | `/dev/udmabuf` failures | `BDA access failed` | DOOM presentation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| user without access, `main` | 3, no reason given | 2 | switches to the CPU scaler |
| user without access, this PR | same, after the new line naming `Permission denied` | 2 | switches to the CPU scaler |
| user with access (ACL, then `kvm` group) | 0 | 0 | stays on AGC compute presentation |

- DOOM v1.1.1 built from source, relinked with `--exclude-sce-module libc.prx` on `main`, run under Xvfb. The run without access used a private mount namespace in which `/dev/udmabuf` was a root-only file, with the process running as the normal user.
- `ctest -R "agc|guest_agc"` with `ANYPS5_REQUIRE_VULKAN=1`: 227/227 with access; the new line does not appear.
- Windows: not built; the change is inside the existing `#ifndef _WIN32` block.

body:
### What

A `GuestWriteWatch` backend for macOS hosts, as discussed in #1.

macOS has no counterpart to `userfaultfd` write-protect or `MEM_WRITE_WATCH`, so there is no backend today and the driver re-reads every guest buffer on each use. The backend write-protects watched pages: the first write to a page faults, a SIGBUS/SIGSEGV handler records the page and restores its protection, and `Collect` reports the recorded pages and protects them again. A page is protected before its record is cleared, under the lock the handler takes, so a write that lands in between is recorded.

Because the protection is real, three entry points are added (no-ops on Linux and Windows):

- `GuestWriteWatchBeginHostWrite` / `EndHostWrite` lift the protection around a system call that writes guest memory, which would otherwise fail with `EFAULT`. `GuestArena::HostWrite` calls them, next to the Windows equivalent, so the existing file-read sites are covered.
- `GuestWriteWatchProtectionChanged` tells the watch the protection given to watched pages by `mprotect` or by a new mapping.
- `GuestWriteWatchProtection` reports that protection, since a watched page is read-only between a collection and the next write.

Nothing in `main` calls the last two yet, because the macOS memory paths are not in the tree. They are meant for the `mprotect`/`mmap`/`munmap` sites in libkernel's DirectMemory and for the `mach_vm_region` branch of `GuestMemory` in the macOS port. This and the other limits are recorded in TechnicalDebt.

Two details that came from running titles rather than from design:

- `Register` keeps the recorded protection of a page it already watches. Read from the kernel it would be the watch's own read-only protection, and the page would never be watched again. The driver registers buffers repeatedly, so this showed quickly as stale vertex data.
- The lock hands out turns in order. With a test-and-set lock, a thread collecting in a loop kept winning it and writers waiting in the handler starved: the four-thread test took 119 s under Rosetta, and takes 1.4 s with turns.

### Tested

- macOS 27.0.1, Apple M3 Pro, AppleClang 17. The new tests (`collect`, `register`, `host`, `protection`, `threads`) pass natively (arm64) and as x86-64 through Rosetta, three repetitions each. They build without submodules or the prx libraries; `docs/dev/BUILD.md` has the commands, and a `write-watch` job runs them on `macos-15-intel` and `macos-15`.
- One tracked write costs about 19 µs under Rosetta and 4 µs natively on this machine, close to a bare `mprotect` plus signal (21 µs and 3 µs).
- The same code runs two commercial titles on my macOS branch (a loader-based port, not this tree) at a 16.6 ms median flip interval; without a write watch the first of them ran at roughly 20 FPS.
- Linux and Windows: not built here beyond a MinGW syntax check of the two changed files. The Linux and Windows backends are untouched; the new functions are no-ops there.
- `tools/check_conventions.py --base origin/main` passes.

body:
### What

ScreenTester5 (PPSA69420, [Marice/ScreenTester5](https://github.com/Marice/ScreenTester5) 01.000.000) stops at start-up on `main` with, as reported in #1578:

```
FAIL: unresolved ELF import MhC53TKmjVA from libkernel.prx
```

`MhC53TKmjVA` is `sysctlbyname` (`tools/nid_names.py`). The title also imports `sysctl` (`DFmMT80xcNI`). In the #1578 audit, `sysctl` is absent for 27 of the 34 catalog titles and `sysctlbyname` for 14. The only `hw.`/`kern.`/`vm.` sysctl name string in PPSA69420's `eboot.bin` is `hw.ncpu`, which SDL2's `SDL_GetCPUCount` reads with `sysctlbyname`.

`System/src/SystemConfiguration.cpp` now exports both functions, but only for `hw.ncpu` (`CTL_HW`.`HW_NCPU`, MIB `{6, 3}`). It reports the same count as `sysconf(_SC_NPROCESSORS_ONLN)`. Every other name or MIB throws with the name or MIB in the message, so the next one a title needs shows up in its log. The rest follows FreeBSD's `kern_sysctl.c`:

- A name length below 2 or above `CTL_MAXNAME` (24) gives `EINVAL`. A null name gives `EFAULT`.
- A null `oldp` stores the required size in `*oldlenp`.
- A short buffer gets a partial copy, and `*oldlenp` is set to the bytes copied, with `ENOMEM`.
- `hw.ncpu` is read-only, so a non-null `newp` gives `EPERM`.
- `errno` is left alone on success.

Per review on #1405, nothing beyond what this title reaches is included. Other `hw.*`/`kern.*` nodes, such as `hw.physmem`, wait until a title stops on them.

### Log

From #1578 (Windows, `main` 1081602d, `relinker --windows`): `FAIL: unresolved ELF import MhC53TKmjVA from libkernel.prx` for PPSA69420.

@LeandroLP23 ran the title with this PR (Windows 11, Radeon 860M, MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0, Release, `main` 4b6ab6bb, title relinked with `relinker --windows`). On `main` it stops at `MhC53TKmjVA` (`sysctlbyname`). With this PR it gets past it and stops at the next import:

```
FAIL: unresolved ELF import KiJEPEWRyUY from libkernel.prx
```

`KiJEPEWRyUY` is `sigaction`, which touches the signal masks #1431 is reworking, so it is left out of this PR.

### Tested

aarch64 Debian 13 host. The full project cannot be built here because it needs x86-64.

- `core/libs/tests/GuestSystemConfiguration.cpp` gains `CheckProcessorCountSysctl`. It covers the size query, the read through both entry points, the partial copy with `ENOMEM`, `EPERM`, `EINVAL`, `EFAULT`, an unchanged `errno` on success, and the throw for an unknown name and an unknown MIB. Linked with `SystemConfiguration.cpp`, it passes natively against glibc.
- Without the change the test does not link (`sysctl_nid_postfix` and `sysctlbyname_nid_postfix` are undefined). Three mutants of the new code each make it abort: no `ENOMEM` on a short buffer, no `EPERM` on `newp`, and a wrong size query.
- `SystemConfiguration.cpp` and the test compile for x86_64-linux-gnu and x86_64-windows-gnu with `-Wall -Wextra` (Zig 0.17 clang) without warnings.
- `python3 tools/check_conventions.py --base origin/main` passes.
- Run with PPSA69420 by @LeandroLP23 (see Log). I haven't run it myself.

body:
### What

Fix resident stencil storage materialization in AnyPS5's native user-space graphics implementation. A matching R8_UINT descriptor at a resident D32S8 stencil-plane address currently throws before dispatch. It now binds a storage image seeded from the resident stencil aspect and copies actual shader writes back to that aspect. Attachment uses refresh the storage content; unchanged lookups reuse it. Depth is preserved and the recorder retains images and scratch buffers through queued transfers.

Related to #1409 and README Status's libSceAgcDriver rendering capability. Private runtime retests of this exact head on two fresh processes pass the reproduced stencil/array materialization blocker and stop at a later unsupported depth-plane storage path. This is measured execution progress; the viewport remains black at FPS 0, with no rendered scene or gameplay controls verified.

The supported path is one matching level and layer of R8_UINT through a 2D or 2D-array view, SW_64KB_Z_X, over D32S8 with DB_STENCIL_INFO.TILE_STENCIL_DISABLE set. Other depth/stencil formats, HTILE stencil, descriptor metadata, extent reinterpretation, mips, multiple layers, nonzero slices and other tiling modes throw. Unsupported depth-plane and descriptor refusals identify the resident target and descriptor fields. Raw CPU accesses to resident depth/stencil memory remain outside this backend's synchronization model. Console layout/compression behavior remains unverified.

Vulkan's [depth/stencil aspect copy table](https://docs.vulkan.org/spec/latest/chapters/copies.html#copies-buffers-images) defines the D32S8 stencil buffer plane as S8_UINT. The implementation transports those bytes through a device buffer between the stencil aspect and the R8 storage image; it does not reinterpret the combined depth/stencil image as a color storage image. The single-layer array path uses the correct array view type, permitted by the [Vulkan image/view compatibility table](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkImageViewCreateInfo.html). No shader instruction semantics change.

Adjacent and competing work is acknowledged: #425 implements depth storage and mentions a stencil follow-up; #454 carries depth/coherence work and its discussion reports Celegans12's local stencil patch and a planned stacked PR. This independent, narrow implementation adds an executable synthetic coherence regression on main. It has no unmerged dependency. If complementary depth retirement, clear or sampled-array work lands first, combine the resource lifetime/coherence changes and rerun this regression and complete validation. The final complete scan (2026-10-08 16:08 UTC, 345 open PRs / 50 issues) reviewed all 164 shared-file results: 104 distinct results with no captured conflict in candidate paths and 60 captured branches with textual conflicts. Current main `4b005b229e24be9ec3f185def9e59cbc03aa9e4a` merges cleanly with this validated head. Its independent color/DCC, import-watch, recompiler and build advances were compared to the pinned base; no change to this defect, regression or dependency requires a rebase. Other open branches are not claimed to be mergeable together.

### Tested

Pinned base: 07c2405c356b96bc46edef72cbb6d4786aa109c2. Head: c46ecda78121a05a02ae7748d27b5029eace4f80. The identical base fixture reaches the real attachment positive control, then fails with the existing unsupported storage access at the resident stencil address. Windows 11 / MinGW GCC 15.2.0 / NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080 (driver 616.92): the updated focused regression passed, all-target Full build and libs passed, 451/451 tests passed with no skips. body:
### Summary

Fixes #1667.

sceSaveDataSetupSaveDataMemory2 previously ignored the boolean return of write_file_replace when writing initial SaveDataParam metadata (init_param). If the parameter replacement failed, it proceeded to return SAVE_DATA_OK.

Because the blob file had already been created or grown, a subsequent setup call with the same size skipped initialization (!have || existed < memory_size evaluated to false), leaving the slot permanently without its requested metadata.

### Solution

1. Checked write_file_replace when writing param. On failure:
   - For fresh slots (!have): removes the newly created blob so retrying setup with the same size re-runs initialization cleanly.
   - For slot growth (have): restores the previous blob contents and size.
   - Returns SAVE_DATA_ERROR_INTERNAL (0x809F000B) without populating the result struct.
2. Extended core/libs/tests/SaveDataMemoryMetadata.cpp with regressions covering fresh-slot metadata failure/retry and growth failure/retry.

### Verification

- All savedata suites (savedata_memory_metadata, savedata_memory_growth, savedata_core_write_replacement, savedata_native_write_replacement, savedata_replace_file_failure) pass 100% locally under ctest in Release (MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2).
- 	ools/check_conventions.py passes with zero violations.

body:
### What
`pthread_getcpuclockid` in libkernel, and `clock_gettime`/`clock_getres` for the clock it returns.

- As in FreeBSD (`thr_getcpuclockid.c`, `kern_clock_getcpuclockid2`), the clock is `CPUCLOCK_BIT | tid`. Guest threads had no thread id, so every `PthreadPrivate` gets one from a registry when it is constructed (created and adopted threads) and leaves it in its destructor.
- `clock_gettime` on that clock returns the thread's CPU time: on Linux from the host thread's CPU clock, taken on the thread when it starts or is adopted; on Windows from `GetThreadTimes` on its handle. A thread that has finished or does not exist returns -1 with `EINVAL`, like `tdfind` failing in `kern_clock_gettime`.
- `clock_getres` on it returns the resolution of `CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID`. Process CPU clocks (`CPUCLOCK_PROCESS_BIT`) throw.
- `pthread_getcpuclockid` returns `EINVAL` for a null thread and `EFAULT` for a null output.

Caller: PPSA99005 ([blackbearreloaded/ps5-opengl](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-opengl) v1.0.1) imports `pthread_getcpuclockid` (#1578; 19 of the 34 catalog titles in the audit there). In its SDK (ps5-opengl-sdk 1.0.1) the only reference is Mesa's `libmesa_util.a` `u_thread.c.o`: `util_thread_get_time_nano` (`src/util/u_thread.c`) calls `pthread_getcpuclockid` and then `clock_gettime` on the result, for the calling thread and for queue threads, so the clock has to work in `clock_gettime` too.

### Log
PPSA99005 ([blackbearreloaded/ps5-opengl](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-opengl) showcase v1.0.1), relinked on Linux (Ubuntu, GCC 15.2.0, `main` f1451396, bundled `libc.prx` kept) and run in a `bwrap` sandbox. On `main` it stops on `mkstemp`, as in #1578:

```
./app.elf: symbol lookup error: ./app.elf: undefined symbol: uEtgPWgPxOk
```

With the open PRs for its earlier absent imports merged locally (#1978, #1869, #1656, #1729, #1613, #1714, #1482, #1650, #1872, #1641, #1685, #1859; no conflicts), the stops are:

| Merged on top | Stop |
|---|---|
| the 12 PRs above | `Wh7HbV7JFqc` (`getrlimit`, #1675) |
| + #1675 | `JZKw5+Wrnaw` (`pthread_sigmask`, no PR yet) |
| + #1675, a local throwaway `pthread_sigmask` export | `nnoxZUHK+SA` (`pthread_getcpuclockid`, #1676) |
| + #1675, #1676, the throwaway export, #1529 | no absent import; Mesa starts its threads and the title then aborts in the AGC driver (#2026) |

Each stop is the loader's line, e.g. `./app.elf: symbol lookup error: ./app.elf: undefined symbol: Wh7HbV7JFqc`. The throwaway `pthread_sigmask` only exports the NID and throws when called; it was not called before the abort.

### Tested
<!-- OS, title or homebrew, what was checked. "Not tested" is a valid answer. -->
Ubuntu, Linux 7.0, GCC 15.2.0, full build with `BUILD_TESTING=ON`. New test `guest_thread_cpu_clock`: own clock tracks `CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID`, another thread's clock reads that thread and does not advance while the caller burns CPU, `EINVAL` after join, resolution, null arguments. Full `ctest --repeat until-fail:3`: 465/465 (together with #1675). Patched `libkernel.prx` exports `nnoxZUHK+SA`.

`getrlimit` in libkernel for `RLIMIT_DATA` (2), the only resource the importing titles read.

body:
### What

Adds the POSIX `mlock` export to libkernel as a wrapper over the existing `sceKernelMlock` (#359), beside `munmap` and `mprotect` in `DirectMemory/PosixMemory.cpp`: 0 on success, otherwise -1 with the guest errno taken from the kernel error code the sce form returns (`EINVAL` for a range that wraps around zero, `ENOMEM` for an unmapped or reserved-only range, `EPERM` and `EAGAIN` when the host refuses the lock), as FreeBSD 11's [`mlock(2)`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/stable/11/lib/libc/sys/mlock.2) lists them. The signature is FreeBSD's, `int mlock(const void *addr, size_t len)`; page rounding and a zero length at a page-aligned address returning 0 come from `sceKernelMlock`. An unexpected host error still throws there.

Second commit, asked for below: `munlock` (`OG4RsDwLguo`) and `sceKernelMunlock` (`xQIIfJ860sk`, listed in aerolib), the same pair for unlocking. The host unlock is `munlock` on Linux and `VirtualUnlock` per committed region on Windows, where pages that are not locked count as unlocked. Results follow FreeBSD 11's `sys_munlock` and `vm_map_unwire` ([`vm_mmap.c`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/stable/11/sys/vm/vm_mmap.c), [`vm_map.c`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/stable/11/sys/vm/vm_map.c)): 0 for a mapped range whether or not it is locked, a reserved-only range included, `EINVAL` for a range that wraps around zero, `ENOMEM` for an unmapped range; an unexpected host error throws. `sceKernelMlock` shares the page rounding with it.

Overlap: #1633 (`madvise`) and #1857 (`msync`) add functions at the same place in `PosixMemory.cpp`; adjacent additions, whichever merges second needs a one-line rebase.

In the Linux audit of the homebrew catalog (#1578), `mlock` was absent for 14 of the 34 relinked titles. A bundled `libChakraCore.prx` imports both `mlock` and `munlock` (@EdouardSence below).

### Tested

- Linux (CachyOS, kernel 7.2.9, GCC 16.2.1), full build with `BUILD_TESTING=ON` and `ANYPS5_ENABLE_SPIRV_TOOLS=ON` on this branch rebased onto `main` d70b8998: `guest_mlock` and `guest_memory` pass `--repeat until-fail:3`; `tools/check_test_registration.py` and `tools/check_conventions.py --base upstream/main` pass.
- `guest_mlock`: the `sceKernelMlock` cases of `guest_memory` through the POSIX form (without the Windows working-set check): zero length at an aligned address with errno untouched, an unaligned start inside a flexible mapping (on Linux `VmLck` grows by the rounded length), locking twice; -1 with errno 22 for a range wrapping around zero, errno 12 for a reserved-only range and for the mapping after `sceKernelMunmap`. Written before the implementation; it failed on the unresolved export and passes with it.
- `munlock` cases in the same test, written first and failing on the unresolved export: zero length with errno untouched; an unaligned start whose rounded range unlocks the whole mapping (`VmLck` back to its starting value on Linux); unlocking an already unlocked range returns 0 with errno untouched; lock one page, unlock it (`VmLck` up by one page, then back); -1 with errno 22 for a range wrapping around zero; 0 for a reserved-only range; -1 with errno 12 for the mapping after `sceKernelMunmap`.

body:
### What

Work around an Intel iGPU driver bug in `EmitMulHigh` (the only emitter of `OpSMulExtended`), reported in #1246 by @krishnaraya4.

The Raptor Lake driver returns a wrong high word for `OpSMulExtended` when one operand is the constant `-1`, `-2` or `-32768`. Integer multiplies are exact in Vulkan, so this is a driver bug. The signed path now computes the signed high word from the unsigned product (Hacker's Delight 8-3):

```
hi = umulhi(a, b) - (a < 0 ? b : 0) - (b < 0 ? a : 0)
```

This is exact for all inputs and does not use `OpSMulExtended`. The unsigned path is unchanged. The signed path replaces one `OpSMulExtended` with an `OpUMulExtended` plus a few extra ALU ops (two signed compares, two selects, an add and a subtract) on every device.

The two compares use u32 operands with `OpSLessThan` (signedness is in the opcode, not the type), matching the existing `EmitIAbs32` pattern, so both comparison operands share a single integer type.

Fixes #1246

### Tested

Measured by @johnmaia on the hardware this targets (quoted verbatim from the PR comment). Windows 11, WinLibs GCC 15.2.0 r7, Release, `BUILD_TESTING=ON`, full `ctest` with `ANYPS5_REQUIRE_VULKAN=1`, base `main` `6cc0503d` + #2093 (main alone does not build its tests right now):

| | RTX 4080 | Intel UHD 770 (Raptor Lake-S) |
|---|---|---|
| base | 494/494 | 489/494, incl. `agc_driver_vop3_mad_i64`: `lane 6 i64 neg1 hi is 0x00008000, expected 0x00000000` |
| base + this PR | 494/494 | 490/494, `agc_driver_vop3_mad_i64` passes |

That is the #1246 failure. The four other UHD 770 failures are the same with and without this PR and are unrelated (filed as #2114). The author did not run these; the figures above are third-party measurements.

body:
### What

`LibcExit_nid_no_patch` called `std::exit` after the shutdown callbacks. `std::exit` runs the static destructors of the host libraries (singletons that hold a `std::mutex`) before the guest exit handlers, because the guest handlers are run by an `atexit` runner that is registered at the first guest `__cxa_atexit`. A guest handler that freed memory then locked a destroyed `std::mutex`. On macOS `std::mutex::lock` then throws `std::system_error` ("Invalid argument"), and the `noexcept` destructor of the guest ended in `std::terminate`: `terminate called without an active exception`, exit code 134, on a window close and on SIGTERM.

`LibcExit_nid_no_patch` now calls `CxaFinalize_nid_no_patch(nullptr)` before `std::exit`. The guest handlers run first, while the library objects are alive. `CxaFinalize` removes each entry as it runs it, so the later `atexit` runner finds the list empty and nothing runs twice. A guest handler that calls `exit` again behaves as before (`LibcExit` already guards that).

### Tested

- New test `guest_exit_order` (UNIX only): a forked child registers a guest handler with `__cxa_atexit`, then a host `std::atexit` handler, then calls `LibcExit`; the parent reads the order through a pipe. It fails without the change (host handler first) and passes with it, 3 of 3 runs.
- macOS 27 (Apple M2), x86-64 under Rosetta: one retail title. Before, a window close and SIGTERM ended with exit code 134. After, both end with exit code 0. I ran the test and the title on a macOS port tree whose libc builds; `main` does not build libc on macOS yet.
- Not tested: Linux and Windows (CI). The test is UNIX only, so Windows has no coverage. The change is in shared code and moves the guest handlers from inside `std::exit` to just before it; I did not check other titles or platforms.

body:
### What

`malloc_usable_size` is imported from libSceLibcInternal by PPSA99005 and PPSA99001 (the ps5-opengl and ProsperoRadio homebrew in #1578) and wasn't exported. It returns the number of bytes a block can hold, which is at least what was requested. A null pointer gives 0, as on FreeBSD.

With the default heap it comes from the block header every allocation already carries: the space from the user pointer to the end of the raw block. That covers the extra room of the 16 byte header rounding and the padding added for aligned allocations, and the whole range is writable. A pointer the heap didn't hand out still fails the allocation lookup and throws, the same way `free` does.

When a title installs its own allocator, the call goes to its `malloc_usable_size` entry. The replacement table already carries it (slot 9 after malloc, free, calloc, realloc, memalign, reallocalign, posix_memalign, malloc_stats and malloc_stats_fast, in the order of `MallocReplace` in `SceTypes.hpp`). If a title leaves that entry empty the call throws like the other unregistered allocator entries, since there's no way to know the size without it.

The progress tool counts two functions here because it also counts the `defaultUsableSize` callback, like it counts the other `default*` callbacks in that file. The export itself is one.

PR #1611 also appends to the end of `ApplicationHeap.cpp` and its test, so those two will conflict as text. They add different functions, and whichever merges second needs a small rebase.

### Tested

Ubuntu 26.04, GCC 15.2. `application_heap_tests` covers the title allocator path (the callback is called with the right pointer, null never reaches it), a table without the entry (throws, null still returns 0), and the default heap for 1, 37, 4096 and 100000 bytes plus aligned blocks: the result covers the request and every reported byte can be written. A stack address is rejected. The whole non-GPU suite passes (239 tests). Not run on Windows locally, so the Windows job is the first run there.

### What

One of the host waits #1471 lists as still affected: `VideoOutDriver::presentLoop` waits on `flipQueue->changed` (a `std::condition_variable`) with a 10 ms timeout while no flip is queued, and pumps SDL events and the pad after each wake. On Windows that wait goes through winpthreads, which ends timed waits on `GetTickCount64` steps, so the poll ended 11 to 24 ms later instead of 10 ms. `WaitForFlipRoom` waits on the same condition with a 60 s bound and has the same granularity.

A plain high-resolution sleep is not a replacement here: a flip submitted while the present thread waits must wake it at once. libkernel already has the notify-capable precise wait the guest side uses, `TimedWait::Condition` (event plus high-resolution waitable timer per waiting thread, `std::condition_variable_any` under `APS5_COARSE_TIMED_WAITS`), and libSceVideoOut already links libkernel. The change makes `FlipQueue::changed` a `TimedWait::Condition`, turns the two timed waits into `WaitUntil` with the same bounds and predicates, and the eight `notify_all` into `NotifyAll`. On Linux `TimedWait::Condition` is the `condition_variable_any` path, so nothing changes there. This is the first use of `TimedWait::Condition` outside libkernel.

### Tested

Windows 11 (10.0.26200), WinLibs GCC 15.2.0 (`15.2.0posix-14.0.0-ucrt-r7`), Release, `BUILD_TESTING=ON`.

- Standalone measurement against the built `libkernel.prx`, tick raised to 0.5 ms as `Time.cpp` does, 60 iterations each:

body:
### What

MoltenVK reports `VK_KHR_fragment_shader_barycentric`, but its SPIR-V to MSL step rejects the `PerVertexKHR` decoration that the barycentric path of the translator uses ("SPIR-V to MSL conversion error: PerVertexKHR decoration is not supported in MSL"). Every pixel shader on that path then fails with `VK_ERROR_INITIALIZATION_FAILED` ("Fragment shader function could not be compiled into pipeline"), and the draw is skipped.

The feature is now treated as unavailable when the driver is MoltenVK (`VK_KHR_driver_properties`, `VK_DRIVER_ID_MOLTENVK`), so the existing no-barycentric path is used. The rule is `FragmentShaderBarycentricUsable`, a small header like `SubgroupClock`, so it has a unit test that needs no GPU.

Related: #1547 improves the no-barycentric path that MoltenVK now uses. On `main` today that path does not write the I/J VGPRs, so a shader that reads them for anything other than a plain `v_interp_p1/p2` pair gets 0. Both PRs change `VulkanDevice.cpp` near the same lines; whichever lands second needs a small rebase.

body:
### What

`Dispatch` in `System/src/Signals.cpp` tested the blocked mask with `1u << guest`, bit n. `sigprocmask` keeps the first word of the title's set as it is, and FreeBSD keeps signal n at bit n − 1 ([`_SIG_BIT`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/stable/11/sys/sys/_sigset.h)), which is what FreeBSD's `sigaddset` (and #1641's) produces. So a title that blocked SIGTERM (bit 14) was not protected, and a set with bit 15 blocked SIGTERM instead of SIGURG.

`Dispatch` now tests `1u << (guest - 1)`. The stored mask and the set `sigprocmask` returns are unchanged, so they keep the title's layout. Nothing else interprets the mask's bits; `sigprocmask` only combines and returns it.

Found while adding the sigset functions in #1641: with them a title can build such a set without importing anything else, so the mismatch stops being latent. The two are independent changes; #1641 lists this one under Depends on so they land in order.

### Tested

- Linux (CachyOS, kernel 7.2.9, GCC 16.2.1), full build with `BUILD_TESTING=ON` and `ANYPS5_ENABLE_SPIRV_TOOLS=ON` on this branch (based on `main` 4b005b22): `ctest --repeat until-fail:3` 466/466; `tools/check_conventions.py --base upstream/main` passes.
- `guest_signals` gains two cases: block `{1u << 14}` with `SIG_BLOCK`, `raise(15)` is not delivered, `SIG_UNBLOCK`, `raise(15)` is delivered; and block `{1u << 15}`, `raise(15)` is still delivered. The first was written before the change: on `main` it aborts (the raise is delivered through the block); it passes with the change. The existing round-trip assertions are untouched.
- Windows: run by @hikazey on Windows 11 with the CI toolchain (comment below): `guest_signals` 5/5 with this change, 5/5 failures with `main`'s `Signals.cpp` and the new cases, full suite 457/457. Pending delivery of a blocked signal after unblocking is not implemented here or on `main`; this only corrects which bit is tested.
- Also the same Build workflow run on this commit in the fork's Actions (merged onto `main` 6b56175a), [run 37822080210](https://github.com/SleglJan/AnyPS5/actions/runs/37822080210): `guest_signals` passes its three repeats on Windows, full suite 473/473. body:
Recognize read-direction ALU forms (`add`, `or`, `adc`, `sbb`, `and`, `sub`, `xor`, `cmp`) reading from `fs:[mem]` where `mem` has a base or index register (such as `64 48 33 03`, `xor rax, fs:[rbx]`, reported on NHL 27 in #217).

Following the approach from #767 (for disp32 ALU) and #1233 (for register-addressed MOV loads):
- Recognizes ALU read opcodes combined with register-based memory operands.
- Generates a Windows TLS stub that computes the offset via `lea`, loads the thread pointer, performs the ALU operation against `[thread_pointer + offset]`, and restores scratch registers without disturbing arithmetic flags.
- Handles destination registers `rax`, `rcx`, and general/extended registers (`rbx`..`r15`), for both 64-bit and 32-bit forms.
- Re-relocates sequential instructions when the TLS instruction is shorter than the 5-byte jump.

## Testing

- Extended `core/relinker/relinker/tests/test_tls_function_coverage.py` with:
  - Execution cases for `xor rax, fs:[rbx]`, `xor rcx, fs:[rax]`, `xor rbx, fs:[rax]`, `add rax, fs:[rbx]`, `cmp rax, fs:[rbx]`, `xor r13, fs:[rbx + rcx - 0x10]` (SIB + disp8), and 32-bit `xor edx, fs:[rbx]`.
  - Self-checking verification of computed results, register preservation across all 16 registers, and flag states (ZF, CF).
  - Stub disassembly/byte sequence matching.
  - Short-instruction relocation error verification (`short-alu-before-return`).
  - Removed `register-address-alu` from the rejected list.
- All 4 TLS tests (`empty_tls`, `tls_function_coverage`, `tls_diagnostics`, `guest_tls`) pass 100% under ctest.
- `check_conventions.py` passes with zero violations.

body:
### What
Each direct memory backing keeps a memfd open, so a title such as Dreaming Sarah (PPSA02929) holds about 1100 descriptors at startup and about 1180 once in game. With the systemd default soft `RLIMIT_NOFILE` of 1024, later opens fail with `EMFILE`: `memfd_create` throws "create direct memory backing: Too many open files", or the title's `fopen` returns NULL and it faults in `fread`.

libkernel now raises the soft limit to the hard limit when it is loaded, before the title creates any descriptor, and throws if the limit cannot be read or raised. If the hard limit itself is 1024 the title still runs out of descriptors, as before. Nothing in `core` uses POSIX `select()`, so descriptors above 1023 are safe.

Environments that already raise the soft limit (some IDE terminals, CI runners) do not show it; it reproduces from a default desktop terminal or with `ulimit -Sn 1024`.

### Tested
Arch Linux (kernel 7.2, RTX 4070 Ti SUPER), Dreaming Sarah (PPSA02929), soft limit 1024 unless stated:
- `main` (4b005b22): crashes at startup on 3/3 runs; the process reaches exactly 1024 open descriptors before it dies

### What

Adds the five POSIX signal-set functions to libkernel: `sigemptyset`, `sigfillset`, `sigaddset`, `sigdelset` and `sigismember`, with the semantics of FreeBSD 11's [`lib/libc/gen/sigsetops.c`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/stable/11/lib/libc/gen/sigsetops.c) and [`sys/sys/_sigset.h`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/stable/11/sys/sys/_sigset.h):

- The set is four 32-bit words, the same `GuestSignalSet` layout as `Signals.cpp` (defined again in the new file, with a `static_assert` on its size); signal n lives in word (n − 1) >> 5 at bit (n − 1) & 31.
- Valid signals are 1 to 128 (`_SIG_MAXSIG`). `sigaddset`, `sigdelset` and `sigismember` return -1 with errno 22 for any other value and leave the set untouched; `sigismember` returns 1 or 0.
- `sigfillset` writes all ones to every word, as FreeBSD does; `sigemptyset` writes zeros. Neither fails.
- A null set throws (`std::invalid_argument`); the console would fault.

shadPS4 implements the same five the same way (`src/core/libraries/kernel/threads/exception.cpp`).

The functions go in a new `System/src/SignalSets.cpp` rather than `Signals.cpp`. `Dispatch` in `Signals.cpp` on `main` tests the blocked mask at bit n, so a set built with these functions would block the wrong signal; #1652 corrects that to bit n − 1 and this PR lists it under Depends on. #1431 described moving the mask to a per-thread bit n − 1 layout, but its current head does not touch `Signals.cpp`. The only file shared with #1431 is `libkernel/CMakeLists.txt`.

Overlap: the pr-overlap report lists #1482, #1613, #1616 and #1627 for `__error_nid_postfix`. That is the shared `extern "C"` declaration of the errno accessor each of them adds to reach the guest errno, not an export; none of them touches the same files or lines.

In the Linux audit of the homebrew catalog (#1578), `sigemptyset`, `sigfillset` and `sigdelset` were each absent for 19 to 20 of the 34 relinked titles, `sigaddset` for 10.

### Tested

- Linux (CachyOS, kernel 7.2.9, GCC 16.2.1), full build with `BUILD_TESTING=ON` and `ANYPS5_ENABLE_SPIRV_TOOLS=ON` on `main` 4b005b22: `ctest --repeat until-fail:3` 467/467; `tools/check_test_registration.py` and `tools/check_conventions.py --base upstream/main` pass.
- New `guest_signal_sets` test: empty; fill, then membership of all 128 signals; add at the word boundaries 1, 32, 33, 65, 96 and 128 and delete at 1, 32, 33, 96 and 128, with every other word checked; idempotent add; delete of an absent signal; errno 22 and an unchanged set for 0, -1, 129, 1000, `INT_MIN` and `INT_MAX`, against a nearly empty and a full set; errno untouched by every successful call. Written before the implementation; it failed on the five unresolved exports and passes with them.
- The patched `libkernel.prx` exports the five NIDs (`+F7C-hdk7+E`, `VkTAsrZDcJ0`, `JUimFtKe0Kc`, `Nd-u09VFSCA`, `JnNl8Xr-z4Y`).
- `tools/import_audit.py` on catalog titles, absent imports before → after: PPSA69420 ScreenTester5 9 → 7, PPSA17641 SymphonyStation5 35 → 33, PPSA99007 Yamagi Quake II 23 → 19, PPSA99420 PS5MC 121 → 116. None of them loads yet; the remaining imports are listed in #1578.
- Windows: the same Build workflow run on this commit in the fork's Actions (merged onto `main` 6b56175a), [run 37822072979](https://github.com/SleglJan/AnyPS5/actions/runs/37822072979): `guest_signal_sets` passes its three repeats, full suite 474/474. The first attempt timed out in `guest_raise_exception`, the hang described in #1488, and passed on the rerun.

### What

`s_cselect_b64 sd, exec, 0` (and the same form with vcc or all ones) gives a mask that is the same for every lane. The translation stored it as a plain register pair, so a later read of the pair went through `LaneId`. Metal has no lane number in a vertex shader, and MoltenVK rejects such a shader ("subgroup capability 61 is unsupported for shader stage 1"), so the draw is skipped.

- `s_cselect_b64` with two mask sources now stores the lane bit `scc ? source1 : source2` and marks the pair as a mask, the same way `v_cmp` results are kept. The sources are read before the destination is written.
- A mask of all zero or all one reads as a constant, with no lane number.
- The constant folder folds `((W >> (x & 31)) & 1) != 0` to a constant when `W` is all zero or all one. Some masks only become constant after folding.

The translation is exact. Nothing changes when the lanes differ.

### Tested

- macOS 27 (Apple M2), x86-64 under Rosetta, MoltenVK: one retail title, 30 s run. Before, 8 draws were skipped with "subgroup capability 61 ... stage 1". After, none, and the picture is shown.
- New test `agc_constant_bit_test`: fails without the fold (all-zero and all-one cases) and passes with it.
- This branch does not build libc on macOS (`link.h`), so I ran the test and the existing masked-select, control-flow, shader-disk-cache and DPP-write tests on a macOS port tree that carries the same shader code: all pass. The four changed shader files compile on this branch.
- Not tested: Linux and Windows (CI), and the `scalarSelectMask64` translation by a unit test; it was only checked end to end on the title above.

body:
### What

`GetMipTailLayout` gave `SW_64KB_Z_X` the same mip tail limits as the other 64 KiB modes. In addrlib that is only the case on Navi10. On every other GFX10 chip, including the PS5's gfx1013, addrlib uses smaller limits for 8 and 16 bpp Z-order surfaces. As a result, mipmapped 8 and 16 bpp `Z_X` textures (D16 depth, R8, R16, R8G8 and so on) started their tail too early, and every level was read and written back at the wrong offset.

Source, Mesa `src/amd/addrlib/src/gfx10/gfx10addrlib.cpp` at `d778ede7`:

- `HwlConvertChipFamily` ([L1003-1010](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/-/blob/d778ede72c4c31bf4ed80578688c3e78d9af2dfa/src/amd/addrlib/src/gfx10/gfx10addrlib.cpp#L1003-1010)) sets `dsMipmapHtileFix` and clears it only for Navi10.
- `ComputeSurfaceInfoMacroTiled` ([L3923-3926](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/-/blob/d778ede72c4c31bf4ed80578688c3e78d9af2dfa/src/amd/addrlib/src/gfx10/gfx10addrlib.cpp#L3923-3926)): with the setting on, for a Z-order swizzle at 8 or 16 bpp, the tail limits are divided by `Block256_2d[index] / Block256_2d[2]`. That halves the width at 8 and 16 bpp, and also the height at 8 bpp.

`GetMipTailLayout` now halves the limits the same way. Only the level where the tail starts changes. The tail slot positions stay the same, because addrlib computes them from each level's index inside the tail, not from the limits ([L3999-4001](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/-/blob/d778ede72c4c31bf4ed80578688c3e78d9af2dfa/src/amd/addrlib/src/gfx10/gfx10addrlib.cpp#L3999-4001)).

Results from #1590, `SW_64KB_Z_X` 8 bpp 256x256, 9 levels:

| | surface size | first tail mip | mip 0 at (0,0) | mip 1 at (0,0) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| addrlib, gfx1013 | 196,608 | 2 | 0x20000 | 0x10000 |
| main | 131,072 | 1 | 0x10000 | 0x8000 |
| this PR | 196,608 | 2 | 0x20000 | 0x10000 |

For 16 bpp 128x128 with a full mip chain, mip 0 now starts at 0x10000, as in addrlib, instead of 0x8000.

This follows addrlib's setting for gfx1013. The console's own layout has not been measured, as #1590 also notes.

Fixes #1590

### Tested

CachyOS Linux (kernel 7.2.9), GCC 16.2.1, CMake 4.4.4, Ninja, Release with `BUILD_TESTING=ON`, on `main` f8c2f072. No GPU was needed: `agc_driver_graphics` runs against `MockVulkan`.

- `agc_driver_graphics` gets two new cases: 8 bpp 256x256 with 9 levels, and 16 bpp 128x128 with 8 levels.
- With only the tests applied (red), it fails with `swizzle mode 24, 1 bytes, 256x256, 9 levels, 1 slices: surface or slice size differs from addrlib`.
- With the fix (green), it passes.
- Full suite: 512/513 passed on an RTX 4060 Laptop GPU (NVIDIA 615.71.09). The one failure, `agc_driver_dcc_keys_first_write` (`an unchanged pending image was uploaded again`), fails the same way on `main` without this change.
- `python3 tools/check_conventions.py --base origin/main`: all checks passed.

body:
### What

Implements `madvise` (`Jahsnh4KKkg`) in libkernel. Part of #1578: PPSA99039 and PPSA99001 import it.

Follows FreeBSD 11 `kern_madvise` (`sys/vm/vm_mmap.c`) and `vm_map_madvise` (`sys/vm/vm_map.c`):

- `behav` outside `MADV_NORMAL`..`MADV_CORE` (0..9) fails with `EINVAL`.
- A range that wraps or ends past `VM_MAXUSER_ADDRESS` (`0x800000000000` on amd64) fails with `EINVAL`. Unmapped holes are not an error.
- Every accepted value is advisory. `MADV_DONTNEED` only lowers page priority and `MADV_FREE` lets the kernel discard pages, so keeping the contents is valid for both; the call returns 0 without touching memory.
- `MADV_PROTECT` (10) goes through `procctl(PROC_SPROTECT)` and its privilege check on FreeBSD, so it calls `NotImplemented_nid_no_patch`.

### Tested

Linux (Ubuntu 24.04, GCC 13, Release): `guest_memory` passes with `--repeat until-fail:3`. It now checks all ten values on an `mmap` range with its contents intact afterwards, a zero length, an unmapped range, invalid values (also with zero length), a wrapping range, a start at `0x800000000000` and a range ending exactly there. The test fails when the range check is removed. `check_conventions.py` passes. Windows: `PosixMemory.cpp` compiles with MinGW-w64 GCC 13 (`-Wall -Wextra -fsyntax-only`); not run on Windows. Closes #1615.

### What

Pass the Vulkan physical-device ID into `NarrowSubgroupClock`. On AMD's proprietary Vulkan driver, select the device clock only for devices with measured 20-bit subgroup clocks:

- `0x1114` — Radeon 860M, measured in #1615.
- `0x744c` — Radeon RX 7900 XT, measured in the report on this PR.

Other device IDs and driver IDs keep their existing behavior. Tests cover both reported devices, adjacent unmatched IDs, and other driver IDs. TechnicalDebt records the measurements and the limits of what they establish.

### Tested

Current PR head `df3efcae540ce376ba98c07ec8edb3db92f577bd` is based on upstream `main` `f8c2f072463465f875dedb0d20b66c339160c1a1`.

- Linux x86-64, GCC 12.2: `libSceAgcDriver` builds and `agc_subgroup_clock` passes (1/1) on the current head.

- Windows RX 7900 XT hardware evidence was run on pre-rebase head `a2307237`: `agc_subgroup_clock` and `agc_driver_shader_clock` passed 100/100 runs each. The full CTest result was 505 passed, 1 failed, 1 skipped (507 total); the failure was the unrelated `agc_driver_vopc_compare_table` / #825, and the skip was `guest_video_out_wqhd_detection_no_vulkan`. This is not an exact-current-head Build.
- A Windows Ryzen 5 7600 iGPU (`0x164e`) result showed `narrowSubgroupClock=0` and 600/600 shader-clock runs; that device is intentionally left unmatched. See [the measurement](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/pull/1632#issuecomment-6085934812).
- No PS5 hardware or title was tested. The required upstream Linux/Windows Build and relinker matrix for the current head remains outstanding.

The existing approval review was submitted on `f4fec653`; it predates the `0x744c` extension. Maintainers should review that additional measured-device case as part of the current diff.

### Evidence for `0x744c`

On Windows 11 with an RX 7900 XT and AMD driver `32.0.31041.1004`, the unmodified detector reproduced the clock wrap. The contributor's extension to `0x744c` fixed the regression; an adjacent device ID and non-proprietary driver cases retained the existing behavior. Their report and test results are in [the hardware report](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/pull/1632#issuecomment-6081420610) and [the exact-head retest](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/pull/1632#issuecomment-6082108886). body:
### What

`sceAgcDcbResetQueue` wrote only a single `c0001200 <state>` CLEAR_STATE packet and ignored `op` entirely (the KytyPS5 approximation). This replaces it with the sequence measured on a PS5 (firmware 13.60): an envelope (`ffff1000` / `c0027904 00000342 ce20<op&ffff> <flag>` ... `c0017904 00000342 cea00000`) plus one packet group per set `op` bit, emitted in ascending bit order.

Groups are emitted for op bits `0x001, 0x002, 0x004, 0x008, 0x010, 0x020, 0x080, 0x100, 0x800`. The three bits whose groups the driver's `Pm4::Validate` currently rejects — `0x040` (whole-range ACQUIRE_MEM), `0x200` (EVENT_WRITE event 56), `0x400` (opcode 0x1E) — throw a clear error instead of being emitted, so this change cannot make a title stop inside the driver. Supporting those bits needs the driver-side acceptance first and belongs in a separate PR.

`state` 2 sets the envelope flag dword to `0x00000008`; `state` 3 sets the `0x004`/`0x800` group's payload dword to `0x00840f80`; the other measured `state` values (0, 1, 4, 8, 0xF) produce the state-0 form.

### Tested

Linux, GCC 16.2.0, C++20. The AGC command test suite (`agc_command_tests` — `testPackets`) was extended with exact-byte assertions for the envelope, single groups, the `state` 2 and `state` 3 variants, `op=0x800`, and that an unsupported bit throws and leaves the buffer unmodified; the suite passes. Every emitted byte was checked against the hardware probe output in #1581. Not run on hardware or against a title.

Semantics source: the packet bytes and `op`/`state` behaviour come from the PS5 firmware 13.60 measurement in issue #1581 (the `sceAgcDcbResetQueue` probe loading `libSceAgc.sprx` and dumping the command buffer), not from a cited ISA/driver source.

### What

On Windows `_wopen` cannot open a directory, so `sceKernelOpen` falls back to a directory descriptor when the path is a directory. The fallback ignored the flags: `O_CREAT | O_EXCL` on an existing directory returned a descriptor instead of `EEXIST`, and write access returned a read-only descriptor instead of `EISDIR`.

The fallback now follows FreeBSD `vn_open_cred`/`vn_open_vnode` (`sys/kern/vfs_vnops.c`):

- `O_CREAT | O_EXCL`: `EEXIST`
- `O_CREAT` without `O_EXCL`, `O_TRUNC`, `O_WRONLY` or `O_RDWR`: `EISDIR`
- otherwise: directory descriptor, as before

Linux opens directories natively and already returns these errors.

Linux (Ubuntu 24.04, GCC 13, Release): `guest_filesystem` passes with `--repeat until-fail:3`; the new assertions open the test directory with each flag combination above and a plain read-only open. ### What

Implements `readlink` (`pd02UI9TbOA`) in libkernel_sys. Part of #1578: PPSA99001 (ProsperoRadio) imports it from `libkernel_sys`, which only had the placeholder export. On Windows an import is looked up in its own module and then libc, so it has to live in libkernel_sys.

body:
### What

`sceSysmoduleIsLoaded` returned `0x80A90002` and `sceSysmoduleUnloadModule`/`sceSysmoduleUnloadModuleInternal` returned `0x80A90003` for a module that is not loaded. Both values came in with the first libSceSysmodule commit (1e0fc3f3) and match no SDK: the sysmodule facility is `0x5A`, and the error for this case is `SCE_SYSMODULE_ERROR_UNLOADED = 0x805A1001`. The change returns that value from all three places and names it.

Why it matters for titles: the idiom is `if (sceSysmoduleIsLoaded(id) == SCE_SYSMODULE_ERROR_UNLOADED) { sceSysmoduleLoadModule(id); <init>; }`. With a value that never equals the constant, the title concludes the module is already loaded and skips its own initialisation; the failure then shows up later with nothing pointing back to the query.

Sources for the value:

- Sony's public Vita SDK header, same facility and code: [`vitasdk/vita-headers` `sysmodule.h`](https://github.com/vitasdk/vita-headers/blob/master/include/psp2/sysmodule.h) (`SCE_SYSMODULE_ERROR_UNLOADED = 0x805A1001`).

body:
### What
A suspend point flushes the labels queued since the last submission. It recorded them only inside `if (const auto localDevice = device.Load())`. The Vulkan device is created lazily, on the first draw or dispatch, so labels queued by a title that had not yet drawn were never written. The idle worker then sleeps (`completionsPending()` is false), and nothing writes them later.

RADV on the PS5 ([mihawk-99/PS5_Mesa](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Mesa), `winsys/ps5`) ends every submission with a `RELEASE_MEM` of `CACHE_FLUSH_AND_INV_TS_EVENT` that writes the sequence number to a marker it polls from the CPU. When another submission was queued, the end of that submission was folded into the following suspend point. The marker stayed at 0, and RADV reported `the GPU has not reached submission 1 (at 0) in 10 s` and `VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST`. ccleste (PPSA59322) hits this at startup, before its first draw succeeds.

- The suspend point now records the queued labels either way. `recordDeferredLabels` writes them from the CPU when there is no device, as the end of an ordinary submission already does. It still submits or drains only when a device exists.
- `agc_driver_pm4` test (`testSuspendPointWritesQueuedLabels`):
  - Submits a `WAIT_REG_MEM` on a gate followed by RADV's completion `RELEASE_MEM`, then queues a suspend point while the worker waits.
  - Opens the gate and requires the marker without calling `AgcDriverWaitIdle` first.
  - It fails without the change and passes consistently with it.

### Tested
Windows 11 Pro (26200), MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0 (WinLibs r7), Release, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti.

- The full suite (456 tests) passes, run from the generated `CTestTestfile.cmake` commands because antivirus blocks `ctest.exe` on this machine. That run was on a local branch that also carries my other pending changes; all 222 `agc_*` tests also pass on this branch alone.

body:
### What
Clang's PS4/PS5 target sets the default new alignment and the suitable alignment to 32 bytes: `PSOSTargetInfo` in `clang/lib/Basic/Targets/OSTargets.h` has `NewAlign = 256` and `SuitableAlign = 256` (bits). So `__STDCPP_DEFAULT_NEW_ALIGNMENT__` and `alignof(max_align_t)` are 32 on the console, and PS5 code may store to a fresh `malloc` or plain `operator new` result with 32-byte-aligned AVX instructions.

The guest heap aligned blocks to 16 bytes. Worse, the arena's size classes are multiples of 32 bytes on page-aligned spans, so after the 16-byte header every small block landed exactly 16 bytes past a 32-byte boundary. ccleste (PPSA59322, [darkxex/PS5_Celeste](https://github.com/darkxex/PS5_Celeste)) faults on its first such store: `operator new(40)` returns `0x200104f90` from `malloc`, and the next instruction is `vmovaps %ymm0,(%rax)`.

- `GuestHeap`: the minimum alignment is 32 bytes. The padding is now sized from the 16-byte alignment the raw blocks guarantee (`RawAlignment`), so a 32-byte-aligned pointer always fits its block.
- `guest_memory` test (`CheckHeapAlignment`):
  - Allocates every size from 1 to 600 bytes, three large sizes and a grown reallocation.
  - Requires 32-byte alignment.
  - Fills each block completely, then checks that every block's contents survived, to catch overrun into a neighbour.
  - It fails without the change.

### Tested
Windows 11 Pro (26200), MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0 (WinLibs r7), Release, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti.

- The full suite (456 tests) passes, run from the generated `CTestTestfile.cmake` commands because antivirus blocks `ctest.exe` on this machine. That run was on a local branch that also carries my other pending changes; every `guest_*` test also passes on this branch alone.
- ccleste gets past the fault. It still needs other pending changes to render.

Not tested on Linux.

body:
### What

This is the fix from #1133. A comparison-sampled R32_SFLOAT or R16_UNORM surface that a storage image holds is now sampled from a D32_SFLOAT or D16_UNORM image that the GPU refills from the storage image. It no longer stays a CPU snapshot compared against guest memory.

Vulkan only compares depth formats, and this driver reports no depth-comparison sampling on R32_SFLOAT or R16_UNORM, so `cachedTexture` kept these lookups (`depthCompare`) off the storage-image view path. After every GPU write-back, the next lookup flushed, waited for the GPU and compared the whole surface under the GPU mutex. In Demon's Souls that is a 16 MiB shadow map (1024x1024, 4 layers), compared 10-20 times a second on queue 0x30, and queue 0 waits behind it.

- `Texture(context, source, descriptor, components, Texture::DepthCopyTag)` makes a depth image of the surface's shape. `RefreshDepthCopy()` records a copy from the storage image into a device buffer and from there into the depth aspect, with barriers, whenever `StorageTexture::Version()` has moved since the last copy.
- `cachedTexture` sends a `depthCompare` lookup down this path when the surface is host-imported, R32F or R16 unorm, not 3D, at least 1 MiB, and the storage image has the same format (`CanDepthCopyFrom`). Everything else stays on the snapshot path as before.
- `ShaderResources::Revalidate` refreshes the depth copies of a set after a successful proof, because the fast proof repeats no lookup.
- `APS5_NO_DEPTH_COPY=1` turns the copies off. `APS5_DEPTH_COPY_MIN_KIB` (default 1024) sets the floor. TechnicalDebt has a line for the floor and the 3D exclusion.

New test: `agc_driver_depth_compare_copy` writes a 512x512 R32F surface with a compute store, compare-samples it, rewrites it and samples it again.

Closes #1133.

### Before/after, this change alone

Demon's Souls (PPSA01341 v1.07), boot through the PS Studios movie into the attract movie, 200 s per run. Same build and settings on both sides; the only difference is `APS5_NO_DEPTH_COPY=1` on the "before" side. 3 runs each, interleaved (before, after, before, ...). Each cell is the median of the per-run medians, per 10 s, with the per-run values in brackets.

| | before (copy off) | after (copy on) |
|---|---|---|
| PS Studios movie: queue 0x30 GPU mutex held | 408 ms (354-520) | 34 ms (30-70) |
| PS Studios movie: queue 0 waiting for the mutex | 247 ms (223-317) | 65 ms (60-91) |
| Attract movie: queue 0x30 GPU mutex held | 215 ms (209-231) | 32-33 ms |
| Attract movie: queue 0 waiting for the mutex | 114 ms (108-115) | 30-33 ms |
| Attract movie: syncs on pending GPU writes (`[hooksync]`) | 108 syncs, 104 ms | 5-6 syncs, 6-7 ms |
| Attract movie: presents | 106 (105-116) | 106-108 |
| Depth copies (refreshes) at the end of the run | 0 | 1 (about 1,700) |

On the "before" side, almost all of those syncs are on ranges of up to 16 MiB (the shadow map). With the copy on, none are.

Presents don't move here. On these runs the title presented at about 10-12 fps on both sides, held by something other than this change. In earlier runs on a different build (in the issue), the attract movie went from 384-407 to 429-439 presents per 10 s with this change.

The build is `main` plus other local fixes and open PRs, not this branch alone. Both sides use that same build. The attract row for "after" has 2 runs: the first "after" run died with SIGSEGV at about 97 s, with no error line in the log and no core dump. 13 earlier runs of the same build with the copy on (it is on by default) had no such crash, so I can't tie it to this change. I'm noting it anyway.

### Tested

Nobara 44 / Linux 7.2, GCC 16.2.1, RTX 5070 Ti, driver 595.91.07. Branch rebased onto `main` 9f4bd71c.

- `ctest -j1 --timeout 60`: `agc_driver` + `guest_agc_driver` 184/184, including `agc_driver_depth_compare_copy`. Full run 463/464; the one failure is `guest_dynamic_loader`, which also fails on the #1430 branch on the same `main` and is not touched here.

### What

Fix Linux loader and APR failures found while bringing up Horizon Forbidden West (PPSA01521), with each fix in a separate commit:

- Correct ELF section addresses; preserve executable exports and lookup/debug tags; support main-module `sceKernelDlsym`.
- Return guest errors from chmod; implement `sceKernelFutimes` while preserving POSIX futimes behavior.
- Retain HTTP request-status callbacks/user data with the three-argument ABI; remove registrations on request deletion. The offline backend never dispatches callbacks; handle hierarchy/deletion validation remains incomplete and documented.
- Set APR guest errno, invalidate failed file IDs/sizes and return the successful ForEach count. This prevented stale package selection and a deserialization crash.
- Correct APR's 24-byte object layout; encode gather commands in 12 rather than 40 bytes, avoiding HFW's 1 MiB command-buffer exhaustion. Records remain internal to AnyPS5; 40-bit offsets and 32-bit lengths are retained.
- Evaluate signed minimum in runtime SRT expressions, matching [the existing signed IR/GPU lowering](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/blob/main/core/shader/recompiler/SpirvBackend/src/SpirvAlu/SpirvAluEmitterMath.cpp); no new GPU opcode is introduced.

The integration build reaches menu/loading UI using these fixes **plus** local equivalents of #1269 (media), #1339 (VRR), #1586 (unwind) and experimental image-table changes. Missing imports are already merged in #1436. The open #757 => #758 => #920 image-table series overlaps those experiments and should be tested as well; its code is excluded here. Loading still stops at a bounded material-scan limit; gameplay is not reached.

### Tested

### What

`_Mbtowcx` and `_Wctombx` currently use host CRT conversions despite the guest's single-byte C locale.

On a UTF-8 host, U+00E9 is encoded as `C3 A9` instead of `E9`, while valid guest bytes may be rejected or combined into multibyte sequences. Invalid wide characters can also expose the Windows host `EILSEQ` value (42) instead of the guest value (86).

## Changes

- Delegate conversions to the existing guest `mbrtowc_nid_postfix` and `wcrtomb_nid_postfix` implementations using a 16-bit temporary.
- Preserve existing argument validation and exception paths.
- Extend `guest_locale` regression coverage to include all 256 input bytes, independent decoding of `C3 A9`, errno preservation, output canaries, rejected wide units, and both C and available UTF-8 host locales.

Only `LocaleSupport.cpp` and `GuestLocale.cpp` are modified: 6 insertions and 4 deletions in production code, plus regression tests.

This fix is independent of #1507.

body:
### What

Implement `mkstemp` and `isatty` in `libScePosixForWebKit` for the homebrew imports reported in #1578.

`mkstemp` uses the guest path resolver and existing `open` implementation, creates files exclusively with read/write access and mode 0600, and handles collisions without truncating existing files. Its trailing-X and fixed-name behavior follows [FreeBSD 9](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/stable/9/lib/libc/stdio/mktemp.c).

`isatty` distinguishes terminals, non-terminal files/pipes/sockets (`ENOTTY`), and invalid descriptors (`EBADF`), following [FreeBSD's terminal check](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/stable/9/lib/libc/gen/isatty.c). Windows checks console handles and handles invalid CRT descriptors without aborting.

The socket check calls `GuestSocketIsOpen_nid_no_patch`, a C host helper whose export survives NID patching. This fixes the patched module load failure (Windows error 127) reported in the review. Internal socket callers keep using the existing registry implementation.

Refs #1578. No dependency on another PR. Console verification and existing Windows file-permission limits are recorded in TechnicalDebt.

### Tested

Windows x64, Release, WinLibs MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0 UCRT POSIX:

- Eight focused tests passed: POSIX filesystem, filesystem, resolver, strings, UDP, TCP, poll and memory.
- Full project and patched-library builds passed.
- All 115 patched `.prx` libraries loaded with zero failures using the standalone loader from #1828; the loader is statically linked and starts without unpatched guest libraries loaded.
- Registration/conventions checks and `git diff --check` passed. `git range-diff` confirms the original feature commit is unchanged after rebasing.
- CI on `31b26d7d`: Windows and Linux builds and CTest passed, with 489 registered tests / 203 skipped on Windows and 498 / 25 skipped on Linux; zero failures. Conventions passed.
- The regression covers aliases, binary file I/O, unique names, collisions without content loss, fixed names, missing parents, invalid templates, files, pipes, sockets, closed/invalid descriptors and Windows `NUL`. Terminal tests run when a console or pseudo-terminal is available.
- No homebrew/title execution or PS5 hardware verification.

body:
### What

`DescribeSurface` treats 3D `SW_64KB_D_X` volumes like `Z_X` and `R_X`, as a stack of thin 2D slices. In GFX10 a display swizzle on a 3D resource is thick. addrlib's `HwlIsThick` is `IsTex3d(resourceType) && (isStd || isDisp)` (`gfx10addrlib.h` L229-234), and the `ADDR_SW_64KB_D_X` row has `isDisp` set (`gfx10addrlib.cpp` L85). Only `Z_X` and `R_X` volumes are thin.

addrlib addresses these volumes with `GFX10_SW_64K_D3_X_PATINFO` (`gfx10SwizzlePattern.h`). With the thin layout, every element after the first block row lands elsewhere, and the surface size is wrong:

| `SW_64KB_D_X` 3D | addrlib block | addrlib surface | main surface |
|---|---|---|---|
| 32 bpp 64×64×16, 1 level | 32×32×16 | 262,144 | 1,048,576 |

For example, in a 32 bpp 1×1×5 volume, element (0,0,1) is at 0x20 in addrlib and 0x10800 on main. The guest allocation is addrlib's size, so the thin layout also reads past it.

`D_X` volumes now take the thick path, like `S_X`:

- `ThickBlockExtent` gives them the 64 KiB thick block extents.
- `TextureDetiler` uses a new equation key 0x11a.
- `TextureSwizzleEquations.hpp` gets five rows for that key (1 to 16 bytes per element). They were generated from addrlib's 16-pipe `GFX10_SW_64K_D3_X` pattern rows, the same way as the existing 0x119 rows.

Some of the pipe bits use x/y bits above the block, which the detiler shader already supports because it passes full coordinates, as for 0x119.

Tests:

- `RunTextureTilingTests` pins addrlib's guest size, first tail level and sample element addresses for 32 bpp 64×64×16 (1 level), 8 bpp 100×60×70 (7 levels) and 128 bpp 9×5×3 (4 levels).
- `agc_driver_image_xor_swizzle_volume` now also samples a thick `D_X` volume through the detiler on the GPU.

How it was found: AnyPS5's `TextureTiling.cpp` and equation tables were compared against Mesa's addrlib, compiled unmodified and called through `Addr2ComputeSurfaceInfo` / `Addr2ComputeSurfaceAddrFromCoord`. The config was gfx1013, revision 0x82, GB_ADDR_CONFIG 0x00100044 (16 pipes, non-RB+). Every 2D equation matched bit for bit. For volumes, main has about 4.2 million mismatching `SW_64KB_D_X` addresses at 4 and at 8 bytes per element. That comparison covers 7616 3D configurations, compared wherever both addrlib and AnyPS5 accept them: the swizzle modes AnyPS5 implements, at 8–128 bpp, 15 sizes, 1, 2, 4 or a full chain of mips, and depths of 1, 5, 16 and 33. With this change, the linear-volume rounding fix from #1602 and the Z_X tail limits from #1590 applied together, it reports 0 mismatches in 143,437,500 addresses.

### Tested

Windows 11 (26200), WinLibs GCC 15.2.0 r7, CI configure flags, main at fe9beae0:

- `agc_driver_graphics` and `agc_driver_image_xor_swizzle_volume` pass with `--repeat until-fail:3` on an RTX 4070 Laptop GPU and an Intel Raptor Lake-S iGPU.
- With `D_X` put back on the thin path, `agc_driver_graphics` fails with `SW_64KB_D_X 32 bpp 64x64x16, 1 level: guest size differs from addrlib`.
- Full suite on the RTX 4070: 456/456 passed.

body:
### What

Fixes the TechnicalDebt entry "Per-stage descriptor count": a pixel shader's colour attachments were not counted against `maxPerStageResources`, so a pixel stage whose buffers and images fit the limit could still give a pipeline that exceeds it.

The Vulkan spec's definition of `maxPerStageResources` says that for the fragment stage, the framebuffer colour attachments also count against the limit.

- The graphics `ShaderResources` build takes the draw's colour attachment count (`state.colors.size()`, the list `Pipeline.cpp` builds its colour attachments from). The fragment stage's resource total starts at that count, so its buffers and images are added on top of it. Going over the limit throws "shader descriptors exceed per-stage limits" as before. Vertex and compute stages start at 0, as before.
- The draw resource cache key carries the attachment count, so a build cached for fewer attachments is never reused by a draw with more, which would skip the check.
- The vertex+pixel convenience constructor (used only by tests) draws into its one target, so it counts 1 attachment.
- The TechnicalDebt entry is removed.

#1580 edits the same `Require` checks in `ShaderResources::buildPrepare` for a different reason (update-after-bind limits), so whichever PR lands second needs a small rebase. Because this change seeds the fragment stage's total before those checks, the attachments would count against `maxPerStageUpdateAfterBindResources` too, which the spec also requires.

### Tested

Windows 11, WinLibs GCC 15.2.0 (`15.2.0posix-14.0.0-ucrt-r7`), AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT. Built with `-DBUILD_TESTING=ON`, then ran the full ctest suite.

- `agc_driver_graphics` has a new case on the mock device, with `maxPerStageResources` = 2:
  - A pixel stage with 2 buffers is accepted with 0 attachments and throws with 1.
  - A vertex stage with 2 buffers and 1 attachment is still accepted.
  - 3 attachments with no bindings throw.
  - With the fragment seeding removed, the new case fails ("expected graphics rejection: shader descriptors exceed per-stage limits").
- Full ctest rebased on current `main` (aa277b38): 477 of 479 pass. The 2 that fail, `guest_access` (abort in libc.prx, 0xc0000409) and `agc_driver_vopc_compare_table` ("lane 29 cmp_lg_f32_e32 is 1, expected 0"), also fail, the same way, on `main` at 3c4bdda4 without this change. One crashes inside libc and the other runs only compute shaders, which count 0 attachments.
- `tools/check_conventions.py --base origin/main` passes.

body:
### What

`gmtime`, `localtime`, `mktime`, `strftime` and `asctime` in libc took and returned the host's `std::tm`. The guest's FreeBSD `struct tm` is 56 bytes: the nine calendar `int`s, then `long tm_gmtoff` at offset 40 and `char* tm_zone` at offset 48. On Linux glibc's `std::tm` has the same layout, so nothing was wrong there. On Windows `std::tm` is 36 bytes, so:

- the pointer `gmtime`/`localtime` return points at a 36-byte thread-local; a title reading `tm_gmtoff` or `tm_zone` reads 16 bytes past it;
- `gmtime_s`/`localtime_s` never write `tm_gmtoff` and `tm_zone` into the guest's buffer;
- UCRT's `gmtime_s` only accepts 1969-12-31 12:00:00 to 3001-01-19 21:59:59 UTC (measured on this host), so `gmtime(-86400)` returned null where the console converts it.

The change adds `GuestTm` (`core/libs/prx/libc/include/GuestTime.hpp`, with `static_assert`s on the offsets and size) and converts through it on both hosts:

- `gmtime`/`gmtime_s` compute the UTC fields from the day count (Hinnant's `civil_from_days`), so every time whose year fits an `int` converts; `tm_gmtoff` is 0 and `tm_zone` is `"UTC"`, which is what the FreeBSD libc reports (glibc's `gmtime_r` says `"GMT"`).
- `localtime`/`localtime_s` copy the host's calendar fields and fill `tm_gmtoff` and `tm_zone` from the CRT on Windows (`_get_timezone`, `_get_dstbias`, `_tzname`) and from the host `tm` on Linux.
- `mktime` normalises through the host and then refills the guest `tm` with `localtime_s`, so `tm_gmtoff`/`tm_zone` are set as on the console.
- `strftime`/`asctime` copy the guest `tm` into a host `tm` before calling the host.

On Windows `localtime` and `mktime` still go through the CRT and keep its ~1970 to January 3001 range and daylight-saving rule; that gap is recorded in TechnicalDebt. `gmtime` has no such limit any more.

The test (`guest_time_conversion`, already registered in ctest) now uses `GuestTm` and additionally checks: 1969-12-31 23:59:59, 1969-01-01, 2000-02-29, 3001-01-01, 9999-12-31 and 0001-01-01 (calendar fields, `tm_wday`, `tm_yday`), that `tm_gmtoff`/`tm_zone` are written over a `0xAA`-filled buffer, `INT64_MIN` and `INT64_MAX` return null, `tm_gmtoff == 7200` for `TZ=UTC-2`, a `localtime` → `mktime` round trip that renormalises `tm_wday`/`tm_yday` and sets the zone fields, and `strftime` on a guest `tm`.

### Tested

Windows 11 (10.0.26200), WinLibs GCC 15.2.0 (`15.2.0posix-14.0.0-ucrt-r7`), x86-64, Release, `BUILD_TESTING=ON`.

- Against `main`'s `Time.cpp`, a small driver linking the same translation unit prints `sizeof(std::tm) = 36`, `gmtime(1969-01-01) -> nullptr`, and after `gmtime_s` into a `0xAA`-filled 56-byte buffer the `long` at offset 40 is still `0xAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA`.
- The new test compiled standalone with `g++ -std=c++20 -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -pthread` passes.
- Full build, `cmake --build build --target libs`, then `ctest --test-dir build -R '^guest_time_conversion$' --repeat until-fail:3`: passes 3/3 against the built `libc` DLL.
- Full `ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure --timeout 120`: 439 passed, 13 skipped, 6 failed out of 445. The 6 failures are all `agc_driver_*` shader execution tests on this host's Intel integrated GPU (driver 32.0.101.8831): `agc_driver_flat_store` and `agc_driver_global_vcc_base` time out, `agc_driver_sdwa_float_selectors`, `agc_driver_vop1_float_unary`, `agc_driver_vop3_mad_i64` and `agc_driver_vopc_compare` fail. `agc_driver_vop3_mad_i64` and `agc_driver_flat_store` on Intel are #1246 and #1256; none of them call libc's time functions. The libc tests that do (`file_position`, `guest_standard_streams`, `guest_filesystem`) pass.
- `python tools/check_conventions.py --base origin/main` and `git diff --check` pass.
- Not run on Linux (no Linux host here); the Linux path keeps `localtime_r` and only replaces `gmtime_r` with the pure-arithmetic conversion that the test covers on both hosts.
- No title or homebrew run.
