> ⚠️ **Needs testing on Windows before merge.** The shared mapping is tested on Linux, but the Windows branch of `sceKernelGetCurrentCpu` was not built or run on Windows: the author has no Windows machine. Please build it on Windows and run `guest_current_cpu` and the full ctest before merging.

### What
`sceKernelGetCurrentCpu` returned the raw host CPU index (`sched_getcpu`, or the Windows group-adjusted processor number). Guest thread affinities are only recorded, not applied to host threads, and `sceKernelGetAvailableCpumask` advertises CPUs 0 to 12 (0x1FFF). So on a host with more than 13 logical CPUs (a 16-thread Ryzen, for example) a title could be told it runs on CPU 13, 14, 15 or higher, outside the mask it was given, and index per-CPU data sized from that mask out of bounds. On any host, a thread the title pinned with `scePthreadSetaffinity` to one CPU could be told it runs on another one, which the console's FreeBSD `cpuset` never allows.

The host index now selects a CPU of the calling thread's guest affinity clipped to the available mask (the available mask when they do not overlap): host CPU n reports the (n modulo the number of CPUs in that mask)-th CPU of the mask. The result is always an advertised CPU, it stays within the thread's affinity, and a thread pinned to one CPU reports that CPU. Which CPU the console reports for a thread allowed on several is not known; this is recorded in TechnicalDebt. For comparison, shadPS4 returns 0 and fpPS4's older kernel returns the raw host processor number.

This PR was investigated and written by Claude Code (AI), and posted by me after review.

### Tested
Linux (Arch), Intel 6-core / 12-thread laptop CPU, GTX 1050 Ti (NVIDIA 580.178.04), GCC, Release, `APS5_WRITE_WATCH_IMPORTS=watch`.

New `guest_current_cpu` test:
- the mapping, for host CPUs 0 to 255 and the masks 0x1FFF, 0x1FFB, 0x3, 0x3F, 0x1000, 0x1, 0xFFFF and 0x10000: the result is always in the clipped mask, and every CPU of the mask is reached once the host has as many CPUs as the mask;
- `sceKernelGetCurrentCpu` from the main thread is within `sceKernelGetAvailableCpumask`;
- a thread pinned with `scePthreadSetaffinity` to each available CPU in turn reports exactly that CPU, 64 calls each.

Without the change to `sceKernelGetCurrentCpu` the test fails on this 12-thread machine (a thread pinned to CPU 12, or to a CPU it is not running on, reports the host CPU).

`ctest -j4`: 424/424 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (unmodified main: 423/423, 0 failed, 0 skipped; the only difference is the new test).

Closes #825.

### What

`FPOrdNotEqual32`, which `v_cmp_lg_f32`/`v_cmpx_lg_f32` and the f16 LG compares lower to, is now emitted as `OpFUnordNotEqual(a, b) && (bits(a) & 0x7fffffff) <= 0x7f800000 && (bits(b) & 0x7fffffff) <= 0x7f800000` instead of `OpFOrdNotEqual`. The two agree for every input.

The AMD Windows driver returns 1 for a NaN operand when an ordered not-equal feeds a ballot on a 32-wide subgroup, which is how VCC is read for e32 compares in wave32. `OpFOrdNotEqual`, `FOrdLessThan || FOrdGreaterThan`, `FUnordNotEqual && !IsNan && !IsNan` and an integer OR of the two compares all fail the same way, so the driver appears to fold any float form; checking NaN on the bits avoids it (analysis in #825). The image compare emulation's not-equal (`SpirvImageEmitter.cpp`) feeds a select, not a ballot, and is unchanged. Recorded in TechnicalDebt.

### Failing rows on `main`

AMD Radeon 860M (RDNA 3.5, device 0x1114), Windows driver 32.0.13058.8001, Vulkan 1.3.302, `agc_driver_vopc_compare_table`, wave32 run only; e64, wave64 and wave64 split pass:

### What

On the console, a title whose `param.json` declares `downloadDataSize` finds `/download0` mounted when it starts. Here the host directory (`download0/` in the run directory, where `/download0` resolves) was only created by `sceAppContentDownloadDataGetAvailableSpaceKb`, so a title that opens files there without calling it got `ENOENT`.

`libkernel` now creates `download0/` when it loads, if `app0/sce_sys/param.json` in the run directory declares a non-zero `downloadDataSize`, in the same load-time pattern as the timer setup in `Time.cpp`. It reads only that field with the existing `parseParamJson`, and builds the paths from the current directory instead of `ResolvePath`: resolving a guest path from a load-time initializer fixes the libc path root before the program runs, which broke `savedata_core_write_replacement` (it changes the working directory before its first file access) in a first version of this change.

### Which title needs it

DOOM Shareware homebrew PPSA99666 01.001.000 (lowbit/ps5-doom v1.1.0, the build in #690) declares `"downloadDataSize": 256` and keeps its log and launcher settings in `/download0` (`SAVE_DIR` in `src/ps5/system.c`) without using libSceAppContent. On `main` it logs:

```
[debug:0] ps5: cannot write /download0/doom.log (errno 2)
[debug:0] ps5: cannot open /download0 for listing (0x80020002)
[debug:0] launcher: cannot write /download0/launcher.cfg
```

With this PR none of these appear, `download0/doom.log` holds the title's log, and the title exits with 0.

### What

On the AMD Windows driver, `UnpackHalf2x16` of a byte-selected half converts the unmasked source register. `agc_driver_sdwa_float_selectors` and `agc_driver_sdwa_ldexp_f16` fail on an AMD RDNA2 iGPU (both pass on NVIDIA, and CI has no AMD device):

    sdwa ldexp f16: lane 2 BYTE_0/DWORD -> DWORD is 0x0000fff0, expected 0x00000000

Probing the ldexp shader's SPIR-V on both GPUs (lane 2, input 0xfff0fff0):

| value | AMD | NVIDIA |
|---|---|---|
| `BitFieldUExtract(x, 0, 8) & 0xffff` | 0x000000f0 | 0x000000f0 |
| `UnpackHalf2x16(that).x` | 0xfffe0000 (f16 0xfff0) | 0x37700000 |

In all 11 failing lanes the result is the unselected low half quieted. Replacing the extract with shift+mask, dropping the redundant `& 0xffff`, or feeding the half through the high word does not change the AMD result.

`EmitF16BitsToF32` now decodes sign, exponent and mantissa with integer operations and scales subnormals by 2^-24 (exact in f32). Checked bit-exact against IEEE f16→f32 for all 65536 halves, including ±0, subnormals, infinities and NaN payloads.

### What

`relinker --registry` only described the imports of the executable, so a title whose own modules import system functions (`PSN.prx`, `libc.prx` and others) could not be audited completely. With `--registry` the relinker now also writes `<output-stem>.<module>.registry.json` for every converted bundled module.

An entry is written for each relocation, in `DT_RELA` and `DT_JMPREL`, against an undefined symbol that no other bundled module exports. That is the test `GuestModuleBuilder` already uses to decide that a dependency is satisfied by a sibling. Entries carry `nid`, `library` and `targetOffset`; the symbol has lost its `#` suffix by the time the module is read, so the NID is the bare 11 characters. The executable's registry is unchanged. The import audit from #1461 accepts these files as they are, and its docs are updated for them.

The first commit of this branch is #1461; the second is this change.

body:
### What

On Linux, the narrow integer converters `strtol`, `strtoul`, `strtoll`, `strtoull`, `_Stoull`, `strtoimax`, `strtoumax` and `_Stoul` pass the guest's text and base straight to glibc. The wide converters `wcstol`, `wcstoll`, `wcstoul` and `wcstoull` pass the ASCII prefix of the guest's text. Since glibc 2.38, code built as GNU C++ calls the C23 `__isoc23_*` functions (g++ defines `_GNU_SOURCE`). Those accept a `0b`/`0B` binary prefix in base 0 and 2. C17 has no binary prefix (7.22.1.4p3): the subject sequence of `"0b101"` is `"0"`, so the result is 0 and the end pointer stops at the `b`.

Results on Linux with the code on main:

| call | main (glibc 2.39) | C17 |
|---|---|---|
| `strtol("0b101", &end, 0)` | 5, end +5 | 0, end +1 |
| `strtol("0b101", &end, 2)` | 5, end +5 | 0, end +1 |
| `strtol(" -0B1", &end, 0)` | -1, end +5 | 0, end +3 |
| `strtoul("0b11", &end, 2)` | 3, end +4 | 0, end +1 |
| `strtoimax("0b101", &end, 0)` | 5, end +5 | 0, end +1 |
| `strtoumax("0b101", &end, 0)` | 5, end +5 | 0, end +1 |
| `_Stoul("0b101", &end, 0)` | 5, end +5 | 0, end +1 |
| `wcstol(u"0b101", &end, 0)` | 5, end +5 | 0, end +1 |

Changes:

- `StopAtBinaryPrefix_nid_no_patch` (`Strings.cpp`, declared in `General.hpp`) handles text in base 0 or 2. After C-locale white space and an optional sign, if the text starts with `0b` or `0B` and a binary digit, it returns 0 and sets the end pointer after the `0`. The eight narrow exports check it first. Every other input still goes to the host function, so errno, overflow and the `0`/`0x` prefixes are unchanged.
- The four wide exports apply the same check to the ASCII prefix they already build. `ParseAsciiPrefix` maps the end pointer back to the guest's UTF-16 text as before.
- `guest_math` gets new rows in its strtol/strtoimax and strtoul tables:
  - base 0 and base 2;
  - a sign and leading white space;
  - `0b2`, where glibc already stops after the `0`;
  - `0b101` in base 16, which stays the hex value `0xb101`.
- `guest_math` also checks `strtoll`, `strtoull`, `strtoumax`, `_Stoull` and `_Stoul` on `" -0B11"` in base 0 and base 2.
- `guest_wide_strings` checks the four wide exports on `u" -0b101"` in base 0 and base 2, and `u"0b101"` in base 16. (Thanks @Zheorgyan!)
- The scanf family's `%i` reaches glibc's C23 conversion the same way: `sscanf("0b101", "%i", &value)` stores 5. Because the format is handed to glibc, this is recorded in TechnicalDebt rather than changed here.

The Windows behaviour is unchanged: the UCRT functions accept only the `0` and `0x` prefixes, so the new check returns what they already return.

### Tested

- **Linux, local:** Ubuntu 24.04, glibc 2.39, GCC 13.3.0, Release, `-DBUILD_TESTING=ON`, this branch on d70b899 (current main). `guest_math` and `guest_wide_strings` pass; `guest_math` fails on main with "Guest strtol failed for '0b101' in base 0", and `guest_wide_strings` fails on the first commit, before the wide change. The table above comes from main's function bodies, built with the same compiler and glibc.
- **CI:** the GitHub Actions Build workflow passed on the previous push. linux: ubuntu-latest, GCC 13.3.0, lavapipe, SPIRV-Tools. windows: windows-2025, MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0 (WinLibs 15.2.0posix-14.0.0-ucrt-r7).

body:
### What

The relinker accepted an ELF whose declared relocation table did not lie inside the input file, and then **wrote that offset into the output it generated**.

The defect is specific to an **empty** relocation table. #917 added the overflow-safe per-entry bound (`relaEntryPos`, `RelinkerPipeline.cpp`), but that check only runs inside the `extractRela` loop, and the loop body never executes when `DT_RELASZ` is `0`. Nothing reads the table, so nothing rejects it, and the bad offset travels on — as @Dextroid17 measured by scanning the produced file for each `(tag, value)` pair:

```
empty-past-eof   (DT_OS_RELA 0x2000)               DT_OS_RELASZ 0   DT_RELA 0   DT_RELASZ 0
empty-offset-max (DT_OS_RELA 0xfffffffffffffffe)   DT_OS_RELASZ 0   DT_RELA 0   DT_RELASZ 0
```

So the conversion hands a title a dynamic table pointing outside the file, with a size of zero. That is the "does exactly what it should or throws" case rather than a message preference, and it is why this is worth merging instead of cosmetics.

This is also what separates it from the table-level check @oneandonlydean asked to drop from #1272. That hunk was about the **read** — no read can leave the file, because `relaEntryPos` already bounds it. This is about what gets **written**, which `relaEntryPos` cannot reach.

The fix validates the declared table range before the table is consumed, using the same shape as the existing dynamic string-table guard:

```cpp
if (dynStrTabOffset > raw.size() || dynStrTabSize > raw.size() - dynStrTabOffset)
    throw RelinkerException("Dynamic string table is out of bounds", dynStrTabOffset);

if (dynRelaOffset > raw.size() || dynRelaSize > raw.size() - dynRelaOffset)
    throw RelinkerException("Relocation table is out of bounds", dynRelaOffset);
```

The first term short-circuits, so the subtraction cannot wrap and `offset > size || size > size - offset` decides both an offset past EOF and an offset plus size past EOF, for the system-V path (already translated by `TranslateVirtualAddress`) and the Sony `DT_OS_RELA` path (raw). #1424 covers the separate `DT_JMPREL`/`DT_PLTRELSZ` table and is already merged; this PR covers the `DT_RELA`/`DT_OS_RELA` table itself.

Malformed inputs now fail with the table named, in both output modes:

```
--windows   bad-offset-past-eof   exit=2 output=False FAIL: Relocation table is out of bounds (offset 0x9000)
--to-intel  bad-offset-past-eof   exit=2 output=False FAIL: Relocation table is out of bounds (offset 0x9000)
--windows   bad-range-past-eof    exit=2 output=False FAIL: Relocation table is out of bounds (offset 0x7ff0)
--to-intel  bad-huge-size         exit=2 output=False FAIL: Relocation table is out of bounds (offset 0x700)
```

**Tests** — `tests/RelocTableBoundsTests.cpp` (CTest `reloc_table_bounds`) is C++ on `ElfFixture.hpp` / `RelinkerProcess.hpp`, registered explicitly in `core/relinker/CMakeLists.txt` like `RelaBoundsTests.cpp`, and runs every case under `--windows` and `--to-intel` (the fixture's spare program headers are what let the Linux path reach the code under test). It keeps valid controls (an empty in-file table, an empty `DT_OS_RELA` table, a table holding one relocation entry), both tag families, and a case whose address no segment maps.

**`rela_bounds` (#917) expectation, updated deliberately.** Both of its cases are now answered by the table guard before any entry is read — case 1 has an offset near `UINT64_MAX`, case 2 has `offset + size` past the end — so `RelaBoundsTests.cpp:38` now expects `Relocation table is out of bounds`. Keeping the old `Relocation entry out of bounds` expectation there would mean removing the guard for those inputs, which is the defect itself. The two cases are unchanged otherwise and still require a non-zero exit, so the regression is not weakened: with the guard reverted, `rela_bounds` fails with *"Relinker did not report the table as out of bounds for a table whose offset is near UINT64_MAX"*.

### Tested

- Linux x86_64, GCC 13.3, Release (`-DANYPS5_RELINKER_ONLY=ON -DBUILD_TESTING=ON`): full relinker CTest suite **39/39 passed**, including `reloc_table_bounds`, `rela_bounds`, `jmprel_table_bounds` and `string_table_bounds`
- `cmake --build build-linux --target relinker rela_bounds_tests reloc_table_bounds_tests`
- `ctest --test-dir build-linux -R '^(reloc_table_bounds|rela_bounds)$'` → 2/2 passed
- Windows, MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0 (winlibs), Release, Ninja: `cmake --build build --target relinker`, affected relinker CTest suite **25/25 passed**
- `git diff --check`
- `python tools/check_conventions.py ...` → All conventions checks passed
- pre-fix proof repeated on this head: with only the `RelinkerPipeline.cpp` guard reverted, `reloc_table_bounds` fails with *"Relinker accepted an empty relocation table whose offset is past the end of the file for --windows"* and `rela_bounds` fails as above; with the guard restored both pass
- `--to-intel` no longer stops at `Not enough program header slots`: the fixture carries the spare program headers, and both modes reject the malformed tables with the message above
- The full 400+ test suite was not run in the Windows environment because the unrelated `libs`, FFmpeg and guest targets are not built there; the Linux run covers the relinker in full.

### What

Replace the obsolete float-mode carry implementation with regression coverage for the implementation now on main through #1816. Preserve main's registered-header mode source, prepared-artifact keys, field layout and version-13 capture format.

Extract the existing stage-specific decoder into ShaderFloatMode.hpp and have RegisteredFloatMode call it. The register kind explicitly selects FP16_OVFL at bit 26 for CS, 29 for PS, 31 for GS and 30 for HS, matching the already merged #1816 implementation and its Mesa gfx10.json/gfx103.json register sources. Invalid register kinds throw. Add the decoder to the shader-cache reviewed call list.

Add the portable agc_shader_float_mode target. It covers all four RSRC1 layouts, unrelated bits, unknown versus explicit-zero modes, all eleven control fields across eight shader stages, cache/source-memo/prepared-interface identities, round trips and invalid capture rejection. Genuine version-12 and version-13 fixtures are generated using unchanged serializers from 04477932 and f1451396, respectively. Version 12 remains unknown; version 13 preserves its recorded mode and other versioned fields.

This change does not reintroduce a second float-mode type, a second serialization bump, live queue-register overrides, or new instruction semantics. Linked-stage mode semantics and run-time RSRC1 changes remain separate work.

What
Guest signal delivery in libkernel on Linux, and per-thread guest signal masks on both platforms. Based on current upstream main (311c0493). Five commits; commits 2, 4 and 5 fix defects that adversarial reviews of the commit before each found and confirmed:

1. feat(libkernel): deliver sceKernelRaiseException on Linux

sceKernelRaiseException threw on Linux (NotImplemented), so a title whose garbage collector stops threads with it could not run there. Unity's PS5Util module does this: it installs a SIGUSR1 handler with sceKernelInstallExceptionHandler, raises SIGUSR1 on each thread and reads mc_rsp from the handler's context (see the existing TechnicalDebt entry). [shadPS4](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4/blob/main/src/core/libraries/kernel/threads/exception.cpp) records that libkernel's install is a sigaction wrapper (SA_SIGINFO | SA_RESTART) and the raise a pthread_kill; this follows that model.

The raise sends the host SIGUSR1 to the target thread with pthread_kill. The host handler builds the FreeBSD-layout ucontext the Windows path already uses: general registers, rip, rsp, rflags, cs, ss and the 512-byte FXSAVE area. It calls the guest handler on the target's own stack and writes the registers back. Only the 416 bytes up to XMM15 are written back; the rest of the FXSAVE area holds the kernel's XSAVE frame marker, and overwriting it would make sigreturn drop the upper YMM halves.
errno is left as the handler leaves it. libthr does the same: handle_signal in lib/libthr/thread/thr_sig.c saves errno after the user handler.
A raise on another thread blocks the host signal, takes the target's join lock and returns ESRCH once the thread has finished, so a detached thread's pthread_t is never used after the thread exits. PthreadPrivate records the pthread_t at creation and adoption.
The handler table is lock-free (the host handler reads it). GuestUcontext is alignas(16) like FreeBSD's mcontext_t; its layout and size do not change.
2. fix(libkernel): keep raises off unregistered threads and clamp the handler's MXCSR

Three defects found by an adversarial review of commit 1, each reproduced before the fix:

A raise right after scePthreadCreate reached the thread before RunThread set currentThread. scePthreadSelf() in the handler then adopted a second handle (1997 of 2000 immediate raises), and could deadlock on glibc's per-thread lock when the signal interrupted pthread_getattr_np (gdb backtrace in the review). The creator now blocks all signals around the std::thread construction, so the child starts with them blocked. RunThread restores the creator's mask once the thread is registered, as libthr does.
A handler that set reserved MXCSR bits made rt_sigreturn fail with SIGSEGV. The MXCSR the handler leaves is masked with MXCSR_MASK (0xffbf when it reads 0), as FreeBSD's fpusetregs does. This applies on both platforms; Windows also keeps CONTEXT.MxCsr equal to FltSave.MxCsr.
The no-device pacing sleep of sceAudioOutOutput/sceAudioOutOutputs (sleepUs, since [boykopovar/AnyPS5#955](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/issues/955)) returned early when a raise interrupted it. It now sleeps the remaining time, as TimedWait::SleepNanos does.
3. fix(libkernel): keep guest signal masks per thread in FreeBSD's bit layout

sigprocmask kept one process-wide mask, read only its first word, and tested signal n at bit n. FreeBSD's sigset_t keeps signal n at bit n − 1 (_SIG_BIT), so blocking SIGTERM blocked SIGURG instead. A signal raised while blocked was dropped, and sceKernelRaiseException ignored the target's mask.

The mask is per thread, as libthr's sigprocmask is (it forwards to the kernel's per-thread mask). All 128 bits are kept in PthreadPrivate, a new thread starts with its creator's mask, and SIGKILL, SIGSTOP and SIGTHR cannot be blocked (SIG_CANTMASK, libthr's SIGCANCEL).
A signal raised while blocked stays pending and is delivered once, when it is unblocked, before sigprocmask returns.
On Linux the blocked mapped signals and SIGUSR1 are applied to the thread's host mask, which the kernel enforces and which a query reads back. A handler therefore sees its own signal blocked, as on FreeBSD.
On Windows the thread keeps its pending signals. raise and the CRT dispatcher record a blocked one, a raise on another thread checks the mask while the target is suspended, and sigprocmask delivers what it unblocks.
4. fix(libkernel): block a signal while its handler runs and restore the mask after it

Signal blocked during its handler: on Windows a handler did not run with its own signal blocked, so a raise during it ran the handler again inside itself. A raise now claims the signal's bit in the target's mask with one atomic fetch_or, while the target is suspended (or is the caller); a second raise finds the bit set and stays pending until the handler returns. The CRT dispatcher blocks the signal it delivers the same way.
Mask restored after the handler: FreeBSD's sigreturn installs uc_sigmask. The SIGUSR1 handler's context now carries the interrupted mask, and whatever mask the handler leaves there is installed when it returns. On Linux its mapped bits go to the host frame's uc_sigmask; the CRT dispatcher restores the mask the thread had before the handler.
Ignored signals: a raise of a signal set to SIG_IGN is discarded, as FreeBSD's tdsendsignal does. On Windows, installing SIG_IGN discards the calling thread's pending signal.
CRT dispatcher on Windows: it no longer adopts the thread it runs on (that leaked a handle per Ctrl+C), and it no longer defers a signal the CRT raises itself, such as abort()'s SIGABRT, which FreeBSD's abort() unblocks first.
5. fix(libkernel): make sigprocmask atomic and redeliver a pending raise in place

Atomic sigprocmask on Linux: a SIGUSR1 delivered between sigprocmask's store of the new mask and its host update wrote the handler's interrupted mask back over it. The call returned 0, but the change to a mapped signal was lost (about one call in 100000 under constant raises). sigprocmask now blocks the mapped host signals while it reads, changes and stores the mask, and installs the result with one pthread_sigmask, as the console's system call is atomic.
Atomic sigprocmask on Windows: it claims SIGUSR1's bit for the same span, so a raise in that span stays pending and is delivered when the call returns.
Redelivery in place (Windows): a raise that arrived during a handler was delivered afterwards through the self-raise path, so the second handler saw libkernel's context instead of the interrupted code, its register changes were dropped, and each such delivery nested another frame. Deliver now runs the pending raise itself, as FreeBSD delivers after sigreturn: with the interrupted context the previous handler left, the mask it claims, and the handler installed at that moment.
APC claim timing (Windows): the APC path claimed the signal when the raise was queued, while the target could still be running other code, so a stale interrupted mask could be installed later. The APC now claims when it runs.
TechnicalDebt records that guest setjmp/longjmp do not save the signal mask as FreeBSD's do.
TechnicalDebt: the "throws on Linux" and "does not consult the target thread's signal mask" lines are replaced by what still differs from the console. A new entry records that a SIGINT or SIGTERM sent from outside the process can run the handler on an emulator thread. On Linux, the handler runs wherever the thread was interrupted, emulator code included. On the console, kernel objects are syscalls and libthr defers signals while a thread holds its internal locks; here a host lock held by the interrupted code stays held. Host waits and sleeps resume after the handler, and the calls Linux does not restart return EINTR to the guest.

Tested
<!-- OS, title or homebrew, what was checked. "Not tested" is a valid answer. -->
Ubuntu 24.04, GCC 13.3, Release, -DBUILD_TESTING=ON, after each commit: full build, then ctest with lavapipe and ANYPS5_REQUIRE_VULKAN=1: 409 passed, 0 failed. 23 GPU tests skipped themselves because they need host subgroups wider than lavapipe's 8 lanes.
After rebasing onto c8a2f063, and again onto 311c0493: 415 of 416 passed. guest_sce_net aborts, and it aborts the same way with this branch's files reverted to main, so it is broken on main itself (the IPv6 change in [boykopovar/AnyPS5#1248](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/issues/1248) is the likely cause), not by this branch.
guest_raise_exception, now registered on every platform, covers:
the thread states: self, busy, waiting in sceKernelWaitSema, blocked on a host mutex, leaving a wait;
a register round trip: r12, r13, xmm8 and MXCSR, including a reserved MXCSR bit;
50 raises right after scePthreadCreate, each checking scePthreadSelf() in the handler;
SIGUSR1 blocked on itself and on another thread;
the handler's view of the mask, uc_sigmask round-tripping, and a raise inside the handler being deferred;
a raise during a handler patching r12 of the interrupted code after the handler returns;
two threads toggling a mapped signal for two seconds under constant raises, checking every query (the unfixed sigprocmask fails 4 runs in 5);
a finished thread → ESRCH.
Stress runs of the raise test, all passing: 150/150 serial and 100/100 with 5 in parallel on 4 cores (commit 1); 100/100 serial and 40/40 with 4 in parallel (commit 2); 60/60 serial together with guest_signals (commit 3); 80/80 serial and 32/32 in parallel, each together with guest_signals (commit 4); 40/40 serial with guest_signals and 24/24 in parallel (commit 5).
guest_signals covers:
the bit layout, and pending delivery with coalescing;
all four words, and the unblockable signals;
an aliased set/oset;
inheritance by a created thread, including a signal above 32;
handler mask scoping for CRT signals, and SIG_IGN discards.
Mutation check, all caught. The tests fail when any of these is removed or reverted: the register write-back, the FXSAVE write-back, the r13 read, the startup signal block, the MXCSR clamp, the bit layout, the host-mask update, the unblockable-signal filter, the creator-mask copy, the mask restore after a CRT handler, the SIG_IGN discard, or the uc_sigmask fill and write-back.
Windows: not run (no Windows host here). Every changed file compiles with x86_64-w64-mingw32-g++ (GCC 13, -fsyntax-only -Wall -Wextra); Thread.cpp hits the same three errors on main, from that toolchain's older headers (SetThreadDescription, EfficiencyClass). The Windows logic was reviewed by reading only. CI runs it.

body:
### What

This is the fix from #1132. Sets that sample a depth surface now pass the fast resource proof instead of taking the full walk on every reuse.

`cachedTexture` returned `DepthSurfaceTexture`'s object before calling `logLookup`, so the element had no lookup record and `fastRevalidate` failed with `no record` every time. The walk then succeeded, because the depth surface hands out the same object each time. The only cost was one full walk per dispatch.

- The depth return now logs a record flagged as depth, and `ValidatedSurface` carries the flag.
- `fastRevalidate` and `fastRevalidateEach` prove a depth element with the new `DepthSurfaceHolds(context, address, texture)`: the newest surface at that address still hands out that object, which is what the walk's `DepthSurfaceTexture` lookup would return. The memory, key and pending checks are skipped for that element.
- A new fast-fail reason, `depth surface`, covers a surface that no longer hands the object out.

New test: `depthSurfaceProofTests` in `tests/Recorder.cpp` (`agc_driver_recorder_tests`, a separate commit). It registers a D32 depth surface on a real device, builds a compute set whose only binding samples it, and requires `Revalidate` to take the fast path on the second and third use. The test needs a real device with the driver's `Context`, which the mock harness in `tests/Graphics.cpp` doesn't have, so it sits with the other cache tests in the recorder suite. It builds on `main` unchanged and fails there on behaviour:

```
AGC graphics: a set sampling an unchanged depth surface left the fast proof for the full walk on use 2
```

With `APS5_PROFILE_DRAW=1`, the `[rescache]` line on `main` shows the reason:

```
[rescache] revalidate 1 calls 0.0 ms: fast 0, full 1, failed 0; fast-fail by reason: no record 1; ...
```

On this branch it passes, and the same line reads:

```
[rescache] revalidate 1 calls 0.0 ms: fast 1, full 0, failed 0; fast-fail by reason:; ...
```

The idea for a dedicated test came from @emirplus in #1199, which implements the same change. Thanks to them, and to @oneandonlydean for spelling out what the test has to show.

Demon's Souls (PPSA01341 v1.07), PS Studios movie, per 10 s:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| revalidate calls: fast / full | 72142 / 18697 | 101101 / 2617 |
| indirect proofs: fast / T1 refreshed / full | 2187 / not logged / 9547 | 3017 / 8396 / 463 |
| indirect device call | 193.9-229.6 us | 145.7 us |

The frame rate did not change: queue 0's wait for the GPU mutex took up the time saved.

#425 and #454 change the same lookup (per-use depth copies, retired surfaces). If one of them lands first, a depth record has to skip per-use copies and `DepthSurfaceHolds` has to treat a retired surface as not holding. I'll rebase onto whichever lands.

Closes #1132.

### Tested
Linux 7.2 (Nobara 44), GCC 16.2, RTX 5070 Ti, driver 595.91.07.
- `agc_driver_recorder_tests` (run directly; it isn't registered with ctest): fails on `main` with the message above and passes here. If you want it under ctest, I can register the suite here or in a follow-up.
- `ctest -R "agc_driver|guest_agc_driver"`: 164 of 164 pass. `agc_driver_lds_atomics64` and `agc_driver_scalar_sop1` are excluded; they fail on unmodified `main` on this GPU too.
- All runs used `APS5_WRITE_WATCH_IMPORTS=watch`. On current `main`, this NVIDIA driver refuses the new dma-buf import probe (`vkAllocateMemory` -2), and after that every allocation on the device fails, so most GPU tests fail on unmodified `main` without the variable. The recorder suite also stops at its own dma-buf probe test for the same reason, so the new test runs before that point. #1380 and #1329 turn that probe off on NVIDIA's proprietary driver.
- Demon's Souls (PPSA01341 v1.07): numbers above.

body:
### What

A vertex attribute whose buffer descriptor has stride 0 and `NUM_RECORDS` smaller than one element made the draw throw ("vertex fetch exceeds descriptor byte range"). A title binds such placeholders, a one-byte descriptor read as a 32_32_32_32 float attribute, on thousands of draws per minute.

With stride 0, the descriptor is a raw buffer: every vertex fetches the same element, and the range check is in bytes. Each dword that does not lie wholly below `NUM_RECORDS` reads as zero.

- `ShortRawVertexBufferBytes` (`VertexInput.hpp`) tells whether an attribute is such a buffer, and returns how many bytes are in whole in-range dwords.
- The vertex input step in `Draw` gives such an attribute its own one-element buffer at offset 0. The buffer holds the in-range dwords read from guest memory followed by zeros, instead of joining the guest copy plan. This applies to indirect draws as well, which otherwise copy the descriptor's whole (too short) range.
- Other attributes, including zero-stride buffers that hold a whole element, are planned and copied as before. `VertexBufferReadSize` keeps refusing a short zero-stride buffer if it is ever asked.

### Tested
- Windows 11, MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0: `agc_driver_graphics` passes with new checks for a 16-byte attribute with stride 0: 16 records is not short, 8 records keeps 8 in-range bytes, and 1 record keeps none.
- In a title that binds these placeholders, those draws no longer skip: about 31 000 skipped draws in 120 s went to 0.

body:
### What

On Windows a C++ exception thrown in a host module unwinds through `libc.prx`'s `LibcUnwind`. Two steps of `DecodeFrame` made each throw expensive:

- **Module lookup:** every frame called `VirtualQuery` to find its image, a system call per frame.
- **FDE search:** a module with a plain `.eh_frame` and no `.ehmeta` index (the MinGW runtime DLLs `libstdc++-6.dll`, `libgcc_s_seh-1.dll` and `libwinpthread-1.dll`, whose frames most host exceptions cross) was searched by walking its `.eh_frame` from the start and fully decoding each FDE (CIE, augmentation, pointer encodings) until one matched.

A throw from the AGC driver (for example a draw rejected while its resources are built) therefore took about 1 ms. A title that issues many such draws per frame spent most of its GPU worker time in the unwinder.

- `DecodeFrame` first asks the loader with `RtlPcToFileHeader`, which walks the loader's module list without entering the kernel. It falls back to `VirtualQuery` for images the loader does not know, as before.
- A module's `.eh_frame` is indexed once, on first use, into FDE start addresses sorted for binary search. The index lives in a per-module cache keyed by the section address and guarded by a mutex. The FDE before the pc is then decoded and its range checked as before. `.ehmeta` modules keep their existing binary search.

### Tested
- Windows 11, MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0: `windows_exception_tests` ("typed catch, base catch, catch-all, rethrow, destructors, cross DLL passed"), `guest_exception_handler` and `guest_raise_exception` pass.
- A title whose draws are mostly rejected, sampled from outside the process with a stack sampler during the same scene:
  - before, about 75% of the GPU worker's samples were in `LibcUnwind::DecodeCandidate` and `DecodeFrame`;
  - with the index only, 55% were in `ZwQueryVirtualMemory`, called from `DecodeFrame`;
  - with both changes, the unwinder no longer stands out.
- The driver's draw profile (`APS5_PROFILE_DRAW`) for that scene:
  - time per rejected draw went from 1170 us to about 156 us;
  - draw packets processed per 10 s went from about 8 100 to up to 56 700;
  - presents per 10 s went from 3-4 to 30-70.

body:
### What
On Windows, `sceKernelRaiseException` could lose a delivery: it returned 0, but the handler never ran on the target thread. `guest_raise_exception` hits this in its busy-thread phase in about one run in five on `main` (9619edff, after #1375) and then hangs until the 30 s ctest timeout. Three paths lost deliveries, and a fourth deadlocked them.

**The handler's own return went through `NtContinue`.** A raise suspends the target, points its context at `Aps5RedirectedEntryStub`, and the stub returns through `RtlRestoreContext`. On Windows 10 (19045), `RtlRestoreContext` restores in user mode, with `iretq`, only when `ContextFlags` without `CONTEXT_XSTATE` is exactly `CONTEXT_FULL | CONTEXT_SEGMENTS` (0x10000F, read from the ntdll disassembly); otherwise it calls `NtContinue`. The context was read with `CONTEXT_FULL | CONTEXT_FLOATING_POINT` (0x10000B), so every handler returned through `NtContinue`. When the next raise suspended the thread inside that system call, `SetThreadContext` changed the saved user context, and `NtContinue` then replaced it with the context it was restoring, so the thread went back to its loop without running the handler.
- The context is now read with `CONTEXT_FULL | CONTEXT_SEGMENTS`, so the handler returns through the user-mode restore, which builds its `iretq` frame below the saved context and never enters the kernel.

**Other code returns through `NtContinue` too.** An APC or an exception handler that continues execution resumes the thread through `NtContinue` or `NtContinueEx`.
- A raise that finds the thread inside one of those stubs resumes it and suspends it again instead of redirecting a context that is about to be replaced.

**The APC path was chosen before the thread had stopped.** `SuspendThread` returns before the thread is suspended; `GetThreadContext` waits until it is. `waitCount` was read right after `SuspendThread`, so a thread leaving its wait could still decrement it and drain its APCs with `NtTestAlert` before `QueueUserAPC` queued the delivery, which then waited for an alertable wait that never came.
- The context is now read first, so `waitCount` is read from a stopped thread.

**A raise could interrupt the target inside winpthreads.** MinGW's `thread_local` goes through emutls and winpthreads' `pthread_getspecific`, which holds a per-thread spinlock. A handler that reads a `thread_local`, such as `scePthreadSelf` or the `TimedWait` wait state, on a thread interrupted while it held that lock spun on it forever.
- A raise that finds the target inside `libwinpthread-1.dll` resumes it and suspends it again, as one inside `NtContinue` does.

**Both retries give up after 1 s.** A target that stays inside those `NtContinue` stubs or winpthreads for that long makes the raise throw, instead of spinning forever. In `guest_raise_exception`, the longest retry took 7.4 ms.

TechnicalDebt: the YMM entry names the new flags. A new entry records two things: a handler can still reenter other host code the thread was interrupted in, such as the C runtime's heap, and the raise gives up after 1 s.

### How this relates to #1562
Since `07610212`, #1562 no longer changes `Exception.cpp`. It now moves libkernel's handler-visible state (the current thread, pthread keys and the `TimedWait` state) to fiber-local storage, and makes contended mutex and rwlock waits interruptible on Windows. The two PRs complement each other: with #1562, libkernel calls from a handler no longer take winpthreads' TLS lock, and this PR's retry also covers a `thread_local` in libc or the other prx modules.

In this probe (not part of this PR), a worker loops on libc's `strerror`, whose buffer is a MinGW `thread_local`, and the handler calls `strerror` too:

| build | runs in which all 500 raises were handled |
|---|---|
| `main` | 0 of 5 (the handler hung in rounds 1–98) |
| #1562 at `de12706a` | 0 of 5 (rounds 2–70) |
| this PR | 5 of 5 |

### Tested
Windows 10 (19045), MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0 (WinLibs r7), Release, Intel Core i7-12700H.
- Before: `guest_raise_exception` failed 2 of 5 runs on its own (ctest timeout), and a loop over the test binary hung on runs 12, 3 and 3. gdb on a hung process showed the main thread still waiting for the 9th delivery to the busy thread and the busy thread back in its loop. A 1 ms sleep takes 15.6 ms there, so `ExpectDelivery`'s 5000 attempts outlast the 30 s timeout instead of aborting.
- New phase in `guest_raise_exception`: a thread raises SEH exceptions in a loop and a vectored handler continues each one, so the thread spends much of its time in `NtContinue`. With the first change only, it hung in 4 of 4 runs; with the retry it passes.
- The leaving-thread phase hung in 10 of one series of 30 sequential runs with the first two changes. I could not reproduce that on demand afterwards: 84 sequential and 96 parallel runs of the build with and without the third change all passed. The third change follows from `SuspendThread` being asynchronous, not from a measured before and after.
- A later attempt to measure the third change also showed no difference. I used a stress tool that is not in this PR:
  - A thread waits on a semaphore and then spins without entering an alertable wait.
  - The main thread signals it, raises after a delay of 0 to 50 µs, and checks that the handler runs while the thread spins.
  - 3 × 20,000 rounds delivered every raise while the thread spun, both with and without the third change.
  - So there is still no measured before and after. The change stays because `SuspendThread` is asynchronous.
- New phase: a thread calls `scePthreadSelf` in a loop while it is raised at, and the handler checks it sees its own thread. Without the winpthreads retry it hung in every run (3 of 3 with the final 100 rounds, 10 of 10 in an earlier version); with it, it passes.
- After all four: `ctest -R ^guest_raise_exception$ --repeat until-fail:10` passed all 10 runs (at most 8.7 s each, the 30 s timeout unchanged), and 20 of 20 runs passed with a 200-round version of the new phase.
- Full ctest, two rounds: everything passes except, once, `agc_driver_dcc_keys_first_write`. That test fails without this change too (#1434) and never raises an exception.
- Retry bound: a new phase keeps a thread inside `NtContinue` and checks that the raise throws after 1 s without running the handler. The thread continues a context whose `Rip` is `NtContinue` and whose `Rcx` points at that same context, so each call restores itself.
  - Without the bound, 2 of 2 runs hung in that phase until the ctest timeout.
  - With it, `guest_raise_exception` passed 10 of 10 runs on the branch, and 10 of 10 merged onto `main` 63c57d22.
- Retry durations, traced:
  - Over 5 runs, about 60 raises per run retried. The longest took 666 retries in 7.4 ms, and the average was 0.9 ms.
  - With four copies of the test running at once, the longest took 5 ms.
- Full ctest merged onto `main` 63c57d22: 452 of 454 pass. The failures are `agc_driver_dcc_keys_first_write` and `agc_driver_srgb8_color_target`, the NVIDIA import flakes in #1434.

body:
### What

A sampler with unnormalized coordinates was accepted only for explicit-LOD samples. A shader that used one for an implicit-LOD sample (in a pixel shader), a bias sample or a gradient sample was refused ("unnormalized guest sampler is used by an implicit-LOD sample"). A title's UI pixel shaders do this on most of their draws.

The hardware ignores the LOD for unnormalized coordinates and samples the base level. `agc_driver_image_sample_unnormalized` already shows this for `image_sample_l` with a LOD of 2.7, and for sampler LOD bias and MIN_LOD. Vulkan requires such samples to be explicit with LOD 0.

- `ResourceSpecialization` carries one unnormalized bit per sampler, taken from bit 15 of the S#'s first dword. It is part of specialization equality and the disk-cache key, and `FormatVersion` goes from 7 to 8. `ResourceMaterializer::Apply` copies it to the IR `SamplerResource`, which is serialized with the shader info.
- `EmitSampleOp` emits a sample through such a sampler as `OpImageSampleExplicitLod` with LOD 0: derivatives, bias, an explicit LOD and an LOD clamp are dropped. Comparison samples keep their path.
- `ProveUnnormalized` accepts implicit-LOD and gradient uses. Offsets, comparison, gathers and `image_get_lod` with unnormalized samplers are still refused.

### Tested
- Windows 11, MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0, RTX 5090: `agc_driver_image_sample_unnormalized` passes with a new case. `image_sample_d` with derivatives of 4.0 (normally well above the last mip level) through each of the five unnormalized samplers returns exactly what `image_sample_lz` returns for every coordinate. The other image sampling tests still pass.
- A title whose pixel shaders sample through unnormalized samplers renders those draws. Its skipped draws for this reason went from about 19,000 to 0 in a 4-minute run.

body:
### What

When every `dst_sel` of a sampled view selects constant 0 or 1, a sample or gather returns that constant whatever the texel, filter, LOD or coordinates. Titles sample such placeholders through views the static runtime image interface has no mode for: a 1x1x1 3D R8 texture under a 2D sample with an unnormalized sampler, or a 1D texture under a 2D gather. Both stop at runtime image mode selection ("image descriptor is incompatible with the static runtime image interface"), and the 3D one would then fail the unnormalized proof ("samples a 1D-array, 2D-array, 3D, cube or multisampled image").

- `RuntimeImageModes` appends three constant modes (float, uint, sint) to a direct sampled image whose accesses are all non-compare samples or gathers (`constantSwizzleCompatible`, tracked by `ResourceTracker`). Storage, depth-compare, packed and table images get none.
- `RuntimeImageMode` selects the constant mode of the view's numeric class when all four `dst_sel` are 0 or 1, before dimensions are matched. FMASK, depth-bits, converted and sRGB-decoded views keep their existing modes.
- In a constant mode the emitter returns each channel's constant for a sample, and the dmask channel's constant in all four texels for a gather: 1.0f for float views, 1 for integer views. The selectors come from the image's existing swizzle specialization constants; no coordinate or sampler code is emitted and the image is left unbound.
- `ProveUnnormalized` skips a constant mode only after the run-time-selected check, so bindless table roots still throw.
- The two new `ImageResource` fields are serialized and `FormatVersion` goes from 20 to 21.

### Tested
- Windows 11, MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0, RTX 5090: `agc_driver_image_sample_unnormalized` has new cases, which fail without the change:
  - a 3D view with `dst_sel` (1, 0, 1, 0) sampled with `image_sample_lz`, `image_sample_l` and `image_sample` through all five unnormalized samplers returns exactly (1.0f, 0, 1.0f, 0);
  - `image_sample_lz` dmask 0x6, `image_gather4_lz` dmask 0x2 and `image_gather4_lz` dmask 0x4 under a 2D access return (0, 1.0f), all 0 and all 1.0f on a 3D UNORM view selecting (1, 0, 1, 0); (0, 1), all 0 and all 1 on 32_UINT and 32_SINT views; and zeros on a 1D view selecting (0, 0, 0, 0). These are the values measured on gfx1035.
- `agc_shader_memory`: a 3D view selecting constants passes the unnormalized proof and is not bound; a table root with the same descriptor still fails with "samples an image selected at run time".
- Full `ctest`: 507/507 pass (one skipped as usual).

body:
### What

A sample, gather or `image_get_lod` whose `DIM` field encodes fewer coordinates than the bound resource was refused at SPIR-V emission ("has an image address with too few coordinate components"). A title runs `image_sample_lz` with a 1D address on a 2D texture. This is the sampling counterpart of #1379, which reads missing components of image loads as 0.

`CoordF32` now completes the address:

- A missing position component samples the centre of the first row (or slice): `0.5 / extent` of the base level, from `OpImageQuerySizeLod`. This is exact for an extent of 1 under any filter and addressing mode, and selects that row with point sampling. Bilinear sampling of a taller image reads only that row.
- A missing array layer is layer 0.
- A missing derivative component is 0.
- Cube coordinates still need all components and throw, as does an address with fewer VGPRs than its own `DIM`.

The ISA does not document what the hardware reads for address components the instruction does not provide. Addressing the first row, slice or layer matches what #1379 does for loads.

### Tested
- Windows 11, MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0, RTX 5090: `agc_driver_image_address_dimension` passes. The case that expected `image_sample_l` 1d on a 2D texture to be refused now checks its result: for 32 threads it returns row 0 of the selected level at the requested x (level, x >> level, 0, from a texture whose texels encode their level, x and y). The other image sampling tests still pass.
- A title whose compute shader does this no longer aborts there.

body:
### What
A guest sampler with `ANISO_OVERRIDE` (S# word 2, bit 29) was rejected (`guest sampler descriptor uses an anisotropy override which is not implemented`). Mesa sets this bit on every GFX10+ sampler unless its `aniso_single_level` option is on: `ac_descriptors.c` uses `S_008F38_ANISO_OVERRIDE_GFX10(!state->aniso_single_level)`. With the bit, the texture unit turns anisotropic filtering off when the sampled view has a single mip level (BASE_LEVEL == LAST_LEVEL). The RADV comment in `radv_nir_lower_descriptors.c` describes it as the TA-side replacement for the shader workaround GFX6–7 needed.

- `DecodeSamplerResource` accepts the bit.
- `ShaderResources` records, for each sampler of a draw, whether the images paired with it (`DescriptorBinding::imageSamplers`) are single-level or mipmapped (`Texture::SampledViewRange().levels`).
- A sampler with the bit and an anisotropic filter whose paired images are all single-level is bound as the same S# with point or linear filtering in place of the anisotropic filters, taken from the sampler cache (`SingleLevelSamplerWords`).
- Samplers of mipmapped images keep their anisotropy, as on the hardware.
- One sampler descriptor serves every image paired with it, so a sampler paired with both kinds in one draw still throws (`... paired with both single-level and mipmapped images in one draw, which is not implemented`).
- `GuestSamplerResource` test: `SingleLevelSamplerWords` keeps samplers of mipmapped images, samplers without the bit and samplers without anisotropy unchanged. For a single-level image it gives a non-anisotropic sampler with the same filters and other words, and it throws for the mixed case.

### Tested
Windows 11 Pro (26200), MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0 (WinLibs r7), Release, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti.

- All 222 `agc_*` tests pass. They were run from the generated `CTestTestfile.cmake` commands, because antivirus blocks `ctest.exe` on this machine.
- PS5 OpenGL Showcase (PPSA99005, [blackbearreloaded/ps5-opengl](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-opengl), Mesa 26.2) sets the bit on the anisotropic samplers of its instanced scene. With this change and other pending fixes on a local branch, the scene renders with no draw skipped and the mixed case never taken.

Not tested on AMD, Intel or Linux.

An address-based build served by the cached address space still walked all of its regions for mirrors, sorted the heap mirrors, compared each one's blocks with the write tracker and swept the whole mirror registry. PPSA26344's world keeps about 37,000 heap mirrors (10.6 GiB) in about 2,000 runs; mirror preparation took 37 ms per cache-hit build.

- Each run is still flushed and collected. When `GuestMemory::UnchangedSince` finds no block of the run stamped since the generation of its last complete check, its mirrors skip `ChangedBlocks`; that generation is stored only after the build's blocks were copied.
- `sweepMirrors` skips the registry walk while every live mirror's range is held by the cached space's lease and no mirror changed since the last walk: such a range cannot expire.

### What
An address-based build maps each readable registered range through a host import, else through a heap mirror, a host-visible copy kept current by write tracking. A range mirrored while `APS5_HOST_IMPORT_MIB` was full kept its mirror after a later pass imported it (budget freed by an unmap). Until the guest freed the range, the mirror held host-visible memory and bytes no build read.

- `AcquireRegistered` now releases the heap mirror of each range its pass serves through an import. Recorded work that bound it keeps it until it completes, as for a swept mirror. Image mirrors are unchanged.
- The `[buffers] image mirrors` line (`APS5_PROFILE_DRAW`) counts the released mirrors.
- In PPSA26344 v1.008 (`main` with our open PRs and #290), heap mirrors held 10.6 GiB in 37k ranges while host imports swung between 0.7 and 3.7 GiB with the mirror count flat.
- #290 rewrites `importAllocation` and its call in this pass (it conflicts with `main` already; this change adds no conflict). Its eviction drops imports of ranges that stay registered; the next pass then mirrors such a range anew from the guest bytes. #1085 (ours, `acquireMirror` and the same tests), #1071 (`ClearImageMirrors`) and #1357, #1359 and #1361 (the import `entry` in the same `AcquireRegistered` loop) merge cleanly.

body:
### What
`Amd64OnlyConverter` applied every in-place `--to-intel` substitution (MOVNTSS/MOVNTSD and the in-place SSE4a forms) through `X64InstructionRewriter::Rewrite`. `Rewrite` copies the whole code segment and decodes every instruction in it to adjust references to moved code. The converter only accepts replacements of the same length, so the adjustment is always zero, and the copy and the full scan were wasted once per substitution: conversion time grew linearly with the number of in-place sites.

The replacement bytes are now copied into the segment directly. The output is unchanged.

Before/after for this change alone (`Codegen::MakeAmd64OnlyConverter()->Convert`, one 19.5 MB code segment, `-O2`, best of 3 runs, 1 run for the slowest case):

| In-place sites | `main` | This PR |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 | 687 ms | 632 ms |
| 10 | 2,810 ms | 624 ms |
| 100 | 22,138 ms | 626 ms |
| 1,000 | 224,438 ms | 630 ms |

### Tested
- Windows 11, MinGW-w64 GCC 13.2, Ryzen (Zen 3). Benchmark input: the `.text` of a 19.5 MB x64 system DLL. Instructions that the matcher already reports, or that the decoder rejects, were replaced with NOPs. MOVNTSS sites were then inserted at instruction boundaries. With 0, 10, 100 and 1,000 sites, `main` and this branch produce byte-identical output (FNV-1a over `Bytes`).
- Mixed runs that also insert MOVNTSD and register-form EXTRQ/INSERTQ (trampolines) give the same bytes, trampoline bodies and reports as `main`, or the same exception.
- `amd64_only_converter_tests` and the 23 relinker Python tests (statically linked `relinker`) pass.

body:
### What

Images whose format has no host equivalent are kept in an `R32_UINT` image and converted in the shader: 10/11-bit unorm (format 30) and, with #1394, R10_G11_B11 float (format 43). The host sampler cannot filter them, so sampling them threw ("samples or gathers a converted unorm/float image, which needs filtering in the shader and is not implemented"). A title samples R10_G11_B11 float images from several compute shaders.

This filters those images in the shader:

- The materializer decodes the paired sampler into a new `EmulatedFilter` state on the image:
  - point or bilinear filtering (equal min and mag filters);
  - wrap, mirror, clamp-to-edge, clamp-to-half-border (GL_CLAMP: coordinates clamp to the texture edge, so a bilinear sample takes at most half the border color) or clamp-to-border addressing;
  - the built-in border color (transparent black, opaque black, opaque white);
  - the mip filter.
  
  The state is part of the specialization and the disk-cache entry, and `FormatVersion` goes from 7 to 8.
- The emitter fetches the four (or one) texels with `OpImageFetch`, unpacks them with the existing converted-image path (`UnpackImageTexel`, including the view swizzle) and blends them.
  - The border color replaces the swizzled texel: AMD hardware does not swizzle border colors, which is what `VK_EXT_border_color_swizzle` describes.
  - Texel offsets and 2D array layers are honoured.
  - 3D views use the sampler's Z addressing mode and blend the two nearest slices (bilinear) or pick one (point).
- Levels:
  - Single-level images, `_lz` samples and a sampler without a mip filter use the base level.
  - An explicit LOD (`image_sample_l`) is clamped to the image's levels. The mip filter then selects the nearest level (point) or blends the two adjacent levels (linear).
- Images filtered this way no longer get a point-filtered copy of their sampler, since the shader never samples through it.
- Unnormalized sampler coordinates are used as texel positions on the base level, without scaling by the image size. Images filtered this way are left out of the unnormalized sampler checks, which only apply to host-sampled views.
- Still refused:
  - mirror-once addressing, a border color table, anisotropic or unequal filters and reduction samplers;
  - implicit or clamped LODs across levels, and a sampler or view LOD bias or clamp on a multi-level image;
  - 1D and cube views, bindless tables and gathers.

### Tested
- Windows 11, MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0, RTX 5090: `agc_driver_image_converted_unorm` passes with new cases. `image_sample_lz` across a 32-texel R10_G11_B11 float image, sampled a quarter texel left of each centre, matches a CPU reference for:
  - point with clamp to edge;
  - bilinear with clamp to edge, wrap and mirror;
  - bilinear with half border and a white border;
  - bilinear with unnormalized coordinates;
  - bilinear on a two-slice 3D image sampled halfway between the slices, which returns the average of both slices.
  
  Gathers of such an image, and mirror-once addressing, are refused.

body:
### What

Comparison sampling of a color texture (the emulated `image_sample_c*` path) required the view's X channel to select red. A title runs `image_sample_c_lz` on a 1x1 R8 unorm placeholder texture whose `dst_sel` is constant 0 on all four channels.

The comparison works on the texel's first channel, and the view swizzle is applied to its result. This matches Vulkan, where the component swizzle of a depth-compare view applies to the comparison result, and RADV programs that swizzle directly into the T# `dst_sel`. So when X selects constant 0 or 1, the result is that constant.

- `EmulatedCompare` gains a 2-bit result field: compared, zero or one. The materializer sets it from `dst_sel_x`.
- The emitter returns the constant for zero or one without fetching. Red is unchanged.
- An X channel selecting green, blue or alpha still throws ("...implemented only when the view's X channel is red or a constant").

### Tested
- Windows 11, MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0, RTX 5090: `agc_driver_emulated_color_compare` passes with new cases. A bilinear compare through a view with X = constant 0 returns 0 for every thread, X = constant 1 returns 1, and X = green is refused. The existing red cases are unchanged.
- A title that compares against such a placeholder no longer aborts and continues.

body:
### What

A sampled image used with an unnormalized-coordinate sampler had to be a single-level view starting at mip 0, otherwise binding it threw. A title samples full mip chains this way from compute shaders during start-up: a 10-level 2D view at base level 0, and a 7-level view at base level 3 (a downsample chain).

Vulkan accepts unnormalized samplers only on single-level views, and the hardware samples the view's base level in that mode (the existing test already checks that `image_sample_l` and sampler LOD bias/clamps do not move it off level 0).

- `Texture` keeps the create info for a one-level, one-layer view of the descriptor's base mip (1D, 2D, or the first layer of a 2D array) when the sampled view has more than one level, and creates that view on first use.
- `ShaderResources` binds that view for unnormalized samplers instead of throwing. Views with more than one layer, other view types and a minimum LOD clamp still throw.
- The base-level restriction is dropped: unnormalized coordinates address the view's base mip, which is what the one-level view samples.

### Tested
- Windows 11, MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0, RTX 5090: `agc_driver_image_sample_unnormalized` passes with two new cases for every sampler and instruction: a full 4-level view samples like a 1-level image, and a 3-level view starting at mip 1 samples mip 1 in mip-1 texel coordinates (mip 1 now holds its own pattern).
- A title that samples these views no longer aborts on either view and continues to the next start-up issue.

### What

Both NIDs of `libSceVideoOutVrrStatus` were throwing stubs (#518). A title calls both while it sets up video output:

- `kP2L8t3j-aM` is called without arguments right after `sceVideoOutSetFlipRate`, and the result is ignored. It now returns 0 and does nothing, since the host output has no VRR state to report; it is listed under silent stubs.
- `LibwuIonIBw` is called as `(equeue, handle, udata)` directly after `sceVideoOutAddVblankEvent`, `sceVideoOutAddFlipEvent` and `sceVideoOutAddOutputModeEvent` with the same arguments, and the result is ignored. The title's video out event loop handles event ids 0, 1, 8 and 16; the id 16 handler re-reads the VRR bits of `sceVideoOutGetVblankStatus` and `sceVideoOutGetOutputStatus`. It now registers a video out event with id 16 (`VIDEO_OUT_EVENT_VRR_STATUS`) through the same path as the other add-event functions, removes it on close, and `sceVideoOutGetEventId` accepts it. The event is never triggered because the host VRR state does not change.

The names are still unknown, so the exports keep their `sceVideoOutUnknown00/01` names; the TechnicalDebt entries now record what is known about their signatures.

### Tested
- Windows 11, MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0: `video_out_flip_tests controls` passes with new checks that the id 16 subscription is recorded, that waiting for a vblank does not deliver it, and that `sceVideoOutGetEventId` accepts it.

### What

AnyPS5 relinks guest executables into native Windows/Linux user-space programs. Its libkernel POSIX imports `read`, `_read`, `write`, `_write`, and `lseek` currently let ordinary file failures escape as host exceptions. Translate recognized failures to `-1` and guest `errno`, including Linux `EAGAIN` 11 to FreeBSD guest 35. Preserve successful values, 64-bit seek offsets, previous errno on success, direct `sceKernel` behaviour, and unsupported-operation diagnostics.

The public synthetic VABI regression exercises file and pipe I/O, invalid descriptors/access modes/buffers/whence, zero-length null buffers, sparse seeking beyond 4 GiB, and Linux nonblocking-pipe EAGAIN. body:
### What
Stacked on #759; please review the last commit only.

A capture evaluates every V#, T# and S# a shader uses, even behind a branch the wave won't take. If one is loaded through a null or unmapped pointer read from memory, the capture throws (`null or misaligned address`, `guest memory is not readable`), while the console only faults when a wave runs that `s_load`. #759 covers only flat SRT reads.

- Record time: in `EvaluateRuntimeSourcesImpl`, a descriptor dword read that #759 would record makes the whole descriptor zero; the flat walk records the `s_load`'s dwords as before. If no record names that read, it still throws.
- Run time is #759's runtime check, so it follows boykopovar's guidance the same way: the guarded `ReadConst` faults at the `s_load`'s pc. On `main` a zero V# is an absent buffer, a zero T# a null descriptor and a zero S# a valid sampler, so a zeroed descriptor binds and specializes like zeros read from memory: no new key.
- Still throws: branch conditions, uniform fills, table bases, user-data pointers and descriptor reads no flat slot records.
- PPSA26344 v1.008: about 40 draws a frame use six vertex shaders that load V#s at `*(SRT + 0x98)` only if `s_buffer_load_dword ..., 0x120` is nonzero; the pointer is null in the skipped draws.
- Overlaps: #1747 also edits `EvaluateRuntimeSourcesImpl`.

### Tested
- Windows 11, MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0, based on `main` 1be6f9f1 with #759: configure `-DBUILD_TESTING=ON`, full build, `--target libs`, `ctest`:

`v_mac_legacy_f32` (VOP2 0x06, and its VOP3 form 0x106) now uses the same translation as `v_mad_legacy_f32`, with the accumulator as the addend. Measured on gfx1010, it behaves exactly like VOP3 0x140 (#1281): the product is rounded before the add, f32 denormal sources, product and result are flushed to signed zero in every MODE, and a zero factor gives a +0 product. body:
### What

`v_mad_legacy_f32` (VOP3 0x140) was translated as a fused multiply-add, an assumption recorded in TechnicalDebt as unmeasured. Measured on gfx1010 (the gfx10.1 family of the PS5's gfx1013), it is not fused:

- the product is rounded to f32 before the add: `(1+2^-12)^2 - 1` gives `0x3a000000` (fused: `0x3a000400`), `max * 2 - max` gives `+inf` (fused: `max`);
- f32 denormal sources, the product and the result are flushed to signed zero in every MODE (IEEE 0/1, f32 denormals 0/3), like `v_mad_f32`;
- a zero factor still gives a +0 product (`0 * inf + 1 = 1`, `-0 * 5 + -0 = +0`).

The translation now multiplies, applies the zero rule, adds, and flushes the sources, the product and the result. `FmaLegacy.cpp` pins the measured results of its five encodings (plain, `-src0`, `|src0| -src2`, `src0=0`, `-src0 -|src1|`) for the original 20 rows plus 10 rows that separate fused from rounded and keep/flush denormals; the old rows could not tell the models apart. The TechnicalDebt entry is replaced by what was measured.

`v_mac_legacy_f32` (VOP2 0x06) measured the same on gfx1010. Its translation already rounds the product but does not flush denormals; that is recorded in TechnicalDebt and left for a follow-up PR.

Source of the semantics: measured on hardware, AMD Radeon RX 5700 XT (gfx1010), with `tools/hw-oracle/template.s`. The kernel was assembled and launched on Windows through the AMD driver's `amd_comgr_2.dll` and `amdhip64_6.dll` instead of `oracle.c` + ROCr; the template, its kernel descriptor and float-mode fields were unchanged. The 30 rows gave identical results in all four IEEE/denormal combinations; the separate model check covered wave32 and wave64.

### Tested

Windows 11, MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0 (WinLibs r7), AMD Radeon RX 5700 XT, CI configure flags, full `ctest --output-on-failure --timeout 120`: 399 of 401 pass.

- `agc_driver_fma_legacy` and `vector_mad_legacy` pass. With the previous fused translation, `agc_driver_fma_legacy` fails (`lane 20 (0x3f800800, 0x3f800800, 0xbf800000) v_mad_legacy_f32 is 0x3a000400, expected 0x3a000000`); with the rounding kept but the denormal flush removed, it fails at lane 26 (`-src0 is 0x80000000, expected 0x00000000`).
- `agc_driver_sdwa_float_selectors` (`lane 2 add_f16 BYTE_1/WORD_1 -> BYTE_0 is 0x000000ba, expected 0x00000000`) and `agc_driver_sdwa_ldexp_f16` (`lane 2 BYTE_0/DWORD -> DWORD is 0x0000fff0, expected 0x00000000`) fail with the same messages on unmodified `main` on this GPU; they are unrelated to this change.

body:
### What
Depends on #1265. Until it merges, this PR also shows its three commits; only the last commit is new here.

`note_bda_write` runs a device-scope `OpAtomicCompareExchange` on every probe, also when the slot already holds the page. The written-page table lives in the BDA fault buffer, which is host-visible memory, so every BDA store pays an atomic across PCIe. Almost every store hits a page that an earlier store already noted.

- Each probe now loads the slot with a relaxed `OpAtomicLoad` and runs the compare-exchange only when the slot does not hold the page.
- The slots probed and their order, the pages recorded, and the overflow report are unchanged. If the load sees a stale 0 or another page, the compare-exchange runs exactly as before.

### Why the CAS is the cost
DOOM homebrew PPSA99666 v1.1.1 ([lowbit/ps5-doom](https://github.com/lowbit/ps5-doom), GPL-2.0) presents through a small compute kernel: 1080 workgroups of 64, each reads palette-indexed bytes and stores 1920 pixels through raw pointers, about 2.07 M BDA stores per frame. It waits 500 ms for the frame's fence and otherwise falls back to its CPU scaler.

| | GPU time per dispatch | DOOM |
|---|---|---|
| `main` | 174 ms (`APS5_PROFILE_GPU`) | GPU path, 5.5 FPS |
| #1265 | 248 ms (`APS5_SYNC_DISPATCH`, packet time) | frame 3 exceeds 500 ms, CPU fallback |
| #1265 + this | 8.1 ms (`APS5_PROFILE_GPU`, ~590 dispatches per 10 s) | GPU path, 60 FPS (display refresh) |

Experiments on `main` before writing this:
- Allocating the fault buffer `DEVICE_LOCAL | HOST_VISIBLE | HOST_COHERENT` (ReBAR) instead of system memory gave the same gain: about 170 ms to about 10 ms per frame.
- Moving the BDA range table to device-local memory as well changed nothing measurable, so the table lookups are not the cost.
- `APS5_SPIRV_OPT=full` changed nothing.

This change keeps both buffers where they are and needs no ReBAR.

### Tested
Windows 11 Pro (26200), MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0 (WinLibs r7), Release, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti, Ryzen 7 7800X3D.

- All 195 `agc_*` and `shader_*` tests pass on this branch.
- Built with `ANYPS5_ENABLE_SPIRV_TOOLS=ON`, which validates every module before and after optimization: `flat_store`, `global_store_addtid`, `global_atomics`, `global_atomics64`, `global_atomics_float`, `global_atomics_lanes`, `global_atomic_csub`, `flat_cache_bits`, `global_vcc_base`, `flat_loads`, `d16_memory` and the BDA tests pass (13 tests).
- On `main`, the same change before #1265 also passed all 396 registered tests.
- Tests were run from the commands and environments in the generated `CTestTestfile.cmake` files, because antivirus blocks `ctest.exe` on this machine.
- DOOM measured as in the table. The dumped request (`APS5_DUMP_SHADERS`, `shader_202a81800.req`, 304 code words) replays with `agc_shader_replay`; I can attach it.

Not run on AMD, Intel or Linux.

body:
### What
#414 splits an image read whose T# or S# is a Phi of SRT reads in one block. A descriptor chosen inside a loop or through a chain of branches reaches the read as a web of Phis, for example `Phi(first, Phi(first, second))` across a loop back edge. The plan then throws `GetImageResource dword 0 is not a valid runtime value; chain: Phi(...Phi(...))`.

When the one-block split does not apply, `SplitDescriptorWeb` now takes over:
- `WebSelector` walks all split descriptor dwords together, as one tuple, back through the Phi web. It handles one Phi block at a time, memoized on the tuple, so loop back edges close into a cycle. It stops at 512 tuples and 64 arms.
- Every tuple without Phis is a leaf. A leaf whose dwords can all be recomputed (SRT reads at an immediate offset, user data, uniform arithmetic) is an arm, and equivalent leaves share one arm. It builds a parallel `U32` selector Phi web that carries the arm index.
- The read is copied once per arm, each copy with its own memory entry, and the copies' results are selected per component with `IEqual32(selector, arm)` and `SelectU32`.
- If any leaf cannot be recomputed, or holds a program-counter value (`GetShaderBase` arithmetic, which no descriptor holds), the read is left alone and throws as on `main`. The selector Phis built so far are discarded. Nothing is folded or guessed.

`SplitDescriptorPhi` keeps #414's one-block path (now `SplitDescriptorEdges`) and calls the web only where that path used to give up. The copy-and-select emission is shared between the two paths (`ReplaceWithArmCopies`).

Not covered: a web whose dwords are Phis of different blocks at the same step, such as a join that reloads only part of the T# while the rest comes from an earlier join's Phi. It throws as before.

**UFC 6 (PPSA23566) is not fixed by this PR alone.** In compute shader 0x363c84000, two `s_setpc` jump tables are indexed by the same clamped light type, `min(type, 32)`. Entry 32 of the first table jumps to the join without loading a T#, and entry 32 of the second jumps straight to the two samples at 0x808. So for a light type of 32 or more the samples read whatever the T# registers hold: the second table's address arithmetic from the previous loop iteration, or a saved compare mask. Nothing in the shader rules that path out; only the title's data (no light type ≥ 32) does. Those leaves therefore throw here. Handling them exactly needs a fault raised at run time when the read executes through such an arm, which could build on the deferred-fault buffer from #759. That would be a follow-up.

Test (`verifyDescriptorPhis` in `agc_shader_memory_tests`):
- A compute loop samples at the loop header through `Phi(first, Phi(first, second))`. The plan has two images, the SPIR-V samples twice, and the snapshot holds both T#s.
- The same loop, with T# dword 6 overwritten before the loop by the program counter (`s_getpc_b64`), by EXEC, or by a `v_cmp` mask through VCC, throws.
- With T# dwords 4-7 never written before the loop, it plans a third image. `SsaPass::MakeInitialValue` gives a never-written register the value 0, so the planner sees a constant, as it does for every unwritten SGPR read.
- 63 if-then reloads of distinct T#s plan 64 images, and 64 reloads throw (arm limit).
- Joins that reload either T# dword 7 or dwords 0-6 plan their 4 reachable T#s with 8 joins. With 260 joins they pass 512 tuples and throw (state limit). The state count grows by about 2 per join, so the 4096 of the first version would have needed a 23k-dword program that takes minutes in the front end. 512 leaves room for the deepest web seen in UFC 6 (about 35 Phi blocks per read).
- #414's dynamic-offset case is still rejected.

body:
### What

Two reads of the dynamic tables check bounds with arithmetic that can wrap, or not at all.

**The symbol table, `RelinkerPipeline.cpp:210`.** `dynSymTabOffset` comes straight from `DT_OS_SYMTAB` and is never bounded, and the check adds four to the offset:

```
dynSymTabOffset = 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFE
symOff          = 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFE
check:  symOff + 4  wraps to 2   <= raw.size()   -> passes
read:   memcpy(raw.data() + 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFE, 4)
```

**`extractRelative`, `RelinkerPipeline.cpp:293`.** `pos = relaOff + off`, then `memcpy(raw.data() + pos, 8)` with no bounds check at all, while its sibling `extractRela` at least has one.

Both now compare against `raw.size()` without adding to the offset first, and reject an offset below the table start, which is what a wrapped sum produces. The symbol table has no size tag to bound it with, so that check stays per entry, where it was.

The symbol table case was first reported by @muhzain05 in #917's thread; this makes it a bound on the read rather than another case of the same arithmetic.

### Tested

`core/relinker/relinker/tests/DynamicTableBoundsTests.cpp` crafts an ELF whose `DT_OS_SYMTAB` is `0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFE`, and requires the relinker to report the entry as out of bounds. It is registered as `dynamic_table_bounds` and drives the real CLI through `RelinkerProcess.hpp`.

**Failing on `main`, proven by reverting only the implementation and rebuilding:**

```
FAIL: Dynamic string is not NUL-terminated within DT_STRSZ
```

The wrapped offset lands on a byte that is not the entry, so the relinker reports an unrelated problem in another function. With the change it reports `Symbol table entry out of bounds (offset ...)`.

Full suite on Linux (CachyOS, GCC 16.2.1): **405/405 pass**, including the new test.

**What the test does not cover:** the `extractRelative` check has no differential case. `extractRela` reads the same entries first and its own arithmetic wraps identically, so on `main` the garbage entry usually trips a later check before `extractRelative` is reached; the guard matters for the case where that garbage entry happens to look relative and is skipped. Saying so rather than implying a second proven case.

This does not touch `extractRela`, which #917 repairs — that path already has an open PR.

### What
Addresses the code size reported in #1256. Two changes, one commit each. Neither changes what is stored, which faults are recorded or in which order.

- Every 8- and 16-bit BDA store, and the unaligned path of every 32-bit store, emitted one `get_bda_write_pointer` lookup and one `note_bda_write` per byte at the store site, so a 32-bit store carried five write lookups. These byte stores now call `write_bda_bytes` (one per coherence, `DontInline` like `read_bda_dword_bytes`), which loops over the bytes and does, per byte and in order, the same lookup, the store when the byte is mapped and the write note. Aligned 32-bit stores keep their single 4-byte lookup. The probe-first path of the reads is not used here, as it would change how an aligned store that crosses a range boundary records its fault.
- `note_bda_write` unrolled its 8 compare-exchange probes and is inlined at every BDA store and atomic. The probes now run in a loop that tries the same slots in the same order and stops at the same slot, so the recorded pages and the overflow flag are unchanged.

### What

The integer emulation of round-to-nearest-even f32→f16 conversion (#317) is exact but heavy: a compute shader with ~3600 conversions (2.27M SPIR-V words) never finished compiling on NVIDIA. When the device enables `shaderFloat16` and guarantees `shaderRoundingModeRTEFloat16`, `shaderDenormPreserveFloat16` and `shaderSignedZeroInfNanPreserveFloat16`, the driver advertises `Float16`, `RoundingModeRTE` and `DenormPreserve`, and the recompiler emits `OpFConvert` under the 16-bit `RoundingModeRTE`, `DenormPreserve` and `SignedZeroInfNanPreserve` execution modes. NaNs keep the emulated quiet NaN with the high payload bits. Devices without these guarantees (e.g. RADV's truncating `packHalf2x16`, the reason for #317) keep the emulation.

body:
### What

`EmitFPFract32` emits `GLSLstd450Fract`. Vulkan specifies `Fract` as correctly rounded in the implementation's rounding mode, which may round down. Intel's `frc` does, on the Windows driver and on Mesa ANV:

```
agc_driver_vop1_float_unary: lane 13 fract_f32 v5 is 0x3f7fbd2b, expected 0x3f7fbd2c
```

The input is `0xba85a805`. Its exact fraction is 0.99898028315…, so rounding to nearest gives `0x3f7fbd2c`. On the Windows driver `Fract` stays at `0x3f7fbd2b` even when the module declares `RoundingModeRTE 32`.

Emitting `x - floor(x)` (the first version of this PR) is not enough. When `floor(x)` has a single use, Mesa folds the subtraction back into `ffract` even with `NoContraction` (`nir_opt_algebraic.py`, a rule without `~`), and ANV emits `frc` again. See @hashaam1217's comment below.

`V_FRACT_F32` now emits `fract(|x|)`, which is exact: the fraction of a non-negative float is representable, so there is nothing to round. For a negative non-integer `x` it returns `1 - fract(|x|)`, a single correctly rounded subtraction with the same value as `x - floor(x)`. Edge cases:

- NaN fails both ordered compares and passes through.
- `-0.0` and negative integers give `+0.0`.
- Infinities are marked invalid by `unaryFloatSpecials`.
- A small negative input whose `1 - f` rounds to 1.0 is clamped to `0x3f7fffff` there.

`V_FRACT_F16` takes the same path. The formula is @hashaam1217's.

Source of the semantics:

- Mesa defines `ffract` as `src0 - floorf(src0)` (`src/compiler/nir/nir_opcodes.py`), and ACO emits `v_fract_f32` for it (`src/amd/compiler/instruction_selection/aco_select_nir_alu.cpp`, `nir_op_ffract`).
- LLVM matches `fsub(x, floor(x))`, clamped below 1.0 with the infinity check kept, to `v_fract_*` (`llvm/test/CodeGen/AMDGPU/fract-match.ll`).

Not measured with the hardware oracle. The result follows the f32 rounding mode like any other f32 op (#981).

### Tested

Windows 11 (26200), WinLibs GCC 15.2.0 r7, CI configure flags, main at 4764e59c, `ctest --output-on-failure --timeout 120 --repeat until-fail:3`:

- Intel Raptor Lake-S Mobile Graphics (driver 32.0.101.6790), `ANYPS5_GPU=Intel`:
  - `agc_driver_vop1_float_unary` and `agc_driver_f32_result_clamp` pass; `vop1_float_unary` fails on main.
  - Full suite: 29 failures, all also failing on main for other causes on this device (no `shaderFloat64`, no `shaderDeviceClock`, compute subgroup width #1185, 64-bit atomics #1213, f16 denormals #981, `OpSMulExtended` #1246). None are new.
- NVIDIA RTX 4070 Laptop GPU (driver 32.0.15.9597): full suite 395/395 passed.
