### What
On Linux the relinker wrote each guest module's DT_HASH with one bucket, so every symbol sat in a single chain. Guest modules come first in the global lookup scope, so every symbol lookup from a host prx walked every symbol of every guest module before reaching the host definition. The relinker now writes a standard SysV hash table (gABI ELF hash) with one bucket per symbol, which is how the console's own modules ship it (nbucket == nchain in all seven of Hades II's sce_module prx). The table is built from the final string and symbol tables, after the `#guest` and `__tls_get_addr` renames.

Hades II (PPSA36082) bundles libSceNpCppWebApi.prx with 44906 symbols, and a lookup walked all of them. Its 512 MiB upload pool is freed only after a GPU fence, and the slow lookups were one of the delays in front of that fence: with this change and some local changes it gets past loading (3/3 runs); without it the pool overflows (2/2).

body:
### What
With the pipeline, the committer (`Graphics::Draw` under the GPU lock) is the limit, at about 27 µs per draw in GTA V Performance mode. This trims it to about 23 µs and turns the pipeline on:

- The draw stage's recompile result is shared instead of copied.
- Repeated pipeline lookups with the thread's previous key take an identity fast path (`APS5_PIPELINE_IDENTITY`).
- Draw snapshots are slices of shared arenas instead of a buffer each (`APS5_SNAPSHOT_RING`). Snapshots of at most 4 KiB are copied fresh instead of looked up (`APS5_SNAPSHOT_FRESH_COPY=0` turns that off).
- A storage image's refresh proof is memoized within a collect epoch (`APS5_TARGET_PROOF_MEMO`).
- Two more memos are included but stay off, because they measured no gain: re-proving a reused template from its last fast proof (`APS5_LOOKUP_MEMO`), and per-thread reused draw inputs (`APS5_DRAW_INPUT_MEMO`).

title: perf(agc): cheaper draw commits; pipelined draws on by default

body:
### What
With `APS5_PIPELINED_DRAWS=1`, queue 0's worker decodes, captures and recompiles a draw, and hands it to a committer thread that records it (`Graphics::Draw` under the GPU lock). The two now run in parallel instead of one after the other. Work the committer has not reached yet is tracked by the guest ranges it will write. A later packet that reads or writes those ranges, or one the pipeline cannot order, drains it.

These are ordered as commit items instead of drains:
- labels (WRITE_DATA, RELEASE_MEM), and same-queue waits on them (`APS5_PIPELINE_DRAIN_LABELS=1` drains instead);
- the end of a queue-0 submission, and a released REWIND tail (`APS5_PIPELINE_DRAIN_SUBMISSIONS=1` drains);
- the title's buffer fill kernels (`APS5_PIPELINE_DRAIN_FILLS=1` drains);
- DMA_DATA immediates and copies (`APS5_PIPELINE_DMA=1`).

A draw's write ranges include the storage images it writes and its exact color and depth target ranges (`APS5_EXACT_DRAW_WRITES=1`), not estimates.

Draw-path costs the pipeline exposed:
- `ShaderMemory` moves, so a commit owns its capture's pages.
- A submission made before the worker's current collect epoch began keeps the epoch, so a worker behind a queue of submissions walks a surface once per catch-up (`APS5_SUBMISSION_EPOCH_EACH=1` bumps at every submission). A thread remembers the ranges it walked for the whole epoch.
- The pipeline signals only threads that wait.
- The pending-image and unit-shadow registries take a spinning slim lock instead of `std::mutex` (winpthreads contention showed up as kernel events).
- `ScanPending` skips the registry walk when no pending image can overlap.
- Fewer heap allocations per recorded draw: reused descriptor sets and scratch vectors, and buffer pool size classes are kept.

The pipeline is off by default in this PR; the next one in the series turns it on.

A predicated packet is left to the normal path while predication is active, so a false predicate still skips it.

Note for #374 and #419: they note HTILE and CMASK fills in the DMA_DATA path. Whichever lands second also has to call `NoteDepthMetadataFill` and `NoteColorMetadataFill` in the pipelined DMA commit (`commitDmaStore`).

### Tested

body:
### What
The per-draw capture of a shader's memory (the SRT walk and the guest pages it reads) cost about 15 µs per draw packet in GTA V Performance mode. It now costs about 6.6 µs.

- The SRT evaluator memoizes per plan value in a reused, stamped per-thread array, instead of a hash table allocated and grown on every walk (evaluate 5.3 to 3.6 µs per capture).
- `ExtractPlan` also stores the plan's values as 32-byte records with argument ids, and the walk evaluates that compact copy. The IR walk spent most of its time in cache misses (3.6 to 2.7 µs). The evaluator is a template over the node view, so both walks share every opcode's semantics, memo, cycle and failure rules. A plan that cannot be expressed compactly keeps the IR walk. `APS5_VERIFY_SRT_COMPACT=1` walks both and throws on any difference.
- `ShaderMemory`'s valid/read/recent marks are arrays of 64-bit words scanned with `countr_zero`, instead of bitsets tested bit by bit (about 1 µs per draw packet).
- Captured pages come from a per-thread pool and are found through a short vector with a last-page shortcut. A page that no recorded GPU work writes gets the flush hook a whole-page read would make, then has each 64-byte block copied when a word of it is first read (about 0.3 µs per packet). Pages with pending GPU writes, and unmapped pages, are read as before.
- `APS5_PROFILE_DRAW` splits the capture time into SRT evaluation and materialization, and prints the `[capture]` line once per 10 s instead of every 500 captures (it cost about 2 µs per capture).

### Tested
Windows 11 Pro, AMD Ryzen 5 7600, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5080 (driver 32.0.16.1074), 32 GB, MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0.

body:
### What
A compute FLAT access whose address has the console's shared aperture in its high dword (0x8000xxxx) reads or writes the workgroup's LDS at its low dword. One in the private aperture (0x7000xxxx) reaches the lane's scratch. Other addresses stay guest memory through BDA, as before. This holds for every FLAT access kind in compute:
- dword loads and stores; sub-dword stores and unaligned dword accesses go byte by byte;
- 32- and 64-bit FLAT atomics route to LDS (64-bit ones under the workgroup lock), to scratch (a read-modify-write, since SPIR-V has no atomics on Function storage) or to BDA; an unaligned atomic records a BDA fault.

GTA V's ray traversal keeps its stack in LDS and spills it to scratch through such addresses. Treated as guest memory, the pushes were lost and the traversal never ended (device lost).

`tests/execution/FlatApertures.cpp` runs a table of 121 rows: dword loads and stores, sub-dword stores (aligned and crossing a dword), 32- and 64-bit atomics on shared, private and guest addresses, a wave whose lanes mix LDS, scratch and guest addresses, and wave64.

Source of the aperture bases: the values GTA V's traversal addresses use (shared 0x8000, private 0x7000 in the high 16 bits). No public source confirms them for gfx10 or the console; they, the unaligned aperture semantics and the out-of-range LDS/scratch behaviour are listed as inferred in TechnicalDebt.md, with the scalar operands 235-238 (`src_shared_base`, `src_private_base`, ...) that stay unmodelled.

body:
### What

`sceKernelGetModuleInfoFromAddr` was not implemented on Windows: it called `NotImplemented_nid_no_patch`, so any title whose `libc.prx` asks which module an address belongs to aborted at startup.

On Windows the module is now the PE image that holds the address (`VirtualQuery`, `MEM_IMAGE`):
- **name**: the image file name without `.guest.prx`, as on Linux
- **id**: the `sceKernelLoadStartModule` handle from the dynamic loader, otherwise a stable id from the same range (`ModuleIdForImage_nid_no_patch`, as on Linux)
- **segments**: for an image the relinker produced, its `.elfN` sections (the ELF load pages); for any other image, its first 4 sections with memory access. Protection comes from the section characteristics
- **eh_frame**: for a relinked image, the eh_frame_hdr whose RVA the relinker records in `.ehmeta`, with its size computed from the header encodings and table; for a host image, the `.ehfram` section that `configure_windows_unwind` produces, without an eh_frame_hdr
- TLS fields, `init_proc_addr` and `fini_proc_addr` stay 0; `ref_count` is 1. Addresses outside any image return `SCE_KERNEL_ERROR_ESRCH`

The eh_frame_hdr/eh_frame decoding (pointer encodings, record walk) is shared between the Linux and Windows paths instead of being duplicated. The Linux path behaves the same, and its eh_frame_ptr decoding now accepts every standard encoding instead of only `0x1b`, `0x03` and `0x00`.

`guest_module_info` now runs on Windows too. The fixture and test binary go through `configure_windows_unwind`, and only the eh_frame_hdr check stays Linux-only. The TechnicalDebt entry describes the Windows behaviour instead of saying "Not implemented on Windows".

### Tested

body:
### What
A whole-table bindless image table binds its entries as one descriptor array, sized by the table (the next power of two, at least `APS5_BINDLESS_SLOTS`) up to the device's per-stage sampled-image limit, at most 65536. Before, tables wider than 48 slots were refused. The key indexes the array directly. GTA V's fidelity mode reads a 65536-entry T# heap from a compute pass.

- A table binds the shape (numeric class, dimension, cube) of the access's group, not of its first entry. A 2D access whose table started with a cube or 3D texture sampled zeros for its 2D entries.
- A table entry whose reads build more than one T# is planned for each of them. A heap offset `(key * 32) & mask`, with a contiguous mask keeping at least 16 key bits, matches like `key * 32`.
- A table whose keys select nothing binds null descriptors and an empty mapping, so every key samples zeros, as on hardware.
- A T# in a depth-comparison binding whose format no comparison can read binds a zero texture, as a null T# does.
- `SetBindlessTableLimit` is reviewed for the shader disk cache key (it reaches the key through the specialization's table slots). The disk cache format version is 8.

`tests/ShaderMemory.cpp` covers the table planning cases.

body:
### What
The packed pixel ancillary VGPR may reach its sample-number and render-target-index extracts through a move or a select, and those extracts may only get immediate offsets and counts late in folding (GTA V; data from other titles in this thread). After the fold pass, such a word is lowered when every reader, through `Identity` or a select's value operand, is a `BitField(U/S)Extract` with an immediate offset and count inside the sample field [8,12) or the RTA field [16,29): each extract becomes a direct `SampleId`/`Layer` read. Any other reader (an unmodelled bit, a whole-word compare, a store, a count of zero, a phi) keeps the word live and the shader is refused as on `main`. body:
### What
`StorageTexture::ClassifyFill` reported `FillCover::Keys` only when no live image overlapped the fill. A fill at a surface's DCC key address is now a key fill even when other images overlap that memory.

Transient memory makes this common. In GTA V (Performance mode), the 640x360 bloom target keeps its DCC keys inside the range of a 4K target that is no longer drawn, but whose image is still registered. The title clears the bloom target every frame with a key fill. Because the fill overlapped the 4K image, it was classified `Inside`, so `NoteKeysFill` never ran for the bloom target. The keys held the same clear code every frame, so no refresh saw a change. The bloom target kept its pending results, and its additive draws added to them frame after frame. On screen this showed as blue blobs that grew until a write-back happened to store uncompressed keys.

With the fix, the per-frame fill reaches `NoteKeysFill`, and the next refresh clears the target as before. Classification of fills that do not hit a key address exactly is unchanged.

Related: #903 stores uncompressed keys at the first write of a fast-cleared image. That is a different path, and this change does not depend on it.

body:
### What

A DMA_DATA copy larger than the store limit (64 KiB) runs as a transfer between host imports. When its destination is not registered guest memory, there's no import for it (the GPU can neither read nor write that memory), so the transfer was refused. The packet then drained the device: every batch recorded so far was submitted and waited for, and then the CPU copied.

Such a copy only has to see the source's results:
- The packet now flushes storage results pending over the source and waits only for the batches that write it (`Recorder::SyncThrough`). Then it copies on the CPU without a drain.
- No GPU work reads or writes the destination, so there's nothing on the GPU to order against the CPU store.
- The `[sync]` line counts these copies (`copies into host memory synced on their source`).

### Tested

Linux 7.2.9 (Arch), Mesa 26.2.4 RADV, RX 9070 XT.

- PPSA14632 (LEGO Horizon Adventures) copies 256 KiB of GPU results into host-only memory about 50 times per 10 s, and each one was a device drain. With this change the run has 2 drains in total (one RELEASE_MEM, one other DMA_DATA) instead of ~50 per 10 s, and 526 copies synced on their source. The title is currently limited by GPU time, so this frees the queue 0 worker rather than raising the present rate on its own.

body:
### What

With #943, every Linux direct-memory allocation the GPU uses becomes its own udmabuf and its own imported buffer object, because each allocation had a memfd of its own. Imported buffer objects can't be "always valid" in the GPU VM the way ordinary allocations are, so amdgpu validates every one of them at every command submission. PPSA14632 imports about 7000 allocations (about 5800 of them 64 KiB), and each `vkQueueSubmit` took about 2.3 ms, around 5 s per 10 s, all held under the GPU mutex.

A standalone test on RADV (RX 9070 XT, kernel 7.2.9) measured submits after the first ones:

| imported | per submit |
|---|---|
| 1000 ordinary allocations | 3.5 us |
| 64 dma-buf imports of 64 MiB | 14 us |
| ~7000 dma-buf imports (PPSA14632) | ~2300 us |

So the cost follows the number of imported buffer objects. Their size and the number of ordinary allocations don't matter.

- **libkernel:** on Linux all direct memory lives in one sparse memfd of `DIRECT_MEMORY_SIZE`, at file offset = physical address. `PhysicalBacking` keeps the file and its offset, and `SharedBacking` returns that offset. A range allocated again is zeroed through a temporary mapping, as the old per-allocation memfd was zero-filled.
- **Driver:** an import of shared direct memory that lies inside one 64 MiB chunk of that file creates its own `VkBuffer` and binds it into the chunk's memory, so there is one udmabuf import per chunk. 64 MiB fits udmabuf's default `size_limit_mb`.
  - `HostImport::chunk` holds the chunk, so it lives until the last buffer bound to it retires.
  - Consumers still see one buffer and one device address per import.
  - Ranges that cross a chunk, or whose offset doesn't meet the buffer alignment, are imported alone as before.
- **TechnicalDebt:** released direct memory is not punched out of the file. A live chunk import pins the pages, and the GPU would keep reading the old ones. The process therefore keeps the high-water mark of the direct memory it used.

### Tested

Linux 7.2.9 (Arch), Mesa 26.2.4 RADV, RX 9070 XT.

- PPSA14632 (LEGO Horizon Adventures), 180 s:
  - `vkQueueSubmit` drops from ~2400 us to 46 us on average;
  - the GPU idles 36 ms instead of ~172 ms per present;
  - presents go from ~40 to 80-97 per 10 s;
  - the title reaches content past the boot movies that it had not reached before (new shaders and draws, which are separate issues).
- `guest_memory`: `CheckDirectMemorySharedBacking` now checks that two allocations share one file at offsets equal to their physical addresses, and that a released and reallocated range reads back zeroed. The existing offset checks are relative to the allocation's physical address. I checked that the new checks fail when broken.
- `ctest`: 359 of 359 pass on this branch; 463 of 463 after the rebase onto current `main`.

body:
### What

`scePthreadCancel` and `pthread_cancel` threw, `scePthreadTestcancel` did nothing and the cleanup handler exports did not exist (recorded in TechnicalDebt as "Thread cancellation is not modelled"). This implements deferred cancellation after FreeBSD libthr ([`thr_cancel.c`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/stable/11/lib/libthr/thread/thr_cancel.c), [`thr_clean.c`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/stable/11/lib/libthr/thread/thr_clean.c), [`thr_exit.c`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/stable/11/lib/libthr/thread/thr_exit.c)).

- `scePthreadCancel` / `pthread_cancel` record the request on the thread and wake it when it is blocked in a cancellable wait. A null thread returns `ESRCH`.
- A request is acted on at `scePthreadTestcancel`, the condition variable waits, the `scePthreadSem` and `sem` waits, `scePthreadJoin` and the sleeps, and under their POSIX names. A condition wait takes its mutex back before the thread exits, and a cancelled join leaves the target joinable.
- The thread exits with `PTHREAD_CANCELED` (1) through `scePthreadExit`, which now runs the handlers of the new `__pthread_cleanup_push_imp` and `__pthread_cleanup_pop_imp` exports, newest first. The handler node uses the guest's `_pthread_cleanup_info` like libthr's `struct pthread_cleanup`.
- `scePthreadSetcancelstate` and `scePthreadSetcanceltype` return `EINVAL` for unknown values and, like libthr, test for a pending request when the type is asynchronous. `pthread_setcanceltype` is added.
- `pthread_cancel` moves from `Unimplemented.cpp` to `Pthread/Posix/Thread.cpp` with its real signature.

Limits, recorded in TechnicalDebt: a sleep is not interrupted (the thread exits when it ends, so the `sceKernelUsleep` path keeps its timing), file and socket calls are not cancellation points, and the asynchronous type acts like the deferred one except at the two set calls. The constants and the node layout are FreeBSD's, not measured on the console; the NIDs of the two cleanup exports come from their names and I have not seen a title import them.

#760 adds three lines to `Pthread.hpp` and `Thread.cpp` in other places; this does not depend on it.

### Tested

Windows 11, WinLibs GCC 15.2.0: full build, `libs` target and `ctest` (387 passed; `agc_driver_sdwa_float_selectors`, `shader_clock`, `vop1_float_unary`, `vop3_mad_i64` and `vopc_compare` excluded, they fail on this machine's Intel Arc GPU without this change). New `guest_pthread_cancel` test cancels threads blocked in a condition wait (while the canceller holds the mutex), `scePthreadSemWait`, `sem_wait`, `scePthreadJoin` and a `sceKernelUsleep` loop, checks the disabled state, the asynchronous type, the handler order and the error codes; it passed 40 runs in a row, and 15 with `APS5_COARSE_TIMED_WAITS=1`. Not tested on Linux and not tested with a title.

body:
### What

On Windows, `NativePread`/`NativePwrite` in `core/libs/prx/libkernel/Aio/src/Aio.cpp` seeked a `_dup` of the descriptor and read or wrote through it. `_dup` duplicates the OS handle, and a duplicated handle refers to the same file object, so it shares the file position: every AIO request moved the title's own descriptor to the end of the request. The Linux path uses `pread`/`pwrite` and leaves the offset alone.

The Windows path now saves the descriptor's offset, seeks the descriptor itself, transfers, and restores the offset (throwing if the restore fails). Both functions share one helper; the existing size limits and error reporting (`EBADF` for an invalid descriptor, as the batch test with `fd == -1` checks) are unchanged. The save and restore is not atomic with respect to another thread reading or writing the same descriptor at the same time.

`GuestAio.cpp` now seeks the batch descriptor to offset 2 and checks that it is still 2 after the write batch and after the read batch.

### Tested

Windows 11, MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0 (WinLibs r7), CMake 4.4.4, Ninja 1.13.2, on e79c971f.

- With the new checks and `Aio.cpp` from `main`, `guest_aio_tests` aborts with `Aio check failed at line 109` (the check right after the write batch at offset 8).
- With this change, `ctest -R '^guest_aio$' --repeat until-fail:3`: passed 3/3.
- Full build, `--target libs`, full `ctest`: 393/393 passed.
- Linux: not run locally. The Linux code is unchanged; the new checks hold there because `pread`/`pwrite` do not move the offset.

## What

Adopts a formatting/tooling baseline for the whole tree so style is enforced mechanically instead of by review:

- **`.clang-format`** — LLVM base + deliberate deviations, all documented in the file: `IndentWidth: 4` (the tree is 4-space indented), `ColumnLimit: 120` (long shader-dump/profile lines are atomic; the tree already has 500-char lines), `PointerAlignment: Left` (matches the tree), `SortIncludes: Never` (include order is load-bearing here), `FixNamespaceComments: false`.
- **`.editorconfig`** — LF, UTF-8, 4-space indent, final newline, no trailing whitespace; mirrors the hooks.
- **`.pre-commit-config.yaml`** — `pre-commit/pre-commit-hooks` **v6.0.0** (trailing-whitespace, end-of-file-fixer, check-yaml, check-merge-conflict, check-case-conflict, check-added-large-files, check-executables-have-shebangs, mixed-line-ending → LF) and `pre-commit/mirrors-clang-format` **v21.1.8**. Vendored code under `3rdparty/` is excluded from every hook.
- **`.github/workflows/pre-commit.yml`** — CI job that runs `pre-commit run --all-files` on push to `main` and on pull requests, matching the existing Build workflow's checkout conventions.
- **`CONTRIBUTING.md`** — documents `pre-commit install` and the format requirement.
- **Baseline reformat of `core/`** — `clang-format -i` (21.1.8, the pinned revision). Mechanical: line-wrapping at 120 columns, brace/indent normalization, single-statement blocks. No semantic changes (the working tree before this commit was already hook-clean, so CI `--all-files` passes).

The reformatting commit includes `GuestMemory.cpp`/`ShaderMemory.cpp`, which #1114 also touches — whichever merges second needs only a trivial rebase (`git clang-format` can't auto-merge formatting-only hunks, but the conflict is mechanical).

body:
### What

`sceKernelLoadStartModule` throws away its arguments, and the relinker's Linux guest writer synthesizes an initialisation trampoline that also clears the argument registers:

```cpp
bytes.insert(bytes.end(), {0x31, 0xff, 0x31, 0xf6, 0x31, 0xd2, 0xe9});   // xor edi, esi, edx; jmp target
```

So a converted module always reaches its own start-up code with `args = 0` and `argp = NULL`, whatever the caller passed. This PR delivers them.

That is not cosmetic. On PPSA28997, two of the title's own modules validate the parameter block as the first thing they do and dereference it unconditionally:

```
SaveData.prx:
4d0a: mov (%rsi),%eax     ; *(uint32*)argp - rsi (argp) is NULL
4d0c: cmp $0x10,%edi      ; args >= 0x10 ?
4d18: cmp $0x10,%eax      ; *argp == 0x10 ?

PSN.prx:    rip = PSN+0x3ee7, rbx = 0        (same validator shape)
```

The Windows branch delivers the block, so identical code takes its reported-error path and the title carries on. The gap is issue #918; #846 covers the Windows half of the same asymmetry, where the writer exports `__aps5_guest_initialize` and the loader calls it with `args`/`argp`.

`libkernel` records the pair in thread-local storage before `dlopen` and clears it after - thread-local because `ld.so` runs the initialiser on the calling thread, which makes the handoff per-call rather than per-process, and the emitted stub reads it through two accessors it exports:

```
00: 50            push rax
01: ff 15 <d1>    call [rip+d1]    ; __aps5_get_pending_module_args_nid_no_patch -> &{args, argp}
07: 48 8b 38      mov rdi,[rax]
0a: 48 8b 70 08   mov rsi,[rax+8]
0e: 31 d2         xor edx,edx
10: e8 <d2>       call target      ; the module's own initialiser
15: 89 c7         mov edi,eax
17: ff 15 <d3>    call [rip+d3]    ; __aps5_set_module_init_result_nid_no_patch(eax)
1d: 58            pop rax
1e: c3            ret
```

Two pushes keep `rsp` 16-byte aligned at every call. Calling the initialiser instead of tail-jumping is what makes the `*res` reporting possible. Two undefined symbols and two `R_X86_64_GLOB_DAT` relocations land in the extra block the writer already emits `.dynsym`, `.dynstr`, `.gnu.hash` and `.rela.dyn` into.

Scope is kept honest in two ways: modules the executable needs at start-up still receive `(0, 0)` - which is what both platforms do for them today - and a module with no initialiser gains no slots, no relocations and no imports at all, so `guest_symbol_names` passes unmodified.

The accessor names carry `_nid_no_patch` because `ResolveNids` hashes any unsuffixed export into a NID name; on the first attempt here the built library exported neither name and a plain-name import could never resolve.

### Tested

Arch Linux, GCC, `Release`. `ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure` after `cmake -DBUILD_TESTING=ON`: **392/392 passed** (independently confirmed by @Dextroid17 on a second Linux/NVIDIA box, 390/390 at the time of that check).

On the title (PPSA28997, Linux relink, default configuration, no diagnostic flags), with #906's twin-library gap worked around separately so the module can load at all:

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dlopen(Media/Plugins/PSN.prx)` | `(nil)`, `undefined symbol: wTpfglkmv34`, 4554 retries | non-nil handle x6, no `undefined symbol` |
| SaveData plugin entry | never reached | resolved |
| title's managed bootstrap | never finishes | prints its own "Finished Initializing ... Scripts" milestone |
| early `ERROR...` stall | present | gone |

Reproduction of the quoted fault: relink PPSA28997 with the three launcher-deferred modules made start-up dependencies; the registers quoted are from that core, which reproduces in about two seconds before `main`.

body:
### What

Implements `sceKernelAddReadEvent`, `sceKernelDeleteReadEvent`, `sceKernelAddWriteEvent` and `sceKernelDeleteWriteEvent` for guest sockets (`EVFILT_READ` -1, `EVFILT_WRITE` -2).

- `KernelFilter` gets an optional `pollFunc`. `GetTriggeredEvents` and `WaitForEvents` call it for every event that has one and set `triggered` from the result.
- `GuestSockets::Ready` checks the host socket (`poll` / `WSAPoll`) with a zero timeout. A read event reports the readable byte count (`FIONREAD`) in `data` and a write event the send buffer size (`SO_SNDBUF`). `EV_EOF` is set on `POLLHUP`/`POLLERR`, and for a read event also once the peer has shut down its sending side (`POLLRDHUP` on Linux). Events are level-triggered, as in kqueue without `EV_CLEAR`.
- When nothing is ready, the wait is event-driven, not polled:
  - The thread blocks in `ppoll` / `WSAPoll` on the sockets of the queue's descriptor events plus a per-thread loopback UDP wake socket.
  - Adding, triggering or deleting an event and closing the queue write one byte to the wake socket of each thread blocked on that queue. Each thread registers its wake socket under the queue lock before unlocking, so no wake-up is lost.
  - Timeouts and timer deadlines bound the `ppoll`/`WSAPoll` timeout. `WSAPoll` counts in milliseconds, so on Windows the last sub-millisecond before a deadline is waited on the queue's condition variable.
- Closing a guest socket removes its read and write events from every queue, as `close` does on FreeBSD.
- A descriptor that is not a guest socket and a low watermark above 1 throw; a closed socket is `EBADF`.
- TechnicalDebt (Functional) notes that a write event's `data` is the send buffer size, not the free space in it.

`WaitForEvents` changes next to the lines #1081 touches (the blocking wait with no timeout); the two do not overlap in behaviour, but whichever merges second needs a small rebase.

New test `guest_socket_events` (TCP over loopback) checks:
- no event before a connection
- the listener becomes readable on connect, with the given user data
- a connected socket is writable with `data > 0`
- the accepted socket reports the sent byte count, then nothing once read, then readable with `data == 0` and `EV_EOF` after the peer closes
- a wait with no timeout returns when data arrives from another thread 50 ms later
- a thread blocked with no timeout is woken when another thread adds a write event
- closing a socket removes its event (a later delete is `ENOENT`)
- deleting twice is `ENOENT`, a closed socket is `EBADF`, and a non-socket descriptor and a large low watermark throw

With the wake on `AddEvent` removed, the test hangs.

### Title

PPSA17221 (Minecraft) needs #716 to load the modules in its app root, so every run below is current `main` + #716 + the PRs of this set (#1088, #1090–#1096), plus local changes outside it: dialog, NpAuth and TextToSpeech2 stubs that open PRs cover (#560, #925, #301) and a GPU end-of-pipe change that is not submitted. With all of them the title loads a world. The line below is from a run with only this PR left out, Windows 11, WinLibs GCC, normal user session.

Without it startup stops at load:

```
FAIL: unresolved ELF import JxJ4tfgKlXA from libkernel.prx
```

`JxJ4tfgKlXA` is `sceKernelDeleteReadEvent`; the eboot also imports `sceKernelAddReadEvent` (`VHCS3rCd0PM`), `sceKernelAddWriteEvent` (`R-tyYMpYaxY`) and `sceKernelDeleteWriteEvent` (`cBGTk8S92XM`).

### Tested

Debian 13 (WSL2), GCC 14.2.0, Release: full `ctest`, 0 of 391 failed (151 AGC driver tests report Skipped on this machine), including `guest_socket_events` and `guest_equeue_events`.

Windows 11, WinLibs GCC:
- `guest_socket_events` and `guest_tcp` pass.
- `guest_udp` passes once the `SO_LINGER` checks are removed. Those checks come from the closed #1090, which is still in the local integration tree, and Windows rejects `SO_LINGER` on UDP sockets.
- PPSA17221 with this PR and the rest of the set loads a world.

body:
### What
When the device refused a heap mirror's buffer, or a new mirror would go past `APS5_HEAP_MIRROR_MIB`, `acquireMirror` printed a FATAL line and called `abort()`, so one address-based build short of host memory ended the process. PPSA26344 v1.008 hit it at 478 s, with 6.8 GiB of heap mirrors next to the host imports in the 16 GiB host-visible heap.

- A mirror that would go past `APS5_HEAP_MIRROR_MIB` first sweeps the mirrors whose range the guest freed since the last build's sweep, before its allocation. If it still does not fit, the build throws `heap mirror of 0x...+0x...: past the budget; heap mirrors hold ...`.
- The mirror is allocated once. A refusal throws `heap mirror of 0x...+0x...: vkAllocateMemory buffer: Vulkan result -2; heap mirrors hold ...`, so the draw or dispatch fails like any other allocation; there is no second try. Nothing is registered for the range.
- Nothing changes while memory suffices.
- #290 edits other functions of the file, and this commit applies on top of it cleanly. #1410 and #1411 (ours) change `sweepMirrors` and `acquireMirror` elsewhere; both merge cleanly, and the tests pass merged with them.

### Tested
- Windows 11, MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0, based on `main` 9619edff: configure `-DBUILD_TESTING=ON`, full build, `--target libs`, `ctest`:
- 406/406 tests pass (`ctest --output-on-failure`)
- Same build on lavapipe (Mesa 26.2.4 llvmpipe, 8-wide subgroups, `VK_DRIVER_FILES`): 405/405 pass; `agc_driver_flat_store` is left out there because it takes several minutes on Windows llvmpipe
- `agc_driver_graphics` (`APS5_HEAP_MIRROR_MIB=4`, mock memory limit): a mirror past the budget is made in the memory of the expired mirror swept first; a refused one fails its build with `Vulkan result -2` after one allocation attempt, and is made once the limit is lifted. Fails on main: `FATAL: heap mirror of ...: past the budget`, then `abort()`.
- PPSA26344 v1.008 with #290 (previous revision, same until a refusal): no FATAL in 900 s, host memory peaked at 13.1 of 15.9 GiB.
- Not tested: Linux (CI), console behaviour.

body:
### What
The game window now uses the title's icon. When `/app0/sce_sys/icon0.png` exists, `DisplayWindow` decodes it with the existing `decoder_png` (RGBA8) and sets it with `SDL_SetWindowIcon` right after the window is created.

This completes the icon work:
- #350 embeds `icon0.png` in the generated Windows `.exe`. Explorer shows it, and SDL uses it as the window class icon.
- #353 (open) writes a `.desktop` entry, so Linux file managers and launchers show the icon.
- This PR sets the icon on the running window. On Linux, an ELF has no icon resource, so the title bar, taskbar and alt-tab showed a generic icon until now. On Windows the call sets the same image again.

The icon bytes come from the existing AppMetadata `HasAppIcon`/`GetAppIconData`, which already check the PNG signature. Without `icon0.png` nothing changes. If the icon can't be decoded, window creation throws, like the other `DisplayWindow` failures.

`libSceVideoOut` now links `decoder_png`. No new dependencies or flags.

### Tested
Linux (Arch, KDE Plasma, Wayland session):
- `libSceVideoOut` builds, and `guest_video_out_wqhd_detection` passes.
- Standalone check with the same decode and `SDL_SetWindowIcon` path, a real 512×512 `icon0.png` and `SDL_VIDEODRIVER=x11`: `_NET_WM_ICON` is 512×512, and pixel (100,100) reads `0xffc91312` (ARGB), which matches the decoded RGBA `c9 13 12 ff`, so the channel order is correct.
- PPSA14632 (LEGO Horizon Adventures), with this commit on a test tree of `main` plus other open PRs, `SDL_VIDEODRIVER=x11` under XWayland: the game window's `_NET_WM_ICON` (read with `XGetWindowProperty`) is 512×512, and pixel (100,100) is `0xffc91312`, the same as in the standalone check. body:
### What

Layered draws into 3D color targets render, where they were rejected with `color views of several array slices are unsupported`. Titles fill a volume with one instanced draw: `CB_COLOR_VIEW` covers several depth slices, and the vertex stage picks each primitive's slice through the misc position export (`PA_CL_VS_OUT_CNTL` USE_VTX_RENDER_TARGET_INDX with VS_OUT_MISC_VEC_ENA).

Builds on #423, which carries `PA_CL_VS_OUT_CNTL` to the recompiler. Its commits are at the bottom of this branch until it merges (rebased onto #423's current head, 577b8d57). Only the top commit is this PR.

- **Decode:** `DecodeColorBuffer` takes the slice range of a 3D target into `ColorTarget::layers`, clamped to the surface's last slice. It allows DCC on 3D targets and sizes a tiled 3D target by its whole surface (`SurfaceForTarget` moves to `State.cpp`). `DecodeState` sets `State::renderLayers` and, for a layered draw, USE_VTX_RENDER_TARGET_INDX (`State::layerExports`). Targets of different slice counts and layered draws with a depth target throw.
- **Recompiler input:** the driver ORs `State::layerExports` into the `PA_CL_VS_OUT_CNTL` bits that #423 passes. #423 already passes VS_OUT_MISC_VEC_ENA, so only the render target index is added, and only for layered draws. Elsewhere the layer export stays ignored, as before.
- **SPIR-V:** a vertex stage writing `gl_Layer` declares `ShaderViewportIndexLayerEXT` and `SPV_EXT_shader_viewport_index_layer` when the device offers them, instead of SPIR-V 1.5 `ShaderLayer`, which the driver's Vulkan 1.1 target cannot take. The device enables `VK_EXT_shader_viewport_index_layer` when present. Graphics validation accepts the capability, the extension and a vertex `Layer` output when it is enabled, and a per-primitive `Layer` output of a mesh stage.
- **Attachments:** the resident target's attachment view is a 2D array view of the slices, and the framebuffer has that many layers.
- A TechnicalDebt line records what is not modeled.

### Tested

Linux 7.2.9 (Arch), Mesa 26.2.4 RADV, RX 9070 XT.

- New execution test `agc_driver_layered_volume_draw`. It draws into a 4-slice, 64 KiB-tiled RGBA8 volume through a view of slices 1..3, three bands with one per layer (the layer comes from the misc export), and reads every slice back with the R_X swizzle equation (its slice input included). Slice 0 stays untouched and slice 1 + L holds only band L. With `paClVsOutCntl` left at 0, it fails as expected (layer 1's band lands in slice 1). It skips without `VK_EXT_shader_viewport_index_layer`, which lavapipe has.
  - Mesh case: it recompiles a mesh program with the layer export (Mesh.cpp's geometry program plus an `exp pos1`), checks that it declares a `Layer` output, and validates it against the layered state. Without the mesh `Layer` rule in the validator, this case fails. It does not draw, because lavapipe's LLVM backend aborts while compiling that mesh pipeline (`Cannot emit physreg copy instruction`), which a test cannot catch. On RADV the same mesh draw renders the bands into the right slices.
- `agc_vertex_layer_export` recompiles a vertex shader with a misc layer export. It declares the extension's capability under SPIR-V 1.3 when it is offered, `ShaderLayer` with SPIR-V 1.5 when it is not, and no `gl_Layer` without USE_VTX_RENDER_TARGET_INDX.
- `agc_driver_graphics` covers the slice-range decode (layers, clamping, refusals, a DCC 3D target, the export bit) and the validation of a vertex `Layer` output with and without the extension.
- PPSA14632 (LEGO Horizon Adventures) renders its 64x64x64 RGBA16F translucency lighting volumes this way: two DCC targets, 64 instances, a mesh (NGG) vertex stage. About 270 such draws per 150 s were rejected. With this PR the slice range decodes and the draws record. Their pixel shaders also read the layer from the packed pixel ancillary (#295, merged, and #375 through #423). About half of the draws then stop at a separate limit (`writable guest memory overlaps an immutable snapshot`), which is not part of this PR.
- `ctest` on #423 + this PR: 397 of 397 pass; 468 of 468 after the rebase onto #423's current head.

### What

Graphics shader validation accepts `OpCapability Int64Atomics` when the device enabled `shaderBufferInt64Atomics`. The recompiler emits that capability for 64-bit buffer atomics in any stage, and the device setup enables the feature when it is available. But `ValidateShaders` only accepted its fixed list, so every draw whose shaders use one was dropped with `SPIR-V requires unsupported device capability 12`. Compute dispatches are not validated this way and already ran them.

The device records the feature (`bufferInt64Atomics` in the device state and in the graphics `Context`) and passes it to `ValidateShaders`.

A note for #896, which adds 64-bit image atomics: its second commit does the same for `Int64ImageEXT` with an `imageInt64Atomics` flag. Both PRs change the same `ValidateShaders` signature, so whichever lands second needs a rebase. The combined form is `..., descriptorIndexing, bufferInt64Atomics, imageInt64Atomics`, with `Int64Atomics` accepted when either flag is set.

body:
### What

`SPI_SHADER_COL_FORMAT` 7 (`UINT16_ABGR`) is accepted when the target's `CB_COLOR_INFO` number type is UINT. `DecodeState` rejected it although the recompiler already handles it: an MRT output under mode 7 is a `uvec4` (`SpirvEmitterHelpers`), and a compressed export's 16-bit halves are taken with `OpBitFieldUExtract` (`ExportVector`).

- The target records the export (`ColorTarget::uintExport`). Shader validation then requires a `u32x4` output at its location instead of `f32x4`.
- Blending into such a target is refused, since Vulkan has no blending of integer attachments.
- Format 7 into a target that is not UINT still throws, as does `SINT16_ABGR` (8), whose halves would need sign extension.
- A TechnicalDebt line records that a 16-bit value beyond a narrower target's range (`R8_UINT`) is undefined in Vulkan and the console's behaviour is not confirmed.

### Tested

Linux 7.2.9 (Arch), Mesa 26.2.4 RADV, RX 9070 XT.

- PPSA14632 (LEGO Horizon Adventures) draws into a 2848x1600 `R8_UINT` target with export format 7. About 290 draws per 3 minutes were dropped; they now record.
- New execution test `agc_driver_pixel_uint16_export` draws compressed MRT0 exports under mode 7 into a linear 16_16_16_16 UINT target, one row per pair of packed words (`0x0000ffff`/`0xffff0000`, `0x00010002`/`0xffffffff`, the two swapped, and four distinct halves), and reads every 16-bit component back under the identity, STD_REV (`0x1b`) and ALT_REV (`0x93`) export mappings. A sixth row stays untouched. It fails if the halves are swapped or the mapping is ignored. `agc_driver_graphics` covers the decode, the `uintExport` flag and the blend refusal.
- `ctest`: 464 of 464 pass on current `main`.

This PR addresses the issue where `sceVideoOutOpen` hangs indefinitely on Windows machines with certain vendor HID devices connected (e.g. Corsair iCUE virtual HID, SteelSeries). The block occurs inside SDL's DirectInput enumeration. 
The solution disables DirectInput joystick enumeration on Windows by setting `SDL_HINT_DIRECTINPUT_ENABLED` to `"0"` with `SDL_HINT_DEFAULT` priority.

Fixes #1042

body:
### What

`agc_driver_recorder_tests` is built but never run in CI. On the Linux job's device (lavapipe) it fails on `main` on every run, and the process then segfaults at exit:

```
AGC graphics: the partial publish did not copy exactly the partly covered unit
```

**Cause.** lavapipe runs command buffers on CPU threads, so its writes into a host import go through the page tables, and the write watch collects them as CPU stores. The probe that decides whether imports stay watched only checks a GPU read, which reports 0 of 4 pages on lavapipe, so imports stay watched. In `unitShadowTests`, the whole publish's copy into the import is then collected as a CPU store over unit 3. After the unit is retiled again, the partial publish finds it written since the retile and drops the slab's newer bytes as stale: `PublishShadow` returns 0 and the unit is no longer shadowed. Any write the driver records into a watched import on such a device reads the same way.

Fixes #1429.

Four commits:

1. `fix(agc): compare host imports when device writes reach the write watch`: `ProbeImportWriteProtection` also fills the scratch import on the GPU and collects again (`writtenAfterFill`). When the read or the fill reports pages as written, imported ranges are compared, as on amdgpu. On lavapipe the startup line now reads:
   ```
   [write-watch] host imports resolve write protection: yes (0 of 4 scratch pages written after a GPU read, 4 after a GPU write, 0 after the import); imported ranges are compared
   ```
2. `test(agc): run the recorder tests in ctest`: registers `agc_driver_recorder` with the other driver tests. It skips with 77 without a usable Vulkan device (the Windows job), unless `ANYPS5_REQUIRE_VULKAN` is set (the Linux job). The draw snapshot reuse test (69a94208) assumed watched imports. With imports compared, a draw copies its input every time, as that commit intends, so the test now reports itself as not run there, like the unit shadow test. It also failed on `main` with `APS5_WRITE_WATCH_IMPORTS=unwatch`, the amdgpu path.
3. `test(agc): gate the import window checks on the range's own writes`: `importWindowTests` took its write checks when the scratch import probe reported pages written at import time. That probe runs on a separate mapping. On NVIDIA it reports 4 of 4 pages while the test's range is unchanged, so the case failed (#1532). The case now branches on the range's own `UnchangedSince` after the collect. Suggested by @MarcZX100 and measured by @Dextroid17 (RTX 3080 Ti: exit 1 before, 0 after).
4. `test(agc): report the dma-buf import probe as not run without /dev/udmabuf`: `importWatchTests` required the dma-buf import probe (#943) to succeed whenever the device supports dma-buf import. GitHub's Linux runner has no `/dev/udmabuf`, and many distributions create it as `root:kvm 0660` (#1688), so the suite stopped in CI at `(u) the dma-buf import probe failed at open /dev/udmabuf`. When the probe fails at that step, the case now reports the dma-buf probe as not tested, as it does without dma-buf import. Any other probe failure still fails.

No title needs this. It puts the suite that covers storage write-back, DCC keys, labels and unit shadows into CI, so every pull request that changes those paths runs it.

### Tested

- Linux (Ubuntu 24.04 on WSL2, kernel 6.18), GCC 13.2, Release, `BUILD_TESTING=ON`, lavapipe (Mesa 25.2.8).
- On `main`, instrumented: the partial publish returns 0 and unit 3 is no longer shadowed. Right after the whole publish, `UnchangedSinceCollected(unit3, unit, pre)` is false: the publish's own copy was collected as a CPU write.
- With this PR, `agc_driver_recorder` passes (0.3 s) with `ANYPS5_REQUIRE_VULKAN=1 GALLIUM_OVERRIDE_CPU_CAPS=avx`, over 3 ctest repeats and 5 direct runs. With `VK_ICD_FILENAMES` pointing at no driver it skips; with `ANYPS5_REQUIRE_VULKAN=1` as well it fails.
- `ctest` on the rebased head (`ANYPS5_REQUIRE_VULKAN=1`): 495 tests. The only failures are `guest_sce_net` and `nid_patcher_dynamic_strings`, which fail here on `main` too (the resolver test; the local toolchain adds its own RUNPATH). `tools/check_test_registration.py build` passes. With `VK_ICD_FILENAMES` pointing at no driver, `agc_driver_recorder` skips, and with `ANYPS5_REQUIRE_VULKAN=1` as well it fails.
- Verbose ctest output with the new decision and with `APS5_WRITE_WATCH_IMPORTS=watch` (the old lavapipe decision) differs only in the recorder suite. There, draw snapshot reuse, unit shadows and the watched storage refresh report themselves as not run on lavapipe.
- Rebased onto `f1451396`. With CI's environment (`ANYPS5_REQUIRE_VULKAN=1 GALLIUM_OVERRIDE_CPU_CAPS=avx`), `ctest -R '^agc_driver_recorder$' --repeat until-fail:3` passes. WSL has no `/dev/udmabuf`, so the dma-buf probe reports itself as not tested, as on the CI runner. With `APS5_WRITE_WATCH_IMPORTS=watch` (the old lavapipe decision) it fails at `the partial publish did not copy exactly the partly covered unit`.
- I have no NVIDIA, AMD or Intel hardware. Results from others on this PR:
  - @orbz22 (Windows): RTX 3060 Laptop and Intel UHD pass.
  - @johnmaia (Linux, on `main` with #1210): RX 7600 (RADV), UHD 730 (ANV) and llvmpipe pass.
  - @Dextroid17: RTX 3080 Ti stays watched (`writtenAfterFill` is 0). It passes with the third commit.
- Not built on Windows. The probe is Linux-only, and the Windows job has no Vulkan driver, so the test skips there. With #1028, the Linux job does not skip it, and on Windows it falls under the `agc_driver_*` rule.
- After a failed check the suite still segfaults at exit, as on `main`. That path is not touched here.

GPUs without `VK_KHR_maintenance8` currently skip every 2D derivative case because the seven ordinary cases and five computed-offset cases share one shader. Split that shader so the ordinary cases always run, while only the computed-offset cases remain capability-gated. This follows up on #829, which explicitly left splitting the cases out of scope.

Both programs retain the original instruction encodings, output registers and result slots. The input, expected-result and masking tables are unchanged, as are the 1D and 3D programs. body:
### What

Closes #1012.

#### The hole

Both jobs report a full pass while a large part of the suite does not run:

| job | reported | actually skipped | ran |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| linux | `100% tests passed out of 371` | **20** | 351 |
| windows | `100% tests passed, 0 tests failed out of 368` | **143** | 225 |

On Linux the 20 are `agc_driver` execution tests that need a wave wider than llvmpipe's subgroup size 8. On Windows it is **143 of the 147** GPU execution tests: the runner has no Vulkan driver, `ANYPS5_REQUIRE_VULKAN` is not set on that job, so they exit 77 and ctest counts a skip as a pass.

A test that exits 77 is reported `***Skipped` and **ctest still exits 0**, so a change that makes one more test device-dependent loses its coverage silently while both jobs stay green.

#### What this does

`tools/check_skips.py` reads the file ctest writes with `--output-junit` and fails when a test skips that is not expected:

- **linux**: any test that reports the device limitation it needs — the narrow-subgroup `agc_driver` tests measured on the CI device, plus `agc_driver_conservative_rasterization`, which reports the device has no `VK_EXT_conservative_rasterization`;
- **windows**: any `agc` test, because the runner has no Vulkan driver at all — `agc_driver`, the `agc_driver_*` execution tests and `agc_shader_*`; a skip of anything else fails.

An expected skip that no longer happens is a `note:`, not a failure, so the sets stay current as the images change (a device gaining coverage must not break CI).

Both jobs now pass `--output-junit` and run the check after ctest:

```yaml
      - run: ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure --timeout 120 --repeat until-fail:3 --output-junit ctest.xml
        env:
          ANYPS5_REQUIRE_VULKAN: 1
          GALLIUM_OVERRIDE_CPU_CAPS: avx
      - run: python3 tools/check_skips.py build/ctest.xml
```
```yaml
      - shell: cmd
        run: ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure --timeout 120 --repeat until-fail:3 --output-junit ctest.xml
      - run: python tools/check_skips.py build/ctest.xml --job windows
```

The JUnit file is the reason for the shape: it needs no redirection, so the console output stays visible and no pipe can turn a failing ctest into a passing step. (`python` on the Windows job, which is what the release workflow already uses there; `python3` on Linux.)

#### Notes for review

- `--output-junit` needs CMake 3.21 or newer. Both runners are well past that, and the file is ~240 KB.
- The Windows job's `ANYPS5_REQUIRE_VULKAN` is deliberately left unset: setting it would turn those 143 skips into failures with no driver installed. This change makes the situation visible rather than changing it.
- Worth knowing, and it rules out the tempting shortcut: `LP_NATIVE_VECTOR_WIDTH=1024` makes llvmpipe report subgroup 32, so those 20 Linux tests *run* — but they then fail on a wrong lane value (`lane 16 result 0 is 3038057749, expected 2768569605`), while a real subgroup-32 GPU passes them. The skip is a driver limitation, so the guard is the right answer rather than a device change.
- `tools/check_skips.py --list` prints what a file contains, for updating a set.

AI-assisted: yes.

### Tested

Run here with the CI command and the CI device (`llvmpipe (LLVM 23.1.1, 256 bits) subgroup=8`, `ANYPS5_REQUIRE_VULKAN=1`, `GALLIUM_OVERRIDE_CPU_CAPS=avx`):

| case | result |
| --- | --- |
| the Linux skip that first failed CI, `agc_driver_conservative_rasterization` (no `VK_EXT_conservative_rasterization`) | `1 test(s) skipped, all expected` — exit **0** |
| a narrow-subgroup skip, `agc_driver_look_back_scan` | `1 test(s) skipped, all expected` — exit **0** |
| a skip whose reason is not a device limitation | `error: … skipped` — exit **1** |
| the three Windows names CI reports, `agc_driver`, `agc_shader_fusion`, `agc_driver_foo`, with `--job windows` | `3 test(s) skipped, all expected` — exit **0** |
| the same file plus one non-`agc` skip | `error: … skipped` — exit **1** |

The Windows case is exercised against a file built from that job's own log, which is why the rule is a prefix and not a list — a new GPU test should not fail that job. The Linux rule is a *reason* match rather than a name list: the first CI run of this branch failed on `agc_driver_conservative_rasterization` (run 37820232450), which skips because the device lacks `VK_EXT_conservative_rasterization`, not because of its subgroups — the rule now accepts either.

Verified locally today on the rebased head, with the CI command and the CI device:

- the guard, run against a real `build/ctest.xml` from `ctest --test-dir build --output-junit ctest.xml`: `0 test(s) skipped, all expected` — exit **0**;
- one skipped test whose message does not report narrow subgroups: `error: guest_foo skipped ... the job lost that coverage and ctest still reports every test as passed` — exit **1**;
- `--job windows` with an `agc_driver_*` skip: exit **0**; with a non-`agc_driver` skip: exit **1**;
- `--list` prints the skipped test and its reason.
- the file is written at `build/ctest.xml`, which is the path both guard calls read (an `--output-junit` path resolves against `--test-dir`).

body:
### What

v_fma_f64 sent any subnormal operand to a separate multiply and add, so it rounded twice. Results in the subnormal range were also rounded twice even with normal operands: once to 53 bits in the scaled domain and again by the power-of-two rescale. Both cases can differ from IEEE 754 fusedMultiplyAdd in the last bit. The second case was not in the technical debt entry.

Subnormal operands are now widened by 2^64 and go through the exact Boldo and Melquiond path with their exponent lowered by 64. That path now also keeps the sign of the residual between the 53-bit result and the exact sum. When the result lands exactly on a midpoint of the subnormal grid, it is moved one ulp towards the exact sum before the single final rounding. Normal results are rebuilt by setting the exponent, so only a subnormal result rounds. v_div_fmas_f64 shares this path, so its subnormal cases change too.

Source of the semantics is IEEE 754 fusedMultiplyAdd with f64 denormals kept, which the existing f64 path already assumes. I could not compare these cases with RDNA hardware (my GPU is GCN), so the technical debt entry now says that instead of describing the old gap.

Note: the TechnicalDebt.md hunk conflicts textually with #697 and #944, which add lines right above and below the old v_fma_f64 entry. The shader code does not overlap with any open PR. Whichever lands second only needs to keep both lines.

### Tested
<!-- OS, title or homebrew, what was checked. "Not tested" is a valid answer. -->
Linux (GCC 15), no title. New test agc_driver_f64_fma_subnormals with 32 vectors, expected values from glibc fma: 17 of them fail on main and all pass with this change. Full ctest with ANYPS5_REQUIRE_VULKAN=1 passes 370/370 on RADV (R9 380) and on lavapipe, same skips as main.

Outside the repo I modelled the emitted sequence in C++ and checked about 200M random and near-boundary inputs against std::fma, plus the scaled v_div_fmas_f64 path against exact rational arithmetic, with no mismatches. A throwaway GPU fuzz of 320k vectors per driver also had no mismatches; the old code failed 322 of 64k.

body:
### What
The device-local tier of `BufferPool` only reused a buffer of the exact same size and usage. Partial storage-image detiles and retiles ask for a new size and the other transfer direction almost every time, so in PPSA26344 the tier sits at its 512 MiB budget and misses and evicts ~77 buffers per frame. The release thread then spends ~38 ms per frame in `vkFreeMemory`, which on NVIDIA also holds up `vkQueueSubmit` (mean ~0.7 ms).

- Device-tier requests of 1 MiB and more round up to an eighth of their octave (at most 12.5% larger); smaller ones keep their power-of-two classes.
- Device-tier buffers are created with `STORAGE | TRANSFER_SRC | TRANSFER_DST` added (`BufferPool::Usage`), so uploads, write-backs and staging shadows share a list; `SHADER_DEVICE_ADDRESS` and `INDIRECT` requests keep their own.
- `Take` serves a request from the smallest retained buffer of its class up to twice its size; the buffer returns to its own class. Callers bind and copy explicit sizes, as with the small classes.
- Host tiers, the budget, LRU eviction and reuse only after release are unchanged. `APS5_NO_BUFFER_CLASSES=1` still matches exact sizes.
- #290 adds GPU memory accounting in the same files; the `Resources.cpp` conflict is textual, so whichever lands second needs a small rebase.

### Tested
- Windows 11, MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0, based on `main` ab9437e3: configure `-DBUILD_TESTING=ON`, full build, `--target libs`, `ctest`:
- 368/368 tests pass (`ctest --output-on-failure`)
- Same build on lavapipe (Mesa 26.2.4 llvmpipe, 8-wide subgroups, `VK_DRIVER_FILES`): 367/367 pass; `agc_driver_flat_store` is left out there because it takes several minutes on Windows llvmpipe
- New `agc_buffer_pool` (mock device): size classes, shared directions, the 2x fit, reuse only after release, budget. Fails on main.
- Scratch detile/retile benchmark, RTX 3080 Laptop: frees 68 to 9 per frame, release thread 46 to 4 ms, submit mean 0.48 to 0.17 ms.
- PPSA26344 v1.008 (with #903): device-tier misses 79 to 40 and release thread 43 to 17 ms per frame, submit mean 0.69 to 0.55 ms; same frames.
- Not tested: Linux (CI), console behaviour.

body:
### What

A port without a matrix sent source channel n to destination channel n, so a mono voice reached only the left channel of a stereo mix. A port that selects a voice matrix (`SCE_NGS2_VOICE_PARAM_PORT_MATRIX`, or command 7 of `sceNgs2VoiceRunCommands`) whose levels were never set mixed nothing at all, at any port volume.

Both now mix through the console's default channel map:
- mono reaches both stereo channels at -3 dB and the centre of 5.1 and 7.1;
- stereo folds to mono at -3 dB per side and passes through to stereo, 5.1 and 7.1 unchanged;
- wider sources fold down with 0.5 and -3 dB gains;
- the map covers every source width from 1 to 8 channels into 1, 2, 6 and 8 channels;
- a selected matrix whose levels were never set mixes exactly like no matrix;
- matrices with levels are unchanged, including a partly set matrix, which still mixes only the rows it has. A level count of 0 still empties the matrix, which then reads as unset; the library rejects that count, and #2337 makes it throw;
- into 3, 4, 5 or 7 channels the map throws. The library rejects submixer and mastering voices of those widths, so it has no map for them.

TechnicalDebt records that the map comes from the PS4 library.

### Reference

- **PS4 firmware 11.00 `libSceNgs2.sprx`**, dumped and decrypted from a console. It was loaded on Windows with a small test loader and driven through its exports; neither the loader nor the library is part of this PR. One sampler voice per source channel was rendered through a submixer into 1, 2, 6 and 8 channel mastering voices, with no matrix and with an unset matrix, and the levels were read from its output. The test values are its results.
- **PS5 firmware 10.06 `libSceNgs2.sprx`** (the module titles import as `libSceNgs2`): its readable ELF headers match the PS4 library: the same `.eh_frame_hdr` size (3,460 bytes, 431 functions) and code plus read-only data within 1% (321,328 bytes against 323,432). A decrypted PS5 SELF was not used; anyone with a decrypted PS5 `libSceNgs2.sprx` can help confirm this.

### Tested

- Windows 11, WinLibs GCC 15.2.0 r7, Release.
- `ngs2_render` `TestDefaultChannelMap`:
  - 26 source channel to destination combinations from 1 to 8 source channels, with the PS4 library's levels;
  - a 4-channel submixer throws, and the system is destroyed after it.
- `ngs2_render` `TestUnsetMatrix`, selecting matrix 0 without levels:
  - a mono source at port volume 0.5 renders 0.25 at -3 dB on both channels;
  - a stereo source renders its two channels unchanged.
- With `main`'s `Render.cpp` both tests fail. Six mutations each make them fail.
- Full ctest merged with `main` d70b8998, together with #959, #2336 and #2337: 507/507.
- Seen in PPSA22520 (Animal Well): the title music is a stereo sampler patched to a stereo submixer. The title selects matrix 0 with command 7 and never sets its levels, so on `main` the title screen is silent. With this change the music fades in and plays.
- Linux not tested.

body:
> This PR depends on #964 for the default channel map, so its diff includes #964.

### What

Both functions threw `NotImplemented`. They now pan as the console library does.

- `SceNgs2PanParam` (16 bytes: angle, distance, full-band level, LFE level) and `SceNgs2PanWork` (40 bytes: up to 8 speaker angles, unit angle, speaker count) replace the reserved arrays. The layouts are from SharpProspero and match the PS4 library.
- `sceNgs2PanInit(work, angles, unit_angle, num_speakers)` takes 2, 4, 5 or 7 speakers:
  - The speakers are given in the order L R, L R Ls Rs, L R C Ls Rs or L R C Ls Rs Lb Rb. They are kept in a fixed circular order, not sorted, plus a wrap-around entry one full turn after the first.
  - The unit angle is 360 or 2π. With null angles any other value means 360; with explicit angles it throws.
  - With null angles the defaults are 90/270, 40/110/250/320, 0/40/110/250/320 and 0/40/110/150/210/250/320 degrees. For a 2π unit they are converted to radians, except the wrap-around entry, which stays in degrees as in the PS4 library.
- `sceNgs2PanGetVolumeMatrix(work, params, num_params, format, out)` writes the matrix for formats 1, 2, 6 and 8, laid out by destination channel (`out[channel * num_params + param]`), for up to 8 params:
  - each angle pans with a sine law between the two neighbouring speakers;
  - a distance below 1 blends in the opposite direction;
  - full-band levels are scaled by `fbw_level`, and `lfe_level` goes to the LFE channel;
  - when the format differs from the speaker layout, the levels fold through the default channel map from #964;
  - `num_params` 0 returns at once and a null output returns `INVALID_OUT_ADDRESS`, as in the PS4 library.
- The PS5 error codes aren't known, so the other invalid arguments throw. That includes a speaker angle equal to the unit angle, on which the PS4 library loops forever, and angles so large that a turn no longer changes them, for the same reason. Every param is checked before the matrix is written.

TechnicalDebt records the details and the PS4 source.

### Reference

- **PS4 firmware 11.00 `libSceNgs2.sprx`**, dumped and decrypted from a console. It was loaded on Windows with a small test loader and called directly; neither the loader nor the library is part of this PR. The panning code was read from its disassembly, and the test values are its own results.
- **PS5 firmware 10.06 `libSceNgs2.sprx`** (the module titles import as `libSceNgs2`): its readable ELF headers match the PS4 library: the same `.eh_frame_hdr` size (3,460 bytes, 431 functions) and code plus read-only data within 1% (321,328 bytes against 323,432). A decrypted PS5 SELF was not used; anyone with a decrypted PS5 `libSceNgs2.sprx` can help confirm this.

### Tested

- Windows 11, WinLibs GCC 15.2.0 r7, Release.
- `ngs2_render` `TestPan` uses 15 cases with the PS4 library's output, to 1e-6:
  - the default layouts in degrees and radians;
  - a full turn on two speakers;
  - distance below and above 1;
  - each layout into 1, 2, 6 and 8 channels with the LFE level;
  - custom 5- and 7-speaker angles;
  - angles past a full turn.

  It also checks the init layout, the wrap-around entry and the throws: unknown formats, 9 params, NaN, null work or params, 0, 1, 3, 6 or 8 speakers, a speaker angle equal to the unit angle, angles of ±1e30 and an infinite speaker angle in the work, and a work whose unit angle was overwritten. A NaN in the second param leaves the output untouched.
- A separate fuzz run compared this implementation with the PS4 library on 200,000 random cases. All matched bit for bit.
- On `main` the test fails, because both functions throw `NotImplemented`. Sixteen mutations of `Pan.cpp` each make the test fail.
- Full ctest merged with `main` d70b8998, together with #964, #2336 and #2337: 507/507.
- Seen in PPSA22520 (Animal Well): `sceNgs2PanInit(work, NULL, 360, 2)`, then one `sceNgs2PanGetVolumeMatrix(work, &param, 1, 2, out)` per sound with `angle = fmodf(pan * 180 + 270, 360)` and distance 1. Its positional sounds pan by ear.
- Linux not tested.

body:
### What

Adds `ANYPS5_USE_SYSTEM_DEPS`, OFF by default (implements #400). With it ON, `SDL2`, `freetype`, `Vulkan-Headers`, `SPIRV-Headers`, `glslang` and `SPIRV-Tools` come from the system instead of the bundled submodules. The default build is unchanged: the option only wraps the existing `add_subdirectory` calls and skips the bundled shader-cache submodule stamps.

Design:

- `cmake/SystemDeps.cmake` resolves each package with `find_package(... CONFIG)` (`freetype` through `FindFreetype`) and re-exposes them under the target names the rest of the build already uses: `SDL2-static`, `freetype`, `glslang`, `SPIRV`, `glslang-standalone`, `SPIRV-Tools-opt`, `SPIRV-Tools-static`. Because of that, no other CMake file changed except the two submodule stamps in `core/shader/recompiler/CMakeLists.txt`, which would otherwise depend on the missing bundled paths.
- Every package is required. A missing one fails the configure (`find_package(... REQUIRED)`), and if `glslang` is found without the tools, or the headers are incomplete, the configure fails with a named error. Nothing falls back to the submodule, as you asked.
- The system glslang splits the headers (`<prefix>/include/glslang/Public/...` and `<prefix>/include/glslang/SPIRV/GlslangToSpv.h`), unlike the bundled single root; the helper adds both.
- Vulkan-Headers must provide `VK_KHR_maintenance8`, which the agc driver uses. The helper checks it at configure with `check_cxx_source_compiles` on `VkPhysicalDeviceMaintenance8FeaturesKHR` and fails with a clear message when the headers are older. Ubuntu 24.04 (headers 1.4.304) fails there; Ubuntu 25.10 (1.4.321) passes.
- `SDL2` is linked from the system as a shared library (`SDL2::SDL2`). The prx libraries are shared objects and distribution static SDL2 is built without PIC, so `libSDL2.a` cannot be linked into them (`relocation R_X86_64_PC32 ... can not be used when making a shared object`). The default build keeps its own static SDL2. The other five packages link fine from the system.
- `ffmpeg-core` (carries `ffmpeg.patch`), `libjpeg-turbo`, `stb`, `VulkanMemoryAllocator` and `LibAtrac9` always stay bundled and still need `git submodule update --init`.

On your Linux-only vs Windows question: the interface is platform-neutral, but I only exercised the Linux packages, so I would call the Windows side untested rather than claim it. If you prefer to scope it to Linux for now, that is a small change to the helper.

### Tested

Ubuntu 25.10 and 24.04 in linux/amd64 containers (the host is arm64; Docker Desktop runs the containers through Rosetta). Packages: `libsdl2-dev libfreetype-dev libvulkan-dev spirv-headers glslang-dev glslang-tools spirv-tools`, GCC 15, Ninja, x86-64 as the project requires.

- `-DANYPS5_USE_SYSTEM_DEPS=ON`: configure OK and `cmake --build . --target libs` builds.
- `-DANYPS5_USE_SYSTEM_DEPS=ON -DBUILD_TESTING=ON`: configure OK; `pad_sdl_tests` builds (the executables keep `-static-libgcc -static-libstdc++` and link the shared system SDL2).
- Ubuntu 24.04 (Vulkan-Headers 1.4.304): configure fails with the `VK_KHR_maintenance8` message, at configure time.
- Missing package (`-DCMAKE_DISABLE_FIND_PACKAGE_glslang=ON`, and separately `SDL2` and `SPIRV-Tools-opt`): configure fails with a named error each time.
- Default (flag OFF): still reaches `add_subdirectory(3rdparty/SDL2)` and `add_subdirectory(3rdparty/freetype)`.
- The relinker and the rest of the tree are untouched; both paths use the same target names.

Not tested: Windows, and no PS5 title.

body:
### What
For a raw M4AAC stream (`ui_config_number` 2) the maximum channel count was written into the AudioSpecificConfig as the channel configuration. The maximum only bounds the stream:

- The Smurfs Dreams (PPSA21607) creates its decoder with `ui_max_channels` 8 and sends stereo. Channel configuration 8 is reserved, so `avcodec_open2` fails and `sceAudiodecCreateDecoder` throws `cannot open an FFmpeg decoder`.
- With a maximum of 6 (configuration 6) or a maximum of 8 mapped to configuration 7, FFmpeg opens the decoder but decodes no frame of a stereo stream, as the elements do not match the layout.

The raw decoder now starts from the mono/stereo configuration (mono when the maximum is 1, stereo otherwise) and on the first access unit that it cannot decode moves on to configurations 3 to 7 whose channel count is within the maximum, keeping the first one that decodes. With the stereo configuration a mono raw stream decodes as 2 channels, so 2 is reported, not 1 (the same as on `main` with a maximum of 2). Trying configurations until one decodes is our own inference, as no reference documents how the library picks the layout; this is listed under "Unknown function info" in `docs/dev/TechnicalDebt.md`. ADTS streams are unchanged, and the channel count reported by `sceAudiodecDecode` still comes from the decoded frame.

### Tested
- CachyOS, Linux 7.2, GCC, Release, based on `4b005b22`. `guest_audiodec` now also decodes the raw stereo stream with a maximum of 6 and of 8 channels; both abort without the change. A raw 5.1 LC frame (fixture and test by @Dextroid17, thanks) decodes as 6 channels with a maximum of 6 and of 8; it aborts with a maximum of 2 and without the change, so the loop past the stereo configuration is covered. Full ctest: 463/463.
- The Smurfs Dreams (with #911 for `libSceAudiodec.native`): the decoder opens and its stereo 48 kHz stream decodes.
- Windows not built or tested.

The array layer is now round-half-even (measured on RDNA2 by adriadam10), correcting `floor(z + 0.5)` from #668. NaN rows were added, and TRUNC_COORD with bilinear is documented. See the reply below for details.

### What

A follow-up to #668, which was merged before the review fixes were pushed. It carries the changes that answer the four review points from that PR; nothing else. Two commits on current `main`:

1. `fix(agc): compare NOT_EQUAL unordered and refuse reduction filters and TRUNC_COORD in the color compare emulation`
2. `test(agc): cover 2D arrays and GREATER in the color compare emulation`

### How each review point is addressed

1. **2D array.** `EmulatedColorCompare` gains a 2D array case (two layers, a different red table per layer): it covers the layer size query and the `floor(z + 0.5)` clamp, with layer coordinates below 0, between layers and past the last one.
2. **NaN.** `NOT_EQUAL` is now `OpFUnordNotEqual` (true when the reference or the texel is NaN). I could not verify the hardware's NaN behaviour, so the TechnicalDebt entry says so: it is the IEEE `!=` and as Vulkan defines it for its own depth compare, not confirmed on hardware.
3. **Sampler fields.** `FILTER_MODE` (word 0 bits 29 to 30) with a min/max reduction mode throws, and so does `TRUNC_COORD` (bit 27) with point sampling. The test checks both are rejected and that the default values still run. The TechnicalDebt entry lists both.
4. **Other compare functions.** The test now runs `GREATER` as well as `LESSEQUAL`, which guards the operand order.

### Tests

Linux, GCC, NVIDIA RTX 3070, on `main` at `5895ea72`:
- `agc_driver_emulated_color_compare` passes, 4 runs in a row (the new 2D array, GREATER and rejection cases included).
- The full `ctest` passes: 359 of 359, with one test (`agc_driver_pixel_valid_mask`) skipping itself.

I did not run the new cases against the unfixed code in this round.

### Notes

- #639 (still open, and already conflicting with `main`) touches `ResourceMaterializer.cpp`, which this change edits by four lines. Whichever lands second rebases; the emulated compare then needs the runtime-mode form you described in the review.
- Nothing here changes behaviour for titles that don't use a compare sampler on a color texture.

body:
### What

Guest address space on Linux is placed inside the PS5 window instead of wherever the kernel's top-down `mmap` happens to land, so a title's allocator accepts the mapping. `sceKernelAllocateDirectMemory`/`sceKernelMapDirectMemory` with `addr == NULL` now return addresses in `[0x2_0000_0000, 0xFC_0000_0000)`, which is the bound `sceLibcMspaceCreate` enforces.

The arena reserves the free intervals of that window up front (`PROT_NONE | MAP_NORESERVE`, 1 GiB chunks), so no later host mapping - driver, library, hinted `mmap` - can appear inside it, and commit can keep `MAP_FIXED` semantics, which is what committing over the arena's own reservation requires.

Also in this change, from review:

- A reservation chunk that fails with `EEXIST` is recorded as occupied, so the arena cannot hand it out. Any other failure throws, with the address and the size.
- An in-arena unmap keeps the range reserved, through the same `PROT_NONE` replacement that `GuestArenaReset` uses.
- A partial overlap between a commit and an already-used range throws instead of being overwritten, and the unwind releases only what the failing call marked.
- An unmodelled protection value throws.
- The tests cover the kernel API with `addr == NULL`, not only the arena entry points.
- `GuestArenaReset_nid_postfix` no longer releases address-space accounting on Linux (@blawesom). The Linux variant released the range in addition to resetting the memory, while the Windows variant only resets and leaves accounting to the caller. Two call sites released again after the reset, and `Contains` is span-based, so both released twice under two separate lock acquisitions: a thread that allocated the range in between had its entry erased and the arena handed the range out twice. Every caller already releases explicitly, so the contract is restored rather than duplicated.
- The fixed-mapping probe test is Linux-only (@blawesom). It used `mmap`, `PROT_READ`, `PROT_WRITE`, `MAP_FIXED_NOREPLACE` and `EEXIST` directly, which does not compile under MinGW.

Fixes #692.

### Tested

Arch Linux, kernel 7.2.8-arch1-2, GCC, `Release`, `cmake -DBUILD_TESTING=ON`: `ctest` **491/491** on this head, rebased onto current `main`. The slowest test in the suite takes 4.19 s and the two tests added here take 0.01 s each, so nothing approaches the 30 s limit.

The Windows build cannot be compiled here (no MinGW). The guard was verified by tracking preprocessor nesting: before the change the probe body and its call site are outside every `__linux__` block, after it both are inside. CI has to confirm the build itself.

The new kernel-API tests were verified to fail without the change. Making `ArenaAvailable()` return false gives `0% tests passed, 1 tests failed`, and restoring it gives `100%`.

Reservation feasibility was measured before adopting it. With an unlimited address space, 1000 GiB of the window reserves in 1 GiB `PROT_NONE | MAP_NORESERVE | MAP_FIXED_NOREPLACE` chunks, with zero failures on kernel 7.2.8-arch1-2. Under `ulimit -v 67108864` (64 GiB) the arena aborts with `guest arena: cannot reserve 0x19c0000000+0x40000000 (Cannot allocate memory)` instead of passing in silence, and at 128 GiB it fails at `0x29c0000000`.

The reservation does not reduce allocatable device memory. A probe that reserves the same 997 GiB window and then allocates `VK_MEMORY_HEAP_DEVICE_LOCAL_BIT` memory gives identical totals with and without the reservation: 22 GiB before `VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DEVICE_MEMORY` on an RTX 4070 Laptop, and 4 GiB on the AMD 780M, at both 1 GiB and 256 MiB step sizes. This is reported against #861's head in the discussion below.

Title evidence (PPSA28997, native Linux relink): the window placement is what the boot stands on. `sceKernelGetDirectMemorySize` reports `0x360000000` on both platforms, and with the window in place the bundled player/JSON chain stops rejecting the address and the title reaches on-screen video.

Independent reports on other titles:
- @alfalfa-star, PPSA14632: `sceKernelMapNamedFlexibleMemory` → `sceLibcMspaceCreate` now lands inside `[0x400000, 0xFC00000001)` and `Common::initialize` stops failing with `0x80553504`.
- @ghreprimand, PPSA01341: guest mappings move from host addresses such as `0x7fff94400000` into `0x200000000` / `0x200300000`, and the title passes the allocator fault.
- @fisherjoey, Demon's Souls (PPSA01341 v1.07, RTX 5070 Ti): without this PR the title SIGSEGVs under `_dl_init` in 2 of 2 runs; with head `c2e15098` it boots, plays the attract movie at about 30 fps, and exits with code 0 in 2 of 2 runs.

#1370 (partly overlapped allocations) has since merged and this head is rebased on top of it. #1360 remains an alternative to the eager reservation; I will rebase onto it or drop the reservation on the maintainer's call.

### What

`Pipeline::AcquireFramebuffer` first pruned its cached framebuffers (a `use_count` and an `expired()` per owner of every entry) and then scanned them, on every draw. A hit is rotated to the back, so consecutive draws into the same targets find it there. The back entry is now checked first; the prune and the scan run only on a miss, as before.

#419 changes the same function for multisampled targets. The two don't overlap in purpose: the entry comparison is now one `matches` lambda used by both the back-entry check and the scan, so whichever lands second only needs #419's `owned` check moved into that lambda.

### What

`AnyShadowedOverlaps` is asked on every guest access the flush hook sees and on several draw and copy paths. It collected the overlapping shadows into a `std::vector<std::shared_ptr<UnitShadow>>` (an allocation, and a reference count increment and decrement per shadow) only to read them under the registry lock it already holds. It now visits them in place through `anyOverlapping`, which `overlapping()` also uses for the callers that need the list.

### Tested

Windows 11, MinGW GCC 15.2, RTX 2080 Ti. This branch builds, and the 165 agc driver, recompiler and execution test targets pass with it stacked on the other changes I'm sending.

Measured alone on Sonic Origins Plus's heaviest menu page (about 1,650 draws per frame), as asked. The base is `main` at this PR's base (5895ea72) plus the commits my branch needs to boot this title and to sample it (a launcher script, the title's boot fixes, the process sampler; none of them are in this PR), against the same base with this commit on top. Three interleaved rounds, each the median of six FPS readings:

| | Round 1 | Round 2 | Round 3 | Mean |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| base | 11.48 | 11.39 | 11.76 | 11.54 FPS (86.7 ms) |
| with this PR | 11.76 | 11.87 | 11.81 | 11.81 FPS (84.7 ms) |

Ahead in every round, though the gap is larger than the profile supports, so the profile is the better figure: over two 15 s profiles per side, `AnyShadowedOverlaps` took 39 of 5,119 AGC worker samples on the base and 24 of 4,920 with this PR. body:
### What

`Pm4::Execute` resets a queue with `queue = QueueState{}` (`0x09`). The temporary holds `constantRam`, 48 KiB, so the function's frame was 0xc1e0 bytes and every call paid `___chkstk_ms` probing 12 pages, whichever packet it handled. Execute runs for every packet that isn't a draw, so on a busy queue that is thousands of probes per frame.

The reset now builds the new state on the heap and moves it in, so the frame is 0x100 bytes and the probe is gone (checked in the disassembly of libSceAgcDriver.prx). A reset is rare, so the allocation doesn't matter.

### Tested

Windows 11, MinGW GCC 15.2, RTX 2080 Ti. This branch builds, and the 165 agc driver, recompiler and execution test targets pass with it stacked on the other changes I'm sending.

Measured alone on Sonic Origins Plus's heaviest menu page (about 1,650 draws per frame), as asked.
